NOVEMBER 12, 1996
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, November 12, 1996 at 7:34 p.m. The
Clerk was asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk
Graham stated a quorum was present and recorded the following; Supervisor Obst,
Clerk Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Zaban, Trustee Wiegandt and Building
Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with several additions: Update of legal descriptions;
Don Weite letter (Pebble Brook roads); radon testing kits; office staff
Christmas bonuses; secretarial position to be filled and an application
received for this position.
TRI COUNTY OFFICE ON THE AGING - Donna Hobart, representing the Tri County
Office on the Aging made a presentation to the Board requesting a $3,000.00
donation from Williamstown Township toward the construction of a new kitchen
for the Meals on Wheels program. Similar requests are being made of all area
townships and cities serviced by the organization. The organization needs to
reach their goal of $1.5 million by December 31, 1996 in order to qualify for a
challenge grant from the Kresge Foundation. Ten people were serviced by Meals
on Wheels in Williamstown Township in 1995, with many others taking advantage
of the community dining hall meals in Williamston. Treasurer Nilsson moved that
the Township donate the requested $3,000.00 to the Tri County Office on the
Aging towards construction of a new kitchen. Supported by Clerk Graham. Motion
passed unanimously.
WILLIAMSTON COMMUNITY FIRE BOARD REPORT - Representative Keilholtz
Several members of the Ingham County Board of Commissioners believe that the
Williamston Community Fire Board is taking an unfair advantage of the County’s
paramedics since we do not have any of our own and are not paying anything
extra for a County paramedic to go on a call when necessary. We only have First
Response and EMTs available and these people are serving on a volunteer basis.
Average cost for an EMT to go on a run is $5-$6 per hour. Average cost for a
Paramedic is $20 per hour. Concerns expressed that the county does not
understand the large area (103 square miles) that our department covers on a
strictly volunteer basis. Commissioner Grebner is the chair of the Law and
Courts committee. Commissioner Schaefer, our area’s representative, is also on
the committee.
The Fire Board will purchase a new generator. The Fire Board will also purchase
a used Fire Truck that the Fire Association will repair. Concerns expressed
that drivers must know the roads in the area better.
ATTORNEY’S REPORT - Stephen O. Schultz
Holding off on action against ‘Noo Fear’. Mrs. Betty Speaks has started
eviction proceedings against Mr. Squires. She filed a Landlord/Tenant Action in
District Court and was awarded a default judgment on November 4, 1996. She can
issue a writ on the 14th with a 30 day notice for eviction. She is currently
following all proper procedures for eviction and as long as she continues to do
so the Township will not take further action.
Annexation Petition filed by the City of Williamston - No notice of hearing has
been sent by the Boundary Commission yet, but a Legal Contingency Hearing has
been scheduled for December 17, 1996 in the morning. No major flaws are evident
in the petition, if the Boundary Commission finds the petition legally
sufficient, then a public hearing in the Township will be scheduled for early
1997.
Capitol City Rifle Club - Supervisor Obst raised the issue of the letter
received from the rifle club. The typed response seemed to raise some issues
that were not addressed earlier. Received a complaint regarding outside
lighting. Question of expanded lighting not really an issue because they are
not expanding their lighting, rather they are repairing some faulty lighting
that they already have. This will have the perception of expanded lighting, but
it really isn’t. Hours of operation also an issue. CCRC believes that operating
within their standard hours of operation is at their sole discretion and not a
violation of the Township’s nuisance ordinance. The standard hours of operation
have always been 9:00 am to 8:00 PM. They are agreeing on an annual basis to
certain reductions in hours. For 1996 this was 9:00 am to 5:00 PM on Saturday
and Sunday with the exception of certain matches and closing altogether on
certain days such as Mother’s Day. The Township disagrees that the 9:00 to 5:00
on Saturday and Sunday are voluntary and a written response is in order to
insure that 9:00-8:00 was not grandfathered in on weekends when the nuisance
order was adopted. This issue will be considered again at the next Board
meeting with a proposed response.
Sewer and Water Issues and an annexation request - Mr. Bruce Michael, developer
of River Wood, would like to know the board’s position on sewer and water
hookups available to the township and whether or not they are going to agree to
a 425 agreement with the City of Williamston. If the sewer hookup issue cannot
be successfully negotiated with the city then he has no choice but to file for
annexation to the city.
Much discussion followed regarding sewer taps that were still available to the
township. The city is claiming that there are none left. Township under
contract with the firm of Jones and Henry to do a study on the subject. They
concluded that the township has at least 20,000 gallons/day left with a
Residential Equivalency Unit (REU) being 210-300 gallons, or a minimum of 67-95
taps. The Township believes they have 35,000 gallons/day left which would be
117-167 taps. Jones & Henry is also the City of Williamston’s engineer. A copy
of the report was furnished to the city. Per Attorney Schultz, there are many
issues available that would allow the township to take the city to court if
necessary to get the sewer taps that the township is entitled to.
Supervisor Obst recommends that Mr. Bruce Michael go ahead with his plans for
developing River Wood while remaining in the township and that if the city will
not allow the sewer taps, then the township will go to court over the issue.
Mr. Carl McIntosh, engineer for the Hideaway Woods IV subdivision, is also
concerned about the city allowing required hookups to sewers. He has plans to
build a pumping station that will accommodate 55 lots, even though only 15 are
currently approved. Claims the city is telling him he must get approval from
the township first and that the township is telling him he must get approval
from the city first. Needs to know if the board can approve the plat while the
pump station is being planned. He will submit the plat to the township in a
week or so. The board has been given a conceptual layout for all 55 lots. The
time frame for developing them all is at the discretion of the board since the
land for the remaining 40 still needs to be rezoned before that phase of the
project can proceed. Further discussion between the board and Mr. Carl McIntosh
regarding how well the pumping station designed for 55 lots will work when
there are only 15 lots hooked up.
Per Planner Martin, the township did not sign the final plat for Brookshire
until the city had signed and approved the sewer plan. Planner Martin wants to
be sure that Mr. Carl McIntosh is aware that the final plat approval will not
be signed until the plans are approved by the city.
Per Attorney Schultz, the city may approve the 55 tap pump station, but that
does not obligate them to sell the remaining taps to the township at the time
that they are required.
The tap fee of $1,000 is not paid until a building permit is pulled at the
township. This is part of the building permit application criteria.
Further discussion between the board and members of the audience regarding the
remaining taps available to the township. Even if city allows all the taps that
the township believes they are contractually entitled to, the three
developments represented at this meeting alone would use them up. Township
believes the city is holding sewer taps hostage in order to have some leverage
for annexation issues.
BUILDING DEPARTMENT ACTIVITY - Walter Aven
37 new home permits have been issued in the township since the beginning of the
year. This is up from last year.
Spagnuolo’s has been issued a building permit to remodel the interior of their
property on Grand River as a restaurant. They need to be made aware that
special use permits are required for operating hours and parking. Two-thirds of
the existing structure will be used as a restaurant and the remaining one-third
will be rented out as office space.
PLANNING COMMISSION REPORT - Chair, Mickey Martin
Perry rezoning request - Planning commission recommend denial of the rezoning.
There are no other RE zones in the vicinity. Approval would result in spot
zoning. There are other lots in the area that are around 5 acres. The citizens
of the area petitioned that their area remain Ag Small Farm when the new zoning
was approved, even though they were initially slated to be RE. Treasurer
Nilsson moved that based on findings of fact and the planning commission’s
recommendation to deny the rezoning, that the rezoning be denied. Supported by
Supervisor Obst. Discussion followed.
When Mr. Perry obtained the property he realized he would not be able to split
the property for ten years based on splits his grandfather had already made. At
the time the land was obtained by Mr. Perry, AG Small Farm had a minimum
acreage of 5 acres. Mr. Perry was unaware that when the new zoning ordinance
went into effect that AG Small Farm now had a 10 acre minimum.
Supervisor Obst observed that for good zoning purposes the rezoning should be
denied, but that what is reasonable with what is going on in the surrounding
area it should be approved. Suggested an alternative that a new zoning
ordinance be adopted where an AG Small Farm property with at least 600 feet of
frontage be allowed to split off one five acre parcel. Supervisor Obst
recommended turning down the proposed rezoning in favor of turning the issue
over to the Planning Commission to adopt the suggested ordinance. Mr. Perry
stated he didn’t care what zone he ended up with as long as he was allowed to
make the split he requested. He has approximately 1100 feet of roadside
frontage, so that would not be an issue for him. Clerk Graham stated the main
problem is that the residents were afraid of the new zoning name ‘Rural
Estates’. They feared the word ‘estates’ would increase the taxable value of
their property. It would not. Per Planner Martin, the frontage requirements for
RE and AG Small Farm are the same. The only difference between the two zones is
the minimum acreage. Roll call vote on the motion before the board was taken.
Those voting in favor of the motion to deny rezoning were Treasurer Nilsson,
Trustee Zaban and Supervisor Obst. Those against the motion were Clerk Graham
and Trustee Wiegandt. Motion passed.
Trustee Zaban moved that the Planning Commission be asked to have a public
hearing to discuss modifying the zoning ordinance so that a 5 acre parcel could
be split off of an Ag Small Farm parcel that had sufficient frontage. Supported
by Trustee Wiegandt. Motion passed unanimously. Time frame for this new
ordinance to take affect would be at least 90 days. Supervisor Obst apologized
to the Perrys for the delay this action causes.
Mr. Bruner rezoning - A clerical error on the zoning map has been discovered.
Mr. Bruner’s property is shown as RE on the map when in fact it should be RR.
Since the map was voted on, a new vote is required to correct the error. Clerk
Graham so moved. Supported by Trustee Wiegandt. Motion passed unanimously.
Fee Schedule - Planner Martin has been keeping close records of the bills
involved with site plan approval. In many instances the $685 set fee is being
used up in the first 2 or 3 changes to a plan. Several developments have
submitted many more changes and the township is losing money. Suggest that a
$1500 escrow account be set up for plan approval of developments, with the
unused balance to be refunded. Treasurer Nilsson moved to create a $1500 escrow
account for plat revisions, renewable at a rate of $500. Supported by Trustee
Wiegandt. Motion passed unanimously.
CITY OF WILLIAMSTON ANNEXATION PROPOSAL - 425 ANNEXATION AGREEMENT
The City is proposing a 5 year exemption from city taxes for developed property
and a 20 year exemption for undeveloped property. Supervisor Obst read parts of
his Oct 14th letter to the city outlining proposed procedures to follow for
negotiations with the City of Williamston. Instead of entering into proposed
negotiations, the city countered with a “last and final offer” ultimatum.
Annexation petitions have been filed for North Green I and II and the Odell
property. No one else in the proposed areas have stated that they wish to be
annexed by the city. The need for another meeting with the city was suggested
since what was in their letter was not what they had discussed at the last
meeting. Supervisor Obst’s letter was an attempt to address all outstanding
issues with the city when entering into a 425 agreement. If, at the end of the
agreement, the land reverts back to the township, then a buffer would have been
established beyond which the city cannot annex. If the land reverts to the city
at the end of the agreement then no such buffer would exist.
Planner Martin questioned why the township would want to enter into a 425
agreement with the city. Response was that it would solve the sewer agreement
issues and square off boundaries, among other things.
Treasurer Nilsson suggested that we respond to the city’s ultimatum with one of
our own. Comment from the audience was that responding to an ultimatum with an
ultimatum does nothing to further negotiations. This type of response would
just set up a confrontational, and possibly hostile situation between the city
and the township. That is not in the best interest of either entity. The city
has been looking for citizens willing to serve on a committee with citizens
from the township to attempt to resolve some of these issues where elected
officials have been unsuccessful. So far the city has been unsuccessful in its
search. The township has people ready and willing to serve on such a committee.
Another suggestion from the audience would be for a representative from the
township to attend the city council meetings and a representative from the city
to attend the township board meetings. Due to the city council’s tendency to
conduct certain elements of their meetings in closed sessions, this may or may
not be beneficial.
Attorney Schultz commented that the sewer situation in particular should be
looked at on a service level instead of a boundary level, and some sort of
joint operating agreement entered into with the city. This agreement could be
modeled after the successful cooperation between East Lansing and Meridian
Township’s joint operation of their sewer and water system. However the city
does not seem to be able to get beyond their “us vs. them” mentality.
It was mentioned that one of the problems is that the city has had a high turn
over in elected and appointed officials in the past ten years. People currently
in office may not be aware of the history of the current sewer agreement and
are therefore attempting to play games with it.
Planning Commissioner Brian Jennings commented that the regional fire
department seems to work well. We need to enter into more similar regional
service agreements. As a citizen in the city’s proposed annexation area he
stated that he definitely did not want to be annexed by the city. He saw little
or no benefit for a 17 mil increase in his taxes. He would like to see a
regional board created between Williamstown and Wheatfield Townships and the
City of Williamston to work out such issues as sewer and water.
It was generally agreed by the township board not to accept the October 23,
1996 425 annexation proposal from the City of Williamston. Options available
are: 1) Make a counter proposal; 2) Set up a meeting with city officials; or 3)
Work through subcommittees.
Mr. Bruce Michael asked what the Township’s position would be if he went ahead
and asked for the needed sewer taps in his development and the city turned him
down. Attorney Schultz replied that the township would take the city to court
immediately.
Mr. Carl McIntosh suggested getting elected officials out of the negotiations.
Form a committee of concerned citizens from both municipalities to work out the
details of an agreement and present their recommendations to the city council
and township board for approval. Supervisor Obst restated that the township has
people who are willing to do just that but that the city has been unsuccessful
in finding people to serve on such a committee. Mr. Carl McIntosh stated that
he would take it upon himself to recruit city citizens willing to participate.
Planner Martin asked Attorney Schultz if it would be feasible for the township
to put themselves in the driver’s seat and annex the city. Attorney Schultz
stated that there is a process of detachment that the township could attempt,
but the draw backs out weigh the benefits. Most notable is that along with the
township obtaining a percentage of the city’s assets with such an agreement,
they would also obtain an equal percentage of the city’s debt. Another option
suggested was that the city and township merge and form a charter township.
This is also possible, but again not financially feasible considering the
city’s outstanding debts.
Treasurer Nilsson suggested that we reply to the city with a letter stating
that the proposed agreement is not acceptable and propose a meeting with the
city to work out the differences. It was also suggested that citizen
participation in the negotiating process be included in the letter.
Regarding existing sewer taps - requests must continue to be honored on a first
come first serve basis. The treatment plant is capable of servicing more
residents than currently stated. Supervisor Obst stated that the city’s mayor
told him that the only leverage the city has to obtain land is the sewer.
Attorney Schultz - the state law that requires a residence within 200 feet of
sewer line to be connected to the sewer system does not apply across political
boundaries. The Department of Public Health has been unwilling to involve
themselves in such debates.
Question from Mr. Bruce Michael - Approximately 170 homes are currently
requesting sewer hookups just from the three developments represented at
tonight’s meeting. Even if the city honors all the taps the township believes
they are entitled to will there be enough to go around? Calculations determined
that it would be close. Other options proposed were small community septic
systems such as are in place at the township’s two planned developments.
HASLETT ROAD - Recommendations will be delivered to the board the week of

be amended when new construction methods, materials, etc. become available.

LETTER FROM DR. WAITES

own permit since our rules are stricter than the DNR. Clerk Graham stated that
burning permits were not required by the DNR for agricultural land, but that
the Township requests that they take one out. The Township is using the money
set aside from the permits to print the newsletter, where burning and
environmental issues are discussed among other things. Suggested that we need a
two part carbonless form created and a committee set up to come up with the
wording. Currently person burning must have a copy on their person, and the
Township retains a copy for its records. The permit is called in to the
dispatcher and they refer it to the fire chief. A printed copy is currently not
required by nor being forwarded to the fire chief.

JANUARY 7, 1997
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, January 7, 1997 at 7:34 PM. The Clerk
was asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham

PUBLIC COMMENTS:
John Taylor - Oak Leaf -
Mayor's letter to editor of the Enterprise seemed to be a challenge to the
Township. Only solution he proposed that he thought viable for curing the
City’s financial problems was annexation. He talked about a need for sense of
community. Moved to the area because of the rural nature of the Township and
the nature of the city. Township residents obviously shop in the city and are
in and out of the city regularly. This Mayor and city council has made a dent
in Mr. Taylor’s image of the area. Does not appear to have been much planning
involved in their recent developments. Cited such things as building too close
to Williamston Road, putting in an oil change downtown and putting in a truck
stop next to the new restaurant. The truck stop will attract many trucks to the
area, especially on Williamston Road. These things do not fit Mr. Taylor’s
image of how development should proceed in this community. City has made a mess
of it. There is also a lot of development in the Township. Mr. Taylor wants the
board to know his view that he did not move to this area to see significant
development. He does not want to see any, but low, low density development.
Does not believe that the sewer capacity issue fits in how the Township should
develop. It is not inevitable that high density development come to this
Township. Cited examples from Livingston County where development has been
slowed. Does not believe it is the job of this board to promote significant
development. Haslett road issue allows for more development by allowing more
traffic. Concerned that board has voted 3-2 for development that most people in
the community do not want. Believes both the township and city are off track,
but especially the city.
Supervisor Obst: - invited Mr. Taylor to Jan 16th meeting on the Haslett Road
issue. Does not want to stop development, but promote it in such a way so that
it is not obvious that it is there. The entire board wants to preserve the
charm of the township and the rural nature with the master plan, etc. Sewer
capacity is a difficult issue. More capacity would encourage more development,
but reality is that the development will still occur, but it will occur in the
city due to annexation. Annexation issues are already before the boundary
committee.
Mr. Taylor - not saying no development - but wants to see lower density
development.

PLANNING COMMISSION REPORT - Mickey Martin
Brunner Issue:
57-60 acres is currently on the zoning map as RE. The property was originally
zoned RR. When the new zoning ordinance was adopted the planning commission
proposed to rezone this parcel and surrounding parcels to RE. Mr. Brunner
requested at that time to remain RR. The commission agreed to do that and
reported to the board that he would remain RR. Board saw the recommendation
letters and the chart for all the rezonings. Due to an oversight the map was
never changed. No one caught the oversight at time of final adoption. When Mr.
Brunner went to sell his property the issue came up. Planning commission
recommended to approve leaving it as RR. Planning commission minutes page 3
have the record of the public hearing. Findings of fact also in the packet on
Mr. Brunner's property.
Obst: Findings of fact were accepted bottom of page 5. Recommended correction
of administrative error.
Area residents submitted a petition to the board objecting to the RR zoning of
the Brunner parcel. Surrounding parcels are all RE and the neighbors believe RR
will allow for higher density housing than they want to see in their
neighborhood.
The following residents voiced their concerns and objection to zoning the
Brunner parcel as RR:
Mr. & Mrs. S. Terry, Mr. J. Creighton, Ms. R. Zimmerman, Mr. F. Goodman, Mr. P.
Apostle, and Mr. and Mrs. J. McGarey. Concerns stated were lack of informing
neighbors that Mr. Brunner had asked to remain zoned RR initially so that
objections could have been made known at that time. Fear that development of
the property if zoned RR would result in doubling the number of residents in
the immediate area. Life savings tied up in their properties on the assumption
that the area would retain its rural nature. Traffic on Zimmer Rd, especially
at the corner of Zimmer and Grand River, becoming a major problem for
residents. The Township’s inability to get a traffic light installed at this
intersection to date. Do not believe that proper procedures were followed in
granting Mr. Brunner RR initially, and in addressing the correction to the map
from RE to RR.
Planner Martin and members of the board addressed issues raised. Proper
processes were followed.. RR under the current zoning is the same as RR was
under the former zoning ordinance. The parcel could not be zoned to anything
denser than RR. The board has been trying to get a traffic light at Zimmer and
Grand River for the past 5 years. It is the state police departments decision
on where traffic lights will be installed. They have a list of 11 warrants, at
least some of which must be met before a light will be installed. They will no
longer install one just by the will of the people. They did that in another
township and then were successfully sued when a fatality occurred at the
intersection after the light was installed.
Treasurer Nilsson moved that the map be changed to reflect the RR zoning.
Supported by Trustee Wiegandt. Motion passed unanimously.
Supervisor Obst stated that he does not believe nature of the area will be
changed. We will do our best to get the traffic light. A state trooper is going
out to look at the intersection with the Ingham County Road Commission.
Clerk Graham stated a petition from the people in the area will carry more
weight than anything else the township can do on their own.
Mr. Terry stated that he hopes the board will be more responsive to the
petition for the traffic light than they were to the petition from the
surrounding residents on the zoning ordinance. Believes the board has sided
with the land owner who is leaving the township instead of the 19 home owners
who are staying.
Attorney Schultz stated that it is illegal by state law to zone by petition.
Zoning has to be based on a planning ordinance and other state laws.
Supervisor Obst stated that statutes allow that this zoning can be reversed by
a referendum on a ballot. The Board appreciates the citizen input and
understands the consequences of going against what the people want as we are
elected officials.
Schneider, Brannan and Schwartz Rezoning. Recommendation to approve the
rezoning. Total of 74 acres, rezoning 13.2 acres to AG-SF and the small parcel
of RR to AG-SF. Keeps major portion in agricultural and satisfies concerns of
the neighbors. Will square off properties in the area, no new parcels will be
created. Mrs. Stillwell be contacted to change the zoning of her property from
AGC to something more conducive to her property.
Trustee Wiegandt moved to approve the planning commission’s recommendation.
Treasurer Nilsson supported. Motion passed unanimously.
The Board agreed to have Planner Martin contact Mrs. Stillwell about changing
the zoning of her land, and if she is agreeable to this, to hold a public
hearing on her rezoning.
Woodview 2 - Final Plat. Has not gone to the planning commission yet. Asking

Subdivision Control Ordinance - Brian Jennings - Praised by the board and
Planner Martin for his efforts..
Reviewed comments from public meeting. Believes that most of them that
addressed the ordinance were covered in the ordinance. Recommends approving
subdivision control ordinance as well as zoning changes required for the

FEBRUARY 4, 1997
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, February 4, 1997 at 7:34 PM. The Clerk
was asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Zaban, Trustee Wiegandt and Building
Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: New business: letter
with alleged sewer tap request and sewer assessment refund. Old business:
Township burning permit.
HASLETT ROAD ISSUE:
Norm Obst’s evaluation letter was read into the record. George Durak, chair of
the Transportation and Utilities Committee was puzzled by the petition that had
been submitted to the Township Board. After the surveys that had been taken and
the individual questioning of the residents he didn’t understand why there was
a petition filed requesting the speed limit be lowered to 45 MPH when this
issue never came up in his questioning of the residents. Supervisor Obst’s
letter requested that the Ingham County Road Commission study the speed issue
and make a recommendation for a speed limit. He also stated that per the
brochure provided by Bob D’Alcorn of the Ingham County Road Commission, that
the driving environment determines drivers’ average speed. Supervisor Obst was
of the opinion that improving the road would make it safer, and thus the
driving environment would be one where drivers were more likely to drive
faster. Treasurer Nilsson disagreed with this. She believed other factors, such
as pedestrian and bike traffic, and houses all along the road are also part of
the driving environment and therefore speed will not increase significantly if
at all. Mr. Durak looked at studies on Grovenberg and College road where speed
limits are close to Haslett. He thinks that it is a false conclusion that speed
will increase. If it does increase it may only be by a mile or two.
Chuck Cleland, chair of the Advisory Board stated that according to the theory
in the pamphlet, the safest road would be a dirt 2 track where people are going
very slow and the road is not improved. The Ingham County Road Commission
(ICRC) contends these modifications will change neither the volume nor the
speed. The advisory council noted that this road is not just going to be
improved, but safety will also be enhanced by increasing the line of site and
removing some trees. There is only speculation on how much the speed will
increase. It will be a mistake to conclude that the speed will increase
significantly. Based on the booklet from the ICRC, it is an impossible task to
lower the speed limit to anything lower than what it is now.
Supervisor Obst stated that the point in the letter was that it is important to
recommend that lowering speed is not for vehicular safety. He’s looking at best
speed to maintain the character of life and safety of the area - Ag equipment,
pedestrians, bikers, etc. In light of these objectives, what is the best speed?
Needs more questions answered before a recommendation can be made.
Treasurer Nilsson moved that a decision be delayed until the March meeting to
allow time for questions to be answered by the ICRC. Seconded by Trustee Zaban
who believes a lot of information was conveyed at the public meeting that needs
to be considered before a decision be made. He thinks there should be a
detailed plan of what trees stay and which ones have to go.
Much discussion followed among members of the board and others attending the
meeting regarding landscape plans and stop signs. There was concern over giving
the go ahead for the project without first having a detailed landscape plan
from the ICRC. However, the viewpoint was also raised that the ICRC is not
going to spend the money to have such a plan developed before they have some
kind of OK from the township to go ahead with the project. It was generally
agreed that stop signs might be a good way to help control speed on Haslett
Road. Examples of where this seems to have worked were given, including the
recent 4 way stop at Putnam and Church in the City of Williamston. The issue
here would be to get the ICRC to go along with the stop signs and propose which
intersections would most benefit from them.
People were generally impressed with Dr. Morton, the Tree Expert the ICRC had
come to the public meeting on January 28, 1997. There was some belief that if
the ICRC continued to use the services of Dr. Morton, then the township could
have a more confident feeling that their landscaping concerns would be
addressed in a manner that would benefit the area.
There were also concerns about the line of sight along many areas of the road.
This is especially a problem when farm equipment is on the road. Treasurer
Nilsson also read statements from the Bus director for Williamston Schools and
the Williamston Post Master. Both of these people voiced concerns that their
employees do not feel safe performing their jobs along certain stretches of
Haslett Road. There are many places where there is nowhere to pull over and
where the busses’ flashers are not always seen in time.
Mrs. Jane Nico, a current bus driver for the school system, stated that many
roads in the district have no shoulders, or poor lines of vision where extra
precautions must be taken by the drivers to ensure safety. This is not an issue
particular to Haslett Road.
Discussion among the board members that they would like to re-word the motion
before the board. They want to see the project go forward, but they also want
to have their questions addressed satisfactorily. Treasurer Nilsson withdrew
her motion, the withdrawal was seconded by Trustee Zaban.
Further discussion followed on how best to word the motion so that the ICRC
would get the support from the township they were looking for while at the same
time ensuring that the remaining questions of the township are answered
satisfactorily.
Treasurer Nilsson moved that the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees
supports the Haslett Road improvements proposal and recommends the Ingham
County Road Commission work with a Township representative on speed, safety and
landscaping issues. The motion was seconded by Clerk Graham.
Supervisor Obst stated that he is interested in pursuing the proposal further,
but wants to work out these other issues first. He does not agree with the
motion as written and needs more assurances. He cannot support this motion.
Trustee Zaban stated that he thinks the ICRC can provide more detailed answers
on stop signs before a go a head is given.
Supervisor Obst called for a roll call vote:
   Ayes:      Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Clerk Graham
   Nayes:      Trustee Zaban, Supervisor Obst
The motion passed.

BURNING PERMIT - Chris Nilsson
Suggestion for an annual permit (calendar year). The township will keep the
information from the annual permit in a database and send a paper copy to the
resident so that they can have it with them when burning. In order to validate
the permit the resident would call the township and verify their parcel and
driver’s license numbers to receive an activation number that would be good for
up to three days, at that time we would call the fire department like we do
now. The Activation number would be given to the resident and the dispatcher.
We also see this as a good opportunity to promote fire safety with a copy of
the burning ordinance and/or a fire safety brochure being given out with the
annual permit. This will now go to the Williamston Community Fire Board for
their consideration and approval.
Mr. Bartels, who wrote the letter, is encouraged with the approach we are
taking here with the annual permit. The permit as designed was approved by the
board.

MARCH 4, 1997
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, March 4, 1997 at 7:35 PM. The Clerk was
asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Zaban, Trustee Wiegandt and Building
Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: New business: Salary
motion from budget meeting. Mrs. Hepfer entered a letter on the Haslett Road/
Secondary Commercial Network issue. An additional 4 applications (for a total
of 5) were received under the development rights resolution.
Reports:
FIRE BOARD REPORT - Harold Powell
Need to expand equipment and building. We currently cannot get the doors open
on one rig without hitting another one. Not up to date on things. There is an
increased need for emergency work. The Fire Board is considering possibly
buying a lot or two next to the current location; moving to a new, larger
location; or adding an additional location. Some of the larger new homes going
into the area require that the department obtain a ladder truck. The old
pumpers are getting old, it is almost impossible to get parts for them. The
fire board anticipates having an expansion plan in place in the next few
months. The funds would need to come from a millage. Each local government
serviced by the fire department would have to vote their own levy. The
expansion is just in the planning stage. The new ambulance is in service. One
of the older ambulances was involved in an accident, but it has been repaired.
We are now getting the 911 money from the County.
Burning permit concerns - chief and assistant chief do not like the year long
permit. Did not think it could be easily enforced. Trustee Wiegandt thought a
cooperative effort between the board and municipalities can make the process
more easily available to the public. He believes we can come up with a solution
that will please everyone. Trustee Wiegandt will work with Treasurer Nilsson to
fine tune the permit process. Trustee Zaban stated that the fire board only had
the one night to look at the permit proposal. He believes further discussion
will allow us to come up with something that is satisfactory to everyone.
ATTORNEY - Steve Schultz
Another busy month.
Ongoing discussion with the city to try to resolve the lawsuit. No success in
doing this. City requested that we sit down and negotiate. Question on what
would be discussed. Issue presented was annexation petition. Cannot get over
the issue on whether we have sewer capacity while saying we don't. City
proposed that we summarily dismiss the lawsuit and then they will sit down and
talk. City has attempted to correct their errors in violating the open meeting
act.
Clerk Graham stated that Dennis Irwin Stabenow called looking for a neutral
location for a meeting. Boundary commission declared the petition legally
sufficient. There will be a public hearing April 10, probably at one of the
schools. There is a list of 18 criteria the boundary commission must consider
to determine whether or not to approve the petition. Principal areas of
dispute: are sewer, water, and public vs. private roads.
Regarding the letter from Mr. Kendall on Haslett road and the width of the
easement; the case law that Attorney Schultz was asked to look at checked out.
The cases Mr. Kendall is relying upon are good cases that presume the easement
is 66 feet wide, but can be rebutted if the owner can prove there was a use in
place prior to the easement being accepted and that there was encroachment.
Property owner must establish the use, not the township. The Road Commission
will have to deal with this issue directly with the land owners - possibly to
condemn and take over the land.
Special assessments in sewer district number one - Mr. Bartig wanting to be
reimbursed for sewer taps that were never used and does not intend to use. Is
it advisable legally to pay back to folks some of the assessment levied to
build that line. No property right and no right to a refund for an assessment
district that was never used. No legal liability. There is case law that when
an assessment district was set up and folks not originally in the district paid
a hookup fee to tap into the district then there can be a refund to all those
assessed on a prorata basis, and not just those who hadn't used their taps.
This is permissible and legal. To just refund people who hadn't used their taps
is not. A prorata rebate to everyone would be allowed. Courts concerned with
abuse and have specific time lines for challenging an assessment. If they try
to challenge after the time line then the courts would be appearing to play
favorites. Only way to make a refund is to do it prorata once the time for
challenge has passed. We are not obligated to provide sewer at this time. No
property right that guarantees tying into the sewer. Property is improved by
having the line run through the property. Taps are available only on a first
come first serve basis. Assessment was not an assessment for capacity. It was
an assessment to have the pipe put in the ground. The assessment was for the
line and not for purchasing plant usage.
Proposed amendment to zoning ordinance regarding wireless communications and
land division in the sub division control ordinance based on legislation in
late 1996.
Hearing on city's motion before Judge Houk is March 12 at 1:30. Motion by the
city that we did not utilize the meeting clause before going further to sue in
breach of contract. The city is contending that because the township did not
officially declare that a given meeting was held specifically to fulfill the
legal obligation of the contract in all the meetings that were held over the
past two years between the two, that the lawsuit should be dismissed.
BUILDING REPORT - Walt Aven
There has been a slow down on new permit applications. More building is
currently being finished than started. Mr. Garcia has decided he may try to
salvage the original building after having removed the breezeway and other
little attachments that were added at less than code.
PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
Needs action on Sky Line outdoor advertising. Applied for a 233 square foot
billboard off premise sign on Betty Speaks’ Grand River property that is zoned
Light Industrial. The Planning Commission recommended denial of the billboard.
They determined it was not compatible to the residential areas to the west and
also not to the problems of that site to begin with. It does not meet the goals
of this township for a rural atmosphere. Also felt it was too close to the city
limits. A lot of discussion followed. There are currently negotiations for
someone to purchase the property from Mrs. Speaks. He would want to set up a
marine store to sell and fix boats.
Mr. Haskins from Sky Line plead their case before the board. They have looked
at the area for some time. He has clients that have requested sites for this
area. They felt they met all the guidelines set up in the zoning ordinance
that. They plan to do some landscaping and cleaning up of the area. They felt
they were doing the right thing. The sign would be visible from both
directions. They would take the ash trees out at the property owners request
and then put in suitable landscaping. They were going to put in an I-Beam
structure, but have agreed to put in a pole structure which is more expensive
and more attractive.
Sky Line believes this is the only location in the township which meets all the
criteria for off-premise signs. It is not a huge billboard - the guidelines
specify a maximum of 300 square feet. They are proposing a sign that is less
than 250 sq. ft. The ordinance says that signs "shall be allowed" in the light
industrial zone. They would be removing two non-conforming signs from the
premises and feel they will be improving the overall look of the site. There
was a public hearing on the application - no one showed to speak against the
issue. McKenna and Associates recommended approval based on certain criteria
which they believe their proposal meets. The sign would not be illuminated and
trees would be cut down on the west property line and be replaced with a stand
of white pine trees closer to the road. McKenna agreed to the sign and the
location of it with conditions. The sign would provide opportunity for local
businesses to advertise. It would not be a detriment to the area. Sky Line has
numerous signs throughout the Lansing area that are bought in packages. The
sign would be an affordable means for local people to advertise. Mrs. VanDoozen
submitted an objection, but she has put up two new billboards in the area
herself since writing the letter.
Building Inspector Aven needs clarification on whether or not the billboard is
considered a free standing sign since only one free standing sign is allowed
per site. An on premise free standing sign must be 100 feet away from an off
premise sign. Further clarification on this issue is still needed.
If the property is sold and the new owners request rezoning the sign will
become a legal non-conforming use. The lease would transfer to the new owners
of the property.
Board discussion on wanting to clean up what is already a trashy looking site.
Some opinion that billboards would not improve the look of the area; that the
site is too close to the city limits; that billboards do not tie into the
master plan of the township; and that there would be people protesting the sign
once it was up..
A review of the permit process was requested of Planner Martin. The zoning is
correct, but only with a special use permit. Special Use Permit process - take
information in, hold public hearing, hold meeting on recommending or denying
the permit - go through the nine criteria and answer them according to the
special use permit. This was all done. Questions on who Sky Line’s clients are
- MSU, PHP, Roof Top Landing, CATA, MADD, Schools, Circus, Capitol Cadillac,
etc.
Motion by Trustee Wiegandt that we table the decision for thirty days until
questions of ownership change are cleared up and to see if the new owner would
like to go forward with the process. Seconded by Treasurer Nilsson. Motion
passed. The thirty days will also be used to respond to questions of
interpretation of the free standing sign part of the zoning ordinance.
Zoning amendment change to allow 15 acre Ag-Small Farm parcels to split off a 5
acre parcel if lot size requirements are met. The Planning Commission
recommends denial because of the new state ordinance which now allows splits on
parcels that have been previously split without waiting another 10 years. This
change would currently affect 14 parcels. Commission believes they would be in
effect granting special uses for these parcels. Negates the Purpose of the Ag
Small Farm Zone.
Discussion followed about a need for these splits to happen. Concerns from the
Planning Commission that there would be a domino effect in allowing these
splits. There would not be a domino effect because parcels divided must have
been in existence at the time that the provision was adopted. Wording of the
proposed ordinance has been changed to make it clearer. It now reads:
Any parcel in the AG-SF district may be divided to create one (1) new parcel
that may be as small as five (5) acres in size, provided that all of the
following criteria are met:
·The parcel being divided must have been in existence at the time of adoption
of this provision, must not have been split from another parcel during the
preceding ten (10) year period, must be at least fifteen (15) acres in size,
and must have at least two (2) adjoining parcels that are five (5) acres in
size or smaller.
·Aside from the parcel that is smaller than 10 acres, all other resulting
parcels shall be at least ten (10) acres in size.
·All resulting parcels shall comply with all applicable requirements of the
Zoning and Land Division Ordinance, including lot width and setback
requirements, except that the parcel that is smaller than 10 acres need not
comply with minimum lot size standards.
Lots legally created pursuant to these requirements shall be considered
conforming with respect to minimum lot size.
Clerk Graham moved that the new wording of the proposed ordinance be sent back
to the Planning Commission for review and comments. Seconded by Trustee
Wiegandt. Motion passed. Another public hearing is not required.
Question on Williamstown estates - we should have a new flood plain map
shortly. Can make paying of legal fees required before going further with any
other permits. If dropped, then legal fees will be attached to the tax bill.
Mrs. Stillwell property - returned signed application to be rezoned to AG-SF to
conform to the area.
Mr. Spagnuolo has filed a special use permit. They are going forward with the
offices. He needs a building permit before he starts remodeling the office
area. The new restaurant will be more of a sports bar. It will have pool
tables, arcade games, a big screen TV, etc. The Ingham County Road Commission
needs a site plan as well from him.
Mr. Hubbell needs two plans. He has not submitted a second plan, so we cannot
proceed further until we hear from him. We have not heard from him since the
letter of Feb. 14, 1997 was sent.

ASSESSOR'S REPORT
Meeting Wednesday, March 5th with 2 members of the Board of Review. This is the
first year township is doing the tax and assessment programs on their own.
Certain municipalities have property owners meet with the assessor prior to the
Board of Review to reduce the load on the Board. This procedure has been OK’d
by the Township Board of Trustees if the Assessor can schedule the meetings.
Taxable value now appears before assessed value on the assessment sheets. This
should make the forms easier to read.
A suggestion was made that the newsletter for February, 1998 include an article
to assist in answering questions on when the SEV goes up, why does it go up.
Property sales in the immediate neighborhood have a strong impact on this.
Sales uncap property, so they are the main reason for heavy increases in the
assessment to keep them consistent with property values.
Mr. Powell had a question on assessments for land that has sold the development
rights. Supervisor Obst did not believe the sale of development rights would
not have an impact on the assessment, but would have to research the question
further. Mr. Obst thought it might be possible that assessments on this type of
land could go down because they no longer have the development potential
figured in.

HASLETT ROAD AND THE SECONDARY COMMERCIAL NETWORK -
Haslett Road improvements are to be paid by category D funds, if they are not
on the secondary network, they will no longer be eligible for category D funds.
The Board needs clarification on what differences exist (if any) between all
season roads and the secondary commercial network. There were also concerns
voiced of ever having Haslett road paved if we don't do it now. All season
roads can have truck traffic now. The Perry exit off of I-69 at M-52 is the
primary truck route to I-96. Haslett has been an all season road since 1979.
Classification is not changing on Haslett road. May see an increase up to
Shoeman road now that I-69 is finished. Truckers don't want to use roads such
as Haslett, they want to stay on the expressway as much as possible. The title
is new, but the use is the same. Mr. D'Alcorn's letter states that these roads
are all season roads that act as collectors for the major highway routes.
Trustee Wiegandt stated that the use of the road will not change they are just
changing the name to continue to qualify for the category D funding. The
Michigan Department Of Transportation (MDOT) has mandated this designation.
Discussion among the board about how involved the Township needs to be in the
planning of the road improvements.
Letter read into the record by Mrs. Hepfer --- Because the silent majority
isn’t here tonight, I would like to speak for them. I hope the Township Board
will vote in the affirmative to have Haslett, Meridian, Williamston and Shoeman
Roads be considered Secondary Commercial Network roads because the Ingham
County Road Commission budget funding is dependent on that approval.
As I understand it, if Haslett Road is not part of that network then the other
three roads cannot be either. These township roads will only be maintained and
will not be improved because there will not be any funding for that.
Haslett Road has not had any major improvement since the early fifties and its
condition has deteriorated to the point that it cannot be easily fixed. Please
give your approval so that these roads are Secondary Commercial Network roads
and that the Haslett Road Improvement Project can go forward. -Emma Hepfer,
March 4, 1997.
After much discussion among the board members it was decided that the county
did not need the township’s approval to go ahead with the project. They were
only looking for our consent to further good will among the various government
entities. It was decided that Treasurer Nilsson would draft a letter to Mr.
D’Alcorn of the road commission stating that after much discussion the township
has agreed to the 4 Township Roads inclusion in the Secondary Commercial
Network as proposed by the County Road Commission.

PUBLIC COMMENTS:
Bench Mark Project - Wendy Pincumbe
Miss Pincumbe would like to see the speed limit on Mitchell Rd lowered to 35
miles per hour from the current 45 miles per hour. She submitted a petition
signed by her neighbors to the Board. She received some of her information from
Officer Howard Dahlstrom of the Williamston Police Department (also Constable
of the Township). He was aware of two attempts to lower the speed limit - the
first one was successful in lowering it to 45 from 55, the other attempt to
lower the speed to 35 was not. Miss Pincumbe’s main concern is the high school
students leaving the school on Mitchell driving towards Williamston Road
traveling too fast. This poses a dangerous situation for the people who live in
the area who might be walking or biking along this stretch of the road,
especially students walking to and from school.
Clerk Graham moved that the petition and Miss Pincumbe’s research be forwarded
to the Ingham County Road Commission and our County Commissioner, Randy
Schaefer with a vote of approval from the Board. Seconded by Treasurer Nilsson.
Comment by Trustee Zaban that the board is highly in favor of Miss Pincumbe’s
petition. Motion passed unanimously. Brian Jennings, from the Transportation
and Communications Committee will also be contacting Miss Pincumbe to further
enlist her help in seeing this speed limit dropped.

Submitted a proposal for landscaping the North West side of the township hall.
Two plans were submitted that will include low maintenance, low growing shrubs.
The first plan will also put some plants in the front of the building. Price
estimate is included in the plans. If the plants are ordered through the
nursery instead of the catalog then the plants would be available when needed
for planting. He also has a cost estimate for 3 gallon plants that would be a
little cheaper than the local nursery, Christians.
Clerk Graham informed Mr. Laumer that Mr. Hayes also has a nursery that might
be more reasonable than others. The mowing company used by the Township would
pull out the older shrubs that are dying. Other scouts would be included in the
project so that Mr. Laumer can demonstrate his leadership skills. He should
have approval for the project from the Scouting Council within a month.
Clerk Graham is in favor of the more extensive plan, so is Treasurer Nilsson.
Cottage Gardens is the wholesaler that has the 3 gallon plants. Trustee
Wiegandt motioned we go with the more extensive plan. Treasurer Nilsson

Secondary Commercial Truck Route Issue - John Taylor, 1533 Corkwood Trail
Mr. Taylor would like the Board to revisit the Secondary Commercial Truck
Routes proposed by the Ingham County Road Commission and rescind their approval
of the Township roads that are included on the list. He is especially concerned
about Williamston and Haslett Roads. The Tri-County Regional Planning
Commission is voting on this issue on May 6th and Mr. Taylor would like the
Township to rescind their approval before that time. Mr. Taylor is concerned
that inclusion in the network would mean increased truck traffic on these roads
and that they may be added to the commercial operators county map, which would
encourage trucks to use these roads. Mr. Taylor realizes the Township has no
formal approval in the matter but he believes their vote could have an
influence on the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission. Mr. Taylor’s letter
was submitted to the Board. The Board will revisit this issue later in the
meeting.

ATTORNEY'S REPORT - Stephen Schultz
Reviewed the new subdivision ordinance and land division ordinance and also the
opinion by McKenna and Associates with regards to the landing strip
regulations.
Freedom Of Information Act Requests: Regarding a request for certain documents
by Attorney Lett. The documents were provided within 5 days of his request.
There was no statement in the cover letter that if he disagreed he had certain
rights under the freedom of information act. This type of response is required
under the freedom of information act even if 100% of the information that was
requested was given. Attorney Schultz would be happy to provide standard text
for these types of responses in order to be sure that nothing happens
incorrectly. All requests for documents, whether they are written or verbal,
even if they don’t state that they are a freedom of information act request,
need the standard text included in the response.
Litigation With The City: Agreed to a meeting with the City on April 16 where
each side will lay out their concerns. The City has proposed the meeting be
held at the City Hall Annex in order to avoid a room charge. We have an
agreement on the content of the meeting. The structure of the meeting with the
City will be a presentation by the Supervisor and the Township’s Attorney; the
City Manager and the City’s Attorney; and then open discussion. This is an
informational meeting only - there will be no deliberations and no decisions
will be made. The purpose of the meeting is for the two sides to come together
and figure out where the other side really stands on the issues so that
negotiations will be more beneficial. No minutes will be taken. The meeting is
for everyone to find out where each side is coming from. There was more than a
mild suggestion from the judge that this meeting take place.
By the 15th of April the Township must advise the City who our expert witnesses
are going to be. They have to let us know who theirs are by April 29th. On May
19th there will be a status conference with the judge. We are set to go into
mediation on August 22. Mediation consists of 3 attorneys, one from the
plaintiff side of the bar, one from the defense side of the bar and one
neutral. If the results of mediation are not acceptable to one side or the
other, then going back to court at that time would be a more expensive
proposition.
The Boundary Commission Will Hold A Public Hearing April 10 At 4:00 PM
regarding the annexation request on the west side of town. Attorney Schultz
would invite and encourage anyone who wants to attend to please be there. It is
important for the boundary commission to see how important an issue this is for
the township. The order of the proceeding is as follows: hear from the
petitioner, the city, the township and then anyone else who has any comments.
This meeting will be held at the Community Center.
Treasurer Nilsson questioned the fact that Joe Cox, the City of Williamston’s
Attorney, is on the Boundary Commission. This is correct. Mr. Cox will not be
serving on the panel - there is a conflict of interest here. 5 members are
assigned to each case. There are 3 permanent members appointed by the governor
who hear every case. Each county has two members who are appointed by the
senior probate judge in that county. The three state commissioners do a good
job of maintaining their independence and attempts to remain neutral. None of
them has a discernible pattern of voting. There is a 30 day period for
submission of written materials after the hearing, and a 15 day period to
respond to the written materials. There will then be a judicated session where
they will gather all the materials and discuss them. At that time they will
decide on their findings and it will be at the next meeting before they approve
their findings. Once the Boundary Commission makes its decision it is difficult
to have it overturned in court.

Zoning Ordinance Text Amendment Of The Ag-SF Lot Splits. Changed the wording.
The proposed amendment now reads:
Any parcel in the AG-SF district may be divided to create one (1) new parcel
that may be smaller than ten (10) acres but not less than five (5) acres in
size, provided that all of the following criteria are met:
·The parcel being divided must have been in existence at the time of the
adoption of this provision, must not have been split from another parcel during
the preceding ten (10) year period, must be at least fifteen (15) acres in
size, and must have at least two (2) adjoining parcels that are five (5) acres
in size or smaller.
·Aside from the parcel that is smaller than ten (10) acres, all other resulting
parcels shall be at least ten (10) acres in size.
·All resulting parcels shall comply with all applicable requirements of the
Zoning and Land Division Ordinance, including lot width and setback
requirements, except that the parcel that is smaller than ten (10) acres need
not comply with minimum lot size standards.
Lots legally created pursuant to these requirements shall be considered
conforming with respect to minimum lot size.
The provision should be placed in two sections of the ordinance:
·Section 15.03, sub-section B, as a footnote to the 10-acre Minimum Lot Area
standard.
·Section 26.02, Schedule of Regulations, as a footnote to the 10-acre minimum
lot size standard in the AG-SF district.
Trustee Wiegandt moved that the Zoning Ordinance be amended to include the
above provision in the specified locations.. Supported by Trustee Zaban.
Supervisor Obst called for a Roll Call Vote:
Ayes:   Trustee Zaban, Treasurer Nilsson, Supervisor Obst, Clerk Graham,
Trustee Wiegandt
Nayes:   None

MAY 6, 1997
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday May 6, 1997 at 7:34 PM. The Clerk was
asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt and Trustee Zaban. Building
Inspector Aven was excused.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: Old Business - Cherry-
Valle subdivision and Skyline Billboard Request. New Business - Tom Hamlin
Request.
TOM HAMLIN REQUEST - Public was told that Mr. Hamlin asserted that our Zoning
Ordinance was unconstitutional and that the Township’s Attorney was planning to
respond tonight, at the Board of Trustees meeting because the Board of Appeals
does not have the authority to act on this request. Mr. Hamlin would like to
rent a house to 4 unrelated graduate students in a subdivision that is zoned
for single family residences. The definition of a family according to the
Williamstown Township Zoning Ordinance is as follows:
1.   A domestic family, that is, one or more persons living together and
related by the bonds of consanguinity (blood), marriage, or adoption, together
with servants of the principal occupants and not more than one additional
unrelated person, with all of such individuals being domiciled together as a
single, domestic, housekeeping unit in a dwelling.
2.   The functional equivalent of the domestic family, that is, persons living
together in a dwelling unit whose relationship is of a permanent and distinct
character and is the functional equivalent of a domestic family with a
demonstrable and recognizable bond which constitutes the functional equivalent
of the bonds which render the domestic family a cohesive unit. All persons of
the functional equivalent of the domestic family must be cooking and otherwise
housekeeping as a single, nonprofit unit. ...
Refer to page 1-13 of the Williamstown Township Zoning Ordinance for the
complete definition. Mr. Hamlin’s request states that the Zoning Ordinance is
not constitutional and that it discriminates. Mr. Hamlin had no comment other
than what is already stated in his letter to the board.
The Township also received comments and letters from people in the neighborhood
defending the ordinance as written. Supervisor Obst deferred to Attorney
Schultz. Mr. Schultz looked at the Township ordinance with respect to the
definition of family and if there is any new case law on this issue. Most cases
challenge ordinances that state specific numbers. Those have been stricken. The
Court has laid down some guidelines. There is no case law in this state and
only one odd one in another state that would show that our definition is
improper or unenforceable. There is case law looking at our definition that has
been sustained or found valid. Would enforcing the ordinance be discriminatory
under the Elliott-Larson civil rights act as stated in Mr. Hamlin’s letter?
There is nothing in this ordinance that forces a landowner to violate the
Elliott-Larson civil rights act. The requirement that the residents must be a
family does not require anyone to discriminate against anyone. It only means
that the people living there must live as a family - traditional or non-
traditional, nothing more and nothing less. The requirement does not
discriminate against various types of familial status, just that they must be
living together as a family. Attorney Schultz is comfortable with the ordinance
and that it is a fact specific issue. If they are living as a family, then they
are OK.
The following residents of Red Cedar Manor Subdivision voiced their opposition
to the property in question being rented to a group of 4 unrelated graduate
students: Clay Bradon, Don & Karen Bouffard, Ed & Sharon Carter, Veronica
Matejko, Alexis Smith, Marirose Carrillo, Vickie Selinger and John McLaughlin.
Other citizens voicing statements were Nancy Fink and Michael Musser. Concerns
stated were negative effects on property values, changing the character of the
neighborhood, negative impact on quality of life in the neighborhood. Opinion
was that the current pricing structure on the rental would be a deterrent to
most families and that it encouraged the type of group rental that is
undesirable and illegal in this neighborhood. There were also concerns about
how the residents would be notified if there were any further Township meetings
that addressed this issue. Supervisor Obst advised them that they would receive
written notification by mail if there were any further developments regarding
this issue.
Mr. Hamlin stated that he has lived in this community for 10 years, and he has
coached many kids in the community. He is not trying to do anything against the
law. He does rent to college students, but he is very particular about the
college students he rents to. The four that are interested in this property are
very responsible graduate students, who have passed vigorous qualifications and
will be in the area for 6-8 years. Mr. Hamlin stated that he has never had this
problem before in any of the other communities where he owns rental property.
The residents of Red Cedar Manor submitted a petition to the Township Board
should any further action be required in this matter.
SKYLINE BILLBOARD ISSUE - Mr. Rick Imshaug, owner of Skyline Advertising.
The Township Board tabled this issue in the past due to some concern that the
owner of the property did not want to go forward with the application. The
Board received a letter from Mrs. Speaks today. It stated that she does not
favor the sign but does not want to withdraw her name from the application due
to possible legal action against her from Skyline. There was a recommendation
from the Planning Commission to deny the sign dated Feb. 27, 1997. The motion
passed, but not unanimously. Treasurer Nilsson motioned that the Township Board
deny the Special Land Use Permit for the sign from Skyline Advertising on the
1476 E Grand River property. Seconded by Trustee Zaban. Discussion: Heard back
from Mrs. Speaks that she does not want the sign because she is still in the
midst of negotiations for selling the property. Nothing has been finalized yet.
Trustee Wiegandt stated that it was a problem of looking into the future to
determine what somebody else may or may not want.
Michael Musser stated that he is the individual who is in negotiations with
Mrs. Speaks to buy the property in question. He would like the sign to be
denied. The sign has no significance with what he plans to do with the parcel.
Negotiations will not be finalized until early winter. He has a five year plan
that he has discussed with the Planning Commission. Will get a copy to the
board. The plan does not include this type of sign on the property. Mr. Musser
is concerned that the sign will not permit any use by any organization within
the community. Only paid advertisers of Skyline will be allowed to use the
sign. Believes the sign would be unattractive and not an asset to the community
and that it would detract from his business.
Mr. Imshaug stated that the proposed sign meets all the guidelines of the rules
and is actually well within the boundaries. The matter was referred to McKenna
and Associates. Skyline has exceeded the recommendations set by McKenna for
approval. We have submitted letters from businesses in the community. Dozens of
local charities use Skyline’s billboards at no charge. If the sign is denied at
this location then it appears the township is saying that they do not allow
billboards in this township.
Trustee Zaban stated that there are similar signs in the township further west
on Grand River. He doesn't feel the proposed sign meets all the criteria
because the piece of land to the west is not commercial, but residential. Mr.
Imshaug stated that the ordinance does not say anything about what zoning can
be adjacent.
Attorney Schultz - point of information - either incorporate the reasons set
forth by the Planning Commission or state some findings about why the motion is
opposed. When he reviewed the lease he found the legal description of the
property to be leased is defective. The lease states that the property to be
leased is the west property line, there is no width mentioned, just the line.
Attorney Schultz is not sure if we granted the special use permit, what
property is to be included in the lease - there is no width to the parcel.
Trustee Zaban moves that the original motion be amended to include the findings
of fact from the Planning Commission dated Feb. 27, 1997 denying the Special
Land Use Permit, the letter from Mrs. Speaks dated May 6th, and the defect in
the lease that does not specify the width of land to be rented. Motion has been
amended. Supervisor Obst is concerned about residential uses to the west, the
fact that Mrs. Speaks does not feel it is in her interest to have the sign, and
the fact that there appears to be a legal defect in the lease. Motion passed
unanimously.
Nancy Fink - Special Use Permit to be used at the discretion of the board. Have
to look at each case because of having various different zonings next to each
other. Should be evaluated on a one by one basis for this purpose.
FIRE BOARD REPORT - Walter Keilholtz
Submitted to the board. Question from Attorney Schultz regarding the width of
streets and turning radiuses in Riverwood. If they are city streets then they
are not bound by the Ingham County Road Commission’s guidelines. This is a
concern from a public safety point of view and also an annexation point of
view. All roads in Williamstown Township must meet the County’s guidelines for
width and turning radiuses. Mr. Keilholtz stated that the Fire Board does not
have regulations on this, nor the authority to impose any. Trustee Wiegandt
stated that they were private roads when the development was built so they do
not come under the guidelines of the Ingham County Road Commission The Fire
Department will go down the roads as far as they can with their trucks and then
go the rest of the way by foot.
Mickey Martin asked Trustee Wiegandt if two cars were parked along the side of
the street across from each other in the City’s Riverwood Development, could
the fire vehicles get through? The answer was no, they could not.
Attorney Schultz - County road standards are sufficient in the Township, but in
the City where they are not county roads, whether the annexation is approved or
not, the Fire Board ought to have regulations that require the roads to meet
the guidelines. Trustee Wiegandt - The Fire Board does not have this authority.
It must be the City that accepts these standards for public safety reasons. If

ADVISORY COUNCIL - Chuck Cleland
The original purpose of the council was that the Board wanted to reorganize the
Township government on a committee structure. Committees were very large, there
were many of them and most of them never met. We tried to reorganize the
structure into 5 standing committees. Most of these committees still don't
work. Two work well and one special committee - the park committee - works
well. Most of the participation by citizens is driven by issues that hit home
to them. We have not made good progress in getting the committees to function
well.
One option is to proceed as usual.
Option 2 - Do we need the standing committees? Is it sufficient just to have an
agricultural person or a transportation person on the council and then when
necessary to appoint special committees when a need arises? Advisory Council
suggests going with option 2.
Problem 2 is how the Advisory Council itself is working. The Council does not
think that it is working well. If the Council hasn't provided the Board with
good information and advice then we need to fix the relationship between the
Council and the Board. The Council has in the past just operated on Supervisor
Obst’s advice to them. No formal mission statement, or agreement from the Board
on how the Board should work with the Advisory Council was ever established. We
need better communication between the Board and the Council. There should be a
Board member attending Advisory Council meetings. This would further the
discussions. What issues does the Board want the Council to study? We believe
the Council would be better used to study long term complex issues: e.g.,
inter-governmental affairs, long term open space, long term agricultural
problems, etc. Also specialized problems in the township where a specialist in
the township could be utilized. It is preferable that the Advisory Council
provide advice to the board in the form of alternate choices and perceived
impacts. They are willing to make some of those long term predictions and put
them in the frame work of alternate choices. Reorganization has had some
successes, but also many failures. We need to do some fine tuning to make the
advisory council work better. Clerk Graham stated that she would like 30 days
to think about the issue.
The Council’s understanding of their role is that many issues could be referred
to them without the Board thinking them out during public meetings. Is this
something that the board will find useful? Chuck Cleland should be the
interface between the various committees and the Board.
Treasurer Nilsson sees the Council as very beneficial. She likes the idea of
reorganization and would volunteer to be the Board representative on the
Advisory Council.
Supervisor Obst had a little more in mind with regard to a mission statement
for the Council. The Township is constantly running into problems that it
wasn't prepared for or hadn't foreseen. He would like the Council to also work
on anticipating problems before they happen and not just be reactionary. This
would take a lot of research on the council’s part.
Mr. Cleland stated that If we are going to ask people to do this then there has
to be some feedback. Need to develop a rapport between the Council and the
Board so that the people on the Council feel that their information is
prioritized against other information coming in - that their research efforts
are recognized and weighed in as a factor when considering their
recommendations.
Treasurer Nilsson suggested having a regular spot on the Board’s agenda for
collecting issues to be studied by the Advisory Council.
Mr. Cleland stated that the Council needs some affirmation that the board
subscribes to this procedure. If their advice is not taken that is fine, but
let the Council know what other considerations were taken by the board when
their decision was made.
