ADVISORY COUNCIL - Rutgar Hoag
The Advisory Council’s Proposed Statement Of Purpose:
Williamstown Township Advisory Council Statement of Purpose
The purpose of the Williamstown Township Advisory Council is to provide advice
to the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees and to coordinate citizen
participation in Township affairs. The Advisory Council will, at the suggestion
of the Township Board or by its own initiative with the consent of the Township
Board, undertake the study of problems which may affect the long term health,
safety and welfare of Township residents. These problems may be those which
concern individuals, neighborhoods or the Township community as a whole.
In its regular course the Advisory Council, through its committee system, will
collect and analyze information to present to the Township Board. The Council’s
advice will be in the form of possible courses of action including an
assessment of the probable impacts of alternative decisions.
From time to time the Advisory Council will advise the Township Board on the
appointment of citizen volunteers to various Township Committees.
Treasurer Nilsson moved to accept the statement of purpose as submitted by the
Advisory Council. Supported by Trustee Wiegandt. Motion passed unanimously.
Transportation and Communications Committee - Suggestion to appoint Mr. Brian
Jennings as the acting chair of the Transportation and Communications Committee
and to appoint Mr. Jim Ballard to the committee. Treasurer Nilsson moved that
Brian Jennings be approved as acting chair of the Transportation and
Communications Committee; supported by Trustee Wiegandt. Approved unanimously.
Trustee Nilsson moved to appoint Mr. Ballard to the Transportation and
Communications Committee; supported by Trustee Wiegandt. Motion approved
unanimously.
Open Land Committee - The Advisory Council would like to request that the
Township Board appoint a committee to study the future of open land in the
Township. Proposed committee members are Dan Kraft (Chair), Ger Schultink,
Nancy Fink, Dwight Kampe, Chuck Cleland, Jerry Eidt, Mickey Martin and George
Petrides. The first meeting will be June 11. Mickey Martin estimates the
committee will meet for 9-12 months. Nancy Fink thinks it will possibly be less
based on the information already accumulated. Mr. Kraft will be delegating
different areas to different people; he will not be doing all the research
himself. There will be a member of the Advisory Council at the Board meetings
every month to keep the Board up to date on this and the other Committees'
activities. Committees will be abolished once they have achieved their purpose,
with the exception of a few Committees who would have ongoing responsibilities,
such as the Transportation and Communications Committee.
The Open Land Committee would be concerned with the following tasks:
1.   Conduct a survey to find out what is meant by the term “rural atmosphere”,
the degree to which open space is valued, what kinds of open spaces are desired
and what citizens are willing to sacrifice for “rural atmosphere” and open
space. The survey would also find out if citizens are willing to financially
support the acquisition of open space.
2.   Explore the various reasons for preserving open spaces such as ground
water recharge, conservation easements for the preservation of natural habitat,
recreation uses, preservation of farmland and other commercial uses of open
space, as well as the containment of residential development.
3.   Update the Township Master Plan in regard to open space by reviewing the
location and amount of existing open space and suggesting what portion of this
space should be preserved, for what purpose and how it would be maintained.
4.   Suggest the mechanisms for the preservation of open land such as
conservation and farm land trusts, purchasing of development rights and
associated issues. Among the latter are the ordinances, holding foundations and
funding which are necessary to maintain open space.
5.   As a result of this study the Advisory Council would from time to time
suggest various actions by the Township Board which would promote the
preservation of open space in the Township.
6.   Inventory if the current open space in the Township.
7.   Estimate of build up potential of open spaces.
8.   Soil analysis of current open spaces in the Township.
Treasurer Nilsson suggested that it would be a benefit to the community to make
educational efforts through the Township Newsletter, The Lansing State Journal
and the Enterprise to define the items that this committee would be
considering, different zoning methods, etc. Nancy Fink would like to see an
article in the next newsletter defining Local Easement Open Space and how it
might benefit our community. The committee will not need funding at this point.
If a survey is to be included in the newsletter, it will need to be to the
editors by mid July. Treasurer Nilsson moved to create an Open Land Committee
to study open land issues as listed above and to appoint the people suggested
by the Advisory Council to said committee. Supported by Trustee Wiegandt. The
motion was approved unanimously.

action.

ASSESSORS REPORT - Norm Obst
The State Department of Treasury has identified 50,000 parcels where the
homestead exemption claim made by the owner has been rescinded by the owner
because they have moved or because the use of their property has changed. A
valid form must be submitted by the property owner. If these properties do not
have a homestead affidavit claim from the new owner (or are agricultural
property), the treasurer in possession of the tax roll (at this time that is
the County) will have to generate a bill for additional non-homestead taxes
due. There are approximately 50 parcels in this township that the State has
identified. Assessor Obst sent letters to the property owners involved in an
attempt to get the situation cleared up before a tax bill is sent. There has
been a lot of concerned response to date.
Zoning Board Of Appeals (ZBA) - Norm Obst
There are strong differences of opinion among Board members on how the they
should carry out their duty. Norm Obst wrote a letter to the Board of Trustees
and the Planning Commission asking for clarification on what the ZBA has the
authority to do. The Zoning Ordinance, in Supervisor Obst’s view, states two
different standards for allowing the ZBA to grant requested “non-use”
variances:
1.   ...by varying or modifying any of its rules or provisions so that the
spirit of this Ordinance is observed, public safety secured and substantial
justice done.
2.   ...only upon a finding that practical difficulties exist.
There is confusion among the Board of Appeals members as to whether both
standards need to be met before granting a variance, or if only one of them
needs to be met. Mr. Obst would like the Planning Commission to take a look at
this and provide some direction to the ZBA. Clerk Graham requested 60 days to
study the issue - Supervisor Obst suggested that even 90 days may be more
appropriate. The ZBA description was changed between the old Zoning Ordinance
and the New One, that is why this issue has come up at this time.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Haslett Rd, Meridian Rd And The Proposed Secondary Commercial Network
Several citizens voiced concerns that the Ingham County Road Commission (ICRC)
had misled them and/or the Township Officials in regard to what construction
will actually be done on Haslett Road and funding of roads that are designated
as part of the State’s Secondary Commercial Network (SCN). They were Dr. Terry
Braden, Mr. David Doyle, Mr. David Nico, and Mr. Robert Kendall, Jr.
Concerns voiced were:
·One of the main objectives of the ICRC was to make Haslett a safer road to
travel. Belief was that taking out the hills would make the road faster, and
therefore not necessarily safer.
·Residents of Haslett Road were led to believe that construction was going to
be more minor than what they are now hearing will be done, especially with
Haslett being on the list of roads for the proposed SCN.
·Residents being told at the Tri-County Planning Commission that there was no
funding connected to a road being designated part of the SCN and the Township
having been told that roads not on the SCN will not be eligible for category D
funds from the State.
·Concerns over trees to be removed. ICRC taking property without condemnation
or compensation to the property owners. Belief that the ICRC is not necessarily
acting in an ethical manner. Request that the Township officials must document
and follow up on all issues to make sure the Board’s considerations are taken
care of.
Walt Aven, who lives on Haslett Road related his latest experience that
demonstrates a very serious safety issue with the current condition of the
road. Most recently he and his wife were traveling on the road and when they
came over the top of a hill there were two cars headed straight for them, one
in each lane. He swerved to miss the oncoming car and missed it by only a
couple of inches because he didn’t have far to swerve before he would have
landed in a ditch or hit a tree. He has also witnessed two fatal accidents in
front of his house on Haslett Road.
Concern About The Gun Club - Larry Hughes, 4292 Dobie Road
Mr. Hughes’ property backs up to the Gun Club. His children have told him about
shots being fired in the trees over their heads on several occasions while they
were playing at the back of their own property. On Saturday, April 26, 1997 Mr.
Hughes personally experienced this situation himself. He went over to the Gun
Club to check out the situation and found two cars there: a Ford with license
plate number XP9 943 with three kids between the ages of 14 and 19 shooting
pistols; and a Chevy with license plate number FAY 681 driven by two men who
said that they were leaving. Mr. Hughes suspects the shots on his property came
from the kids, but he has no proof one way or the other. He is concerned for
his family's safety. People who use the Gun Club need to be careful about where
they shoot. At the east Mr. Hughes’ property is higher than the Rifle Club's
property. This was not an isolated incident. His children have reported several
other times where they had a similar experience on their own property. His son
had it happen to him on April 2, 1997 at about 4:30. The Board agrees that this
is a very serious situation and they will follow up with the Gun Club.

Park Surveys - Mickey Martin
As of June 2nd, 95 park surveys had been received by the Township. More were
received today. This is approximately 6% of the total number of surveys that
were sent with the Spring Newsletter. The national average for direct mail
surveys is only 3-4%. Based on this, the Park Committee is very happy with the
response.
The preliminary results so far are between 80 and 90 % positive toward the
park. 3 that are totally unhappy about the park - upset that the Township
bought the property. 75% were willing to support it financially. The responses
are more in favor of non-sporting uses for the park - picnics, family reunions,
canoeing, having an open area there. Least was for sporting activities. A
variety of age groups and family situations responded.

Larkin Country Side Acres - Tentative Preliminary Plat approval. The Planning
Commission recommends approval with conditions as stated in the minutes of the
July 17, 1997 Planning Commission Meeting. Commissioner Kraft mentioned a
situation where a basement could not be dug on a lot due to groundwater
problems and thought this was another site where such a problem could occur
because of the poor soils. Attorney Skilton did not think that the ruling in
that case would be applicable here. She stated that due to the Governmental
Immunity Rule the Township would not be liable in such a case, only the
developer would be liable. Additional trees may need to be planted along the
rail road tracks. That area is fairly densely populated with plants already.
This was a concern of Supervisor Obst. Planner Martin stated that it was early
in the process, and further discussion of this type of concern would be
appropriate in future stages of the process. This is the Tentative Preliminary
Plat. Those types of issues will come up for discussion in the Planning
Commission before approval of the Preliminary Plat. At this time we are just
looking for approval of the basic layout of the subdivision. Clerk Graham moved
that the Township Board grant approval for the Tentative Preliminary Plat with
the 5 conditions specified by the Planning Commission in their minutes of June
17, 1997. Supported by Trustee Zaban. Question from the Board on the reasons
behind Planning Commissioner’s Fink dissenting vote. Commissioner Fink stated
her vote was because the zoning was not recommended by the Planning Commission
and she still does not believe that the subdivision should be approved at this
density. Motion passed unanimously.
Steeplechase - Formerly Mr. Bruner's property on Zimmer Rd. The Planning
Commission recommends Tentative Preliminary Plat approval with conditions as
stated in the Planning Commission Meeting minutes of June 17, 1997. The lots
are clustered on a smaller area with 50% open space. Detailed landscaping has
to be submitted before Final Preliminary Plat approval. Ownership name on the
plat has to be corrected. Approval subject to the necessary agencies.
Clarification of the lot layout and where there would be problems with on site
water disposal. The water map and the lot layout map show slightly different
areas, so it is misleading in that some of the lots appear to be in the
unbuildable area. Differences were clarified. Also strongly supported that a
deceleration lane not be put in - people would tend to use it (illegally) as a
passing lane. Street Lighting not recommended for this subdivision. There will
be a Homeowners Association with very restrictive covenants, particularly
regarding the use/non-use of the common open areas. The developer proposed
waving the 25 year right to change the use of the open space and also may allow
a conservation easement of the river front area. Sufficient guarantees to the
Township that the open space will remain that way in perpetuity. The Homeowners
will be assessed a small fee for maintenance of the walkway and entrance sign.
Trustee Wiegandt moved that the Township Board approve the Tentative
Preliminary Plat with the conditions specified by the planning commission.
supported by Trustee Zaban. Motion passed unanimously.

Gypsy Moths - Cindy Winter from Pebblebrook (president of the homeowners’
association). Residents of one house cannot sit on their deck because of the
severe infestation. Other neighbors also have severe infestation. Have wrapped
the trees, scraping, etc., but have not had any luck. A lot of people are
complaining this year about the moths. The Township will look into spraying for
next year. The sprays kill all the butterflies and caterpillars, not just the
gypsy moths. Some viruses and fungi do seem to just kill off the gypsy moths.
Mrs. Winter was asked to go back to the residents of Pebble Brook and get their
opinion on funding options for spraying next year. Clerk Graham suggested a
survey in this quarter's newsletter to see what areas are involved and if
people would be willing to pay a small assessment for Township wide spraying.
Too late this year to do anything. Spraying needs to be done in late May,
depending on the season/weather. Can kill the individual bugs this year, but
you need to spray before they come. The Board realized it was too late to get
an assessment on the ballot this year for spraying, so will put an item in the
newsletter asking if the spraying was done if people would be willing to
voluntarily pay a small fee for it.

AUGUST 12, 1997
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday August 12, 1997 at 7:35 PM. The Clerk
was asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban and Building
Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: reimbursement for the
swim team. Pines Office Park. The Rifle Club.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Auditor’s Report - Mr. Michael T. Gaffney
Submitted the report from the audit of financial statements and went over some
of the highlights. On page 1 of the Audit Report the Township received an
unqualified and clean opinion. This is the best rating you can get. The General
Fund detailed statement starts on page 22 with the General Fund Statement of
Revenues. On page 23 the Total Revenues in the General Fund for 1997 were
$819,000, compared to $472,000 for 1996. The difference is mostly due to the
DNR Grant for purchase of the park land. On page 27 the Total Expenditures were
$927,000. This is an Increase of approximately $500,000 over the 1996 figures
mostly due to purchase of the park land for $400,000. Some of the other areas
that accounted for the increase were Legal fees up $17,000; Building Inspection
fees were also up. Bottom line on page 27 was that expenditures exceeded
revenues by $107,000. The ending fund balance is $855,000. The Township is in
good solid financial condition. There are no cash flow problems.
Also submitted was a Highlight Report of Internal Control Structure. This
report contains comments related to the accounting systems. Two areas that were
commented on can be found on the 2nd page of the letter: 1) The budgeting
process of the DNR Grant - the Township only budgeted the net cost of the park
land rather than the gross revenue and expenditure (i.e. did not include the
grant in the budget); and 2) Accounting for escrow activities. The Township
changed the policy for plat fees that are being collected. We are now tracking
the amount collected vs. the amount actually used. However, there was not
sufficient information being maintained to track the expenditures correctly.
The systems are operating efficiently and effectively.
Trustee Wiegandt commented that he enjoyed reading the report. It was put
together in a very clear and easy to read format. Treasurer Nilsson questioned
if the Escrow accounts in question were the Planning Department’s accounts.
Planning Coordinator Martin stated that the auditor had been given hand written
accounts which admittedly were not sufficient. Computer records were kept that
are more complete, it was just an oversight that these were not made available
to the auditor. The situation has been discussed with the auditor who was here
and it has been determined that the Township actually does have a sufficient
recording of the hours and other expenses associated with the escrow accounts
and that these computer records will be made available at the time of the audit
in the future to be balanced out as of March 31st every year.
FIRE BOARD REPORT - Harold Powell
Other than everyday housekeeping the board is just studying the facilities
issue at this point. Other than the current location there appears to be only
one other location in Williamston on the water line that would be available.
This site is on Corwin Road one lot off of Grand River on the City side. There
are other properties possibly available at the present location. Everything is
still very tentative. Supervisor Obst stated that he received a call from a
Township resident who suggested that no other equipment is required except for
possibly Tankers. Mr. Powell responded that the Fire Department should have a
ladder wagon or snorkel gun to get to the top of some of the newer buildings in
the area. Trustee Wiegandt stated that the department had been talking about
new equipment for over a year. One truck is over 30 years old and another one
is over 20 years. They both currently function well, but parts are not readily
available for them. They need to be replaced with updated equipment so that if
something does go wrong we are not caught without spare parts to fix the trucks
quickly. The biggest concern is that we need to update/replace some of the
older equipment rather than adding anything else. Outside of the light truck we
are not asking for any more units, just updating some old equipment. Supervisor
Obst suggested that this would be a good topic for the next Township
newsletter.

Shirley Graham, Clerk            Susan Jennings, Recording Secretary
SEPTEMBER 2, 1997
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday September 2, 1997 at 7:38 PM. The Clerk
was asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban and Building
Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following addition: Septic System
requirements.
OLD BUSINESS
Red Cedar Rec. Swim Team Reimbursement - Tom Barrett
Mr. Barrett stated that the Red Cedar Rec. Board would discuss the Swim Team
reimbursement issue at their meeting on Sept. 3rd in an effort to come up with
an equitable solution to the problem of residents of Williamstown Township
being charged more to participate on the swim team than residents of other
participating municipalities. The Township provides $15.00 per child registered
in all Red Cedar Rec. activities. This money is used for year round
programming, not specifically for the swim team. Williamstown Township, the
City of Williamston and Locke Township all contribute $15 per participant. No
other municipalities are contributing at this time. Mr. Barrett acknowledged
that there was an inequity in the fees that were charged. Williamstown Township
residents paid more this year to be on the swim team than they did last year.
All other municipalities paid the same fee as last year. There is a $300
surplus in the swim team’s budget this year. There were 40 Township residents
on the swim team this year. The $300 surplus does not include the $15 per
participant being paid from the Township. The Township Board will wait until
the October meeting to make a final decision on reimbursement after the Red
Cedar Rec. makes their decision.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Haslett Road Project - Robert D’Alcorn, Ingham County Road Commission (ICRC)
The Township has received a revised set of plans from the ones received earlier
in the year. The ICRC tried to save more trees and disrupt less area. Changed
overall width of the shoulder where it was possible. The Michigan Department of
Transportation (MDOT) wants a 6 foot shoulder, but they will allow a 5 foot
wide shoulder where trees are involved. Ditches changed from 2.5 feet to 1.5
feet. Slopes changed from 1 on 4s to 1 on 3s. Curb and Gutter will be put in
where there are major cuts (2 feet or more and the banks are high). There will
be 4 feet of paved shoulder with the remaining 1 to 2 feet being gravel. The
ICRC will put in retaining walls where appropriate. Bob Peterson, a design
engineer with the ICRC, was also here. He showed a graph that displayed the
differences in the two plans. Referred to George Durak’s report and the walk
through and found there is little change, and actually an improvement in
drainage to the property area. There will be a passing lane going in at Haslett
and Shoeman Road. This is the one major change that hadn't been previously
discussed. The ICRC now has to get with the residents of Haslett Road and show
them what is going to happen on their individual properties. The ICRC will
replace trees that are being removed. They need to get with the residents to
see where they want the new trees planted. The Jacubiak property has the most
trees coming down. The ICRC will contact them to work out tree replacement
plans. The ICRC will be doing essentially the same type of thing that was done
between Williamston Rd and M-52 on Haslett Road this year. They will curb and
gutter intersections. This defines the intersections better, especially at
night, and keeps the gravel from being wiped out by school busses, trucks and
farm equipment. This will be the same cross section as the section that was
just done. Supervisor Obst asked how the trees were chosen for replacement. It
will be up to the property owner to pick out the types of trees that they want
planted. Dr. Morgan has taken the revised plans and is researching which trees
will be able to be left alone based on how much the roots will be covered and
other changes that some varieties may be able to withstand and others may not.
With the combination of category D funds (State) and urban STP funds (Federal)
there are enough program dollars through the Tri-County to improve Haslett Road
from Meridian to Zimmer and then Zimmer to Williamston in just 2 years.
Street Lights In The Woodview Subdivision - Doug Price
Mr. Price has been working with Detroit Edison to get the street lights
installed in Phase II of the Woodview Subdivision. The Township special
assessment has been paid to Detroit Edison to get the street lights installed.
Detroit Edison is saying that it is a contractor problem. Mr. Price would like
to see the Township pressure Detroit Edison to get the lights installed. One
suggestion was for the Township to go through the Public Service Commission. We
might also want to remind Detroit Edison that we are coming to a time when we
can choose our own utility companies and that good service now would help them
keep customers in the future.
REPORTS
Fire Board Report - Harold Powell
They have received their audit report and it looks very good. Facilities - a
new generator has been installed. It has not been wired in yet. The generator
will be valuable in case of a major storm or other local disaster so that the
fire barn can be used as a central command center. The architect was
hospitalized, so there is no update on the building plans. There was a comment
made at the last Township Board meeting about the Fire Department may better
spend their money on another water wagon. Every water truck in the county is on
call when there is a fire. Mr. Powell believes the fire department’s money
could be better spent on replacing some of their 20-30+ year old equipment.
Attorney Report - Steve Schultz
Annexation - the 30 day materials have not been served by the Boundary
Commission so there is no date set for adjudication.
Law Suit pending against the City of Williamston - met with the City in an
effort to resolve the issue. Was supposed to receive a proposal last Friday
from the City, but it has not been received.
Litigation last Thursday on information requested from the City on their
records of our sewer usage. The Township never received the requested
information. The Township filed a motion in July to compel the City to provide
it. The Township received a draft of information saying that the information
requested was attached, but it wasn't. All discovery must be completed by Dec.
18. The Township needs the information to know if the settlement negotiations
are based on a mutually agreed upon set of facts. The Court extended discovery
through Dec. 5 and directed the City to provide all requested information by
September 10th or the Court will rule in favor of the Township including all
court fees incurred by the Township to be paid by the City. Attorney Schultz
did receive a disturbing summary of what the City of Williamston believes the
Township’s sewer usage to be. He still needs to view the underlying documents
to know how the City came up with these numbers. It might be beneficial to
delay another meeting with the City until after the 10th so that we would know
where we stood.
Building Permit Activities - Walt Aven
Mrs. Kruger's property at 5660 N. Williamston Road - she is not in good health
and the house is in bad shape (small fire there). She is back in the house.
Fire Chief thinks the house should be condemned. Building Inspector needs to be
invited in before he can do this. Thinks there may be other alternatives for
her housing that her medical advisors would have to arrange.
The Jablonski's do not have a certificate of occupancy (C of O) for their home.
The house is now up for sale. If the new owners do not obtain a C of O, there
could be major problems with any potential future insurance claims if there
were a fire or other problems. The Building Inspector does not have the
physical means of keeping the owners out of the house. He may have better luck
keeping the new buyers out. The house is located east of Zimmer on the south
side of Sherwood Road. The current owners are on record as having been notified
of the situation. There is a definite tax disadvantage for not obtaining the C
of O. A homestead exemption cannot be granted until a C of O is issued.
Planning Commission Report - Mickey Martin
Steeplechase - Mr. Bruner's property off of Zimmer road. The Final Preliminary
Plat had a few issues remaining. OK’s by Conservation Easement Subcommittee. In
Aug. 22nd letter asked for several changes. They have all been made. Three
minor revisions to the greenbelt landscape plan have been made. County and
State agencies final approvals will be coming. MDEQ has been applied, papers
should be coming. Have submitted to the local utilities. Recommend Approval
with condition that all items in letter of Aug. 22 be realized. All items have
been addressed with the exception of some points in the declaration and
restrictions that Attorney Schultz is going over. We need to clarify the legal
description of the property included in the conservation easement. The language
needs to be clarified that the Township has the right to control the use of
that land and the ability to prohibit the construction of any permanent
structures on that property. The scope of the rights of the township need to be
clarified. The Township does not want to get into a situation where it needs
the approval of the property owners. Significant concern regarding reservation
of rights. The intent is not to allow the property owners association to repeal
the easement. The conservation area needs to be defined. All of Attorney
Schultz’ issues are easily fixable. They just need to change the language for
approval from the property owners. The Township Board can grant approval of the
final preliminary plat on the condition that the attorney and the applicant
come to an agreement on these covenants. Mr. Obst had a question on a planning
commissioner’s concerns of ground water issues. Mr. Dean stated that he does
not feel that this is an uncommon thing in Ingham County. You just have to
raise the level of the homes to avoid this problem. The septic systems have
been approved by the health departments of the County and State. Most of the
parcels would have systems that are below grade, some are at grade. Lot 6 would
have a backup system. The property is well above the flood plain. There were
some changes in the size of certain lots to meet the county requirements for an
alternative system. Lots 15 and 22 were always larger than 40,000 sq. ft. Lot 6
was required to be enlarged to 2 acres. Clerk Graham inquired if the county's
requirement for a drain field size being in line with the subdivisions square
footage requirement for the houses is being met, and the answer was yes. There
was a question on the tax assessment of the common conservation easement area.
The land will be part of the association lands. The value of the open space
will be included in the value of the lots, so there wouldn't be any extra
assessment.
Trustee Zaban moved that the Board of Trustees approve the final preliminary
plat for the Steeplechase Subdivision with the conditions as stated; with the
attorney and applicant coming to agreement over the covenants and restrictions;
and the approval of the county and state agencies and the permit by the MDEQ.
Supported by Trustee Wiegandt. Treasurer Nilsson questioned when they could
start selling lots - not until after final plat approval. Motion passed
unanimously.
A-1 Rental - Site Plan approval and Special Land Use approval. The parcel is
zoned B-2, and a rental business is a permitted use in this zoning. A Special
Land Use Permit is required for the mini storage part of the business. Phase 1
would be the rental building and 85 storage units; Phase 2 is an additional 190
storage units; and Phase 3 is slated for 240 storage units. The size of the
units may change based on consumer demand. There is a limit on the total square
footage for storage and a maximum number of units. The Township would require
an easement for a service drive along Grand River in case there is more
development in the area. The sign has been designated as a total height of 6 ft
and square footage of 96 sq. ft. The sign on the building will be a back lit
sign. The Planning Commission has required an extensive amount of landscaping
for the different phases. The property is across the street from the new
Township park and near a residential area. There will be no outdoor storage of
any kind allowed (e.g. motor homes, boats, etc.). This includes no outdoor
storage of the rental equipment as well. The parking lot cannot be used for
storage. Attorney Schultz needs to look at the document that pertains to a
drain easement on the property.
Mr. Helfmann stated that with the current conditions of improving the building
and doing all the landscaping in phase one that this is no longer a feasible
project. The building improvements required by the Planning Commission are for
brick walls on the Grand River side and a pitched roof. Mr. Bill Jacovack also
spoke on behalf of A-1 Rental. He stated that the recommendation to do all the
landscaping for all three phases required a significant amount of money that
may never be necessary if phases 2 and 3 are never done. If the additional
landscaping could be done at the same time as phase 2 and phase 3 then A-
1 Rental does not have a problem with the additional requirements. Mr. Jacovack
proposed that all the Grand River landscaping be done with phase 1, with the
additional landscaping to be done in phase 2. If phase 2 is not done then the
landscaping on the south side of the property would be done within 3 years. The
Planning Commission wants the landscaping all the way around the property, not
just on the south and Grand River (north) sides. The property to the west is
currently zoned Ag-Commercial, but the master plan proposes it to be zoned
residential eventually. Mr. Jacovack believes it to be grossly excessive to
have to front $20,000 in landscaping costs when the land to the west may never
be developed. He also has a problem with going to a customized building when
the landscaping protects the building from road front visibility anyway. They
have worked out the situation on loading space and have complied with the
revisions to the best of their ability. He believes the current recommendations
are excessive and make the cost of the project prohibitive. He would like to
see item 2 of the requirements for a Special Land Use Permit removed. This item
calls for the improvements to the building, which the applicant feels is
redundant and unnecessary when the requirements for the landscaping accomplish
the desired effect of screening the building from the road. With the
requirement that the exterior must be a finished quality and design compatible
with structures on surrounding property the applicant can no longer order a
stock building from the manufacturer. Exterior of the mini-warehouse must be a
finished quality and design compatible with structures on surrounding property
is a requirement of the Township’s Zoning Ordinance. Mr. Jacovack believes the
combination of the screening and the improvements to the building is excessive
- one or the other would be fine, but not both.
Comments from the audience included: All up and down Grand River will see much
worse looking buildings with absolutely no screening than what they are
proposing for this building. Believes the design is compatible with the area.
The people that are looking into buying the property have put in a lot of time
and money into the project and the screening they are proposing would make the
additional changes to the building unnecessary. Could put in the initial
screening now and plant smaller trees for phase 2 and phase 3 so that they
would grow to screening size by the time they are needed. The issue is one of
redundancy. The Planning Commission has taken it upon themselves to dictate the
design of the building. Have to go with either the building or the screening,
but cannot dictate both. Compatibility is a matter of opinion, not a hard fact.
Being redundant.
Board Comments: Trustee Zaban stated that the only change he would make if a

Clerk Graham voiced the opinion that she still has a problem with requiring

Septic Systems - We are starting to develop lands that are in marginal areas.
According to Attorney Schultz the Township has the authority to have stricter
regulations for septic systems than what the County requires. The Planning
Commission would like to have some stricter standards, not just the minimums,
because of the marginal land in the Township. The Commission would like a joint
meeting with Bruce Gruner of the County Health Department and a sub committee
to see what he believes are marginal areas. The Commissioners have questions
such as can viruses be passed to the ground water when there is only a 2 foot
difference between the septic system and ground water, etc. With the stricter
requirements the Township would still ideally have Mr. Gruner inspecting our
systems, but he would use our higher standards. Our standards would be
incorporated with his. The Commission would like to have the go ahead to set up
this sub committee. Marginal land for a septic system is heavy clay soils,
something that would not infiltrate in less than 24 hours. Don't want to
reproduce problems that the Quinlan Subdivision had several years ago.
Engineered systems do require more maintenance than a regular drain field or
below ground systems. We may or may not end up with stricter requirements. We
will at least have the county requirements. According to Attorney Schultz for
bona fide health, safety and welfare reasons the Township does have the right
to deny building based on their own criteria as opposed to the County's
criteria. It should be site specific, stating that such and such a lot requires
a specific system. Trustee Wiegandt moved that the Planning Commission go ahead
with their septic system regulation planning. Treasurer Nilsson seconded.
Motion passed unanimously.

Pollution Prevention Week
September 15-21, 1997
WHEREAS, the Township of Williamstown takes great pride in the state’s natural
resources and supports a clean and safe environment; and
WHEREAS, pollution prevention, also known as source reduction, is a progressive
approach that eliminates or reduces pollution at its source; and
WHEREAS, pollution prevention is the most environmentally sound method of
protecting our natural resources; and
WHEREAS, pollution prevention can improve environmental conditions and maintain
the health and safety of workers in the workplace; and
WHEREAS, pollution prevention can increase industrial efficiency, commercial
competitiveness, and can save participating businesses time and money; and
WHEREAS, by focusing on rigorous pollution prevention, Michigan can meet the
challenges of having both a healthy community and business environment for its
citizens; and
WHEREAS, Pollution Prevention Week is an opportunity for government to join
forces with business, industry, environmental groups, community organizations,
and the citizenry at large to take action toward a prosperous and sustainable
future;
THEREFORE, be it resolved that September 15-21, 1997, is Pollution Prevention
Week and the Township of Williamstown does hereby urge all community members
and businesses of Williamstown Township to participate in local and regional
celebratory and educational activities.

OCTOBER 7, 1997
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, October 7, 1997 at 7:34 PM. The Clerk
was asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban and Building
Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following additions under New Business -
Detroit Edison and a road closing application for Hart Road between Germany and
Haslett.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Sue Creagh - Red Cedar Rec Director
Ms. Creagh was hired as the new Director of Red Cedar Rec (RCR) in July and
reports to Jeri Mifflin, Director of Williamston Community Education. RCR will
be offering all the same programs they did last year with a few additions. Ms.
Creagh’s goal is to keep an open line of communication between the City of
Williamston and the surrounding Townships so that RCR can more effectively
respond to the recreational requirements of the community. It is no longer the
Townships’ and City’s responsibility to appoint members to the RCR Board.
Billing of the local participating municipalities will also be reviewed.
Currently RCR is only billing for Baseball and Swim Team. The scope of
activities offered by RCR has increased greatly and their requests for
reimbursement from the municipal units needs to be updated to reflect this
change. RCR is looking for input from the Townships and City on how billing
should be handled. This year RCR has decided to send out the request for
reimbursement based on the past philosophies because that is what the current
budget is based on. RCR will be reimbursing $20 to each of the members of the
swim team who were charged $98 instead of $78 to participate on the 1997 team.
RCR plans on issuing these checks by Dec. 1, 1997. Delays are due to processing
paper work and coordinating with the Williamston School District, who manages
the account that the reimbursement funds will come from.
FIRE BOARD REPORT
Treasurer Nilsson had a question on whether a decision had been made to buy the
property on Mullett Street. Clerk Graham, who also serves on the Fire Board,
stated that the property is up for sale at a reasonable price. The Fire Board
is looking favorably at obtaining it for a parking lot. Even though a gas
station used to be located there, the site has been certified to be clean. This
lot is located directly across the street from the present Fire Barn. Moving
parking over there would enable expansion and remodeling of the current
building. Supervisor Obst had a question regarding water capacity. Trustee
Wiegandt, a volunteer firefighter for the department, stated that the tanker
carries 2500 gallons and each of the two pumpers carry 800 gallons of water.
There is a mutual aid pact with all of the fire departments in Ingham County
and throughout the Tri-County area plus Laingsburg and Perry to respond in
cases where more water would need to be carried in than what the local
department can provide.

PLANNING COMMISSION - MICKEY MARTIN
Sidewalk Ordinance - waiting for Attorney Schultz to write up liability policy.
The Planning Commission’s charge was to remove liability from the Township and
place it on the property owner. Except for subdivisions, some commissioners did
not believe that the property owner should be responsible for maintaining the
sidewalks in front of their property. The Commission needs the Board’s view on
this and the Commission is also holding a public meeting to discuss the issue.
Per Attorney Schultz, in general the property owner is responsible, either
directly or through special assessments. Per Treasurer Nilsson and Trustee
Wiegandt - the Township does not have a public works department to handle
maintenance of sidewalks. It would have to be done by the property owner. If
the Township was responsible it would have to be contracted out. Clerk Graham
would like to prevent the Township from being liable for injury lawsuits, but
thinks the Township should have the sidewalk inspected at least twice a year
and maintain the sidewalk since the Township is who had it installed.
Commissioner Jennings pointed out that the Sidewalk Ordinance is going to be
around a long time and in the future will most likely be used primarily in new
subdivisions. Inspector Aven suggested that if the Township hires someone to
clean the sidewalk, then they should be the same people responsible for the
inspections.
ADVISORY COUNCIL REPORT - RUDD HOAG
The Council welcomed two new members at their October meeting - Rex Lamore,
member at large and Helen LaBlanc who will be serving on the environmental
committee.
The Wetland program for the computer goes back to 1939 and includes water
flows. Meridian township is almost done. Our computer is ready, just waiting
for the rest of the data. Also looking at a well inventory for the Township.
Will work with the County Health department on this.
The Recreation Committee went over the master plan for the park. They need to
come up with an initial Site Plan. The Township can have the model parks from
the MSU class come out here and then use those ideas to come up with a plan.
McKenna and Associate can draw up a plan. Parks and Rec. Plan must be updated
before March of 1998 in order for the Township to still be eligible for grant
money to develop the park. The Township can request up to $500,000 for
development. The State had 200 applications for the grant money last year.
McKenna gave Planning Coordinator Martin an estimate of $3900 for updating the
recreation plan. The Township would have to hold public hearings on a proposed
plan. The cost of a Site Plan for the park would be above and beyond the $3900
and would be charged on an hourly basis. It would help if the Township was as
prepared as possible before McKenna arrived. The time estimate is for 2 people
being here for half a day doing sketches, plus time back in their office to
turn the sketches into plans. The State requires that the Recreation Plan be
updated every 5 years. Supervisor Obst questioned the direction the Park
Subcommittee was going in. He thought the subcommittee was going to be doing
fund raisers to raise the money to help cover development of the park.
Treasurer Nilsson stated that you can't really fund raise until you have a
plan. Applying for the grant is a fund raising activity. Per Trustee Wiegandt -
there is some money available for the park from the lease of the land for
farming in the first year that the Township owned the property.
Transportation Committee - next goal is to look at the Mitchell and Vanneter
road area. Hope to walk it in mid November with Bob D'Alcorn from the ICRC and
talk to the schools about their plans for the land they purchased off of
Mitchell Road.
Gypsy Moth - Tom Ellis presented an excellent program. Started taking a survey.
The Township now has some materials that they can hand out to people who
inquire about the moths.
Open Land Committee - Nancy Fink will take over the chair from Dan Kraft.
The issues of Detroit Edison violating their franchise agreement and junk cars
have been handled by the board.
Commercial And Residential Committees - will look at getting natural gas
extended throughout more of the Township.
New Topic for the Council to investigate - Putting the Township on the
Internet. There are two separate issues that need to be looked at. The first is
putting the Township on line so that it has access to the information available
on the Internet/World Wide Web. This would include cost factors for a dedicated
modem line and fees to subscribe to an Internet Service Provider. Clerk Graham
believed the cost for an additional phone line would be approximately $35 per
month. The second issue to address would be having a web page created for the
Township. Items involved here would be cost of having the page created and
maintained; cost of having the page hosted by a service such as Voyager; and
what information would the Township like to provide on its website.
Trustee Zaban asked for a clarification on what constitutes a “junk car”. To
NOT be considered junk a vehicle has to have a current license plate, 4 tires,
working battery, motor, etc. The Township does not allow an unlicensed vehicle
to be covered by a tarp. That is considered open storage, which is prohibited.
It was agreed that all of the facts of the Ordinance pertaining to junk cars
should be stated in the next (January, 1998) issue of the Township Newsletter.
Per Clerk Graham - the Township needs a bid from McKenna before we can give
them the go ahead to work on the park project.

The Fire Board was surprised to learn that the Library Committee wanted the
Fire Department to move to a new site and building and have the Library take

and found the present site to be the best location in the area for a Fire
Station. The Fire Board believes that it is a separate entity from the Library
and wishes to remain so. The Board voted to purchase the Beech property across
the street from the current location. It was decided to put the title into the
three municipalities names. The Attorney for the City of Williamston stopped
the sale at closing. The Fire Board is still working with the architect. They
can’t go much further without knowing what kind of zoning variances they may
need from the City. The Strata Company is waiting for further payment before
repairing the fire wells that were not capped properly. Treasurer Nilsson asked
who owns the current property. The current Fire Barn property is jointly owned
by Williamstown Township and the City of Williamston, with Wheatfield Township
paying monthly rent to both municipalities. The current charter of the Fire
Board prevents them from holding title to any real estate directly. Per
Attorney Schultz - The real estate is held by the constituent municipalities. A
Fire Authority (incorporation of the current Fire Board) or Fire District
(which could also include Locke and Leroy Townships) can be voted in that would
have the authority to ask the voters directly for a millage or bonds for
additional building for the Fire Department.. Per Clerk Graham the question
would have to be put to the voters next August to form either a Fire Authority
or District, then it is the District or Authority that can call the vote.
Should the authority or district pass a millage or bond issue then a Fire
Building Authority would be created to administer the funds and bid the
construction. Harold Powell questioned who can sit on the Building Authority.
Elected officials, and members of the Fire Department and Fire Board/Authority/
District cannot serve on the Building Authority. The building authority would
not be discharged until all outstanding bonds are paid off. The Fire Authority
would be like a separate corporate entity. The Fire Board is looking to obtain
their own counsel to put the issue of creating a Fire Authority or District on
the ballot in August. The Fire Board did not favor a joint building authority
with the library.
PLANNING COMMISSION REPORT - Mickey Martin
Jeffrey Foote Property - Proposed Pond
Mr. Foote has appeared before the Planning Commission and the Township has
received a letter of complaint regarding the property. Supervisor Obst wrote a
letter to Mr. Foote on Nov. 24 requesting that he stop all work on the
property. Mr. Foote asked if he could drill a well on his property to test if
other wells would be affected when he filled his pond. The Township has
subsequently discovered that Mr. Foote does not need to dig another well to
determine if there would be negative impact to neighbors. He can perform the
required draw down test with the currently existing wells. Mr. Art Schultz
asked that If water does go down in the other area wells, what is the Township
going to do? Planning Chair Martin stated that one of the things on a study
would be testing as many wells as possible - i.e. have the neighbors
participate in the draw down test. They will also look at well logs in the
stratosphere of where he is tapping into the water. Once the pond is filled,
the estimation is that Mr. Foote’s wells will be pumping 70 gallons per minute
to keep it full during the summer. There is a question on how far out other
people's wells in the area will be affected by this project. Planning
Commissioner Fink stated that there was no way to know exactly where, or how
many, other wells may be affected. Mr. Harold Powell said that when Meridian
Township put their community wells down his well went from a 40 foot draw to an
80 foot draw. Mr. Foote told Supervisor Obst that no work had been done since
Oct 8. Mrs. Gerre Imhoff said that their main concern is how their well will be
affected, which is currently around 450 ft. They are also concerned about the
ecological impact of the project to the area - not just the wells. Supervisor
Obst stated that Mr. Foote is currently in violation since he has no building
permit or site plan approval. Anyone here tonight that is interested will be
notified of the site plan review. Normally it is just neighbors within 500 ft
that are notified. The Township may also post notification of the meeting in
the paper since this issue could affect a much larger area than the immediate
neighbors.
Other than the City of Williamston, the only other large wells in the immediate
area are the 2 - 10 inch wells servicing Eagle Point Condominiums. Mr. Foote’s
pond will have an 8 inch well running continuously. Planning Chair Martin said
the Planning Commission has requested a hydrological study. The Planning
Commission is concerned about the slopes and soil erosion. The Planning

slopes’ design and maintenance so they can evaluate for erosion and run of -
they have not received one yet. Visually, there is an impact for the neighbors
already. Supervisor Obst stated that the standards for site plan approval need
to be looked at. Mr. Gerald Imhoff asked if Mr. Foote had received a building

to redo the roof. Mrs. Gerre Imhoff asked if there are any state laws that are
being violated and aren't privacy fences limited to six feet? If a fence is
limited to 6 ft, then how can you just shove the dirt up 14-16 feet? A fence
would have to follow the contour of the land. Despite what Mr. Foote had told
Supervisor Obst, that his neighbor, Jim Sikarskie had no problems with what Mr.
Foote is doing; Mr. Sikarskie said that he does have some concerns. He is very

rational in dealing with his concerns to date. Mr. Fred Rupp asked if the Board

“Appearance - Landscaping, earth berms, fencing, signs, wall and other site

NEW BUSINESS
Community Septic Systems - Mickey Martin
November 6th there was a meeting held to discuss the long term management and
care of community cluster septic systems and the role the Drain Commission may
play in this management if the Township will agree to the liability and
responsibility of them. Present at this meeting were Bob Godbold, Bruce Gruner
and Gary Rowe from the Ingham County Health Department; John Catterino and
Holly Mercer from the State of Michigan DEQ; Eric A. Schertzing, Deputy Drain
Commissioner; Bob Hayes and Mickey Martin from the Williamstown Township
Planning Commission.
Pine Knoll and BAAN.GAN.AKA are the only developments in the township that
currently have community septic systems. No new developments with this type of
septic system will be permitted until the township agrees to accept full
responsibility and liability for the approval of the systems, the proper
installation and on site inspections, continuing operation, all maintenance and
drive by monitoring, etc. This would be a major responsibility and liability
for the township to undertake. The County and State are of the opinion that
these are not permanent systems. The Township should agree to accept this
responsibility by allowing the community septic systems only if they are
looking to hook these sites up to a public waste water treatment plant. If
that's not in the future of the township, then the township should not take on
this responsibility. The Township can hire the Ingham County Drain Commission
to do the drive bys, monitor the alarms, etc. We would have to write our own
ordinance and have the Ingham County Drain Commission agree to provide the man
power to monitor the systems. The Health Department would also need an
agreement to know what their function would be and how they would be kept
informed.
Pine Knoll’s system has already failed with only 6 houses on it. Neighbors were
annoyed and turned off the alarm. No one who needed to know about the problem
knew until the next house was going to hook up to the system. Livingston County
will no longer allow new developments to have community septic systems because
of problems with existing systems and assessing limitations. This would be a
big responsibility for this township to take on. We would need more staff.
Current mechanisms in effect are reactionary. The homeowner can be assessed if
something goes wrong. The County and State wants the Townships to take the
responsibility and liability for the systems and not homeowner associations.
Treasurer Nilsson stated that she could not vote to have the township take on
this responsibility right now and that the systems do not fit with the goals of
the township to contain growth. Clerk Graham stated that if we go forward with
these systems, then starting Jan 1998 we would have to do a study and make an
assessment based on the people that are already connected to these systems.
Mr. Chad Walter stated that these septic systems are an issue all down the I-96
corridor. The developers are looking to extend from Brighton. He was here to
support the community disposal systems. Mr. Walter is a resident and the
developer of the BAAN.GAN.AKA land condominium community, which uses a
community septic system. In his view a large part of the problem is financial
and political. We have the means to handle almost any system that the soil
might demand. BAAN.GAN.AKA’s system has an enormous amount of redundancy and is
expected to last forever. They have 4 drain fields and use them in alternating
years. Problems arise when you have a poorer quality of design, maintenance and
monitoring. If the township waits until the demand hits, then they will be in a
reactionary position. If you see the development coming and plan for it now,
you will not be in a reactionary position. Soils dictate what can and should be
done. Mr. Walter believes soils will dictate that the community system can be
done. If not, then go with mound systems which are costly and must be rebuilt
periodically. If you have a community system then you have the ability to
assess the property owners using the system for future problems so that you
have the money when you need it. There are standards available for the
construction, maintenance and monitoring of these systems. The township has the
authority to require higher standards, but they would not have to reinvent the
wheel. Monitoring has to be done regularly. The County has the staff to provide
the service as long as the Township will fund it. There are also other
individuals around who the Township could contract with to provide monitoring
services. There are several firms that are starting up maintenance contracts
throughout Michigan that could be hired for maintenance work. As the projects
are coming on line these companies are sculpturing services to provide them to
whomever requires them. There are also some very qualified engineers in the
area to design the systems. Access to money - if you have a home owners
association in the form of a land condominium you have the taxing authority in
place. Can this liability be bonded? Don't know yet. Mr. Walter asks that the
Township look at the issue carefully before voting on it. Feels that it is an
excellent solution for the soils in this area. The Township will not have a
sewer system for a long time because of how land is partitioned in this
township. Biggest issues are the vehicles for politics and the vehicles for
money to make it work. Supervisor Obst asked if the Township wanted to pursue
this issue further? Planning Chair Martin stated that it will cost money to
investigate the issue. These systems have the potential to increase development
twice as fast in the area than if we don't allow them. The State is not going
to control our growth, we need to do it ourselves. Need to consider the
responsibility and liability. There was a question from the audience on a
central system disposing into the Red Cedar. Clerk Graham confirmed that the
feasibility system did dispose into the river. It is an issue of looking at
water course disposal or on site disposal. Planning Commissioner Fink raised
the concern of needing to convert all green fields from Detroit to Chicago to
development. At what risk do we allow this to happen? Trustee Wiegandt
commented that this is still a general law township. We are on the verge of
growing, but we don’t have to grow too quickly at this point if we don't want
to. Taking on policy at this stage of the game is a little premature. He would
like more time to study the issue - maybe 6-8 months. Supervisor Obst moved
that at this time the Township does not want to go forward with the community
septic systems. Supported by Clerk Graham. The two developments that we have
are both quite nice. Clerk Graham stated that if you have an owner operator it
is much better than a tenant. Planning Chair Martin stated that these systems
will encourage higher density. Trustee Wiegandt stated that if the State of
Michigan doesn’t want to get involved in these systems then why should this
little township do it? Clerk Graham stated that the Township should not have to
pay for this, it should be self supporting. Planning Chair Martin stated that
it would be the townships responsibility to make sure that it is self
supporting. Clerk Graham would like more information. Mr. Walter stated that
each parcel in the township already has a density figure attached to it. In
BAAN.GAN.AKA the system did not increase the density, it allowed more of the
land to be kept as a natural area where the drain fields are. Every parcel
already has a density figure on it. Now the question is how do you do it the
best way you can? Preplanning puts the township in a stronger position to
handle the growth in the future. Vote taken on the motion - motion passed
unanimously. Trustee Zaban brought up the Larkin development where the county
has vetoed every proposal put to them so far for septic systems. Mr. Walter’s
development is working wonderfully. Problem is that not all developers are as
conscientious. Planning Chair Martin should talk to Mr. Walter to determine how
the system is proceeding and then report to the Board before researching
community systems any further.

Township Calendar & MTA Legislative Updates
The Michigan Townships Association (MTA) requested the Township Board pass a
resolution regarding legislation for future road jurisdiction options.
Treasurer Nilsson moved and Clerk Graham supported that the Board adopt the
following resolution:
WHEREAS, Michigan township officials are elected to represent over four million
citizens; and
WHEREAS, There are in excess of 85,000 miles of primary and secondary roads
located within the boundaries of townships; and
WHEREAS, The comprehensive transportation fund, Public Act 51 of 1951, created
a formula to distribute transportation funds for road creation, repair and
improvements among governmental units having jurisdiction over roads; and
WHEREAS, Because townships do not have jurisdiction over roads, they receive no
direct funding from Act 51; and
WHEREAS, However, without being obligated by statute to contribute any funds
for road purposes, townships annually send millions of dollars from their
general and special funds and/or special assessments to assist in road
construction, repair and maintenance; now, therefore, be it hereby
RESOLVED, That the township of Williamstown support legislation that would
include townships in the Michigan Transportation Fund distributions; and be it
further
RESOLVED, That a township planning fund be created within Act 51 from the urban
and rural road set asides provided for in the Michigan Transportation Fund
spent only with township input and without matching funds; and be it further
RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolution be sent to Representative Gustafson,
and Senator Byrum, Governor Engler and the Michigan Townships Association.
Resolution was passed unanimously.

1998 Meeting Minutes
JANUARY 6, 1998
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, January 6, 1998 at 7:36 PM. The Clerk
was asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban and Building
Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: Budget review; request
from Ingham County Saddlemates 4-H club to use the hall; request from
Manchester Plastics to use the hall;. sanitary sewer district #2 - compilation
of monies paid; Fire Board minutes from 12-11-97; and the January newsletter
deadlines.
REPORTS
Fire Board Report - Darrell Brown
The Fire Board agreed to reinvest the CD that came due into another 12 month CD
at the best available rate. They have received bids for the generators that
were up for sale. The Board has agreed to accept a bid of $1000 for the main
generator. They have also informed the interested party that there is another
generator available if they are interested. The Board has informed their
architect firm that things were to be put on hold due to the property
acquisition situation. The person that purchased the Beech property will not
use it for a couple of years and may be able to work something out where the
Fire Board could use the property in the mean time. It is still hard for the
Fire Board to understand why the members representing the City had not
conversed with the City Council about the proposed property purchase. The Fire
Chief and Board still believe the current location is the best location for the
Fire Department to serve the community. There are concerns among members of the
Fire Board that the Library seems to be of greater concern to the City than the
fire department. The Fire Board had to give up the $1000 deposit because of
what happened with the attempted purchase of the property. The Fire Chief
believes the Fire Board should hire an attorney unrelated to any of the
municipalities around. Mr. Lounsbury purchased the property the fire board was
interested in purchasing. Treasurer Nilsson asked what the general feeling of
the Fire Board was in regards to combining with the Library. The Fire Board
does not believe they are compatible entities and does not want to risk having
a bonding issue defeated because of the Library being included. The Fire Board
questioned why the City doesn't put the Library in the US Plastics building
where they are already moving the Police Department and DPW? There is certainly
no more room to add the Library at the current Fire Department location. Mr.
Harold Powell raised some fundraising issues in combining the Fire Board and
the Library. The two entities serve the community in different ways. Half of
Wheatfield and part of Williamstown are in school districts other than
Williamston. People tend to use the libraries associated with the school
district that they belong to. That could drastically hurt a millage issue if
they try to combine with the fire department, especially since there is already
a new 1 mill millage rate at the county level for the library district. The
Fire Board serves three different municipalities and at least 5 different
school districts. This is not quite the same situation as Delhi Charter
Township, where the Library, Town Hall, Police and Fire Departments are all
located in the same new facility.
Attorney's Report - Steve Schultz
Brief Delivered On The Foote Pond Issue. The Township is in a position to
prevent the drilling of any wells until site plan approval. Flooding would be
private cause of action. The property owner would have to file a trespassing
suit. The Township could not be involved. Blight and nuisance ordinances do not
apply.
Sidewalk Ordinance - Can the Township, through the ordinance, require the
property owners to accept the responsibility and the liability to accidents on
the sidewalk due to the sidewalk not being maintained properly? The Township
does have the ability to do this. It is a policy issue for the Township to
decide whether or not they want to do this and to what extent they may want to
do this. This does not mean the Township could not be sued. It means the
property owner would also be sued. In most cases the plaintive is looking for
their damages, and they don't really care where it comes from. Typically our
insurance carrier and the property owner's insurance carrier would be sued. It
is up to the Board to decide how they want to distribute the risk and
responsibility.
Annexation And Ongoing Litigation With The City. There was a public hearing at
the Boundary Commission on December 11th. The 30 day materials are due Monday,
January 12th. Attorney Schultz will put together a letter to address the water
issue and the scurrilous attack of the City's Engineer. The Engineer himself
was not happy with how his comments were taken out of context. The Township
does not want the record left with some of those erroneous statements left
unchallenged. Attorney Schultz met with Supervisor Obst and Trustee Wiegandt
with respect to the proposal received from the City to try to resolve the sewer
litigation. The Township is still working on its response.
MTA Convention - The law firm will have a dinner for clients on Tuesday,
January 20th. Wednesday and Thursday Attorney Schultz and a couple other
attorneys from the firm will be speaking at some of the workshops.
Treasurer Nilsson had a question about the Sidewalk Ordinance mentioning a
civil infraction vs. criminal misdemeanor. The Township can make it a civil
infraction to fail to maintain the sidewalk in front of your property. Also,
special assessment districts can be used to fund sidewalks and their
maintenance, but private property owners can challenge districts set up by the
Board.
Supervisor Obst is concerned about high attorney fees. He realizes the current
situations with the City of Williamston have necessitated an increase in the
time required of the attorney in the past year. However, he would like to
improve communication between the Township office and the Attorney’s office to
have estimates on services requested ahead of time.
A neighbor in the Foote situation (if flooded) would have to file a civil
lawsuit for trespass. This would be to stop the trespass and to be reimbursed
for damages. This is a private dispute between two people and the Township's
ordinances would not apply, since it is not a "public" problem. The Township
can require a lot in terms of site plan review to help prevent the problem from
occurring in the first place, but once the problem occurs it is a private
dispute. The Township can prevent drilling of the wells until a site plan has
been approved.

Planning Commission - Mickey Martin
Proposed Changes To Zoning Ordinance Dealing With The Zoning Board Of Appeals
(ZBA).
Instead of all five criteria having to be met, the proposed change would
require that there be unique circumstances and the ZBA will consider the
remaining 4 criteria in making their determination. The request must be unique
to the property and the general area. This will give the ZBA a little more
flexibility to make their determinations on a one on one basis. Self created
circumstances will be looked at a little more in depth. The Planning Commission
is looking for the Board to approve the changes or send them back to the
Planning Commission for further modifications. Trustee Wiegandt made a motion
to approve the proposed amendments. Supported by Clerk Graham. Roll Call vote:
   Ayes:   Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Zaban, Trustee Wiegandt, Clerk Graham,
Supervisor Obst
   Nays:   None
Lot Splits - Fee Schedule
Because of the new State Land Division Act it is possible to obtain up to 16
splits very quickly without platting. Currently the Township charges $75 for
the application and then $50 for each resulting parcel. The Planning Commission
would like to retain this fee for the first 4 splits. When there are 5 or more
resulting parcels involved in a split the Planning Commission would like to set
up an escrow account under the same guidelines as are currently in place for
the platting of subdivisions, so that the lot split request can be sent to the
Township’s planning consultants and any other organizations deemed necessary
for a review without cost to the Township. The initial amount put into escrow
is $1500. When this is used up, the account must be replenished in $500
increments before further action would be taken on the part of the Township.
These larger lot splits are starting to come in. Planner Martin received one
today with 5 splits, and is expecting at least 2 more in the near future, one
with 9 and the other with 16 splits. Some of them are quite complicated. The
money left in the escrow account at the end of the process would be returned to
the applicant. Treasurer Nilsson moved that the Board approve revising the fee
schedule for lot splits to $75 plus $50 for each resulting parcel up to 4. Any
splits that have 5 or more resulting parcels would be put into an escrow
account of $1500 replenished at $500 increments per current policy when
necessary with fees assessed as according to the current policy. Seconded by
Trustee Zaban. Motion passed unanimously. Effective immediately.
Foote Property - Supervisor Obst wrote a letter informing Mr. Foote that he
must stop and desist all work. Mr. Foote asked how he could do the hydro test
if he doesn't drill the well? Planning Chair Martin responded that Mr. Foote
needed to provide a work study plan for the hydro test. This plan would have to
show how they planned on conducting the test and explain why the well would be
necessary to perform the test. The Township received a reply last Friday from
Mr. Foote’s engineers that was inadequate. The Township will send
recommendations from Planning Commissioner Hayes to RC and Associates to give
them a spelled out version of the phone conversations and the first letter. At
this point RC is saying that the study requested is cost prohibitive and they
are not going to do it. The Township is still requiring the work study plan
before they will allow the drilling of the well. Commissioner Hayes suggested
sending the study to STS for review, since Commissioner Hayes himself is not
personally bonded to represent the Township as an engineer.
The stop work order stands. The letter received from RC associates was not
sufficient to be considered a work study plan. Planning Chair Martin’s response
will emphasize that the stop work order will not be removed except by action of
the Township Board at such time as the conditions for the study have been met.
The current excavation at the site has the proposed pond built up like a dike.
Water will be held above the original grade. An engineering review will be
required to determine the stability of the pond. Mr. Foote could be held liable
in civil litigation should water seep out the sides and flood the neighbors.
Per Building Inspector Aven, Mr. Foote needs to have a review of how well the
walls are constructed and what they are constructed of. He would also be
required to pull a building permit should he receive site plan approval. The
building permit requires an engineered plan by a certified engineer who is
bonded and would be liable for the integrity of the proposed pond.
Building Inspector Aven also pointed out that the work study plan will have to
explain what Mr. Foote is going to do with the water he pumps for the draw down
test. He will not be allowed to put the water from the draw down test into the
pond. Mr. Foote needs an engineered drawing that shows the slopes, the perk
test, etc. that show the pond will hold the anticipated water. He will have a
difficult time changing things if required after the pond is filled.
The letter from Planning Chair Martin to Mr. Foote’s consultants is going to
reinforce the issue that there is a stop work order in effect and that
construction plans drawn up by an engineer are required for site plan approval,
and if approved, a grading permit.
Community Pool - Planning Chair Martin met with Al Gooch who was hired by the
school district to do an assessment of pool costs, possible programs,
management, personnel, etc. Mr. Gooch has run community pools for the last 25
years in the Midland area. The scheduled opening date for the pool is May 1998.
The pool is 75’ by 42’, and handicapped accessible. There is also a 12 person
hot tub connected to the pool. It would be possible to have 4 different
functions occurring simultaneously at the pool. The Township would like a good
accounting of costs. Mr. Gooch indicated that it should be fairly easy to track
costs. Chemicals and personnel would be fixed costs. Utilities would have to be
prorated since they share meters with the rest of the high school. Mr. Gooch is
looking at ways to inform the Townships of their usage. He will propose some
sort of a sign in. He is looking at a card with a bar code on it. People could
then buy a membership, or get a day card. It would then be easy to track who
used the pool when and for what. Should easily be able to generate the usage
reports that the Township would be looking for. Mr. Gooch asked how the
Township would want to pay their allotment - one lump sum or monthly billing.
One lump sum would be preferable by the Clerk and Treasurer who cut the checks.
His goal has been for user fees to pay most of the funds. The Midland pool is
currently 67% user fees, 22% United Way supplements, 11% foundation and
corporate funding. Mr. Gooch is not in favor of multiple rates. He would like
one rate across the board regardless of where you live. He is going to every
group who would likely use the pool to see what they want to have. The Township
will send him a copy of the agreement we set up with the school for funding.
