NEW BUSINESS
Ingham County Road Commission - Governors Proposal Of Jurisdictional Transfer
Of Various County Roads. - Joe Pulver, Ingham County Road Commission
Mr. Pulver is addressing all 16 townships in the County to let them know the
changes that MDOT and the Governor would like to see. The following is the
outline of his presentation:
·Loss of Local Road Revenue - The $2 million of primary road revenue
transferred each year to local roads will not be available.
·Loss of Federal Revenue for Primary Road Improvements - MDOT’s goal in the
takeover of Ingham County primary roads is to get control of all Federal
revenue available and use it on projects throughout the State. Federal money
that has been available may not be used to fund projects needed in Ingham
County.
·Need to Increase Local Taxes and/or Special Assessments - With MDOT
controlling all Federal revenue and the State revenue generated by these
primary roads, the only source of revenue for improvements on the roads
remaining under road commission jurisdiction will be from local taxes and/or
special assessments. The revenue we receive from the remaining roads may not
cover all maintenance costs.
·MDOT Will Not Provide Better Service - For roads taken over by MDOT, townships
and residents will lose their local contact. With 500 less MDOT employees, the
State will not be able to respond in a timely manner. When comparing the
condition of State roads to Ingham County roads, you will find most roads
maintained by the Ingham County Road Commission to be in better condition.
·It Will Cost More to Maintain Roads Taken Over by MDOT - MDOT plans to
contract the maintenance for roads they take over. Private contractor costs
will be much higher than those charged by public agencies and MDOT will need to
create another level of costly bureaucracy to administer these maintenance
projects.
·Jobs Could Be Lost to County Residents - If MDOT does contract the maintenance
of the roads they takeover, jobs could be lost to contractor employees from
outside Ingham County.
The Board agreed to review the proposed resolution from the County Road
Commission along with the proposed resolution from the MTA and adopt a
resolution favoring the County at the next meeting.

Proposed Zoning Ordinance Revision To Require Fire Hydrants - Norm Obst.
Supervisor Obst is asking the Planning Commission to investigate requiring
irrigation wells to provide fire hydrants to subdivisions of a certain size.
Bruce Gruner of the Ingham County Health Department has informed Supervisor
Obst that this type of well, which would not necessarily pump potable water,
would be allowed for fire hydrants. The Fire Department requires that the wells
provide at least 40 lbs of pressure at the hydrants. Supervisor Obst is making
this proposal based partly on discussions held at the Boundary Commission
Meeting. The Boundary Commission may believe having fire hydrants is a superior
method of fire protection to other methods. Trustee Wiegandt, a volunteer fire
fighter in Williamston disagreed. He believes the current tanker system is just
as safe and efficient as hydrants would be. Planning Commissioner Brian
Jennings was concerned about the seeming conflict of the Township not wanting
to allow community septic systems, but still wanting to promote community water
for the hydrants. If the hydrants were put in place it would be the home owners
associations that would be responsible for the cost and maintenance of the
hydrants. Treasurer Nilsson thinks the proposal is a little reactionary.
Attorney Schultz stated that the fire rating would be the same for the parcels
involved in the boundary dispute whether the property was in the City or the
Township, regardless of whether or not the Township had an ordinance requiring
hydrants. Trustee Wiegandt said the only irrigation well systems he has seen
are out west in areas where there was no other readily available water to fight
fires, and in that case the wells were used primarily for irrigation, which
would not be the case in the subdivisions here. The Planning Commission will
investigate the possible benefits and costs of requiring hydrants in
subdivisions.
It was left to the Planning Commission to determine what size subdivisions and/
or which zoning districts the hydrants would be required in, if it was
determined that it would be beneficial to the Township to require them.
According to Attorney Schultz the earliest time for the Boundary Commission’s
adjudicated session would be March, more likely April. The final decision would
be made at the following meeting. April or May would be the very earliest that
a decision will be made.
Commercial Business Meeting - Manchester Plastics has requested to rent the

city of Williamston. There is no Township connection other than probable

FEBRUARY 3, 1998
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order by Supervisor Norman Obst on Tuesday, February 3, 1998 at 7:35 p.m.
The Clerk verified that a quorum was present. Supervisor Obst reviewed the
agenda, adding discussion of the community pool report. Present were:
Supervisor Norman Obst, Clerk Shirley Graham, Treasurer Christine Nilsson,
Trustee Ronald Wiegandt, Trustee Steven Zaban (8:00 p.m.), Township Attorney
Stephen Schultz, and Building Inspector Walter Aven.
FIRE BOARD REPORT - Darrell Brown
The Fire Board had decided it needed the guidance of an attorney in the matter
of creating a fire district, and had interviewed Mark Adams. He had attended
the January 28, 1998 meeting with the City of Williamston and surrounding
townships to discuss the possibility of setting up a fire district for the five
areas. The Mayor of Webberville had also been present. It had been decided to
ask for approval from the City and Townships for a representative from each
municipality to serve on a new District Fire Board Committee which would
proceed with researching the setting up of a fire district. Mr. Brown reported
that the meeting was a positive step toward cooperation between the
governmental units. The amount of money to be contributed would be discussed at
a future meeting.
Supervisor Obst said the issue was whether the present Fire Board had legal
authority to hire an attorney. Members of the municipalities, acting via the
District Fire Board Committee, could hire someone, and send representatives to
attend meetings. Trustee Wiegandt said a resolution was needed, to state that
the Township’s current representatives were authorized to make a decision to
employ an attorney and spend the necessary funds. He felt practices of the past
47 years had worked well, but now other procedures must be followed. IT WAS
MOVED BY TRUSTEE WIEGANDT, SECONDED BY TREASURER NILSSON, THAT THE PRESENT
TOWNSHIP FIRE BOARD REPRESENTATIVES BE AUTHORIZED TO MAKE DECISIONS FOR
REASONABLE EXPENDITURES FOR THE USE OF AN ATTORNEY IN THE MATTER OF
ESTABLISHING A FIRE DISTRICT. THE MOTION WAS AMENDED TO ADD APPROVAL OF
ADDITIONAL EXPENDITURES FOR A RECORDING SECRETARY.
Attorney Schultz said two agreeing municipalities could not compel the third to
participate. If agreement could not be reached the present Fire Board would
probably disband and a new arrangement would need to be adopted. [Trustee Zaban
entered the meeting] THE BOARD VOTED ON THE ABOVE MOTION, ALL VOTING IN FAVOR.
The Board appointed Trustee Wiegandt to serve as the Township’s representative
on the District Fire Board Committee, which was a separate entity from the Fire
Board, and would only remain in effect until a decision on fire district had
been made.
ADVISORY COUNCIL REPORT - Intergovernmental Concerns - Rutgar Hoag
The Council had met with City of Williamston representatives to discuss fire
and library concerns. An intergovernmental committee was proposed, to include
one board member and one member at large from each municipality, to discuss
mutual concerns. Municipalities asked to join were the City of Williamston, and
Williamstown, Wheatfield, Leroy and Locke Townships. The Advisory Council
recommended that Jim Ballard be appointed chairperson of the Township’s
Intergovernmental Affairs Committee. IT WAS MOVED BY SUPERVISOR OBST, SECONDED
BY TREASURER NILSSON, PASSED, THAT JAMES BALLARD BE APPOINTED CHAIR OF THE
TOWNSHIP INTERGOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS COMMITTEE. Mr. Hoag then asked that the
Board agree to participate on the proposed intergovernmental committee with the
other four municipalities. He suggested appointing two members for that
committee, and recommended James Ballard as the at-large member. Treasurer
Nilsson agreed to serve as the Board representative for one year.
IT WAS MOVED BY CLERK GRAHAM, SECONDED BY TRUSTEE ZABAN, PASSED, THAT JAMES
BALLARD AND CHRISTINE NILSSON BE APPOINTED TO SERVE ON THE PROPOSED
INTERGOVERNMENTAL COMMITTEE WITH OTHER MUNICIPALITIES. Treasurer Nilsson said
she would inform the City Mayor that the Township was ready to proceed with the
committee.

Zoning Ordinance Revisions: Supervisor Obst had expressed concern about some
proposed changes, and Planning Coordinator Martin had reviewed them with
Planning Consultant Christopher Doozan. Side yard setbacks - Mr. Obst felt
reducing them to as little as ten feet could cause a nuisance. According to
Planning Coordinator Martin, the proposed use of the building could be
ascertained when a building permit was granted, and use as a home occupation
would be regulated by the Zoning Ordinance. Shared driveways - Maintenance
problems could arise. Wording was added to include joint use “and maintenance”
of driveways. Attorney Schultz said maintenance problems would clearly be a
private dispute and the Township should not be involved. Use of nonconforming
lots - Mr. Schultz said changing wording to “lacks sufficient frontage” could
create a situation where access to a nonbuildable lot, which may have been
created specifically as such, could be obtained via an easement on neighboring
property. He suggested the revision not be approved, and additional
consideration be given at a later time. Recreational vehicles - Supervisor Obst
suggested screening from the street be required, and inside storage be
necessary over a certain number of vehicles. Ms. Martin said limits would need
to be set for each zoning district and size of parcel, and an enforcement issue
would be created. Audience member Velma Oesterle suggested the Board not
undertake additional enforcement responsibilities if it did not intend to
require compliance. It was agreed that the wording would remain as submitted.
IT WAS MOVED BY CLERK GRAHAM, SECONDED BY TRUSTEE WIEGANDT, PASSED, THAT THE
BOARD ADOPT PROPOSED REVISIONS TO THE ZONING ORDINANCE, EXCEPTING THE ITEM ON
NONCONFORMING LOTS, AND WITH MODIFICATION OF THE SHARED DRIVEWAYS PROVISION, TO
BECOME EFFECTIVE SEVEN DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION.
Sidewalk Ordinance: Attorney Schultz had drafted language for civil infraction
penalties. There had been much discussion by the Planning Commission regarding
the maintenance and repair of sidewalks. In its recommended form,
responsibility would be directed to adjacent homeowners. IT WAS MOVED BY
TREASURER NILSSON, SECONDED BY TRUSTEE ZABAN, THAT THE PROPOSED SIDEWALK
ORDINANCE BE ADOPTED. Resident Gerald Eidt opposed shifting maintenance of
roadsides from the Road Commission to the property owner. Potential liability
was also shifted from the Township and/or Road Commission to the resident.
Those responsibilities fell on a small number of property owners, while
benefiting a larger number of residents. Opposition to future sidewalks could
occur due to the burden on property owners. He asked that the Board reconsider
requiring homeowners to pay for the replacement of sidewalks, which could be a
financial hardship, and asked that the Township assume the replacement
responsibility. Building Inspector Aven said a problem could arise when a
homeowner had directly caused sidewalk damage, due to landscaping,
construction, etc.
Supervisor Obst said the Township could set up a special assessment district;
Mr. Eidt felt that would be appropriate because it would shift some
responsibility to people who directly benefited from a sidewalk. Clerk Graham
agreed with Mr. Eidt. Treasurer Nilsson stated that a sidewalk ordinance had
been recommended by legal counsel, and the Township should not commit to
sidewalk maintenance when it had no public works department. The ordinance
should not give the Township responsibility for clearing of snow, etc.,
although the Township could choose to provide the service, if desired. Trustee
Wiegandt stated that the Board had not set a policy on the matter. Clerk Graham
said the Township could assess all or a part of the costs. The motion was
amended to include the addition of the following wording in two places in the
ordinance: assess cost to property involved “or benefited”. THE BOARD VOTED ON
THE ABOVE MOTION, AS AMENDED, WHICH PASSED UNANIMOUSLY.
Parks and Recreation Master Plan and Park Site Plan: The plan had been approved
by the Planning Commission and recommended for approval by the Board. Some
small modifications needed to be made in the plan, as noted by Planning

SUPERVISOR OBST. NAYS: NONE.
Treasurer Nilsson stated that the purpose of updating the Parks and Recreation
Master Plan had been to qualify for grants for park development. She asked that
a cost estimate be obtained from McKenna Associates to prepare such a grant.
Fire Hydrants: The Planning Commission had been directed by the Board to
consider requiring hydrants in subdivisions. After receiving a report from
Planning Consultant Doozan, the Planning Commission did not recommend pursuing
such requirements. The Board agreed that the evidence indicated tankers were
just as effective, and in some cases more effective, in providing fire
protection.

The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, March 3, 1998 at 7:39 PM. The Clerk was
asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban, Building Inspector
Aven, and Township Attorney, Steve Schultz.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: Planning Commission -
Woodview Final Plat information.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Lisa Crozier - Michigan Groundwater Stewardship Program.
Farm*A*Syst - helps farmers assess their potential risks of groundwater
contamination. When completed they are eligible for the cost share and credits
for the pesticide program. She would like to keep the program going another
year. They are looking for more farmers to participate. Brochures are available
in the Township office for farmers who may be interested in the program.
FIRE BOARD REPORT - Darrell Brown
The Fire Board received a letter from the Lounsbury's indicating their interest
in letting the Fire Board use at least part of their property for parking. The
Fire Board has hired an attorney. The Architect asked for a recommendation from
the Fire Board to do work for the City of Williamston. There was some interest
in looking at the West Side Deli Building for moving the fire barn down there.
The size of the building is appropriate. There would not have to be any
additions. Looks favorable. Good location. New Equipment that must be purchased
due to state requirements. A resolution was proposed to the Board of Trustees
for creating the Fire District Committee and to hire Mark Adams as an attorney
to represent the Fire Board. The Fire Chief was given the authority to get
specs for a new pumper.
Fire Board Resolution - Clerk Graham moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported that
the Township ratify the proposed Fire Board Resolution authorizing
participation in a multi-jurisdictional Fire District Committee and ratifying
the actions of the Williamston Community Fire Board in contracting for legal
services and appropriating the funds. Motion passed unanimously.
Trustee Zaban had a question on what exactly the Lounsbury’s were proposing for
the use of their property by the fire department. They proposed two options -
1. The entire parcel would be for sale if they can find another location for
their business, or 2. They can locate their business on the front half and the
back half would be available to the fire department for parking.
ATTORNEY’S REPORT - Steve Schultz
Annexation Case - voted 3-1 to approve the annexation, with one member not
present. Received a draft of the boundary commissions findings of fact
supporting their decision. Believe several of the finding of facts to be
clearly erroneous. Failed to mention the loss of tap fees and tax revenues to
the township and the effect the loss of the land would have on the Township’s
Master Plan. One of the proposed findings is that the proposed density of the
development on the property in question would require public water, this is not
true. Another finding that is fairly outrageous regarding street safety stated
that the City of Williamston is subject to local, state and federal regulations
to safety. The Commission did not elaborate on what these regulations were and
they are not tied to the safety issues of the case. Proposed development is
consistent with other development in the city. The president of the Riverwood
Homeowners Association, the subdivision that the proposed development is
consistent with, sent letters to the commission stating why the development is
defective. The fire rating and availability of fire hydrants is the same
regardless of whether the property is in the City or the Township.
The February 12 hearing was to deliberate over the facts and take a vote. After
the vote is taken the Boundary Commission directs its staff to draw up the
papers to determine what the facts are to support the decision. On March 5th
the Boundary Commission will present these findings of facts. The Township has
the opportunity to refute the findings at that time and the Commissioners have
the opportunity to change their vote based on this information. It will then be
45 days before the final decision goes into effect. The case can then be
appealed.
Pines Office Park Condominium Documents - Attorney Schultz needs to talk to
Planning Coordinator Martin about the documents received.
BUILDING PERMITS - Walt Aven
Attended annual Michigan Builder's Conference on the new 1997 code. Housing
starts are down in February for single family homes. Report for February
received and placed on file.
PLANNING COMMISSION REPORT - Mickey Martin
Woodview Subdivision - asking to come to the Planning Commission for Final Plat
Approval. Their Final Preliminary Plat Approval has expired. They are asking
for an extension on the Preliminary Plat Approval along with the Final Plat
Approval. Attorney Schultz stated that the Township’s Zoning Ordinance is
stricter than the State Statute. The language in our ordinance states that the
extension may be granted if applied for prior to the expiration date. Does not
give us the flexibility to approve the extension after the expiration. The
Township would have to amend or waive the ordinance to give the extension. If
there were no problems it would take two months to get a new Final Preliminary
and Final Plat (May). Doug Price stated that he agrees the Final Preliminary
Plat did expire. He didn't realize he needed to get the extension. Mr. Price
has all the signatures required from the County for Final Plat Approval. He is
submitting today exactly what the density option states. He has complied with,
agreed to, and conformed to the agreement. He believes they fall under the
previous Zoning Ordinance. He will end up with the same product as was
originally approved. He believes the Township can approve the Preliminary Plat
and the Final Plat at the same time. Nothing has changed since the Final
Preliminary Plat was first approved. Supervisor Obst and Planning Coordinator
Martin agreed that it is probably possible to approve both the Final
Preliminary Plat and the Final Plat at the same time, even though this is not
something that has been done before.
Attorney Schultz stated that the old ordinance has been repealed. The Township
can no longer act under that ordinance. The Township cannot ignore the current
ordinance because that would cause problems for the next case. Unless the
ordinance prohibits it, it should be OK to approve both the Preliminary and
Final Plat in the same meeting. Planning Coordinator Martin will have Planning
Consultant Chris Doozen determine if this approach would be in accordance with
our Zoning Ordinance.
Cardinal Fabricating - applied for building permit for an addition. They didn't
realize they needed a Special Use Permit since it is commercial property. They
also had to get a variance from the Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) since the
building is currently non-conforming. They have received direction from the
Planning Commission. They have been granted a variance to go into the set back
area. The Township has received only positive response from neighbors in
support of the proposed changes by Cardinal Fabricating. Cardinal Fabricating
is asking for prior approval on condition or for the Township Board of Trustees
to hold a special meeting to consider their situation after the Planning
Commission makes their recommendation. They have contractors waiting to build.
Attorney Schultz stated that he would not recommend acting on Cardinal tonight,
as it would be against the Zoning Ordinance. The issue requires a public
hearing before the Planning Commission. The Zoning Ordinance states that “the
Planning Commission SHALL review the findings and SHALL make a report and
recommendation to the board. Board action SHALL base its decision solely on the
basis of the Ordinance Findings of Fact.” This implies the Board must have the
report before they can make a decision. The Board set a special meeting date of
Wednesday March 18th at 3:45 PM to review and vote on the Cardinal Fabricating
issue.
ADVISORY COUNCIL
Helen LeBlanc - Solid Waste Planning Committee. Plan will show what is
currently being done. Current location of land fills, recycling strategies,
etc. Plan will contain future plans for recycling and waste diversion. Need
plan by June, will need to be approved by 60% of municipalities before being
forwarded to the state. The state can then approve or disapprove the plan.
State requirement to update the plan. The State has established the outline
that will be used.
ASSESSOR’S REPORT - Norm Obst
Taxable values are capped at a 2.7% increase. Assessed values are increasing

construction is assessed at current value. Equalization stated an 8.5% increase
for residential and an 18.48% increase for agricultural properties.

Russell Aker - The Township Board has received Constable Dahlstrom’s report.
Debris seems to be gone. Mr. Aker did his own grading without obtaining a
grading permit from the Township. Clerk Graham stated that other junk there is
still a problem - rusting iron/steel and wood piles. Original complaint has
been taken care of. Supervisor Obst asked if it meets the requirements for a
nuisance under the nuisance ordinance. If it does, then that avenue should be
investigated. Building Inspector Aven stated that he needs a permit only if he
brought in more than 50 yards of material. It does not appear that he has done
that. Attorney Schultz stated that a second issue is if the concrete is
considered clean fill. If it is not, then the fact that it is covered up does
not eliminate the problem. The burden of proof is on the land owner to prove
that it is clean fill. Doug Price stated that he believes there is a greater
issue of the township being consistent. The Township should alert the health
department and the drain commission to these problems. Treasurer Nilsson asked
what our course of action is for these types of things. Attorney Schultz stated
that the Township can Issue an appearance ticket to demand that it be cleaned
up in a certain amount of time. Ticket brings him in front of a magistrate in
Mason. They give him a chance to clean it up and if he doesn't, then he can be
fined $500. Other option is to seek an injunction. The Board decided they will
contact Carol Valor of the Drain Commission and give her a list of possible
violations to investigate.

Planning Commission Report - Mickey Martin
Supervisor Obst had a question on the Planning Commission minutes not providing
the roll call vote by name or number of votes on each issue. The minutes simply
state whether or not the motion passed. This mode of reporting is stated in the
Planning Commission’s bylaws. Supervisor Obst believes it may be perceived as

Hideaway Woods #4 - Site Plan Review Revised. Final Preliminary Plat. Went
through final plat in December of 1996. The plan was brought back to the
Planning Commission to provide only six lots that would perk with on site
septic systems since the City is not releasing the sewer and water capacity to
the Township. If the lots are not served by public sewer then they would have
to be developed at R1-S standards. The six lots do not meet those standards.
The Planning Commission made their recommendations and a variance must be
sought to create the lots.
Carl McIntosh - Not had an opportunity to do anything with the Planning
Commission recommendations. He Intends to follow through on each of the items
before the next Planning Commission meeting. Planning Chair Martin recommended
that a majority of the conditions be met before the Board votes on it. It will

Supervisor Obst moved that the plat be approved per the 4 conditions set forth

is still looking to obtain the 55 sewer hookups. These six lots will be
available to hookup to the sewer lines, but they will not be required to hook

Doug Price asked how large the lots are. 21,000 - 31,000 square feet. R1
zoning. They are non conforming lots. That is what the variance would be
required for. This is an issue because the City has not approved the sewer that

Woodview Phase III - Final Preliminary Plat And Final Plat Approval. The Final

MAY 12, 1998
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, May 12, 1998 at 7:44 PM. The Clerk was
asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham
stated a quorum was present and recorded the following; Supervisor Obst, Clerk
Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban, Building Inspector
Aven and Attorney Stephen Schultz.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: Change of July Board
meeting date; cemetery board letter authorization regarding payments; Mitchell
Road access by the schools; Hideaway Woods 4 preliminary plat approval.
Attorney Questions - Stephen Schultz
Fairfax homes annexation was reported on previously. Pre-trial conference with
Judge Houk regarding the sewer agreement. Final Pre Trial on June 15th. Trial
Date will probably be set in July if not settled by then. Proposed site plan
for pond on the Foote property.
Attorney Schultz left at 7:50 PM.

PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
Has two items requiring Board action tonight:
1. Approve the preliminary plat of Hideaway Woods #4. Variance was obtained
from ZBA and all other conditions of the Planning Commission have been met.
Moved by Clerk Graham to approve the Preliminary Plat of Hideaway Woods #4.
Seconded by Treasurer Nilsson. Motion passed unanimously.
2. Foote Pond Issue - held special meeting on April 28th.
Moved by Supervisor Obst and seconded by Treasurer Nilsson to approve the site
plan for a pond at 900 Gulick Rd with the following conditions:
1.   Testing is permitted in accordance with the Strata Environmental Services
outline. The Township will be fully notified in advance of the exact times and
dates of when the testing will be conducted so if the Township wishes it may
have a Township Engineer and/or representative present.
2.   The plans are to be reviewed and approved by the Township Building
Official with respect to the Uniform Building Code Requirements.
3.   The applicant is required to move forward with improvements related to the
berming and the storm drainage system; specifically the storm drainage system
as noted on the RC Associates plan. The drainage system must also be extended
forward north on the west property line to insure that the removal or drainage
of surface waters will not adversely affect adjoining properties including all
of Mr. Sikarskie’s property. This will result in changing the RC Associates
site plan with regard to drainage. This also includes in part that the toe of
the slope on the west side be set back ten feet from the property line and that
the berm along the west line be reshaped to be undulating in form, with a one
on three slope. A new site plan is required to indicate the above stipulations.
4.   Evergreen trees shall be planted at 10 to 15 feet on-center in abundance
on the exterior of the berm as indicated on the landscape illustration exhibit
A.
5.   Other berms on the property are to be reshaped in accordance with the RC
Associates plan: no steeper than a slope of one foot vertical to three feet
horizontal and no berm higher than eight feet. The site plan is to be modified
to show no berms higher than eight feet.
6.   Improvements to the berm and drainage along the west property line are to
be completed within 60 days, except drainage and berm improvements along Mr.
Sikarskie’s property line are to be completed within 30 days.
7.   A performance guarantee must be submitted to cover all indicated
improvements including assuring proper operation of the storm drainage system
and to assure that the project will have no adverse impact on groundwater
levels and quality, and no adverse impact on surrounding wells. Two years after
completion of the approved site plan, if there are no indicated adverse
impacts, the need for the guarantee will be terminated.
8.   A monitoring well must be left installed. During future drought conditions
a report from the monitoring well must be provided to the Township at its
request. A low water level must be established at the time the hydrogeological
study is submitted so that the Township knows what to look for in the future
when they ask for monitoring well data.
9.   The applicant agrees to refrain from using well water to maintain the pond
level when a water table emergency occurs as declared by the Township.
10.   The applicant understands that should the above testing indicate changes
are needed, then it is possible the RC Associates plan may need further
modifications to all aspects including possibly, the size of the pond.
The applicant’s attorney, Mr. Jeffrey Ray, said the motion is not the same as
the motion at the Planning Commission. The applicant does not agree with item 5
- a berm height of no higher than 8 feet.
Mr. Sikarskie was pleased to see that the motion addresses the issues with his
property for drainage, but believes the siltation problems still need to be
addressed. Latest rain overran the current solutions. Fences are down because
they are full of clay. Plan sounds more appropriate than what was previously
submitted. Would like to see the berms no higher than six feet to conform to
privacy fence ordinance and also to control the siltation problems.
Mickey Martin - suggesting opening it up for discussion since new information
from STS was just received today. Point number 1 of motion. Supervisor Obst
would propose to change the motion incorporating STS recommendations.
Ed Everett of Strata Environmental Services - Greatest concern would be is the
water able to migrate out horizontally? There will be some vertical leakage.
There is sand below the clay. Water will tend to stay in the clay and migrate
out horizontally. Bottom is going to be relatively impermeable. STS has
proposed installing piezometers 10 feet below the bottom of the pond. This will
give no information relative to what leakage will occur from the pond. Have
suggested that a skin will develop on soil borings. If pond leaks so much that
it permeates lower levels then the pumps will be running continuously. Pond
right now is holding rain water. Not a permeable liner, or it would have dried
up by now. Points 4 and 5 of the STS letter are what Strata is concerned with.
Problem with data logger - not much room for it in a production well. Become
much less accurate at higher levels (100 feet). Prefer to do it manually which
is acceptable to the state. Will validate their procedures. 10 - don't know
what the impact will be on the water levels yet. Before they get to an adverse
impact they will slow down pumping and/or stop pumping for a period of time. 11
- monitor levels 3 times per day. Arbitrary number. Draw down is straight curve
- time is logarithmic. If water levels are not changing then tests could get
further apart. Expect to eventually get to testing at once per day. Not adverse
to earlier readings to make sure the aquifer is responding as expected. Item 12
- evaporation rates based on the driest month of the year (July) - highest rate
of evaporation. Used as estimate for required water to maintain pond. Does not
include rainfall in the evaporation equation - only evaporation. Will monitor 3
times per day during pond filling (conductness). Changes in aquifer are
typically not instantaneous. If see changes in a day or week then the item
needs to be addressed. No need to monitor 3 times per day. Little chance of
upwelling.
Bob Hayes - Hydrogeologist with STS. Numbers 4, 5 and 6 go together of STS
letter. Suggested alternative method for testing samples and thought it
appropriate to test 10 feet below the bottom of the pond.
Bob Hayes and Ed Everett agreed to get together and work out their differences
for testing.
Mr. Sikarskie - Explains how quickly the clay seals the bottom of the lake -
that is exactly what has happened to his garden. Concerned about mounding
affecting his property. Mr. Everett stated that there are three points in the
pond that are below 95.5 feet. Test will be performed to determine whether
horizontal leakage occurs. Supervisor Obst stated it was acceptable that the
two engineers work this out.
Attorney Ray - would like the issue removed from the table at this time until
the geologists have worked things out. His client still has a problem with item
5 of the motion - berm height. Some points may exceed 8 feet due to slope of
the land. Item 7 regarding performance guarantees - no mention of an amount.
Amount to be determined by the Building Inspector. Unique situation in that 90
percent of the construction has been completed. Building Inspector Aven will
require an engineered site plan that is sealed by an engineer and determine at
that time what the amount of the bond would be.
Mr. Foote commented on Item 5 of the motion - He plans to make it more rolling
instead of just a straight edge on the west side. Will leave the road side and
the north east side the same. Proposing the changes where the current slope is
steeper than three to one.
Clerk Graham had a question about going back to original grade. Mr. Foote
stated the ten foot area will go to peaks and valleys to have catch basins. It
will be taken back to capacity that will handle the drainage. It cannot go back
to original grade.
Mr. Sikarskie - Does not believe the berm is harmonious with the area.
Unnatural looking. Too abrupt. If drainage system takes away the water that is
good, but still not happy with how it looks.
Mr. Foote - stated that the Township’s Planning Consultant, Chris Doozen has
said in the past that the privacy fence issue does not apply here.
Mr. Sikarskie showed pictures of the area prior to construction and now to the
Board. Asking for six feet maximum on the berm height. Believes they should be
treated as privacy fences since Mr. Foote himself said that the berms functions
are as a privacy fence. Attorney Ray said that he has no right to control
neighbor's berms. Mr. Foote now saying purpose of berm is for landscaping.
Mr. Foote stated that once the toe of the berm is moved back to 10 feet from
the property line he would have to lose some height to get it 3 to 1. Planning
Chair Martin stated there is no height limit - it must be a 3 to 1 ratio.
Discussion during planning commission was that they would be an average of 8
feet.
Treasurer Nilsson suggested the Board not go forward with the site plan
approval tonight. Supervisor Obst asked if height issues are not resolved, can
the drainage issues still be discussed separately tonight? Mr. Harold Powell
commented that if the Board approves only part of the motion tonight then the
Foote's are putting themselves at risk. Supervisor Obst moved to withdraw the
motion, seconded by Treasurer Nilsson. Motion was withdrawn. Discussion began
regarding alleged Zoning Ordinance violations.
Mr. Foote has a different opinion of the damage than Mr. Sikarskie. Wants to
have an engineer look at the property. Previous drainage of the garden was to a
ditch on Mr. Foote's property. Mr. Sikarskie said the elevation was raised by
the air strip put in by Mr. Ploucha. Water flow out of the garden was affected
by the air strip. They put a ditch in to drain the water off the garden and the
air strip. Grapes died this year because of standing water. Agrees that the
ditch did drain onto Mr. Foote's property. The 12 foot berm has dumped not only
water, but also clay onto the garden. The level of the land is sinking. Mr.
Foote does not believe there is currently any water draining onto the garden.
Mr. Sikarskie believes there is still water coming from the berm onto his
garden. Silt fence filled up with so much silt that it ruptured over. More clay
was dumped into the garden. Mr. Foote does not believe there have been
problems. Wants to have an engineer come out and look at the garden and take
soil samples. Supervisor Obst read Mr. Sikarskie's letter into the record.
Strata will take soil samples of the garden. Mr. Sikarskie believes the clay
has gone down further than the 6 - 8 inches proposed for the test. Will go down
further than the 8 inches in one sample. Will take 2-3 weeks to get the test
results back. Samples will be sent to an independent lab. Zoning Ordinance
states that changes will not adversely affect drainage on neighboring
properties.
Planning Commission to make a recommendation to the Township Board regarding
item 5 of the previous motion - berm height. The Planning Commission needs to
work out what is harmonious for the area.
Clerk Graham moved that item five should be amended that berm height should be
a maximum of six feet with a 3 to 1 slope. seconded by Supervisor Obst for the
sole purpose of putting the subject into discussion at the next meeting. Motion
defeated 3-2. With Clerk Graham and Supervisor Obst voting for the motion and
Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt and Trustee Zaban voting against the
motion.

JUNE 2, 1998
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Obst on Tuesday, June 2, 1998 at 7:39 PM. The Clerk was
asked to record who was present and if a quorum was present. Clerk Graham

Graham, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban, Building Inspector

ATTORNEY REPORT - Stephen Schultz
Little action on the law suit with the city due to City Attorney Cox failing to
return phone calls from Township Attorney Schultz. Pre Trial set for June 15th
will have to be postponed due to Attorney Schultz being out of the country on
the 15th. Hopes to set the Pre Trial for the 19th.
Fire Board Authority letter of incorporation. Legally looks fine. Attorney
Schultz wanted to clarify Article 7 dealing with levy of property taxes. The
Fire Authority will have the power to levy taxes. If the millage requested
exceeds 2 mils there would be a ballot proposal in all municipalities that make
up the Fire Authority.. If 50% + 1 of the population of all municipalities
combined pass the millage, then the millage would go into effect for all
municipalities in the Fire Authority even if the voters in any given
municipality voted it down. The Township would not have a veto, neither would
any other community participating in the authority. According to Public Act 57
of 1988, two mils is the maximum that the Fire Authority could levy without a
vote of the citizens. Trustee Wiegandt stated that depending on how many of the
surrounding communities decided to participate, the initial levy would probably
be lower than the two mils.
Treasurer Nilsson raised the question of the letter from Sherry Stein of
Foster, Swift... concerning deferred compensation plan. This is on the agenda
under new business, but it was decided to discuss it while Attorney Schultz was
present. Ms. Stein is contacting Carol Johnston at Aetna to resolve how the
deferred compensation plan was initially set up and to discuss the changes that
have occurred in the Tax Code that require the Township to update its plan. The
deferred compensation plan is currently managed by Aetna. [The Township must
conform by December 31, 1998 with the IRS Small Business Job Protection Act of
1996.]
Trustee Zaban asked if the City has not responded to the current proposal yet,
is the likelihood that we go to trial increasing? Attorney Schultz stated that
he was not encouraged by current situation. Supervisor Obst stated that the
City indicated they had formed a committee to work on the agreement but the
committee has had difficulty meeting. Attorney Schultz stated that the trial
date has been set in September and that the slight delay in the pre trial
should not cause the trial to be delayed further.
While Attorney Schultz is out of the Country the following attorneys from
Foster, Swift can be consulted: Attorney John Seurynck for ordinance
violations; Attorney Bill Fahey for items concerning the litigation with the
City; and Attorney Brian Goodenough for rezoning issues.

Dexter Rezoning - There is a request from Mr. Joe Dexter to rezone his 40 acre
Ag Commercial lot to Ag Small Farm so that the property could be split into 10+
acre parcels. Recommendation was to approve the rezoning. The Planning
Commission needs final action on this item this evening. One possible option is
to rezone just the one 10+ acre lot and leave the remaining 30 acres in Ag
Commercial by joining it to the attached parcel. Supervisor Obst asked Mr.
Dexter's opinion on the proposed option. This was not acceptable to Mr. Dexter.
He would have to pay to have it rezoned later. The additional 80 acres that Mr.
Dexter owns is split by a Consumers Energy right of way. Mr. Dexter believes he
would be frozen by having property he couldn't do anything with. The State
purchasing his Land Development Rights is not a very realistic option in the
near future for him because this Township does not participate with matching
funds. Planning Chair Martin does not think that this Township has any worse
chance than any other Township since it is not a requirement that the Township
has matching funds for purchase. Only one Township in the State has this option
through a separate millage. Mr. Dexter believes the State is looking for larger
tracts of land and believes it is becoming more and more difficult to operate a
farm in this Township economically. Planning Vice Chair Jennings wanted to make

because they felt there weren't other viable options in this case. The Planning
Commission believes it must review the agriculture guidance for the Master
Plan. Trustee Zaban stated that part of the reason the Master Plan needs to be
reviewed is because the population encroachment is making it very difficult to
farm in this area. Supervisor Obst suggested rezoning just the 10 acres and
waive the fee for any future applications on the remaining 30 acres. Mr. Dexter
stated that he would like to split the property into three 14 acre parcels.
Intent is to sell one now. Hopes to farm another 8 years and then retire again.
Does not want to go through this process again at that time. Trustee Wiegandt
moved to approve the rezoning request of Joseph Dexter, 43.9 acres, parcel #
3303-03-22-300-007 from Ag Commercial to Ag Small Farm, as recommended by the
Planning Commission minutes of May 19, 1998. Seconded by Clerk Graham. Motion
passed unanimously.

address the fairness issue and to review the Master Plan. Trustee Zaban moved
that the Planning Commission review the Master Plan. Supported by Trustee
Wiegandt. Brief discussion followed. Motion passed unanimously.

Grand River and Zimmer Intersection - Brian Jennings
Due to late notice from the Post Office of the change on their move date, the
Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) and the Michigan State Police had
filled their schedules for the summer and were not available to reschedule this
study until August. The counters that were recently at the intersection were
placed by a different Division of MDOT that does periodic samplings throughout
the County. It was just a coincidence that this intersection happened to be on
the schedule for periodic counts at this time.
Letter From The Ingham County Road Commission On Vanneter And Mitchell Roads -
Brian Jennings
The Ingham County Road Commission voted to not take over jurisdiction of
Mitchell and Vanneter Roads around the Williamston Middle and Senior High
Schools. Reasons given were 1) They have information suggesting that the City
of Williamston will be attempting to annex these roads in the near future. The
Commission did not want to put any money into these roads only to have to turn
them over to the City; and 2) the current state of disrepair on these roads is
such that it would be several years before the County would have the money to
fix them properly. If the Township can get the roads up to specs and eliminate
the annexation threat the County will take another look at the situation.

JUNE 30, 1998
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Norman Obst at 7:40 p.m. Clerk Shirley Graham stated
that a quorum was present. Present were Supervisor Norman Obst, Clerk Shirley
Graham, Treasurer Christine Nilsson, Trustee Ronald Wiegandt, Trustee Steven
Zaban, and Building Inspector Walter Aven.
The agenda was reviewed, with the following additions: John Kane request for
performance bond refund, and Williamston swimming pool report.
FIRE BOARD REPORT - Darrell Brown
The incorporation meeting of the Northeast Ingham Emergency Services Authority
had been held, with all area municipalities present except Leroy Township. Mr.
Brown felt the new board would be a positive addition for the area, and
complimented all parties involved in the project. [Leroy Township signed at a
later date.]
PLANNING COMMISSION REPORT - Brian Jennings
Omnipoint Communications - The Planning Commission had approved the application
for a special land use permit for colocation of a telecommunications antenna on
an existing tower, with conditions which needed to be met. All necessary
materials had not been received, and no action was requested at this meeting.
Hideaway Woods No. 4 - A request for final plat approval had been received, and
it was essentially the same as the approved final preliminary plat. Approval of
the plat was recommended by the Planning Commission. It was moved by Clerk
Graham, seconded by Trustee Wiegandt, PASSED, that the final plat for Hideaway
Woods No. 4 be approved as submitted on the mylar copy. Clerk Graham signed the
mylar and returned it to Hideaway Woods representative Carl McIntosh.
The Pines Office Park - A site plan for this project had been approved two
years ago, with an extension granted in 1997. The Planning Commission and the
Township Attorney agreed that the Zoning Ordinance allowed only one extension,
and site plan approval had now expired. The applicant had been advised to
submit a new application for the project, and told the cost of the review would
be minimal if there were no major changes in the site plan. Clerk Graham said
there had been discussion about a reduced fee for the application. Supervisor
Obst suggested the usual fee of $1500 be requested, which would be placed in an
escrow account, and the unused portion would be refunded to the applicant. The
Board agreed.
Susan Neller Stable and Riding Arena - A hearing was held on June 16, 1998 with
a special meeting on June 23 for deliberation, on the special land use permit
for a commercial stable and riding arena. The application was recommended for
approval by the Planning Commission, with six conditions. The Commission had
reviewed the cutting of trees which might be necessary to allow proper site
distance from a commercial driveway. Moving of the driveway to the west of the
property had been recommended, to lessen its impact on the neighbor to the
east, along with the planting of a double row of trees along the driveway.
Commission Chair Mickey Martin had investigated soil conditions at the west
property line, and had indicated to the applicant where the Commission thought
the driveway should be located. A new site plan had been received, which
indicated where the manure management was to be located. The proposed septic
system was to have been reviewed by Commissioner Robert Hayes, but no report
was available. The Township Attorney had submitted a proposed change in the
written agreement which was required by the Zoning Ordinance.
It had been recommended by the Planning Commission that the driveway be paved
750 feet from the road, with a double row of trees to be planted 15 feet on
center along its east side for 750 feet. These trees were not shown on the new
site plan. The recommended setback from the road for the curve in the driveway
was also not indicated.
Supervisor Obst read a letter from neighboring property owner Larry Salstrom,
which asked for inclusion of additional wording in the written agreement which
would address his concerns. Mr. Obst also suggested the inclusion of an item
stating that violations of the agreement would be considered as violations of
the Zoning Ordinance, and the special land use permit could be revoked for
continual violations of the agreement. Clerk Graham observed that the new site
plan did not address several of the conditions recommended by the Planning
Commission, including paving of the driveway, and said dimensions should be
more completely shown on the plan. It was moved by Clerk Graham, seconded by
Treasurer Nilsson, that the matter be tabled because all information was not
available.
Susan Neller stated she did not feel the location of the trees and the driveway
curve had been specified by the Planning Commission. As shown on the plan, the
curve was located 500 feet from the road, and she disagreed with some of the
Commission’s recommendations. Maynard Beery, the applicant’s wastewater
management system designer, said he had not had the recommendations when he
drew the site plan. The driveway had been moved about 150 feet to the west on
the new plan. Mrs. Neller felt driveway paving would be a constant problem with
the wet land at the western part of the property. She did not think paving and
trees were both needed. Placing trees along the driveway would limit the use of
her land and she did not want to place them there; she would be willing to
plant them along Mr. Salstrom’s property line. Clerk Graham agreed that trees
should not be planted on wet land.
Trustee Zaban said concerns could be addressed at this meeting, and thought the
biggest issue was the amount of driveway paving that had been recommended, and
which he felt was excessive. Mr. Salstrom said the Planning Commission’s
decision to require 750 feet of paving had been based on the effects of
prevailing winds and dust which would blow onto his property.
Supervisor Obst asked if delay of a decision would be harmful to Mrs. Neller.
She said she wanted to build as soon as possible, and asked for a decision at
this meeting. She felt the decision should not be delayed because one person
had not read the information submitted by Mr. Berry. Mr. Beery said the
information had been given to Commissioner Hayes late this afternoon. The
proposed septic system had been approved by the Ingham County Health
Department. He would prepare a new site plan with changes after a Board
decision had been made.
The Board discussed specific issues raised by the Planning Commission.
Driveway - Mr. Salstrom felt this commercial venture would negatively impact
his property values and aesthetics. Conditions recommended by the Planning
Commission had met his concerns, but the new site plan did not reflect all of
these changes.
Paving - Mr. Salstrom stated the Zoning Ordinance required paving of commercial
driveways, except where that provision was waived by the Township. He had
requested that 1000 feet be paved but was agreeable with the 750 decided upon
by the Commission. He requested that the Planning Commission’s recommendations
be adopted by the Township Board. Mrs. Neller said she understood commercial
drives were required to be paved, but asked for a waiver from that requirement
as a farm driveway. She planned on paving the length of a truck and trailer (40
to 50 feet). She said this was an agricultural business. Horses did not walk
well on paved surfaces, and paving 750 feet would limit that use to half the
driveway length. A paved drive would be difficult to maintain over wet soils.
In the written agreement she was charged with controlling dust, which she felt
was sufficient. Trees would also limit dust problems. She planned to do
training of horses in the mornings and lessons in the afternoon, with as many
as five people possibly present at one time in the evening. Lessons would
usually involve one car each hour. They would be closed on Mondays but would
receive deliveries and other equipment could use the driveway on those days.
She said a ten stall barn was not equivalent to a factory or other commercial
operation, and suggested the ordinance be revised to separate types of
commercial operations. Not all commercial driveways should be paved. Trees
along the west side of the property would also inhibit effects of the wind.
Treasurer Nilsson said this was an example of a case where paving should not be
required. Commissioner Harold Powell stated that he favored the operation, but
felt the 750 feet of paving requested would best protect the neighbors from
dust carried by the prevailing winds. Mr. Salstrom said the applicant had
stated previously that as many as three lessons might be given in an hour. He
expected the operation to be a success, and wanted to be protected against its
impact.
Trees - Treasurer Nilsson thought the trees would be more desirable than paving
for controlling dust. Mrs. Neller preferred planting around the adjoining
property rather than along her driveway, to leave her property open. Mr.
Salstrom said the purpose of paving and trees was to minimize the impact of
vehicle activity, and he did not believe trees along his property line would
accomplish that.
Supervisor Obst suggested requiring the paving of 40 feet, with the written
agreement to state that 750 feet of paving would be required if dust became a
problem in the future. Mrs. Neller agreed. Commissioner Powell stated that the
driveway curve should be located 750 from the road so it didn’t follow Mr.
Salstrom’s property line, but felt the trees could be planted wherever Mrs.
Neller wanted. Mrs. Neller said she would move the driveway curve back to the
750 foot location.
Donna Anton, 240 Turner Road, also spoke as a neighbor, saying the driveway was
now proposed to be located closer to her property, but she had no objection.
Trees would be better placed along Mr. Salstrom’s property line, which would
not preclude Mrs. Neller’s use of her land. She felt the stable and arena would
add to the area and be in harmony with current surroundings.
Mr. Salstrom said he was asking for the conditions recommended by the Planning
Commission. Trees along a commercial driveway would do the best job of
minimizing the potential negative impact.
The Board voted on the above motion, which failed. Member Graham voted in favor
of the motion, and members Obst, Nilsson, Wiegandt and Zaban were opposed.
The Board reviewed the proposed change in the written agreement as suggested by
Township Attorney Stephen Schultz, and agreed that it should be included. Mrs.
Neller asked that a provision be added regarding the ability to rebuild in the
case of a catastrophic loss. Mr. Obst said the Zoning Ordinance contained such
a provision. If additional paving were to be added in the event of dust
problems, that provision should also be added to the agreement. Treasurer
Nilsson supported paving 40 to 50 feet, with a review if dust resulting from
the unpaved drive was detrimental to Mr. Salstrom in the future, and she agreed
with trees along his property line. Trustee Wiegandt said unmaintained trees
along a driveway could pose a problem for emergency vehicles, and favored
plantings along Mr. Salstrom’s property. The site plan did not indicate the
composition of the driveway, and dirt roads required maintenance. This drive
was essentially a private road, which the Board did not allow. He felt paving
should extend beyond 50 feet, because dust problems could be expected to result
from a dirt drive. He was concerned about making a decision when all
information was not in place. Trustee Zaban said the recommended 750 feet of
paving was excessive.
It was moved by Supervisor Obst, seconded by Trustee Zaban, that the Township
Board approve the Neller special land use permit, subject to the following
conditions: (1) driveway to be located as shown on current site plan, (2)
proposed septic system must be found to be acceptable to the Township once
additional information is received from Mr. Hayes and possibly Mrs. Neller if
desired, (3) approval of written agreement with revisions, (4) paving of drive
required 375 feet back from road, (5) screening by evergreen trees to be
located along Salstrom property line, a staggered double row 15 feet on center,
375 feet from the road, (6) curve in driveway to be located 750 feet from road,
(7) a new site plan to be submitted with required changes and meeting approval
of the Township. Changes in the written agreement would include: (1)
modification as suggested by the Township Attorney, (2) insertion of paragraph
regarding violations of the agreement, (3) addition of a paragraph stating that
upon future determination of the Township Board that dust is a nuisance to
neighboring property, the Board may require paving to a length of 750 feet, as
agreed to by Mrs. Neller, and (4) addition of paragraph regarding the right to
rebuild in the event of catastrophic loss, as set forth in the Zoning
Ordinance, and (5) no building permit will be approved until these conditions
are met.
Clerk Graham asked if movement of the driveway ten feet to the east would place
it on drier ground; Mrs. Neller said it would. Commissioner Powell said
locating it 60 feet from the west property line, as presently shown, avoided
the worst of the wetness. Commissioner. Hayes’ concern had been for the
operation and maintenance of the septic system. He had provided information,
but it did not cover performance of the systems. Vegetation would be an
integral part of the system. The system was approved by the Health Department,
and Mr. Beery said the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality found this
type of system desirable. A problem that could result would be that not enough
wastewater would be generated and the system would dry up. Plants would need to
be checked to see that it was working properly. If the system failed, there
would be a potential for odor, but any surface flow would not be in the
direction of neighbors, and there would be no immediate impact. This system had
low maintenance requirements and no mechanical components. If it didn’t perform
as expected, an alternative system would be installed.
Supervisor Obst questioned approving the plan when many items needed to be
completed. It was decided that he and Planning Coordinator Mickey Martin would
review new materials when they were received, and a building permit would not
be issued until the site plan was approved. Mr. Obst told the applicant all
details requested must be included in a new site plan. The Clerk asked that
trees be noted as being the required minimum of five feet in height, ten feet
off the neighbor’s property, and that other neighboring property tree locations
be shown. Measurements of neighboring properties should be shown. The Board
voted on the above motion, which was approved unanimously. Mrs. Neller was told
two sets of plans would be needed for review by the building inspector.

MINUTES
AUGUST 6, 1998
The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called
to order by Supervisor Norman Obst at 7:40 p.m. Clerk Shirley Graham stated
that a quorum was present. Present were Supervisor Obst, Clerk Graham,
Treasurer Christine Nilsson, Trustee Ronald Wiegandt, Trustee Steven Zaban and
Building Inspector Walter Aven.
The agenda was reviewed, with the following additions: request for outdoor
concert, alleged lead problem at Capitol City Rifle Club, letter from Fred
Foote requesting appointment, meeting with Marvin Fouty on condominium
ownership, and a Board of Review resignation and vacancy.
TOWNSHIP ATTORNEY’S REPORT - Stephen Schultz
Attorney Schultz reported that meetings had been scheduled with the City of
Williamston to discuss ongoing litigation. No trial date had been set.
Supervisor Obst raised the question about allowing an outdoor music concert,
which had been requested on Township property. Mr. Schultz said such a use was
not specified in the Zoning Ordinance. Section 2.07 deals with temporary uses,
but the types of events referred to as outdoor events were usually carnivals,
etc., held by nonprofit organizations. Possibilities were that (1) the use was
intended to be totally unregulated, or (2) the use had not been contemplated
when the ordinance was written but was not intended to be left as an
unregulated use. Section 2.08 deals with uses not otherwise included. The
ordinance provides uses by right or by special use, and if not listed a use
cannot take place in a district. A use could be allowed by the Township Board
under certain circumstances, or the Board could refer the matter to the
Planning Commission for a recommendation on amending the ordinance to include a
specific use.
Based on the concerns about traffic, parking, temporary structures, noise,
nuisance, police, etc., Mr. Schultz did not believe the Township had intended a
use such as an outdoor concert to proceed without regulation. The Planning
Commission could be asked to suggest an appropriate district and determine
conditions of the use. The planned concert could not go forward because such a
use was not now allowed. Mr. Schultz recommended referral to the Planning
Commission, with the concert promoter informed that such a use was not
permitted, and told that a revision of the Zoning Ordinance would be addressed.
Under the Rural Zoning Act a use could not be banned; a district and conditions
of use must be designated.
Supervisor Obst said a letter had been received from Jeff Foote’s attorney, to
which he had responded that he would bring the matter to the Board for
authorization to take action to bring the site into compliance with the Zoning
Ordinance. Mr. Schultz said the ordinance provided for injunctive relief to
prohibit use or to impose penalties, or the use of an appearance ticket, which
would impose a penalty. Also, Mr. Foote could be cited for violation of the
Nuisance Ordinance. Since there was no question that this was a violation of
the Zoning Ordinance, it could be turned over to the Zoning Official
(Supervisor Obst) for action. Jim Sikarskie, 866 Gulick Road, asked about
enforcement of the Soil Sedimentation Act. Mr. Schultz said the Township did
not have authority to enforce the Act. The Township was dealing with a grading
permit and approval of a site plan, and soil erosion was part of that process.
Remediation was also part of that issue.
A letter had been received which alleged a public health problem from lead in
surface water at the Capitol City Rifle Club, and Mr. Obst asked what measures
were available. Mr. Schultz said the Township had no ordinance to deal with
public health issues or environmental issues. Such authority resided with the
Ingham County Health Department and the Michigan Department of Environmental
Quality. The Township could adopt an ordinance to address public health, safety
and welfare regarding environmental issues. Supervisor Obst stated that the
Township would notify appropriate agencies of the issue. [Mr. Schultz left the
meeting.]
PLANNING COMMISSION REPORT - Mickey Martin
Planning Commission Chair Mickey Martin reported that the Commission had held a
public hearing on the proposed grant application for development of the
Township park. The recommendation was that the application be remanded back to
the Township Board until appropriate matching funds had been raised through
fundraising or a cash match. Results of the open land survey, as it pertained
to the park, had indicated 84 respondents would help raise funds for the park,
while 206 said they would not. Supporting a millage for the park were 137
residents, while 160 did not favor a millage. Ms. Martin said she found the
results to be encouraging. She had been told the grant application process was
very competitive and the Township needed all the points it could get toward
approval of a grant, and cash carried points while in-kind donations did not.
In-kind donations were good, but were also hard to track. Such donations were
easier when a municipality had a public works department to do some of the
work. A total of $3500 had been donated at the present time. A new grant
process for smaller park development projects would become available in April
1999, which might be a better choice for the Township. The Planning Commission
had felt it would be better to delay the application for a grant until the
Township’s share of the money was available.
Treasurer Nilsson agreed it would be better to wait on the application. She
said two prospective Eagle Scouts had asked about projects in the park. A trail
had been mowed and trees had been donated. A sledding hill was being built,
which would form one side of the amphitheater. Parks and Recreation Chair Mike
Nestell wanted to plan a fund-raising event this fall. Trustee Wiegandt said an
item needed to be established in the budget for park maintenance, with work on
development to be addressed more aggressively in the spring.
Advisory Council Chair Rutgar Hoag suggested formation of a Parks Commission,
as this would be a long-term project. The Advisory Council was asked to submit
such a proposal.
It was moved by Trustee Wiegandt, seconded by Treasurer Nilsson, PASSED, that
the Township forego applying for a grant to meet the September 1 deadline,
proceed with fundraising, and review the matter in the spring of 1999.
Kathryn Lo, 290 Sherwood Road, asked how much money the Township had to put
toward the park, and how long it had taken the Township to accumulate the
$95,000 that had been allocated for purchase of the park land. She did not feel
it was feasible to raise a large sum of money within a year. Supervisor Obst
said many people had stated they would support a millage for park development,
and the Township hoped to raise the funds privately.
The Pines Office Park – Ms. Martin reported that a site plan had been approved
two years ago, with an extension granted in 1997. The approval had now expired.
Marvin Fouty had applied for approval of the same plan, and the Planning
Commission had recommended approval. Mr. Fouty was considering making the
project a condominium development, which was not possible under the Zoning
Ordinance as the plan was presently configured. Private roads were a
consideration, but were not allowed by the Township. She said she would meet
with him about condominium possibilities on August 11 at 10:00 a.m. It was
moved by Trustee Wiegandt, seconded by Clerk Graham, PASSED, that the 1996 site
plan for The Pines Office Park be approved, with conditions listed in
Christopher Doozan’s letters in 1996 and 1998.
Treasurer Nilsson asked about the tree ordinance, which the Commission had been
asked to consider. Ms. Martin said she had called Mr. Groh but had not talked
with him. She and Commissioner Nancy Fink had reviewed the proposed ordinance,
and she would again attempt to speak with Mr. Groh.
A Building Board of Appeals, which had been requested by Building Inspector
Walter Aven, was discussed. The Board decided to advertise for prospective
members of that board and the Board of Review in the next Township newsletter.

Township 457 Deferred Compensation Plan – Supervisor Obst said a resolution of
the Board was needed to bring the Township into compliance with the Small
Business Job Protection Act of 1996. This would prevent the Township from
having the ability to use employee funds to settle Township accounts, if it
developed financial difficulty. It was moved by Trustee Zaban, seconded by
Clerk Graham, that the following resolution be adopted. A roll call vote was
taken: Yes – Members Zaban, Nilsson, Obst, Wiegandt and Graham. No – None. The
motion passed unanimously.
RESOLUTION
RESOLVED: That in accordance with the requirements of the Small Business Job
Protection Act of 1996, and notwithstanding Sections 1(b) and 12(b) of the
Township of Williamstown Section 457 Retirement Trust Agreement, said Trust
Agreement established effective September 1, 1992 is hereby terminated
effective as of the date of this meeting of the Township Board; and
FURTHER RESOLVED: That in conjunction with Section 13(a) of the Township of
Williamstown 457 Retirement Trust Agreement, the Trust’s ownership interest in
any asset, including annuity contracts, held by the Trust shall be transferred
to the Township of Williamstown effective as of the date of this meeting of the
Township Board; and
FURTHER RESOLVED: That the First Amendment to the Township of Williamstown 457
Retirement Plan is hereby adopted effective January 1, 1998, or such earlier
date as is required by the Small Business Job Protection Act of 1996 and the
Taxpayer Relief Act of 1997; and
FURTHER RESOLVED: That the Supervisor and Township Clerk are authorized to
execute the First Amendment to the 457 Retirement Plan and any related
documents on behalf of the Township.
NEW BUSINESS
Recycling – Clerk Graham reported that due to changes in hours at Granger
Recycling Center, Martin Wright would be unable to continue with the Township’s
recycling program as presently established. Mr. Wright explained that
participation in the program had steadily increased for the first years, and in
the last two years had reduced slightly. At its peak, 100 to 125 cars
participated, and now on a typical Saturday 65 to 80 people would be served. He
did not feel it was necessary for the Township to provide the service, since
many companies offered curbside recycling, and the Waste Management site in
Williamston was open at no charge. The Township could stop the service and see
what the feedback would be. Having bins available on site all the time did not
work well due to contamination of the recycled materials. Ms. Martin stated the
service should not be discontinued, and someone else should be sought to
provide it. She suggested advertising in the newsletter. Treasurer Nilsson
calculated that the service was costing about $4 per person per month, for
those using the service. The Supervisor asked Clerk Graham to seek a
replacement to provide the service. She would provide a notice for Mr. Wright
to hand out on August 8, his last Saturday in operation, stating that the
service was being discontinued temporarily, noting alternate locations, and
asking if the service was desired and if anyone wanted to provide it.
Request for Outdoor Concert – The Township had received a verbal request from
Nick Gavrilides of Spin Cycle Records to hold an outdoor music event on
property owned by Larry Hughes. Township Attorney Schultz had recommended that
the Township formulate a provision of the Zoning Ordinance that would indicate
where such events could be held, and under what conditions. Such a concert
could not presently be allowed. Clerk Graham said misinformation had been given
to Mr. Gavrilides about the request. Supervisor Obst said the Board should send
a certified letter to him explaining the situation and stating that the matter
would be referred to the Planning Commission for a recommendation. Many issues
were involved in the issuance of such a permit, including health, police,
drinking, etc.
USA Plastics Building – Supervisor Obst noted that the building, located in the
Township, had been purchased by the City of Williamston. He said the City
wanted the Township to give them that land, and the issue could become part of
an agreement worked out regarding the lawsuit with the City. No Board action
was required.
Capitol City Rifle Club, Lead Contamination Issue – Supervisor Obst explained
that a letter had been received from Ger Schultink, expressing concern about
possible lead contamination of surface water at the Rifle Club site. Attorney
Schultz had said the Township had no authority regarding environmental issues,
and should refer such matters to the County or State. Mr. Schultink said his
letter had addressed the widespread lead contamination at gun clubs.
Neighboring resident Larry Hughes had provided results of lead sample tests.
Mr. Hughes was asked how the samples were obtained; he said he had collected
them himself. In answer to a question about trespassing, he stated that he did
not trespass as he was a member of the Rifle Club. Mr. Schultink felt 50 to 100
samples at $25 each would show if there were reason to be concerned, and
environmental agencies should be asked to coordinate a site assessment.
Supervisor Obst said he would ask the Advisory Council to formulate a
recommendation. It was moved by Treasurer Nilsson, seconded by Clerk Graham,
PASSED, that the issue of alleged lead contamination at the Capitol City Rifle
Club, as described by Mr. Schultink, be referred to the Advisory Council for
review. Ray Lemmen, 1800 Germany Road, asked about work being done at the Rifle
Club, and whether they were in violation of the Zoning Ordinance since they
were changing their site. Mr. Obst said a new backstop berm was being
constructed, which was expected to reduce noise. A building permit had been
applied for and the Building Inspector was checking the grade of the berm.
Operation at the club had been voluntarily stopped pending results of a lawsuit
against them. He said new legislation permitted expansion of gun clubs and
reduced townships’ authority over them. However, he would check with the
attorney about whether they were in violation of the ordinance. Larry Hughes,
owner of adjoining land, said the addition of lighting had allowed increased
activity, in violation of their site plan, and he thought a permit had not been
issued for that addition. Mr. Schultink did not think expansion was allowed,
and asked for an opinion from the attorney. Mr. Hughes explained that his
lawsuit was the reason the club was closed; the suit covered use of a driveway
and safety violation of lead flying onto his property. He said changes were
being made due to safety violations. He had asked for a permanent injunction to
close the club due to safety violations. Mr. Schultink asked that the Township
request a copy of a safety audit required by the National Rifle Association to
see if they are in compliance; Mr. Obst agreed to request the audit.
Office Furniture – Clerk Graham said a proposal had been submitted for office
equipment, totaling a $1700 increase over the $2082 that had been approved
previously. It was moved by Clerk Graham, seconded by Trustee Wiegandt, PASSED,
that the budget be modified to approve an increase of $1700 from $2082 that had
been approved for office furniture.
Fred Foote Letter – Mr. Foote had asked to be appointed to a Township board or
commission. Supervisor Obst asked the Advisory Council to suggest where his
service would be most beneficial.

Mr. Aven mentioned the Building Board of Appeals, which Supervisor Obst said

being made in the building code, and he would report when problems were
resolved.

The regular meeting of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES was called

was present and if there was a quorum present. Clerk Graham stated a quorum was

PUBLIC COMMENTS & QUESTIONS
Ingham County Sheriff Department - Break-In Update - Detective Pete Ackerly
Detective Ackerly stated that there has been a rash of break-ins in
Williamstown Township since July. A suspect, Mr. Valsquas, is currently
incarcerated in the Clinton County Jail. He is a 5 ft 7 inch, 260 lb. Hispanic
male who was working as a cement contractor. It is through this work that he
chose the homes for break-ins. He had just come off of a 10 year prison term
and 2 year probation. There were 7 break-ins in Williamstown Township that he
is suspected of committing since July. He is also suspected of two break-ins in
Wheatfield Township, and several in Livingston and Clinton Counties. There is
an article in the September 2, 1998 Enterprise on this investigation that
pictures the car suspected of being used in these robberies. Anyone having seen
this car in the area, or having any further information on this case is asked
to call Detective Pete Ackerly at 676-8256.
Abraham & Gaffney, P.C. - Audit Report Review for Fiscal Year Ending 3/31/98
Received a clean report from the auditors. There were no areas to be addressed.
Sound and efficient accounting methods are currently being used by the
Township, with no recommendations for improvement.
Northeast Ingham Emergency Service Authority (NIESA) - Harold Powell
NIESA will be asking for an operating millage of one mill for the next five
years on the November Ballot. NIESA is made up of the communities of
Williamstown Township, the City of Williamston, Locke Township, Leroy Township,
Wheatfield Township and the Village of Webberville. There will be a need for a
full time secretary, and when Chief Hunt retires a full time Fire Chief will
need to be hired. There are currently EMTs available on a full time basis with
the exception of weekends when the coverage is strictly by volunteer EMTs. Both
fire barns are in need of expansion. A public awareness program of the
authority is currently in the works. They are looking for municipal support of
the ballot question.
