ADVISORY COUNCIL - Rud Hoag
Recommendations for the Township Board:
1. Recommend the Board initiate sponsorship and co-hosting of a joint MTA
informational seminar with the three other Townships (Locke, Leroy and
Wheatfield) regarding becoming a Charter Township. The four supervisors would
initiate this meeting. Rex LaMore will contact Supervisor Obst with additional
information on this proposed meeting. No objections from board. Supervisor Obst
will follow up with Mr. LaMore.
2. Recommended that the Board draft a charge for the Advisory Council regarding
specific criteria for committee actions. The Council is seeking to improve
communications with the Board. The Council would like charges to be clearly
outlined from the Board in writing so that the committees know exactly what the
Board expects of them and what time line they are expected to follow.
3. Recommends that the Board hold informational meetings regarding possible 425
agreements between the Township and the City of Williamston to gather public
input. Supervisor Obst agreed that a Township meeting is a good idea to discuss
what a 425 is and how it would impact the Township. A joint meeting with the
City would have to wait until negotiations are further along with the City. The
Council will schedule this meeting for a Monday night, before October 28th if
possible.
4. Recommended that a Parks and Rec. committee be established as a committee on
its own and the Board establish the objectives and goals. Treasurer Nilsson
suggested some goals and objectives for a Township Parks and Rec. Committee:
   to oversee development of new Township park property on Grand River Road
   a. Immediate fund raising for grant match.
   b. Volunteer project approval and coordination.
   c. Be responsible for a maintenance schedule of any existing facilities.
Treasurer Nilsson moved and Trustee Zaban seconded to create a parks and rec.
committee with the committee’s chair to become a member of the Advisory
Council. Motion passed unanimously. There was general agreement to go in the
direction outlined by Treasurer Nilsson. Fred Foote to be appointed to the Park
and Rec. committee should he so desire.
5. Recommended that the Supervisor write the DNR and Ingham County Health
Department informing them that some of the residents are concerned of possible
lead contamination of the ground water at a Gun Club site in their
neighborhood. Supervisor Obst agreed to do this and he will also contact the

Since Williamstown is a General Law Township it does not have any law

City/Township Negotiations And The Beeman Road Proposed City By-Pass Route.
Supervisor Obst read a letter from Miss Virginie Codran, age 12, into the
record. The Board agreed to charge the Transportation Committee with looking at
the City’s study and in particular their finding that there would be 80 trucks
a day using a Beeman Road by-pass. A City worker has told a Township resident
that no trucks would be allowed on such a by-pass.
The residents on Beeman Road are all against such a by-pass going in. They do
not want to see any further increase in traffic on this road. The road is
heavily used by pedestrians, bicyclists and various sports teams of the schools
for running. The residents want to maintain the type of atmosphere and traffic
on the road that prompted them to buy their homes on this road to begin with.
They feel that a dramatic increase in traffic, especially truck traffic would
make this road no longer safe for pedestrians, children and cyclists.
The residents submitted a letter to the board stating that they are adamantly
opposed to any Township Roads being turned over to the City of Williamston as
part of any potential 425 agreement. The residents wish to be kept informed of
any developments in the negotiations with the City, especially as they apply to
Beeman Road. Supervisor Obst stated that the Township’s Master Plan states the
Township’s intent to maintain the rural atmosphere of the area.
Trustee Wiegandt stated that for safety reasons (specifically fire) we may need
another route over the river that is closer to town than Dietz or Zimmer,
though he is not convinced that Beeman is the appropriate location for such a
route. Treasurer Nilsson was concerned that the City appeared to only looked at
this one location for another bridge over the river. Clerk Graham is not in
favor of a crossing at this location citing the areas wet lands, cemetery, golf
course, etc. that would be involved. She does not want to see increased traffic
on Beeman or Rowley road there. She agrees there is a need for another bridge,
but not here. She is also not convinced of the City’s contention that the
Putnam Street bridge would have to be completely closed down to rebuild it. The
M-52 bridge was rebuilt by only closing one half of it at a time.
There cannot be a 425 agreement without a public hearing. Those in the 425 area
can put it on the ballot to overturn a 425 agreement. A 425 agreement of some
sort is one possible settlement of the sewer litigation with the City of
Williamston.
Trustee Zaban stated his concerns about what the City wants to do.
Realistically the City would probably win an annexation if the property owner
wanted it. Supervisor Obst stated that there are currently property owners who
are interested in going into the City because they want to develop with sewer.
That is how the Beeman Road issue is tied to the law suit. He also stated that
the Township is not going to sacrifice any residents to settle the sewer
lawsuit. Supervisor Obst stated that he hoped the Board has made it clear that
they have the same objectives as the residents present and that the Board will
contact them as soon as they have more information.
Submission Of Petition To Pave Barry From Loundsbury To Williamston Road - Ron
Decker. There were only two property owners along this stretch of road that are
not in favor of paving Barry Rd. 81% of the residents want the road to be
paved. Road is often washed out. Treasurer Nilsson talked to Bob D'Alcorn of
the Ingham County Road Commission on this subject. He agreed that it is less
expensive to maintain a paved road, but it takes a substantial amount of money
to pave the road initially. He will work on figuring out when the paving would
pay for itself vs. maintaining the dirt road. Drain has already been put in
down at Bentley Road. Will forward the request for paving to the Transportation
Committee.
Larkin Country Acres - proposal appears to violate the lot split ordinance.
Waiting to hear from their attorney. Trying to split into lots that don't have
access to public roads.

ATTORNEY REPORT: Stephen O. Schultz
Getting ready for Dec. 7 joint town meeting with the City. On Friday,
Supervisor Obst, Attorney Schultz and the Township Planning Consultant, Chris
Doozen will review materials and put together remarks.
900 Gulick Rd. - Supervisor Obst and Attorney Schultz have met with Mr. Foote
and his attorney, Mr. Ray to try to reach an agreement before the scheduled
Dec. 10th hearing. The Township is looking for compliance with the Zoning
Ordinance. If compliance can not be agreed upon then the Township will keep the
Dec. 10th court date.
Researched The Following Issues:
·Liability of the Township if private drives that service more than one parcel
are allowed.
·The Edwards’ variance request to have two residences on one lot, which has
been addressed and was not granted by the Zoning Board of Appeals.
·The proposed agreement to dissolve the Fire Board and transfer its assets to
NIESA. An issue has come up regarding the Township’s liability after the Fire
Board is dissolved. Paragraph 4 of the resolution provides that while the
Authority is assuming certain liabilities of the Fire Board it is not assuming
civil liability for damage claims. Appears the D of O policy is a claims made
policy which could make the Township or City liable. The rest of the resolution
is fine. Attorney Schultz suggests approving the resolution contingent on
having sufficient coverage for liability. if claims made policies exist, then
the Authority will have to get tail policies to cover this situation.

Trustee Zaban moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported to approve the presented
resolution to dissolve the Williamston Community Fire Board and transfer the
fire equipment and other assets to the Northeast Ingham Emergency Service
Authority (NIESA) contingent on satisfactory resolution of the insurance
issues. Motion approved unanimously.
Zoning Ordinance Issues
Proposal for lot splits in Ag-Commercial Zone. Attorney Schultz believes the
Township may be getting ahead of itself by adopting an ordinance that requires
land be put into an open space or agricultural preservation trust before a
Development Rights Ordinance has been adopted. There is also an Ag space bill
in the state senate and a couple of other development rights bills in the
process at the state level. If they don't get voted on during this lame duck
session then they will have to start the bill process over again. Attorney
Schultz believes it would be in the best interest of the Township to wait a
month before voting on this particular change in the ordinance. Treasurer
Nilsson sought clarification of what land would be affected. Land division in
the Ag-Commercial district would allow for up to 4 lots of one to five acres
each with a shared driveway, or up to 4 lots of two to five acres each that
have public road access to be split from an original lot of at least 40 acres.
The remaining 20+ acres would be put into a trust.
Per Planning Coordinator Martin the only changes from the original proposals to
amend the Zoning Ordinance were for the kennels and the Ag-Commercial land
division. The outdoor event removed the minimum of 100 people requirement.
There have been no other changes since the September 22 correspondence.
Treasurer Nilsson moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported to approve the proposed
Zoning, Land Division and Subdivision Ordinances text revisions as recommended
by the Planning Commission, except for the parts dealing with the Ag-Commercial
Land Division. Motion passed unanimously.
PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
Rezoning of the Schraft property from RR to Ag-C. Planning Commission has only
received comments in support of the change. Treasurer Nilsson moved and Clerk
Graham supported to approve the rezoning or 40 acres from RR to AG-C, as
applied for by George and Patricia Schraft. See Planning Commission minutes of
11/17/98. Motion passed unanimously.
Edwards proposed Zoning Ordinance changes. Mr. Edwards would like to see some

Transportation Committee - Road Funding - Brian Jennings. Reviewed the
Transportation Committee's recommendations for road funding. The second
recommendation was for funding of subdivision roads. A sliding scale was
developed for percentage of Township funding when fixing subdivision roads.
Questions on the PASER Surface Rating - the Township normally improves roads
that are rated between a three and a four. The lower the number on the scale
the worse the condition of the road. The Township would pay 100% of the cost
when the road gets to level two or one. The residents of the subdivision can
petition to have their roads repaired at any time, but they would have to
contribute a percentage of the cost based on the condition of the road at the
time of the request. The better the condition, the higher the percentage the
residents have to pay directly and the lower the percentage that the Township
will contribute. Supervisor Obst suggested a public hearing be held to discuss
the policy proposal.
The first recommendation was for a sum of $100,000 be set aside for road
improvement each year, to be adjusted for inflation, with 25% set aside in an
escrow account for future major road projects. Recommendation to be considered
at the 1999/2000 budget meeting. Discussion followed.
Appointment of Richard Kill to the Transportation Committee. Trustee Zaban
moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported, to appoint Mr. Richard Kill to the
Transportation and Communications Committee. Motion approved unanimously.
Recommends that the Board allocate $500 for the Commercial Development
Committee to work with MSU students for further research.
Dwight Kampe proposed the students look at Grand River Rd. and take inventory
of what kind of developments currently exist. The students will also talk to
the property owners to see if they have any immediate plans for any kind of
development or improvements. They will also help to determine what kind of
development along Grand River the Township would be receptive to. Supervisor
Obst suggested that the Township should have a budget for how the $500 would be
spent. Mr. Kampe agreed that this would be an important part of the project for
the students to come up with such a budget. Supervisor Obst also stated that
one of the primary concerns of the city of Williamston is what is going to
happen along Grand River outside city limits. He recommended that the students
talk to City officials to get their opinions on development along the
Township’s stretch of Grand River Rd. There was general agreement by the
Township Board that this is a project they would like to do. Mr. Kampe is to
return to the Township Board with a proposed budget for approval in the amount
of $500.00.

ATTORNEY'S REPORT - Stephen O. Schultz
Insurance Policies Associated With The Former Fire Board - A letter was sent
indicating the need to get tail coverage. Concern is that there will be tail
coverage for about 22 months, but claims related to the old Fire Board could
still be filed after that time, though the likelihood is diminishing. All the
municipalities and NIESA have to be concerned about how long this coverage is
needed. Can renew it annually. If NIESA does not renew it then the
municipalities need to decide if they need the coverage. Clerk Graham stated

The regular meeting of the Township Board of Trustees was called to order at 7:

PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
No action items.
Proposed Tree Ordinance - met in subcommittee with the resident who recommended
the ordinance. The Planning Commission was undecided as to what kind of tree
ordinance was best for the Township. A survey was devised to determine the
scope and desire for a tree ordinance. The Planning Commission took the survey
and answered negatively for implementing an ordinance. The only possible need
they saw for a tree ordinance might be in the public right of ways. Even here
the Township would need to work with the Ingham County Road Commission (ICRC)
and the Township could be held liable if someone runs into a tree that the ICRC
had determined should be removed, but the tree ordinance prevented the removal.
The Planning Commission concluded that it saw no reason to enact a tree
ordinance at this time and a problem that such an ordinance would address had
not been identified. Recommendation is to not proceed at this time. Supervisor
Obst suggested that the Township should go back to the individual who
recommended the ordinance and allow him to address the Board on it. Treasurer
Nilsson suggested accepting the report and passing it along to anybody who
wants it, and they can then comment. Trustee Wiegandt stated that when the
Township looked at this almost a year ago we were in the process of developing
plans for the park. He questioned if we need something to set a precedence for
conservation. He had no concern other than what should be used as guidelines.

Road Funding Policy - Treasurer Nilsson moved and Clerk Graham supported to
adopt the following Road Funding Policy:
The Williamstown Township Board will maintain its current and future road
system if it allocates $77,000 per year, subject to inflation, to be used in
conjunction with the Ingham County Road Commission’s matching funds. The roads
scheduled for maintenance will be selected through a PASER Surface Rating
system previously adopted and with input from the Ingham County Road
Commission. If at any time property owners within the Township wish to have
their roads improved prior to being selected, they may petition the Township
for the improvements and share the cost through a special assessment. The
percent of the project that the Township will pay for will depend on the
condition of the roads to be improved. The Township Board will use the
following cost sharing guidelines:
   PASER Surface Rating         Percent of Improvements Paid by the Township
      10                      0%
       9                      0%
       8                      0%
       7                      25%
       6                      25%
       5                      50%
       4                      75%
       3                      75%
       2                     100%
       1                     100%
A majority of the resident property owners, along the road to be improved,
would be required to sign a petition requesting the improvements be made. The
petition must state the estimated total cost of the improvements, how the cost
will be divided among the property owners, the number of years the special
assessment will be spread, and the percent of cost sharing with the Township.
This policy will apply to all Township Roads equally, subdivision and non-
subdivision, but not County Primaries.
Motion passed unanimously.

their surveys and criteria. Corner met only 2 of the 7 criteria. Still trying

Open Land Survey Results - Nancy Fink
Report accepted and placed on file. Some of the results included 95% of
respondents agreeing that the overall quality of life in the Township is good.
77% believe it is becoming less tranquil. 83% participate in outdoor recreation
in the Township. 27% thought the Township should develop more outdoor
recreation areas outside of the park. Some of the conclusions reached as a
result of the survey were that housing development in agricultural areas is
undesirable. The Township should develop growth boundaries, buffer zones to the
agricultural areas. Need to update maps in Master Plan. Talked about bike
trails being in the Master Plan. Suggested developing a bike trail along Grand
River Rd from the City limits of Williamston out to the Township Park. This
idea was met with enthusiastic support from those present.

Revised Fire Hall Lease Resolution
Clerk Graham moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported to adopt the following

Resolution Approving Lease of the Township Property Located at 627 East Grand
River, Commonly Known as the Fire Hall, to the Northeast Ingham Emergency
Service Authority
   WHEREAS, the Northeast Ingham Emergency Service Authority, ‘NIESA’, was
established to provide emergency services including fire suppression and
ambulance services within the Township and adjacent areas; and
   WHEREAS, the Township Board previously agreed to lease the fire hall to
NIESA upon terms acceptable to the Township; and
   WHEREAS, the Township is the owner as a tenant in common of an undivided
one-half interest in the real estate.
   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:
1.   The Township Board consents to the lease of the property located at 627 E.
Grand River, the “Fire Hall” to the Northeast Ingham Emergency Service
Authority, on terms contained in the attached Lease, with the following
modifications all approved as to form by the Township Attorney:
1.1   Modification of paragraph 14 to read as follows:
   Destruction of the premises. If the premises are damaged or destroyed by
fire or other cause, the buildings shall be repaired or rebuilt and the
proceeds of insurance upon the premises shall be applied to cover the cost. If
the available insurance proceeds are insufficient to cover the cost of repair
or rebuilding and lessee chooses not to supplement the insurance proceeds with
its own funds, the lease shall terminate automatically as of the date of
destruction and the insurance proceeds shall be distributed as the parties
shall agree. Under no circumstances shall lessors be obliged to spend their
funds to repair or rebuild the premises under this paragraph.
2.   The Township Supervisor and Clerk are authorized to execute the agreement
on behalf of the Township upon approval as to form by the Township Attorney.
Roll Call Vote

Trustee Wiegandt
   Nays:   None.
Resolution adopted.

ATTORNEY REPORT - Stephen O. Schultz
No action required.
900 Gulick Road - Involved in attempting to resolve the Foote Pond matter.
Reviewed planning commission minutes and offered comments to Planning
Coordinator Martin, Clerk Graham and Treasurer Nilsson.
City Litigation - Pretrial is set for Monday March 8th. The trial date is March
22nd. If cannot settle before then we will be going to trial on that date. Met
to exchange ideas on a possible settlement of the sewer issue only. Believe
there is some possibility here that will not involve any property transfers,
only sewer issues.
Larkin Country Acres Lot Split Request - Looking at the request. Nothing more
until Board of Appeals.
Noted two issues from last meeting’s minutes
Advisory Council Charge Form - the charge form from the Board to the Advisory
Council has to follow the open meetings act.
Horizon Cable Vision - Has some suggestions that he can offer the Cable
Commission in addressing the complaints in view of the transfer. Shortcomings
in performance will be in the record when their franchise comes up for renewal.
By the time their renewal comes around there will be alternatives. It is not an
empty threat to say that we treat these things seriously and will make them a
matter of record. The new company will inherit the franchise and all the
obligations that go with it. This is the time to put the new provider on notice
and get their attention. Also may want to consider comparing notes with other
communities using Horizon. A joint letter may be even more persuasive.
Phone Michigan Franchise Request - Looking at the franchise request for several
other Townships that the law firm represents. Will do one review for all four
townships and will split the cost between the townships. This is the first of
several requests that we will probably see now that the local telephone company
has been opened up for competition. There is currently tension between two
aspects of the state’s statutes - the Townships rights to set up a franchise
and the ordinance saying there will only be a permit fee to use the right of
ways. Two conflicting requirements.
Development Rights Ordinance - need to get an opinion to the Planning
commission on this.
Occupancy of 1500 Grand River Road - does not appear that it is at a stage
where legal action is warranted yet. Building Inspector Aven sent a letter to
Williamston City Manager, Dale Soumis on Feb. 5th, reminding him that the City
needs an occupancy permit and cannot use the building until they got one. Mr.
Aven has written another letter restating the Feb. 5th letter and that a permit
has not been issued. He will issue a temporary permit for the office on the
condition that all vehicles and fuel be removed from the garage portion until
that portion of the building is in compliance and a final certificate of
occupancy is issued. The Building Inspector will hand deliver this letter.
Attorney Schultz stated the reason he doesn't want to authorize any action
tonight is because there isn't an imminent threat to health, safety and welfare
in the office part of the building. If the City doesn't agree to bring the
garage up to code before using it then that is another issue because they would
be flaunting the codes. At that time the attorney would recommend pad locking
the building. Inspector Aven stated that the building is in better shape than
it was when USA Plastics occupied it. He assumes the City will have the
vehicles out by tomorrow night.
PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
900 Gulick Road - The Planning Commission was presented with a new site plan
and landscaping plan for the pond. The Commission rejected the plan that was
submitted due to inadequate information available on the plan for slope,
drainage and run off. The Commission has proposed a motion that any future site
plans must meet the 10 conditions proposed by the Planning Commission. If Mr.
Foote ever decided to fill the pond with pumped water he would have to go
through the strata testing that was specified last Spring.
Jim Sikarskie stated that if the ten points are followed it will be a major
step forward. He said that they had a ten point document before submitting the
last site plan that they didn't follow. Is there a date by which these
guidelines must be met by? Concerned it is just another delay tactic. This has
been going on for close to 2 years. He realizes they are legally acceptable
delay tactics, but when will it stop. Attorney Schultz stated that in his
discussions with Foote's attorney they went through the ten points that were
established at the May meeting to say this is where the Township is at. Got the
response that the indemnification is unnecessary if they don't draw the well.
Will no longer fill it with a well, so those requirements are now moot. With
respect to the 8 foot berm, that was never agreed to by Jeff Foote in May of
1998 or at any time since. Only standards we have to work with are 1 on 3 slope
and harmonious. cannot necessarily dictate 8 foot berms. Mr. Foote was prepared
to meet the other requirements laid out by the Board. Mr. Sikarskie was under
the impression that the community would have the ability to present their view
on what is harmonious. The berm facing the road has not changed. It is still 10
to 11 feet high. He has not reduced it where the public views it, only behind
the barn where he views it. Supervisor Obst had asked Chris Doozen, the
Township’s Planning Consultant, about the harmonious issue. Part of it does
relate to height. Height of berm does affect run off. Shorter berms do not have
as much of an erosion problem. The Township may be left open to a charge that
an 8 foot limit is arbitrary and capricious. The Ordinance requires under
landscaping that the grass planted be maintained and not allowed to die. If it
does die it must be replaced immediately or at the beginning of the next
planting season. A violation here would be handled the same as any other zoning
violation. Mr. Sikarskie recommends that looking at adjoining properties would
be the most important requirement for harmonious. Contours that are there need
to be used for comparison for harmonious. Wanted to express appreciation to the
Planning Commission for the product they ended up with and the ability to voice
his concerns and opinions. Incorporate Section 5.04, sub-section C.9 of the
Zoning Ordinance into any approval of the site plan. That would pick up all of
Mr. Doozen’s comments that no undesirable trees are used and can verify that
the proper number of trees have been planted. Would put it right in the motion
for site plan approval. Attorney Schultz doesn't think it will be an issue, but
it is a prudent thing to put in the motion.
Supervisor Obst moved and Clerk Graham seconded that the site plan for a pond
at 900 Gulick Road be approved subject to the applicant meeting the article 5
requirements of the Zoning Ordinance, and the following conditions:
1.   If the pond is intended to be filled with well water, then prior testing
shall be completed in accordance with the Strata Environmental Services
outline. The Township will be fully notified in advance of the exact times and
dates when the testing will be conducted so if the Township wishes it may have
a Township Engineer and/or representative present.
2.   The plans are to be reviewed and approved by the Township Building
Official with respect to the Uniform Building Code Requirements.
3.   A comprehensive storm drainage plan must be presented, illustrating storm
water drainage along the entire east and west property lines. This plan shall
be designed by a registered professional civil engineer. The toe of the slope
on the west side shall be set back a minimum of ten feet from the property line
with a one on three slope. A new site plan is required to indicate the above
stipulations.
4.   Berms on the property are to be reshaped in accordance with item 3, above,
so they are no steeper than a slope of one foot vertical to three feet
horizontal. The plan must also be modified to illustrate the berms on the east
side.
5.   A performance guarantee must be submitted to cover all indicated
improvements including assuring proper operation of the storm drainage system
as well as landscaping and maintenance requirements in the Zoning Ordinance.
6.   If the pond is intended to be filled with well water, then a monitoring
well must be left installed. During future drought conditions a report from the
monitoring well must be provided to the Township at its request. A low water
level must be established at the time the hydrogeological study is submitted so
that the Township knows what to look for in the future when they ask for
monitoring well data.
7.   The applicant agrees to refrain from using well water to fill or maintain
the pond level. If in the future the applicant chooses to fill the pond with
well water, prior approval from the Township shall be required. If the
applicant violates this agreement, resulting in a deleterious impact on nearby
properties, wells, or groundwater supply or quality, the applicant agrees to
indemnify nearby affected property owners for costs to repair or rectify such
impacts, including legal, engineering and consultant costs.
8.   The applicant understands that should the above testing indicate changes
are needed, then it is possible the plan may need further modifications to all
aspects including, possibly, the size of the pond.
9.   Elevations shall be referenced to a U.S.G.S. benchmark.
10.   Berm height shall not exceed that indicated on the topographic map
received by the Township on January 4th 1999.
Discussion of the motion followed, including questions on the amount of
performance guarantee required - to be determined based on the project; per
item 3, a new site plan is required; and concerns raised about the berm facing
the road not undulating and being higher than eight feet. If trees won't grow
there, then he would be in violation and would have to reshape the berms at
that time.
Per Attorney Schultz, acceptance of this motion on the part of the applicant
would settle the law suit. Motion approved unanimously.
Township Attorney Schultz left the meeting at 9:15 P. M..

1999-2000 Budget Approval/Township General Appropriations Act:
A Resolution to establish a General Appropriations Act for Williamstown
Township; To define the powers and duties of the Williamstown Township Officers
in relation to the administration of the Budget; and to provide remedies for
refusal or neglect to comply with the requirements of this resolution.
The Board of Trustees of Williamstown Township resolves:
SECTION 1:   TITLE.
This resolution shall be known as the Williamstown Township General
Appropriations Act.
SECTION 2:   CHIEF ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER.
The Supervisor shall be the Chief Administrative Officer and shall perform the
duties of the Chief Administrative Officer enumerated in this act.
SECTION 3:   FISCAL OFFICER.
The Clerk shall be the Fiscal Officer and shall perform the duties of the
Fiscal Officer enumerated in this act.
SECTION 4:   PUBLIC HEARINGS ON THE BUDGET.
(for general law townships) Pursuant to MCLA 141.412; MCLA 141.413, notice of a
public hearing on the proposed budget was published in a newspaper of general
circulation on (date--at least six days prior to the public hearing), and a
public hearing on the proposed budget was held on April 1, 1999. Budget Hearing
Notice published on March 21, 1999 and March 28, 1999.
SECTION 5:   ESTIMATED REVENUES.
Estimated township general fund revenues for fiscal year 1999-2000, (Year
ending March 31, 1999) including an allocated millage of one mill; voter-
authorized millage of zero mills; and various miscellaneous revenues shall
total $513,499.
SECTION 6:   MILLAGE LEVY.
The Williamstown Township Board shall cause to be levied and collected the
general property tax on all real and personal property within the township upon
the current tax roll and amount equal to one mill as set forth by the Tax
Allocation Board.
SECTION 7:   ESTIMATED EXPENDITURES.
Estimated township general fund expenditures for fiscal year 1999-2000, (Year
ending March 31, 2000) for the various township activities (cost centers) are
as follows: See attachment, $669,359.
SECTION 8:   ADOPTION OF BUDGET BY REFERENCE.
The general fund budget of Williamstown Township is hereby adopted by
reference, with revenues and activity expenditures as indicated in sections 5
and 7 of this act.
SECTION 9:   ADOPTION OF BUDGET BY COST CENTER.
The Board of Trustees of Williamstown Township adopts the 1999-2000 fiscal year
general fund budget by cost center. Township officials responsible for the
expenditures authorized in the budget may expend township funds up to, but not
to exceed, the total appropriation authorized for each cost center, and may
make transfers among the various line items contained in the cost center
appropriation. However, no transfers of appropriations for line items related
to personnel or capital outlays may be made without prior board approval by
budget amendment.
SECTION 10:   APPROPRIATION NOT A MANDATE TO SPEND.
Appropriations will be deemed maximum authorizations to incur expenditures. The
fiscal officer shall exercise supervision and control to ensure that
expenditures are within appropriations, and shall not issue any town order for
expenditures that exceed appropriations.
SECTION 11:   TRANSFER AUTHORITY.
                  Deleted. N/A
SECTION 12:   ALLOTMENT OF APPROPRIATIONS.
No later than the first day of the fiscal year, each department, board or
commission of Williamstown Township shall submit to the Chief Administrative
Officer a statement or proposed allotments of appropriations based on expected
periodic requirements. The Chief Administrative Officer shall review, modify or
approve the proposed allotment plan for any cost center.
SECTION 13:   PERIODIC FISCAL REPORTS.
The fiscal officer shall transmit to the board at the end of each of the three
quarters, and at the end of each month occurring during the fourth quarter, a
report of financial operations, including, but not limited to:
a)   a summary statement of the actual financial condition of the general fund
at the end of the previous quarter (month);
b)   a summary statement showing the receipts and expenditures and encumbrances
for the previous quarter (month) and for the current fiscal year to the end of
the previous quarter (month);
c)   a detailed list of:
1)   expected revenues by major source as estimated in the budget; actual
receipts to date for the current fiscal year compared with actual receipts for
the same period in the prior fiscal year; the balance of estimated revenues to
be collected in the then current fiscal year; and any revisions in revenue
estimates resulting from collection experience to date.
2)   for each cost center: the amount appropriated; the amount charged to each
appropriation in the previous quarter (month) and for the current fiscal year
and as compared with the same period in the prior fiscal year; the unencumbered
balance of appropriations; and any revisions in the estimate of expenditures.
SECTION 14:   LIMIT ON OBLIGATIONS AND PAYMENTS.
No obligation shall be incurred against, and payment shall be made from any
appropriation account unless there is a sufficient unencumbered balance in the
appropriation and sufficient funds are or will be available to meet the
obligation.
SECTION 15:   BUDGET MONITORING.
Whenever it appears to the Chief Administrative Officer or the Township Board
that the actual and probable revenues in any fund will be less than the
estimated revenues upon which appropriations from such fund were based, and
when it appears that expenditures shall exceed an appropriation, the Chief
Administrative Officer shall present to the Township Board recommendations to
prevent expenditures from exceeding available revenues or appropriations for
the current fiscal year. Such recommendations shall include proposals for
reducing appropriations, increasing revenues, or both.
SECTION 16:   VIOLATIONS OF THE ACT.
Any obligation incurred or payment authorized in violation of this resolution
shall be void and shall subject any responsible official(s) or employees to
disciplinary action as outlined in P.A. 621 (1978) and the Williamstown
Township personnel manual.
SECTION 17:   BOARD ADOPTION.
Trustee Wiegandt moved and Treasurer Nilsson seconded; PASSED to adopt for the
1999-2000 Fiscal Year the General Appropriations Act for WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP,
originally adopted by the Township of Williamstown on April 4, 1989, and the
foregoing resolution as read. Roll Call Vote:
   Ayes:   Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban, Treasurer Nilsson, Supervisor Obst,
Clerk Graham
   Nays:   None.

Bob Peterson of the Ingham County Road Commission (ICRC) concurred with the
Township’s Transportation Committee’s 1999 road improvement recommendations and

recommendations into the record:
1.   Set at least $50,000 aside for Vanneter and Mitchell or begin engineering
work.
2.   Do not resurface Newman, but allocate funds this year to complete the
project next year ($31,439).
3.   Do not pave any gravel roads (North Branch and Wilgus).
4.   Gravel Road Reconstruct on Milton and Bentley only after contacting the
residents in the area and reviewing their input ($16,240).
5.   Do not do Gravel Road Reconstruct on Barry.
6.   Set remaining moneys aside for future years when higher than average
number of roads need to be maintained ($77,000 - $47,679 = $$29,321 set aside).
7.   Set an additional $23,000 aside for future large projects as outlined in
the Master Plan.
Brian Jennings clarified that with the additional $23,000 to be set aside per
year for future large projects (such as bridge construction, or situations
similar to Vanneter and Mitchell) the Transportation Committee is recommending
a total of $100,000 to be budgeted for road construction per year.
Pebblebrook Place/Quarton Road still has four lots that have not started
building. The Transportation Committee believes there will still be heavy
construction traffic on Newman Road this year until all the homes on Quarton
are built. They would like to schedule Newman Road construction as late in the
year as possible this year, or early in 2000 so that it can be done after the
heavy construction traffic is done. Mr. Peterson said the Board can wait until
May to make a decision on the Newman road upgrade and still be able to be
scheduled by the ICRC for later this year.

vocal in the past about not having improvements done. Were on the list for last
year, but was dropped for fiscal considerations. Will send letter to the
residents.

Update On Haslett Road Project From Van Atta To Hart - Bob Peterson, ICRC
Bid went to C&D Hughes. Will start in mid June. Should be done by end of
August. Two sections require full depth reconstruction and will require
detours. The plan in the State Transportation Program is to improve the section
from Hart to Barton in 2000 and the section from Barton to east of Williamston
Road in 2001. Mr. Peterson will submit an article for the May Township
Newsletter detailing the project and detours. Each property owner affected by
the project has been contacted and agreements have been signed regarding
grading and tree removal.

it is very costly and you do not get a new surface on the road. When you fill
the cracks you may keep some of the water out, but you don't do anything for
the road surface. Chip and Seal will fill the cracks and give the road a new
wear surface. Mr. Jennings will forward the Transportation Committee’s report
from last year on this topic to the Board. Treasurer Nilsson wanted to do a
test crack fill.

American Legion - Conrad Taschner
Request for funding under Act 63 of 1915. The Act requires all local governing
bodies to fund veterans’ flags and holders. Brought in a sample of a Bronze
holder that will last forever. Have tried other materials and these were the
best. Asked the city to go 50/50 with the Township. They approved that. The
legion has been using their own money, but they have run out. Would like $200
every year from both the City of Williamston and Williamstown Township. They
are in the process of taking a survey to determine exactly how many veterans
are in the cemetery. According to the law every veteran must have a flag. The
funds will be kept by the Cemetery Board. The Boy Scouts have agreed to put the
flags out every year. Flags go out the week before Memorial Day and come down
the week after the 4th of July. The Township would allocate the funds from
either the cemetery fund or the office surplus. This detail will be decided
when the auditors come at the end of May. Treasurer Nilsson stated that she was
impressed with the petition that was submitted. Treasurer Nilsson moved and
Trustee Wiegandt supported to approve, per Act 63 of 1915, funding of current
1999 expenses in the amount of $176.00 (one-half of $351.99). In addition,
approval of an annual appropriation of $200.00 for future purchase of flags and
holders, as needed to support the American Legion grave marker funding. Motion
passed unanimously.
Woodview Lot 50 - Doug Price
The declaration of restrictive covenants and the Plat for the Woodview
Subdivision state a 50 foot set back is required for building a home. The
Zoning Ordinance requires a 25 foot set back in this zone. Building with a 50
foot set back on lot 50 would impede the natural drainage of lot 37. They would
like to build with a 40 foot set back to prevent this from happening. If the 50
foot requirement were only in the restrictive covenants, then the developer
would be able to make this change. Since the 50 foot set backs are also on the
Plat, which is part of a binding density option agreement with the Township,
the Township’s Planning Consultant and Attorney are both of the opinion that
the issue must go before the Zoning Board of Appeals. Mr. Price disagrees with
this assessment of the situation. He was scheduled to close with a buyer for
this lot on Friday, May 14th. After much discussion Trustee Wiegandt moved and
Trustee Zaban supported to expedite this and waive the board of appeals fee for
a variance to the setback on lot 50. Passed unanimously. Will schedule a Board
of Appeals meeting for Wednesday or Thursday next week (May 19th or 20th) if
the applicant requests.
Proposal For Landscaping Around The Building - Landscape Bob
Made a presentation showing what plantings he proposed for around the Township
Hall. He proposed using drought, heat and cold hearty plants that would require
a minimum amount of maintenance and would not out grow their space. Stated he
can do the job for $19,700 if the Township went with everything in his
proposal. This price is all inclusive, including removal and dumping of the old
stuff. He would like to incorporate the Eagle Scout plantings into the
landscape. He indicated watering would be necessary the first year to help the
plants get established. After that, rain water should be sufficient. Left a
copy of his plan and sketch for Board consideration.
Proposed Sewer Hookup - Russell Aker
In light of the pending resolution of the law suit with the City of
Williamston, Mr. Aker is interested in getting on the list of potential future
sewer hook ups. Supervisor Obst stated that on a first come first serve basis
there is no capacity left because of all the people who have already requested.
The Township Board has to come up with a policy to determine who gets the
hookups. Supervisor Obst suggested that Mr. Aker put together a proposal for
how many hookups he is requesting and how they would enhance the Township. The
Township has 100 Residential Equivalency Unit (REU) hookups with the agreement.
The Board will keep Mr. Aker informed of what the process is going to be in
determining distribution of the hookups.
City Building at Corwin and Grand River
A Township resident stated a concern about whether or not the City was lawfully
occupying the building at Corwin and Grand River. Building Inspector Aven
stated that the City has been issued a temporary certificate of occupancy for
the front office and the garage. The City is seeking a waiver from the barrier
free status of the building from the state. Once this issue has been resolved a
permanent certificate of occupancy will be issued. The parts of the building
being used are safe and to code. The City has not been given any special
treatment in the issuance of the temporary certificate of occupancy. It is a
normal practice in this type of situation.
Direction Of The Community
Another Township resident expressed his feelings and concerns about the
direction of the community in general. His concerns will be taken to the
intergovernmental committee.
Proposed Bentley Road Improvements - Shirley Graham
Gravel Reconstruction requires surveying the Road creating traffic lanes 11
feet to each side from the center and ditching. The Road Commission has 33 feet
from the center in each direction to work. 11 surveys were sent to the
residents in this area. Eight were returned. No one wanted trees cut. Six
responded no to cutting trees and two made no comment on this item. Four
respondents stated the ditches need to be cleaned, and four said they did not.
Mr. Ronald Decker stated that it seems to him more important to improve Barry
Road before reconstructing other gravel roads. Would like to consider black
topping Barry Road before paving Bentley Road.
Mitchell Road
A Township resident expressed his deep concern for the traffic situation on
Mitchell Road, especially regarding pedestrian traffic and the lack of safety
for the school children in the area. He chided the Board for their inactivity
in this area. In response, it was indicated the Board was unable to obtain a
lower speed limit despite many efforts and the City of Williamston was
unwilling to help fund road improvements.
Fee Schedule Change - Mickey Martin

unanimously.

John Kane - Building Permit To Replace The Temporary Model Home
The Minutes from 1994 show that the Site Plan that was approved allowed for a
model home that would be a temporary structure for no more than three years.
The model was removed in 1997. There was no provision in the Site Plan for
another model to be put on the site at a later time, nor was this discussed at
any of the meetings with Mr. Kane. The Board generally agreed that putting new
models on the site as old ones became obsolete was probably Mr. Kane’s intent
from the beginning, but provisions were not made to do this in the original
site plan. The Township’s Planning Consultant, Chris Doozen, believes another
site plan needs to be approved to accommodate future model homes on this site.
Too much time has passed for the original Site Plan to be modified. The Board
discussed various options and agreed that Mr. Kane needed to make a written
proposal to the Board in order for them to be able to accommodate his request.
Planning Coordinator Martin will contact Mr. Kane to ask him to bring back to
the Board a proposal that can be considered. Building Inspector Aven indicated
that there would need to be a separate building permit for each model home he
would put on the site.

Community Hall Rental Reservation & Cancellation Policy
Due to problems with people canceling their hall rental reservation too close
to the date of their event for the Township to rent the hall to other parties
who have expressed an interest, there is a need for a cancellation policy. The
office secretary has proposed adding the following wording to the Community
Hall Rental Form:
Reservations shall be made upon receipt of Hall Rental fee. Payment secures
your date.
Cancellation Policy:
A. All refunds for cancellations shall be requested in writing.
B. A full refund shall be given for events canceled prior to one month of event
date.
C. A partial refund (50%) shall be given for events canceled within on month of
less
of event date.
Trustee Zaban moved and Treasurer Nilsson supported to approve the change of
the Township Hall Reservation Process as stated above. Motion passed
unanimously.

The regular meeting of the Township Board of Trustees was called to order at 7:

Received a clean or unqualified opinion. Also received favorable review of our

PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
Need action on several items.
Nature Center Addition To The Zoning Ordinance - Moved by Supervisor Obst and
supported by Trustee Zaban to approve the Planning Commission’s recommendation
to add Nature Centers to the Zoning Ordinance. Motion approved unanimously.
Development Rights Ordinance - Participation would be completely voluntary on
the part of the land owner. There is nothing in the proposed ordinance that
would require a land owner to give up their development rights. This proposed
Ordinance is putting a vehicle in place should anyone decide they want to give
up their development rights by either gifting or sale. There is no funding
provided for at this time for the Township to purchase development rights.
Supervisor Obst moved and Trustee Zaban supported to approve the Planning
Commission's recommendations to adopt the Development Rights Ordinance. Motion
approved unanimously.
Royce Lockwood Rezoning Request - Mr. Lockwood owns 160 acres, he would like to
rezone 30 acres of it. He would like to rezone 20 acres to Ag Small Farm and 10
acres to Rural Estates parcels. The remainder would stay in Ag Commercial.
Supervisor Obst had a question on the Williamston School District’s
involvement. The school’s are purchasing 125 of the remaining 130 acres. The
house and barn are on the proposed 20 acre parcel. The two five acre parcels
have frontage on Sherwood Rd. Treasurer Nilsson moved and Trustee Wiegandt
supported to approve the Planning Commission’s recommendation of the rezoning
of 30 acres, out of a total of 160 acres, from Ag Commercial to Ag Small Farm
and Rural Estates. Motion approved unanimously.
Revision To Zoning Ordinance - Splitting By Right 4 Parcels In An AG-Commercial
Zone. If a property owner takes advantage of this opportunity then they give up
all development rights on the remaining acreage. Moved by Supervisor Obst and
supported by Trustee Wiegandt to approve the Planning Commission’s
recommendation of the revision to the Zoning Ordinance allowing splitting by
right four parcels in the Ag-Commercial Zone. Motion approved unanimously.
ADVISORY COUNCIL - Rud Hoag

PUBLIC COMMENTS AND QUESTIONS
Pat Callihan - Meals on Wheels Tri County Project Coordinator Williamstown
Township
Currently delivering to 16 people in the Williamston area and serving around 60
at the dining site. Reimburse volunteers at a rate of 25 cents a mile. Drivers
typically drive 45 miles a day. Average client receives 138 meals a year. Cost
$4.15 per delivered meal. Cost at dining site is $2.25 each. Ask for a donation
from the client of $2.00 for the hot/frozen meal and $1.00 for the sack lunch.
No one is refused a meal if they cannot pay. The Township’s requested
contribution of $1,250 was determined by a list of the Townships and the number
of people served. 0-10 clients was $500. Average between 50-100 clients in this
Township puts the Township in the $1,250 bracket. Reason for the request is
this year’s County budget and the cost of the food has gone up. The Board was
not clear on how the numbers were reached. They would like to get some
additional information from Jim Allen, director of Meals on Wheels, before
deciding how much to contribute. The Board generally agreed that they find the
program very beneficial and they will decide on a contribution at the next
meeting after talking to Mr. Allen.
QUESTIONS OF THE ATTORNEY - Vincent P. Spagnuolo, of Murphy, Brenton &
Spagnuolo, P.C.
Attorney Spagnuolo also represents CATA, East Lansing Meridian Sewer and Water
Authority, Delta Township, and the Ingham County Library Authority. He does not
believe it is always the best use of his time and the client’s money to have
the attorney at the Township meetings. He sees potential problems with
attorney/client privilege issues by speaking at the public meetings and views
“shooting from the hip” answers to public questions as being close to mal-
practice. Delta Township has him come to specific board sessions where he has
worked on a project. They pick and choose when he comes to maximize the value
for his services. He has represented Delta for over 20 years and two of the
other three for over 11 years. Supervisor Obst asked about the potential for
issues coming up at meetings where the Board may not even realize they should
consult the attorney. One way to keep him updated is to have him review the
agenda packet prior to the meeting, and then review the minutes afterwards.
Attorney Spagnuolo questioned who is authorized to contact him? The Supervisor
or the Clerk have access to the attorney. Anyone else with issues clears it
through one of those two people. Planning chair has access after clearing it
through the Supervisor.
The Boundary Commission approved the legal sufficiency for the Bond property

The regular meeting of the Township Board of Trustees was called to order at 7:

JIM ALLEN - MEALS ON WHEELS, DIRECTOR
They are predicting a $30,000 deficit for the Tri County Council on the Aging
for the next fiscal year. To determine each municipality’s share, they looked
at the need and divided it out by the number of clients served in a particular
township or city: 0-10 clients $500; 11-30 $750; 31-50 $1,000; 51-100 $1,250.
Williamstown Township served 60 people. They do not see service decreasing in
the foreseeable future. They do keep records detailing exactly where clients
live in relation to City/Township boundaries. They plan on requesting to be put
on the budget as an annual item. Federal grants cover administrative overhead.
State Grants cover some, also some from clients themselves. The cut backs in
USDA reimbursement along with increased clientele, have both contributed to the
current shortfall. Motion made by Trustee Wiegandt, Supported by Treasurer
Nilsson to approve the requested $1,250 for Meals-On-Wheels services in the
Williamstown Township community for the year 2000. Motion approved unanimously.
CHARLES WITHEY - RED CEDAR RECREATION
They are looking for additional ball and soccer fields. They primarily use the
school fields, but they have also used some church fields. They are looking to
expand the development and improvement of fields. Their current emphasis is on
maintaining current fields, rather than actually developing new fields. They
don't have the funds to build new fields. They anticipate the increase taking
effect with the fall 1999 billing. Will send out a summary letter indicating
number of children from each entity. Supervisor Obst asked if there would be a
report on what the extra money was spent for? There is not a separate category
for the extra funds. It will be brought in as a general fund item. Treasurer
Nilsson stated that the Township would appreciate a report on how the money was
spent for the year. Mr. Withey stated that they are in the process of changing
directors, and consequently, budgets. Will forward reports as they become
available. Treasurer Nilsson moved, and Trustee Wiegandt supported to approve
the increase in contributions to Red Cedar Recreation Association to $10.00 per
child per program, billed three times per year, beginning with the fall 1999
billing. Discussion followed as to what the impact on the budget would be. The
increase would be approximately $3,000 per fiscal year. The fall and winter
billings would include the increase for the 1999/2000 fiscal year. Motion
approved unanimously.

Larkin Countryside Acres
The Planning Commission recommends granting Tentative Preliminary Plat Approval
with the following conditions:

recording of the road right-of-way and construction of the road to achieve
compliance with access requirements of the Land Division Ordinance and

extended to provide a cul-de-sac at the end, subject to Road Commission
approval.
3.   Drainage issues as discussed shall be worked out with Drain Commissioner
and adjoining property owner, and issues regarding responsibility of drainage
basins and the legal means by which such responsibility would be assigned shall
be resolved, taking into consideration that certain basins will not be within
the boundaries of the plat.

30, 1999 letter must be complied with.
5.   Approval shall be subject to approval by agencies having jurisdiction,
including but not limited to the Drain Commission, Michigan Department of
Environmental Quality and the Health Department.
There is currently no public access to Meridian Road. The project needs to be

out to Meridian Road. Trustee Wiegandt moved and Clerk Graham supported to

Hideaway Woods Sewer Request - Carl McIntosh
They requested 55 sewer connections in 1995. At that time they were lead to
believe the sewer capacity was available. in 1996 they were again assured that
the capacity did exist and the zoning of R1 should not be denied on that basis.
They prepared construction plans for sewer but neither the City of Williamston
nor the Township would look at them at that time. After that the Township filed
a lawsuit against the City. Mr. McIntosh and Mr. Perkins considered drawing up
their own lawsuit. Instead, they joined in the lawsuit with the Township
against the City. This process took the better part of two years. Mr. Perkins
spent between $15,000 and $20,000 of his own money in this lawsuit. They need
to have the sewer connections guaranteed to them. Mr. McIntosh stated that he
was told the issue should be resolved at the court date in July. It was two
months later before a signed agreement was reached between the City and the
Township. The Boundary Commission issue is coming up. Again, parties agreed to
a delay of the hearing. Mr. McIntosh believes that he was again mislead and is
convinced that no other outside decisions will be made that will make the
decision to grant or deny them the 55 sewer connections any easier. Of the 100
connections that were negotiated, 15 are already gone. No one else has been
involved in this issue since 1995, spent their own money and time and received
the assurances that they have. Mr. McIntosh stated that it is time for the
Board to make the decision and allocate the 55 connections that have been
promised. Believe they are first in line since 1995 and request that the board
take action and allocate the connections now that the zoning has been approved.
Supervisor Obst stated that the Township never made a commitment to supply
sewer service to the development. He wrote a letter to Mr. McIntosh that stated
if they go ahead with the rezoning request it would be at your own risk. The
Township received a letter from June Stovers representative that they would
like all the capacity. The established deadline for a City agreement is October
22nd. Supervisor Obst recommends the board commit to making a decision at the
next board meeting. Will know at that time if the detachment is going to go
forward. He believes there is a reasonable chance that the Township is going to
reach an agreement with the City. Mr. Obst also questioned the 55 connections
as being the number requested. Is there a number less than 55 that would still
be feasible? Mr. McIntosh stated that two different conceptual layouts of the
property have 55 lots them. Some of the lots are in R1, some in R1S with a
density option, and the remaining lots in tonight’s rezoning. Neither the City
nor the Township has been willing to review the engineering plans for them to
be able to determine how many lots would be required to make the pumping
station economically feasible. None of the City's engineers have reviewed the
plans. They are changing their standards all the time. No way to know what they
will settle on and how they will affect the plans. Someone needs to determine
who reviews the plans - Township or City - in order for Mr. McIntosh to get a
cost estimate. Mr. McIntosh stated that it has been 4.5 years. They have done
everything asked of them to further this along. They need a decision ASAP.
Treasurer Nilsson agrees they've been caught in the middle. The Township never
intended to deceive anybody. This has been a difficult situation all around.
Supervisor Obst stated that he thought he had assured Mr. McIntosh that there
was never any intent to deceive, there were miscommunications that happened.
Mr. McIntosh accepted that. Trustee Zaban stated that the Township only got out
of the lawsuit what was in the original agreement to begin with. The Board are
all as frustrated as Mr. McIntosh. Mr. Charlie Perkins stated that he wants it
to be over with. He wants to be out of town by November 1st for the winter.

before November 1st.

DECEMBER 7, 1999
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:36 PM. Clerk Graham was asked to record who was present and
recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk Graham, Treasurer Nilsson,
Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban, and Building Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: Michigan Department of
Consumer and Industry Services - Liquor Control Commission - transfer of liquor

UNFINISHED BUSINESS -
Township Hall Rental - Township’s Insurance Agent, Don Pixley
The Township currently carries an umbrella of $1,000,000 over the basic
liability of $1,000,000.00. Their insurance company’s legal staff has reviewed
a copy of our rental agreement. They are not going to give a legal opinion. One
of the things they pointed out was that the Township is carrying $1,000,000.
Someone renting the hall should be carrying the same. To increase the average
homeowner’s policy from $300,000 to $1,000,000 liability is usually around $11
or $12 per year. Other Townships in the area require renters to carry
$1,000,000. The renter would need to contact their insurance agent and name the
Township as an additional insured on their insurance. Takes 3 or 4 days
planning to do it. No liquor is allowed on the Township Hall premises, but it
still may happen when Township Officials and staff are not here to monitor. To
protect the assets of the Township it should be mandatory for renters of the
hall to have this coverage. Clerk Graham asked if there was a standard form?
Mr. Pixley stated that there is a standard certificate that the renter would
get from their agent. Other similar facilities require this type of coverage.
Mr. Pixley stated that his office issues this type of certificate frequently.
Question from the audience as to who would have primary liability? Mr. Pixley
stated that it would probably be the host, but that is an issue that would be
decided by the judge if there were a law suit. The judge could split the
liability at any percentage he deemed appropriate to the particular case.
Suggestion from audience to increase the rate to rent the hall and increase the
coverage at the Township. The Board generally agreed to delay the decision
until the next meeting. Clerk Graham will check with other municipalities to
see what kind of coverage they require.

Pinehill Rezoning - 35 acres on Zimmer Road. Request was made to change the
Zoning from Rural Estates (RE) with a 5 acre minimum, to R1 with a 20,000
square foot minimum if sewer is available, or R1S with a 40,000 square foot
minimum if sewer is not available. After receiving input from two public
hearings, the transportation committee, the planning consultant and considering
a great deal of information from the surrounding property owners and neighbors,
the Planning Commission recommends denying rezoning of the property to either
R1 or R1S. Supervisor Obst stated that additional information had been
received. He read a letter from the Vaughns opposing the rezoning. The Township
also received a letter this afternoon from Steven Hayward to Mr. Forsberg dated
Dec. 6th indicating he would attend tonight’s Board meeting. Dennis Forsberg,
representing Pinehill partnership, and Mr. Hayward made presentations. Mr.
Hayward is an architect that specializes in keeping the rural character of
developments. Mr. Hayward’s letter and comments were found to be either
inaccurate, or misleading as stated, in several instances.
Mr. Forsberg stated that in order to maintain the development’s proposed soccer
field they would need 44 homes in the subdivision. The Township would not be
liable for maintenance on the soccer field. It would be supported by the
homeowner association fees. The pond would probably not be as large as
currently indicated on the plan. Drain outlet would be across Zimmer road. Mr.
Hayward stated that the Township’s future land use map shows the 400 feet on
Zimmer frontage should be single family residential in nature. Development plan
shows a 50 foot buffer all around the development. The developer would
volunteer to put limits on the number of lots since there isn't a zoning that
really fits what they are requesting. This property requires sanitary sewers.
There is no obligation on the part of the Township to provide sewer taps to
grant the rezoning. The taps would not be an issue until the Site Plan approval
phase.
Public comments followed. All but one opposed the development, citing such
things as increased traffic, current availability of other building sites in
the Township, unwanted changes to the rural atmosphere, desire for the Township
to follow the master plan that they adopted, and too high of a density for the
area. Would like to see larger lots.
Mr. Forsberg conceded hearing that the residents were against a R1S or R1
zoning, but that maybe Rural Residential (RR) would be acceptable. He stated
that they would take a look and see what they can come up with. He was informed
that this would mean going through the entire process again if they decide to
request RR Zoning. Supervisor Obst stated that a decision on a future RR
rezoning request would be based on zoning ordinance criteria applied to
information received at that time.
Trustee Zaban moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported to adopt the Planning
Commission’s recommendation for denial of the Pinehill Partnership rezoning
request for either R-1 or R-1-S zoning, based on considerations required by
Section 27.06(C)4 of the Zoning Ordinance and information in Planning
Consultant, Christopher Doozen’s, letters of July 29 and November 8, 1999.
Motion passed unanimously.
Transportation Committee Report - Brian Jennings
Zimmer and Grand River Options presented by MDOT - MDOT is recommending a
modern roundabout for the intersection. However, they have been unable to
satisfactorily answer many of the Transportation Committee’s questions about
this type of intersection. Mr. Jennings has done some research on his own and
found that modern roundabouts are fairly new to the U.S. and are different than
the traditional center of town traffic circle. They have been in Europe for
several years. There seem to be a lot of circumstances where traffic circles
eliminate a lot of problems that other options have not been able to. The
majority of modern roundabouts in the U.S. are in the West, Florida and New
England. There are very few in the Mid-west. Road structures differ in
different parts of the country. Very little data on how well one might work in
this area, especially at an intersection such as Grand River and Zimmer, where
the two roads have very different traffic volumes. The Township has a video
tape of a seminar that states the modern roundabouts don't work everywhere and
if they are not designed correctly they can cause more problems than they fix.
MDOT has not done a final feasibility study on this intersection, and
consequently they don't know if they can fit a modern roundabout into the
available land at this intersection with the correct geometry. The
Transportation Committee is recommending informing MDOT that if they need an
immediate recommendation, the Township is not prepared to support a modern
roundabout at this time. If MDOT is willing and able to provide more factual
data about modern roundabouts, the Township would like to keep an open mind and
work with them. Until and unless modern roundabouts can be proven to be a
better option, the Township would like to recommend signalizing and adding left
turn lanes at all approaches for the intersection.. Mr. Jennings will keep
doing his research and contact MDOT to inform them that the Township is not
getting the information it needs, and wants some better answers to the
questions. If the State is having Mr. Crown design the modern roundabout, the
Township would like to have him give a presentation to the Board, Planning
Commission and the Advisory Council.

JANUARY 11, 2000
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:44 PM. Clerk Graham was asked to record who was present and
recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk Graham, Treasurer Nilsson,
Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban, and Building Inspector Aven.

PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
The Planning Commission is working on the update of the Master Plan. They are
having five guest speakers at their meeting on January 25th. They invited the
Board to attend this meeting. Have also invited the surrounding Townships’ and
City of Williamston’s Planning Commissions and the Advisory Council. Have
mapped all the active agricultural land in the Township. Mapped new housing in
the last nine years. Mapping the wooded lands. It appears that the Township has

FEBRUARY 1, 2000
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:36 PM. Clerk Graham was asked to record who was present and
recorded the following: Supervisor Obst, Clerk Graham, Treasurer Nilsson,
Trustee Wiegandt, Trustee Zaban and Building Inspector Aven.
The agenda was read over with the following additions: Letter of agreement from
the auditors and a complaint that was received today.
Deputy Drain Commissioner - Eric Schertzing
Maintenance - The 1999 Drain Maintenance work in Williamstown Township included
digging on the Squaw Creek Drain which services the township and also the
outlet of the Bullett Lake Drain. We anticipate the year 2000 projects to
include clean out of parts of the Squaw, Atzinger, Bullett Lake Drains and
perhaps some work on the Corcoran Intercounty Drain. Clerk Graham asked about
the Leiprandt issue by the school. Mr. Schertzing stated that there is not a
county drain there at this time. School properties do not fall under the
jurisdiction of the Ingham County Drain Commission and could possibly create a
problem for neighboring properties without the Drain Commission being able to
prevent it. The Drain Commission is currently looking at the area to see if a
county drain needs to be put in place. Mrs. Leiprandt has been advised of the
status from the Drain Commission.
Supervisor Obst had a question on paragraph 4 of the proposed spending
resolution. The Drain Commission is authorized to spend up to $2,500 per mile
for maintenance before going to the local municipalities for authorization.
There are approximately 6 miles of the Bullett Lake Drain that need to be
cleaned out at an estimated cost of $30,000. This would be $15,000 above the
pre-authorized amount. The Drain Commission is asking to spend two years of
maintenance money in one year. They do not need to go to a Board of
Determination to maintain an existing drain. Mailing was done to everyone in
the watershed letting them know that Mr. Schertzing would be here tonight with
the spending resolution. The assessments for the cleaning of Bullett Lake Drain
are $1,400 at large to be paid by the Township, $9 per agricultural acre and
$11.25 per residential acre. To be spread over two years since they are
spending two years’ money to do the clean out. Property owner of the beginning
of the drain very much in favor of the clean out being done. The Drain
Commission needs the approval of both Williamstown and Locke Townships.
Treasurer Nilsson had a question on how the spending allowance and the actual
cost of cleaning out a drain are related. They are not. The spending allowance
is something determined by State Legislatures and does not reflect the actual
costs of doing the clean outs. Trustee Zaban moved and Trustee Wiegandt
supported that the Township approve the following spending resolution for the
clean out of the Bullett Lake Drain as proposed by the County Drain Commission:
WHEREAS, the Ingham County Drain Commissioner, Patrick E. Lindemann, has
advised the Board of Trustees for the Township of Williamstown that, pursuant
to Section 196 of the Michigan Drain Code (MCL 280.196; MSA 11.1196), an
inspection has been made of the Bullett Lake Drain and it has been determined,
as a result of the inspection, that certain maintenance must be performed upon
the Drain; and,
WHEREAS, the Ingham County Drain Commissioner, Patrick E. Lindemann, has the
authority to expend Two Thousand Five Hundred and no/100 Dollars ($2,500.00)
per mile in any one (1) year for the maintenance of the drain, and where it is
estimated that expenditures in excess of Two Thousand Five Hundred and no/100
Dollars ($2,500.00) per mile are necessary, those amounts may not be expended
until approved by Resolution of the governing body of each township, city and
village affected by more than twenty percent (20%) of the cost; and,
WHEREAS, the Ingham County Drain Commissioner, Patrick E. Lindemann, has
advised the Township of Williamstown Board of Trustees that it will be
necessary to expend funds in excess of Two Thousand Five Hundred and no/100
Dollars ($2,500.00) per mile for the maintenance of the Bullett Lake Drain and
that the Township of Williamstown is affected by more than twenty percent (20%)
of the cost; and,
WHEREAS, the Ingham County Drain Commissioner, Patrick E. Lindemann, estimates
that the cost for the maintenance of the Bullett Lake Drain will be
approximately $30,000.00, which constitutes $15,000 in excess of the authorized
Two Thousand Five Hundred and no/100 Dollars ($2,500.00) per mile.
NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED by the Board of Trustees for the Township
of Williamstown, that pursuant to Section 196 of the Drain Code, the Ingham
County Drain Commissioner, Patrick E. Lindemann, is authorized to expend money
for the maintenance and repair of the Bullett Lake Drain in excess of Two
Thousand Five Hundred and no/100 Dollars ($2,500.00) per mile and, to the
extent that the drain fund for the Drain contains insufficient funds for the
payment of costs incurred for the maintenance or repair of the Drain, then the
Ingham County Drain Commissioner, Patrick E. Lindemann, is authorized to levy a
special assessment, as allowed by law.
RESOLUTION approved this 1st day of February, 2000, by the Township of
Williamstown Board of Trustees, governing body of Williamstown Township.
Supervisor Obst called for a roll call vote:
   Ayes: Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Weigandt, Supervisor Obst, Trustee Zaban,
Clerk Graham.
   Nays: None.
Resolution approved unanimously.
PUBLIC COMMENTS AND QUESTIONS
Catherine Easley voiced her concerns regarding the 425 negotiations between the
City of Williamston and the Township of Williamstown. She stated that the media
are only talking about the Bond Property annexation when discussing the
negotiations between the City and the Township. The detachment group is
concerned about more than just the Bond property and wondered if anything else
was on the table to address their concerns - especially the threat of future
annexations. Supervisor Obst stated that it is a misperception that only the
Bond property is being discussed. It is the intent of both the City and the
Township to address all the concerns of the people interested in the
detachment. There are several 425 agreements being looked at, not just one for
the Bond property. The City of Williamston has adopted a resolution opposing
annexation of any property owner that does not want to be annexed, and 425
negotiations are looking at a way of making this a more long term agreement.
There are scheduled meetings this week and next week between the City and the
Township. Both sides are well aware that there are many concerns besides the
Bond property. Supervisor Obst stated that TAP is, reportedly, scheduling a
meeting where they will invite him to address these concerns. Once preliminary
agreements are reached there would be public hearings scheduled to determine
needed revisions. The intent of the board is to address all of the concerns of
everyone involved in the detachment effort.
PLANNING COMMISSION - Mickey Martin
They had an excellent meeting last Tuesday with the 5 speakers. They spoke to
the Township regarding agriculture in the future in the County in general, and
in the Township in particular. Planning Chair Martin stated that they have
accomplished the current master plan goals to date. The majority of development
over the past ten years has been south of Sherwood Road. The Township has been
able to keep a lot of active agriculture even with the urban sprawl going
forward. Trends in the area and the state are for less live stock. Going
towards management intensive agriculture in the future. This area is not
challenged for agricultural suppliers and support systems. Zoning, purchasing
and transfers of development rights are tools used to keep the agriculture in
the Township. The Township needs to designate areas of the Township where
development rights can be transferred to and from. Will need to invest in these
procedures for the Township to retain the desired character. The Planning
Commission is looking at the east side and west side next to the City of
Williamston to make sure the Township’s plan for these areas are compatible
with what the City has in their master plan.
Neller property - haven't heard anything since last August. They were at the
conceptual plan point. Paid fee for rezoning application, which has been used
up.
Mr. Forsberg asked for another rezoning application. Haven’t heard back since
then. Nothing formal has been initiated.
Mr. McIntosh has come in with a couple of proposals for the Hideaway Woods
area.

Found 70 graves that don't have markers. They are asking the City and Township
