GRAND RIVER & ZIMMER INTERSECTION PRESENTATION - Michigan Department of
Transportation
Tony Kratofil, Associate Region Engineer for MDOT, discussed the safety issues
that exist at the intersection of Zimmer and Grand River. Requests have been
made for a traffic signal, but the intersection does not meet the State’s
warrants for installing a signal. The Township Board had requested more
information on the modern roundabout option. Mr. Kratofil introduced Mr. Leif
Ourston, President of Ourston Roundabout Interchanges, the leading expert in
the United States on roundabout design, and the person hired by the State to
design a roundabout for the Zimmer and Grand River intersection. Mr. Ourston
showed a couple of videos of roundabouts in the Vail Colorado area and in
Britain. He is proposing a 150 foot diameter roundabout for the Grand River and
Zimmer intersection. Road reconstruction is set for the construction season of
2001. Treasurer Nilsson asked about the roundabout in Claremont, California
that was taken out after only eight months. Mr. Ourston stated that particular
roundabout was not designed by him, and was a poor design from the beginning.
23 roundabouts have been built that were designed by Mr. Ourston. All of them
have been successful. Roundabouts on average show a 75% reduction in injury
accidents, and a 50% reduction in accidents of all kinds, as compared to a
signaled intersection. There has never been a pedestrian or bicycle related
crash in a modern roundabout (last 10 years) in this country. Advantages of
modern roundabouts over a signaled intersection are low stop delays; easier to
make the left turn; easier for pedestrians to cross the street; enhanced beauty
of the intersection; elevate whole feeling of town; and reductions in
emissions, fuel waste and noise. France is currently building over 1000 a year.
More information on roundabouts vs. traffic signals can be found at
Ourston.com. MDOT and ICRC emphasized that the intersection is still not close
to meeting warrants for a traffic signal. Currently, the options are keeping
what we have or a roundabout.
Mr. Joe Dexter voiced his concerns about getting large farm equipment around
the roundabout. Mr. Ourston stated that it would be large enough to accommodate
the equipment. Mr. Dwight Kampe stated that he was in favor of the roundabout.
Ms. Jane Reagan, Planning Commission Chair for the City of Williamston, stated
that she was in favor of the roundabout design and that the City was
investigating installing roundabouts at up to three locations. Supervisor Obst
asked the transportation committee to study the information provided and make a
recommendation to the Advisory Committee in time for a recommendation to be
made to the Board by the June 6th Board meeting. Mr. John McLaughlin,
representing the Transportation Committee, stated that the committee would be
very much in favor of doing this. Mickey Martin, Planning Commission Chair,
stated that there will need to be a lot of public education to convince the
community that this is the correct thing to do. She suggested making the videos
available to loan out. Supervisor Obst suggested the Transportation Committee
get some feedback from the City officials as well. Mr. Bob D'Alcorn, P.E.,
Managing Director of the Ingham County Road Commission, stated that the
roundabout at Marsh and Hamilton will be in operation by mid June. They are
using their road construction radio station to educate people on how to drive
the circle. Mr. D’Alcorn also indicated that he was in favor of construction of
the roundabout at the intersection of Zimmer and Grand River.

Transportation Committee - John McLaughlin
They went over the ICRC’s list of suggested improvements. Started with gravel
roads. Feel should be left alone because of low density on them. Individuals
living on them should be contacted if decide otherwise.
Question about crack filling and micro surfacing for temporary repairs of the
roads. Cost for duration of crack filling not warranted. Impressed with micro
surfacing but want to wait for another winter before recommending it for the
township.
A resident of Red Cedar manor asked for repair. There are some spots that need
attention on Congdon. Overall it is in good condition. The committee will
advise the neighborhood of the rating system, and what their direct cost would
be, to see if there is interest in doing something.
It was brought to the committee’s attention that there is some subdivision
development pending across from the Middle School off of Vanneter. The
committee suggests waiting for a schedule of development before scheduling any
construction work on Vanneter and Mitchell. They recommend continuing to set
aside funds for the project and possibly use some of that money now to start
doing engineering work. Supervisor Obst had questions for Mr. D’Alcorn on the
ICRC’s previous proposal vs. their current bare bones proposal. The previous
proposal included curb and gutter, underground catch basins, rebuilding the
road. Current proposal was just for resurfacing, slight widening of shoulder,
slight improvement of drainage at Rowley and Vanneter and drainage that needs
to cross Mitchell at the athletic fields. Would not involve curb and gutter.
The County can roll over funds to next year. Mr. D’Alcorn suggested that the
Township state that they are saving for a larger project. The County
Commissioners are more likely to approve the request if they know it is to save
for a large project. The County approved carrying over the remaining $10,516
from 1999 to 2000. Williamston Schools will be asked by the Ingham County Road
Commission to pay for fixing the drainage problem that they created on Mitchell
Road when they built the athletic fields behind the High School.
Treasurer Nilsson and Trustee Zaban believe in crack filling and want more
information on why the Transportation Committee is against it. The
Transportation Committee was more impressed with micro surfacing than crack
filling, but they want to see how well the micro sealing stands up to another
winter before making a recommendation. Micro surfacing costs approximately
$15,000 to $20,000 a mile. Crack filling costs about $1,200 a mile, but only
lasts a year or two. The Board asked the Transportation Committee to come back
to them with a cost analysis of crack filling vs. micro surfacing and to
further justify their position on crack filling.
The Transportation Committee also reported that it is their belief that the
time has come for the Township to look more seriously at other sources of
income to maintain our roads. Even though there is not a lot going on now, the
Township is going to have more subdivision streets and more serious road
reconstruction in the future. Supervisor Obst requested that the Transportation
Committee come back to the Board with recommendations. Supervisor Obst also
asked for recommendations to implement the committee’s proposal to meet Master
Plan road objectives.
Clerk Graham was contacted by three residents on Barry Road that would like
their road paved. Various requests have been made in the past. The
Transportation Committee had not received any comments from anyone wanting the
roads paved. The Board has asked the committee to come up with recommendations
and cost estimates for paving Barry road.

JUNE 6, 2000
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:35 p.m. Deputy Clerk Florence DuBreuil recorded those present as
Supervisor Norman Obst, Treasurer Christine Nilsson, Trustee Ronald Wiegandt,
Trustee Steven Zaban and Building Inspector Walter Aven. Clerk Shirley Graham
was absent. It was moved by Trustee Wiegandt, seconded by Trustee Zaban,
passed, that the absence of Clerk Graham be excused.
Supervisor Obst reviewed the agenda and added the following: Request from Doug
Stover from Ingham County Equalization and Tax Services, Tom Aker’s request for
sewer service, appointment to the NIESA Board, Planning Commission resignation
and appointment, information from Robert Bond’s attorney, and a possible
special meeting of the Board to sign 425 agreements with the City of
Williamston.
INGHAM COUNTY EQUALIZATION AND TAX SERVICES – Doug Stover, Director
Mr. Stover asked that the Township provide Ingham County with the electronic
export of the 2000 assessment roll. All other Ingham County townships had
already done so and the same software was used by 50 percent of the
municipalities in the state. They received many requests for property and tax
information, and such information was not always readily available from
townships. Questions could be answered by the County during regular business
hours. It would also allow the County to do studies and would assist in tax
mapping. The technology would streamline operations, and Mr. Stover would like
to see this done by the end of the year. Supervisor Obst explained that the
Township had not done this in the past due to a desire to maintain residents’
privacy. If such a list existed the Township would be required to provide it
with a FOIA request. At this time no such list exists. The option of denying
the request would be lost if the information were electronically available. He
agreed the process would be beneficial for the County. It was moved by
Treasurer Nilsson, seconded by Trustee Wiegandt, passed unanimously, that the
Township provide the electronic export of the 2000 assessment roll to Ingham
County Equalization and Tax Services.
INGHAM COUNTY SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT – Martha Knorek
Ms. Knorek reported that State law required that county Solid Waste Management
Plans be updated every five years. The new Ingham County plan was now finished
and had been provided to all municipalities. Approval of 67 percent was needed
prior to submittal to the MDEQ for their final approval. Waste generated in
Ingham County could now be sent to 18 facilities in 11 counties, and capacity
was provided for ten years. The budget would be done after the plan was
approved. The County has requested a fee of 62 cents per cubic yard to be
returned to the County for solid waste programs. She asked the Board to adopt a
resolution indicating their support of the County’s Solid Waste Management
Plan. It was moved by Trustee Wiegandt, seconded by Treasurer Nilsson, passed
unanimously, that the Township Board sign a resolution (see page 4) in support
of the Ingham County Board of Commissioners’ Solid Waste Management Plan, as
adopted on April 25, 2000.
COMPENSATION FOR OVER-BOOKING OF TOWNSHIP HALL - Tammy Kalzenski
Ms. Kalzenski explained that she had booked the Township Hall for her wedding
reception and had received a signed contract. It was later discovered by the
Township that there was a previous booking for that date. She had found a new
location after some concern and expense and it had necessitated her making new
invitations. The cost of the Township’s hall was $60 and St. Mary’s hall was
$560. She had been told by Clerk Graham that the matter would be brought to the
Board at this meeting for possible reimbursement. She requested compensation
and a quick resolution of the problem. The Board agreed that some payment was
due. She agreed that $310 would be satisfactory compensation. It was moved by
Trustee Zaban, seconded by Treasurer Nilsson, passed, that compensation in the
amount of $310 would be paid to Tammy Kalzenski for costs incurred due to
overbooking of the Township Hall.
TOM AKER, 1040 East Grand River Road – Request for Sewer Hookup
Mr. Aker had been asked at a previous Board meeting to show the sewer line
which had been placed under Grand River Road for his future use. He submitted a
plan dated May 13, 1996, and approved by the Drain Commission on June 8, 1998,
which showed where the sleeve was located under Grand River, and said he
realized he may have to pump up to the sewer line. He was now asking for one
connection for a single family home. Supervisor Obst explained that the tap
could only come from the Township’s existing allocation of sewer taps, but said
it would be prudent to wait until current 425 agreements were finalized before
making a decision.
PLANNING COMMISSION – Mickey Martin, Planning Coordinator
Fred and Theresa Foote, request to rezone 123 acres at 5820 Shoeman Rd. from
AG-SF to AG-C: The applicants wanted an accessory building larger than that
allowed in the AG-SF district, and requested rezoning to AG-C to allow
unlimited accessory buildings. The use would be for a private horse arena,
which would be in keeping with goals expressed in the Township’s Master Plan as
an alternative use of agricultural land. There had been no comments at the
public hearing and the Planning Commission recommended approval of the
application. It was moved by Trustee Wiegandt, seconded by Trustee Zaban,
passed, that the Board approve the Foote request to rezone 123 acres on Shoeman
Road from AG-SF to AG-C, based on the recommendation of the Planning Commission
and McKenna Associates, Inc.’s letter of May 8, 2000.Bob and Susan Lombardini,
1500 Epley Road, special land use permit and site plan for private riding arena
larger than 2400 square feet in size: All requirements were met. Several
neighbors submitted letters expressing no opposition to the plan. The Planning
Commission recommended approval with the following conditions: (1) the stable
remain in private use, and (2) no outdoor storage to be allowed behind the new
stable. Zoning Ordinance criteria for approval of special land use permits had
been reviewed and were in compliance. It was moved by Trustee Zaban, seconded
by Trustee Wiegandt, passed, that the special land use permit for the
Lombardini private riding arena be approved, with conditions for continued
private use and indoor storage only. Planning Chair Martin reported that many
requests were being received for large accessory buildings for riding arenas,
and the Commission would consider changing the 2400 square foot limit.
Master Plan: A public hearing on the revised Plan would be held on June 27,
2000. Areas with particular revisions included transportation, agriculture
(including alternative agriculture), the Grand River corridor, population, and
an overall update of the entire plan. Also noted and expanded were regional
planning and cooperation, public transit, and affordable housing. The Planning
Commission had gathered master plans from neighboring municipalities and many
of those officials had attended a meeting on the future of agriculture in the
Township.
Hideaway Woods No. : An application had been received from Charles Perkins
requesting rezoning from R-1-S/DO to R-1 for 3.86 acres in Hideaway Woods. The
applicant had asked to use open space from Hideaway Woods No. 3 as open space
in plat No. 5 as well. When the same question had been raised in plat No. 4 in
1996, the Township Attorney had ruled against it. The Township did not plan to
pursue it further at this time, and the applicant had not challenged the
decision.
Planning Coordinator Martin reported that Planning Commissioner Chuck Cleland
had resigned due to retirement and relocation, and she recommended Rutgar Hoag
to fill his term until September 2000. Mr. Hoag had experience with the
Township through the Advisory Council and Zoning Board of Appeals. Supervisor
Obst nominated Rutgar Hoag to fill the Planning Commission vacancy, with his
term to end in September 2000. The motion was seconded by Trustee Wiegandt and
passed unanimously.
ADVISORY COUNCIL – Rutgar Hoag
Transportation Committee
Mr. Hoag reported the Transportation Committee’s recommendation that a study
for Vanneter and Mitchell Roads begin now and other items be put on hold.
Treasurer Nilsson said an Ingham County engineer may have time to work on that
project in the fall, but suggested listing it as a budget item in the event the

and commit to and plan for engineering work to be done this year on Mitchell
and Vanneter Roads in conjunction with the Ingham County Road Commission.
Trustee Zaban will check with other counties to see what types of road repairs
they favor.
Mr. Hoag stated it was the recommendation of the Advisory Council that the
Township Board support the concept of a roundabout with five conditions listed
in their report. An effort would be required to educate residents about
benefits, which would include reduced speed and better access to Grand River
and Zimmer Roads. Deputy Clerk DuBreuil reported that Clerk Graham did not
favor the roundabout. Trustee Wiegandt had received calls from 11 people
opposing such a change. Some preferred turn lanes on both roads if a traffic
light could not be installed. Planning Coordinator Martin said MDOT had not
contacted adjoining property owners to inform them of possible plans. The
Supervisor said MDOT had asked for a recommendation from the Township prior to
their decision. Trustee Wiegandt said he could not support a roundabout without
seeing a specific plan for this location, but such a plan would not be
available before fall and a recommendation was requested now.
It was moved by Trustee Zaban, seconded by Treasurer Nilsson, that the Township
Board recommend that the Michigan Department of Transportation go forward with
the roundabout at Grand River and Zimmer Roads with the following conditions:
(1) MDOT start an aggressive informational campaign in the area regarding
roundabouts, how they work, safety features, etc., (2) MDOT contact all
landowners surrounding the proposed roundabout and review the plans for
workability, (3) MDOT and the Board start educational meetings for the public
on how to use a roundabout, (4) MDOT make every effort to lower the speed on
Grand River Road in the area east and west approaching the roundabout, (5) MDOT
contact the Post Office and try to work out another entrance/exit plan onto
Zimmer and Grand River, and (6) a final recommendation will not be made until a
specific site plan is seen. A roll call vote was taken:
   Aye:   Supervisor Obst, Treasurer Nilsson, Trustee Zaban
   Nay:   Trustee Wiegandt

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
ESOLUTION OF APPROVAL
INGHAM COUNTY SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT PLAN
WHEREAS, Michigan counties, under the “Public Health Code”, have a
responsibility to prevent and control environmental hazards; and,
WHEREAS, the “Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act” requires
counties to conduct solid waste planning processes and to adopt a countywide
solid waste management plan; and,
WHEREAS, the Ingham County Board of Commissioners has approved the Solid Waste
Management Plan; and,
WHEREAS, Part 115 of the “Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act”
requires 67 percent municipal approval for a Solid Waste Management Plan to
obtain approval by the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP Board of
Trustees approves the Solid Waste Management Plan as adopted by the Ingham
County Board of Commissioners on April 25, 2000.

JULY 11, 2000
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:30 p.m. Deputy Clerk Florence DuBreuil stated a quorum was
present and recorded the following: Supervisor Norman Obst, Treasurer Christine
Nilsson, Trustee Ronald Wiegandt, Trustee Steven Zaban, Deputy Clerk Florence
DuBreuil and Building Inspector Walter Aven. Clerk Shirley Graham’s absence was
excused due to illness.
The agenda was reviewed with the following addition: Litchfield letter
requesting a refund of their Special Land Use Permit application fee.
AUDITOR’S REPORT - Michael Gaffney
The Township received an unqualified opinion. There was a 10% increase in
revenues over the previous year. This was partially due to the one time
settlement payment from the City of Williamston. There was a 5% decrease in
expenditures. This was partially due to the reduction of road work last year.
Report on Internal Control Structures - Overall systems work quite well. There
were a couple of minor issues noted. The Sewer Replacement fund and Debt
Service fund did not have an adopted budget. The Township needs to adopt one
for the Debt Service Fund for the 2000/2001 fiscal year. The Sewer Replacement
fund no longer exists.
Accounting transactions - Initial transaction of a performance bond was not in
the general ledger, but the pay back of the bond was. Need to report the entire
transaction in the general ledger.
PLANNING COMMISSION REPORT - Mickey Martin
There were no action items for the Board. A public hearing was held June 27th
to obtain input regarding the proposed changes to the Master Plan. The majority
of the comments were on traffic. In general, people seemed happy with the way
development has progressed in the Township and is planned to progress in the
future. The Planning Commission will deliberate and vote on the plan this
month. MDOT is saying now they will address the problems at Grand River and
Zimmer absent a roundabout and absent a traffic light. There are three Public
Hearings scheduled for July 18th. 1) Rezoning request for Charles Perkins for
the R1S - D/O open area; 2) Shoemaker request for a Special Land Use Permit for
a 2300 sq. foot building; and 3) All Terrain Alterations request for a Special
Land Use Permit and Site Plan Review to expand their facility. Treasurer
Nilsson questioned the Perkins rezoning request. Some of the Open Space
established with Mr. Perkin’s density option was designated as temporary open
space. This means that if circumstances change the property has a possibility –
though not a guarantee – of being rezoned. The recent availability of sewer in
the area is such a change.
PARK AND RECREATION COMMITTEE - Chris Nilsson and Mickey Martin
The construction for the park entrance has been put out to bid. Waiting for
bids to come in. Will also post it on the door at the Township Hall. George
Durak had a question on the Township's involvement in the regional recreation
authority. Chuck Withey has a committee looking into the viability of such an
authority. The Board supports the idea, but not a millage at this time. Need to
do further investigation and planning before money is needed. Have not gotten
past the general concept phase yet, which they need to do to get this going.
1999 Public Act 123 and Legislative update from the Treasurer's Institute - Sue
Jennings
Report accepted. No questions.
OLD BUSINESS
ICRC/ Carryover of Road Improvement Allocations, 1999-2001
MDOT: Grand River Road & Zimmer Road Considerations
The Board hopes the MDOT engineering department can come up with some ideas and
plans for the intersection since the roundabout has been turned down. Will stay
on top of it and see if they can come up with some good ideas for the
intersection. Mr. Durak had a question on how Meridian and Grand River compared
to Zimmer and Grand River. Studies a few years ago showed that a small minority
goes east on Grand River from south bound Meridian.
425 Agreements
The three Act 425 agreements have been signed by both the City and the
Township. The detachment election is cancelled. The injunction is permanent
pending further action from the court.
Sewer For Other Residents And Possible Additional 425's. – Norman Obst
We have opened up talks with the City regarding a possible fourth Act 425
agreement for services to non contiguous property.
Bond Property
There is a meeting with Mr. Bond's attorney, the City and the Township on
Wednesday July 12th at 9:00 a.m.

SecretaryGREATER LANSING AREA REGIONAL NPDES PHASE II
STORM WATER REGULATIONS COMMITTEE
WHEREAS, the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is requiring
nine communities in the greater Lansing area to obtain a National Pollutant
Discharge Elimination System Phase II (NPDES II) Permit by March 2003, and
WHEREAS, the NPDES II permit process is an unfunded federal mandate, and
WHEREAS, the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) has developed
criteria to obtain funding in the form of grants in part from the Clean
Michigan Initiative if communities adopt a voluntary approach to storm water
and watershed management, and
WHEREAS, representatives of the nine communities named by the EPA those being
City of Lansing, City of East Lansing, Meridian Township, Lansing Township,
Delta Township, Delhi Township, Bath Township, Dewitt Township, and
Williamstown Township, have met to develop a cooperative regional approach to
implementing a storm water and watershed management plan, and
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that a committee composed of representatives
from the nine named communities meet on a regular basis to facilitate the
requirements of the NPDES II Permit by developing a regional storm water and
watershed management plan while seeking the input and assistance from other
agencies including but not limited to county commissions, county drain
commissioner’s offices, county health departments, county road commissions,
Tri-County Regional Planning Commission, and the Michigan Municipal League.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the committee shall also meet to develop funding
strategies to implement this regional stormwater and watershed management plan.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Nancy Fink or her designee is authorized to be the
official representative from Williamstown Township to the committee.
BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED, that the storm water and watershed management plan and
any funding strategies must be approved by the participating communities’
governing bodies before implementation.

SEPTEMBER 5, 2000
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:35 p.m. Deputy Clerk DuBreuil stated a quorum was present and
recorded the following: Supervisor Norman Obst, Treasurer Christine Nilsson,
Trustee Ronald Wiegandt, Trustee Steven Zaban, Deputy Clerk Florence DuBreuil,
and Building Inspector Walter Aven. Clerk Shirley Graham deceased August 17,
2000.
The agenda was reviewed with the following additions: appointment of committee
to review our burning ordinance and a resolution honoring Clerk Shirley Graham.
PLANNING COMMISSION: Mickey Martin
Special Land Use Permit for Litchfield Commercial Center. Permit for a sign to
exceed the maximum allowed height of six feet. The Planning Commission has
recommended approving the Special Land Use Permit to erect a sign with a
maximum of nine feet. The nine feet will include a planter on the bottom and/or
a roof and lighting on the top. Motion: Trustee Wiegandt moved and Trustee
Zaban supported approving the Planning Commission’s recommendation for approval
of a Special Land Use Permit for Litchfield Commercial Center for a maximum
sign height of nine feet, based on the fact that visibility was needed for
businesses at the rear of the site, and landscaping and a roof were found to be
attractive and appealing because they were consistent with the design of the
primary building. Motion passed unanimously.
All Terrain Special Land Use Permit to expand and improve their premises. All
conditions of the Planning Commission have been met. Contractors will be able
to go in and get their materials which is why parking in the front had to be
approved. Wholesale operation, not much retail. Can have 25% retail in the
district that they are in. Public comment was in favor. Motion: Treasurer
Nilsson moved and Trustee Zaban supported approving the Planning Commission’s
recommendation for approval of a Special Land Use Permit for All Terrain
Alterations. Supervisor Obst asked if any conditions needed to be added to the
motion. Planning Chair Martin stated that there were no conditions needed on
the motion because they have all been satisfied. Motion passed unanimously.
Larkin Country Side Acres Final Plat - Part of the development will be platted,
part will not. Deed restrictions will cover the entire development. Only the
first 10 lots are platted. The developers have put up performance bonds to
ensure that the infrastructure will be completed. The infrastructure is usually
complete at this point in the process, but they have decided to go with
performance bonds instead. Motion: Supervisor Obst moved and Trustee Zaban
supported approval of the Planning Commission’s recommendation for approval of
the final plat for Larkin Countryside Acres contingent on the execution of the
subdivision improvement agreement. Motion passed unanimously.
Spag's Bar and Grill Modification of Special Land Use Permit. Requesting
outdoor seating. Planning Commission recommending approving this contingent on
landscaping being brought up to standards set in the original Special Land Use
Permit. There will only be low lighting, no high direct lighting other than
what they already have in the parking lot. No current parking will be lost. The
current Special Land Use Permit specifies parking requirements that will still
need to be met. Motion: Treasurer Nilsson moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported
approving the Planning Commission’s recommendation for approval of a Special
Land Use Permit modification for Spag’s Bar and Grill to allow outdoor seating,
conditional upon landscaping being brought up to standards set in the original
Site Plan. There was a question raised on whether or not the prohibition of
outdoor music needed to be added to the motion. It is already stated on the
Site Plan that there will be no outdoor music, so it does not need to be
mentioned in this motion. Motion passed unanimously.
Rezoning Request For Perkins R1-S/Density Option To R1. Talking about the
parcels on either side of the pond. The Density Option stated that the parcels
had to be rezoned to R1 before any development could be done there. Possibility
of 6 to 8 more lots in that area. Land south of it is in R1-S. Mr. Dennis
Sell’s letter objecting to the rezoning was read into the record (see
attached). Carl McIntosh’s letter refuting the Planning Commission’s reasons
for recommending denial of the request was read into the record (see attached).
Motion: Treasurer Nilsson moved and Trustee Zaban supported approving the
Planning Commission’s recommendation for denial of the rezoning request for
Hideaway Woods #3 from R1-S/DO to R1, based on the following: (1) in light of
the original agreement for Hideaway Woods #3, open space would be lost, (2)
there is a potential for water problems caused by disturbing the area
significantly, (3) poor soils would be better suited for lower density
development, (4) the value of the area would not be improved by increasing its
density, (5) rezoning would create a special privilege by profiting only the
landowner while not contributing to the Township as a whole, and (6) public
comments did not favor the rezoning and it would not serve residents of the
Township. Motion passed 3-1 with Supervisor Obst, Treasurer Nilsson and Trustee
Zaban voting in favor and Trustee Wiegandt voting against denying the request.
Rezoning was denied.
PARKS AND REC. - Mickey Martin and Christine Nilsson
The Township heard back from MDOT that we do not have to put in the permanent
access off of Grand River at this time. This will make the entrance work more
affordable. Will start working on the access road. The next Park Committee
meeting will be on Thursday September 14th. Working on the Park Ordinance.
Planning Commission has gotten to the point where they need more input from the
Park Committee. Need to post the No Hunting signs again. Possibly a permanent
sign for the entrance that states no hunting as well. It is part of the DNR
Grant that there can be no hunting on the property.
UNIFINISHED BUSINESS
Woodview Trees - letter from Coralee Thelen of 4102 Vanneter Road. Trees that
were planted on the lot that backs up to her property for screening were moved
and now the required and desired screening no longer exists. The Thelens would
like to see trees of a similar size that were moved to be planted so that the
screening would be restored. This barrier was part of the approved conditions
and is specified on the Site Plan. The subdivision covenants that the developer
gave the property owners stated that trees could not be cut without prior
permission, it did not mention anything about trees being moved. Mrs. Thelen
stated that the intention was stated, and that a reasonable person would think
that if a tree couldn’t be cut without permission then it shouldn’t be moved
without permission either. She believes it is a sham to the surrounding
property owners if the agreements entered into in good faith to allow the
subdivision cannot be enforced. The Township’s Subdivision Ordinance has
clearer language and requirements now that should prevent this type of
situation in the future. Unfortunately, they were not in effect when this
subdivision was created. Mr. Thelen did tell the lot owner that the trees were
required to stay where they were before she moved them. Supervisor Obst
suggested the Board work with the developer, the Thelens and the lot owner to
work out a mutually satisfactory solution.
Aker Request For TAP.
It is appropriate to reserve capacity to properties in the Act 425 agreement
and to have a signed site plan before granting capacity. Purpose of the 425 is
to square off boundaries. Uncertainty about capacity on the east side of the
township. Supervisor Obst’s recommendation would be to hold back on capacity at
this point. Need criteria set up for people to meet in order to grant Taps. If
not doing on first come first serve basis then need a set of reasons on why we
want to reserve it. Recommend working with Planning Consultant Chris Doozen and
Township Attorney Vince Spagnuolo to come up with criteria for granting the
Taps.
NEW BUSINESS
Burning Ordinance - Marc Fabbo
Mr. Fabbo has used the burning permit vehicle to have barbecues/clam bakes in a
fire pit. As the subdivision (Hideaway Woods) is growing, when it reaches 45
homes he will be severely restricted for burning. Suggest a way to keep the
spirit of what they are trying to do, not trying to burn lumber and brush, but
have in ground fire pits. Would like to spearhead a committee to investigate
this and address other issues with the burning ordinance. Board has generally
agreed to appoint Marc to head up such a committee. An announcement will be
made in the next newsletter asking for additional committee members.

Resolution Honoring
SHIRLEY A. GRAHAM, CLERK
Williamstown Township
   WHEREAS, the Township Board and building inspector of the Township of
Williamstown desire to record their heavy sense of loss at the death of their
Clerk, Shirley A. Graham, on August 17, 2000, as well as to record its
affection for Shirley, be it
   RESOLVED, that the Township Board of the Township of Williamstown extends a
heartfelt expression of its sorrow at the loss of Shirley, and does hereby

Township, and who, by being so conscientious, was responsible for the efficient
operation of the Township Office and for the great range of services provided
to our residents; and be it further
   RESOLVED, that an original copy of this resolution is to be tendered to
Shirley’s family as an expression of the Williamstown Township Board’s earnest
sorrow and deepest sympathy.

MTA Resolution To Vote No On 00-2.
Moved by Trustee Zaban and supported by Trustee Wiegandt to adopt the following
resolution regarding Proposal 00-2. Approved unanimously.
RESOLUTION OF
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP, INGHAM COUNTY
In OPPOSITION to PROPOSAL 00-2 to Amend the Michigan Constitution
·Our country’s democratic principles are built on the principle that laws
reflect the will of the majority of citizens, and
·Proposal 00-2 will thwart the ability of a majority of our elected
representatives and senators to adopt new laws necessary for local government
to better serve its citizens, and
·Growing townships are entitled to more state shared revenues to meet the
service needs of expanding populations, and
·Townships are entitled to the same protection of boundaries as is afforded to
cities, and
·Proposal 00-2 does not merely require a two-thirds vote on legislation that
would usurp local control, but also will require a two-thirds vote in both the
House and the Senate for laws that enhance the statutory authority of
townships, and
·Local control can best be preserved through township residents and their
elected township officials communicating their expectations to the Michigan
Legislature that local government is the most appropriate institution for
resolving matters of local concern, now
Therefore be it resolved, that the Board of Williamstown Township opposes
Proposal 00-2 and urges its defeat at the November General Election.
Motion declared adopted.

Watershed Issues – Nancy Fink
The Greater Lansing Area Regional NPDES Phase II Storm Water Regulations
Committee requires that all members be appointed by their respective
municipalities adopting the following resolution. Nancy Fink has agreed to
represent the Township on this committee as one of her responsibilities for
being on the Watershed Management Committee between the Township and the City
of Williamston as created by the third Act 425 agreement this April. Other
members of this committee are Ed Noonan, Ken Zichi, Helen LaBlanc. The
committee is still looking for three volunteers from the City. The Township
will be obliged to having something in place for Pebblebrook to discharge storm
water. Pebblebrook is part of the urban area of Lansing. The City of
Williamston is not included. Permit will be given by the DEQ if go with the
voluntary route or another option is to wait for a later date and go with the
obligatory permits in 2003. If the Township backs out of the regional committee
it will still have to develop its own permit process for Pebblebrook. Mrs. Fink
believes it makes more sense to stay with the committee at this point.
Supervisor Obst moved and Trustee Wiegandt supported that the Township adopt
the following resolution correcting the spelling of Williamstown Township and
replacing unfounded with unfunded. Motion passed unanimously.
Greater Lansing Area Regional NPDES Phase II Storm Water
Regulations Committee
WHEREAS, the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is requiring
nine communities in the greater Lansing area to obtain a National Pollutant
Discharge Elimination System Phase II (NPDES II) Permit by March 2003, and
WHEREAS, the NPDES II permit process is an unfunded federal mandate, and
WHEREAS, the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) has developed
criteria to help obtain funding in the form of grants in part from the Clean
Michigan Initiative if communities adopt a voluntary approach to storm water
and watershed management, and
WHEREAS, representatives of the nine communities named by the EPA those being
City of Lansing, City of East Lansing, Meridian Township, Lansing Township,
Delta Township, Delhi Township, Bath Township, DeWitt Township, and
Williamstown Township have met to develop a cooperative regional approach to
implementing a storm water and watershed management plan, and
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that a committee composed of representatives from
the nine named communities is hereby established and referred to as the Greater
Lansing Area Regional NPDES Phase II Storm Water Regulations Committee.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the committee meet on a regular basis to
facilitate the requirements of the NPDES II Permit by developing a regional
storm water and watershed management plan while seeking the input and
assistance from other agencies including but not limited to educational
institutions & universities, county commissions, drain commissioner’s offices,
county health departments, county road commissions, Tri-County Regional
Planning Commission, Michigan Municipal League and the Michigan Township
Association.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the committee shall also meet to develop funding
strategies to implement this regional storm water and watershed management
plan.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Nancy Fink or her designee is authorized to be the
official representative from Williamstown Township to this committee.
BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED, that the participating community’s governing bodies
must approve the storm water and watershed management plan and any funding
strategies before implementation.
Resolution adopted.

on the property.

Building Permit Fees
Inspector Aven proposed an increase in building permit fees as follows:
   One and Two Family Dwellings
      Living Areas:   $50.00 (from $45.00)
      Garage:   $18.00 (from $12.00)
      Basement:   $12.00 (from $10.00)
The Township is a little under the national average of $51.00 for Michigan.
Meridian Township charges $44.00 and Delta Township, $51.00. City of Lansing
uses the same fees as the Township. The Township does not charge for plan
review, as some others do.
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Zaban supported adoption of the new fees.
Motion passed unanimously.
Township Notaries
Clerk Ellis reported that she is in the process of having all office personnel
certified as notaries public. Township paid for all application fees. Each
notary requires equipment and a state-mandated bond. The Township can purchase
a package which includes the notary bond and a $7,000 errors and omissions
policy for $30 each. Notary stamps are $8.95 each. Clerk Ellis suggested the
Township provide the policy and stamp for each employee.
Clerk Ellis moved and Supervisor Martin supported providing notary packages for
each employee.
Motion passed unanimously.
Ellis asked whether the Board wishes to continue the current policy of free
notarization for both Township residents and non-residents. Sense of the Board
was to continue as-is.
Office Rearrangement
Clerk Ellis reported that she received two estimates for rearrangement of
office furniture. The move will require additional telephone equipment to be
installed adding two new telephones and voice mail. The cost of moving the
furniture is $337.50 (provided by Two Men & a Truck); the cost of telephone
equipment is $1,539.85. Supervisor Martin explained to the public the need for
rearrangement of furniture. Questions were brought up about voice mail. Martin
explained why voice mail would be helpful, how it works and assured that phones
will be answered by an employee during regular office hours.
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported the expenditures for the office
rearrangement and new telephone equipment.
Motion passed unanimously.
Recycling and Solid Waste Disposal
Terry Guerin from Granger Group addressed the Board on Granger’s position on
the County’s proposed solid waste management plan.
Clerk Ellis moved to adjourn with support by Trustee Zaban.
Motion passed unanimously.
Meeting adjourned at 8:53 p.m.

MARCH 6, 2001
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:32 p.m. Clerk Ellis stated a quorum was present and recorded the
following: Supervisor Mickey Martin, Treasurer Nancy Fink, Trustee Martin
Wright and Trustee Steven Zaban. Also present were Building Inspector Walter
Aven and Recording Secretary Deborah Smith.
CONSENT AGENDA
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported the consent agenda, which
included the minutes of the February 6, 2001 Board Meeting, acknowledging the
Treasurer’s report of financial activity for the month of February, 2001;
approving the list of accounts to be paid for March: check numbers 10809 to
10870 for a total of $32,866.08; approving renewal of audit contract with
Abraham & Gaffney, PC.; and accepting and placing on file the Building
Inspector’s report of February, 2000.
Motion passed unanimously.
UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Recycling Funds - Ingham County Solid Waste Management Plan
Jim Wilson from the Ingham County Health Department stated that the Ingham
County Solid Waste Management Plan will be signed by the State of Michigan by
the end of the month. He reiterated the fact that having competition between
landfills will lower the rate charged for disposal, even if the landfill is
further away. Supervisor Martin asked if the Township would receive funds if it
had a recycling drop-off center. Mr. Wilson said the center would have to run
for 10 days out of the month. Supervisor Martin stated that the Township is not
ready to make a decision on this contract at this time. Martin questioned
whether the pending lawsuit will affect the funding mechanism of the plan.
Wilson said the County Commission put the funding plan on hold so as not to
have some facilities pay and not others, so until the lawsuit is ended, there
will be no money collected. Therefore, the plan will be in effect, but the
funding will not. The plan is paid for with the general fund and will continue
until the lawsuit is finalized. Clerk Ellis questioned where things stand with
the lawsuit. Wilson stated that it had just started and he was not at liberty
to discuss it but could be a year or more before the funding mechanism is in
place. Treasurer Fink asked what the overall improvement would be with the new
plan. Wilson stated that not much would change. The plan that was in effect was
a five-year plan and should have been revised in 1995. Curbside recycling is
not cost effective. If we didn’t have recycling, solid waste disposal would be
cheaper.
NEW BUSINESS
Brookstone Subdivision: Tentative Preliminary Plat
Planning Commission Chair Daniel Kraft referred to the site plan in the
February 20, 2001 Planning Commission Minutes. Supervisor Martin stated that
the biggest problem is with FEMA and the floodplain. The applicant is going to
try to prove the parcel is not in the floodplain. According to FEMA floodplain
maps, it is in the floodplain. Supervisor Martin stated the Township is not
permitted to approve a plat that is in the floodplain. Martin asked if there
was any documentation or letter to FEMA asking for clarification. Kraft stated
that all he had was a letter from the Department of Environmental Quality
stating that the applicant would have to get a letter from FEMA amending the
floodplain map. Kraft stated that the Board has 90 days to make a decision on
the tentative preliminary plat. Carl McIntosh, 1145 Wild Cherry, has filled out
an application for FEMA and has requested a letter from the Department of
Environmental Quality to make a change on the map. Martin asked for a copy of
the application, stating the Planning Commission told McIntosh the Board would
want to see that some action was being taken. He did not have the application
with him. Martin reiterated that if FEMA does not amend its map, the plat will
not be approved.
Trustee Wright moved to approve the tentative preliminary plat with all
conditions a shown in the draft minutes of the February 20, 2001 Planning
Commission Meeting. Clerk Ellis seconded. Motion passed unanimously.

of McKenna memo dated March 5, 2001.

JUNE 5, 2001
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:35 p.m. Recording Secretary Smith recorded the following:
Supervisor Mickey Martin, Treasurer Nancy Fink, Trustee Martin Wright and
Trustee Steven Zaban, and stated a quorum was present. Also present were
Building Inspector Walter Aven and Recording Secretary Deborah Smith. Absent:
Clerk Sharon Ellis.
Supervisor Martin made additions to the agenda under New Business: 4701 Zimmer
Road, Township Park, June 11 meeting; and under Unfinished Business, the
Telecommunications Ordinance.
CONSENT AGENDA
Treasurer Fink moved and Trustee Wright supported the consent agenda; motion
passed unanimously.
PUBLIC COMMENT
Frans Wilbrink, 4701 Zimmer Road, questioned the ability of the new Township
Clerk, Sharon Ellis. He stated she has yet to publish a newsletter and he has
not received his voter registration card. He stated that he received a letter
in January 2001 saying he would be getting it soon. He also stated that he has
tried to contact Clerk Ellis but can never reach her. He questioned the
responsibilities of the clerk and her work hours. Supervisor Martin stated that
she agreed with the need for a newsletter and that the Deputy Clerk has been
working very hard to get the voter registration into the state voter computer
system. Martin stated the Board would discuss concerns in a workshop.
Wilbrink also questioned the use of the Township Park, stating that it was
gated off and not accessible to the public. Martin advised that the Township is
working with a contractor on the park road which was expected to be completed
by June 9; however, weather conditions delayed work.
NEW BUSINESS
Crossroads United Methodist Church Site Plan
Planning Commission Chair Daniel Kraft stated that the architecture of the
church was matched by every suggestion made by the Planning Commission. He
stated that those changes convinced the Commission to approve the site plan
with the conditions of receiving approval from the Health Department and Drain
Commission and submitting lighting details for entrance overhangs. Supervisor
Martin stated that the applicant has not yet met the conditions and no building
permit will be issued until it does. Russ Stickle, 5271 N. Williamston Road,
representing the applicant, stated that he would see that the conditions are
met. Martin also inquired about the gate at the Haslett Road entrance. Stickle
stated the church intends to keep the entrance gated at all times except during
heavy use by the church, which would eliminate cut-through traffic.
Trustee Wright moved and Trustee Zaban supported approving the Site Plan with
the conditions of receiving approval from the Health Department and Drain
Commission and submitting lighting details for entrance overhangs. Motion
passed.
Township Park
Supervisor Martin advised of an incident report from the Ingham County
Sheriff’s Office of May 30, 2001 of finding one vehicle stuck and numerous
other vehicles in the park area. The individuals were advised to leave the park
and their names were submitted to Supervisor Martin. Martin investigated and
found substantial damage done to the park. Martin suggested recommending to the
Parks Committee a gate for the entrance, and advised that she would pursue
working with the Sheriff’s Department on opening and closing the park.
Treasurer Fink stated that the destruction to the park is an ongoing problem.
The last quote of damage to the park was approximately $2100.00. Trustee Zaban
suggested that a letter be sent to the parents of the individuals involved.
Frans Wilbrink stated from the audience that the individuals should repair the
damage. Trustee Wright suggested the Board review the options provided in the
ordinance. Bob Pease, 3795 Zimmer Road, stated that he believed the individuals
should be responsible for the damage to the park, not the taxpayer, and the
Board should see that the laws are enforced. Commissioner Kraft referred the
Board to Section 4.06 of the Parks Ordinance, suggesting that the individuals
might want to put in a work day at the park in lieu of the $500.00 fine
provided by the ordinance. The Board advised Supervisor Martin to refer the
matter to the Township Attorney.
4701 Zimmer Road, Building Permit #3433
Trustee Wright read a letter to Frans Wilbrink, 4701 Zimmer Road, from Building
Inspector Walter Aven regarding Building Permit #3433, stating that Wilbrink
was never issued a Certificate of Occupancy for his home because the structure
did not meet Building Code requirements. Wilbrink said he was waiting for the
installation of a stair handrail. Trustee Wright advised an occupancy permit is
required to live in a home and Wilbrink has lived in the home for eight months
without one. Aven stated that he advised Wilbrink verbally and in writing of
the permit requirement and this is the first time he has had to write a letter
in this kind of matter. Wilbrink stated that he would call for a final
inspection in 30 days. Supervisor Martin stated that she expected it done and
asked Aven to submit a report at the July Board meeting.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION APPROVING
TELECOMMUNICATIONS PERMIT AGREEMENT
   At a regular meeting of the Township Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham
County, Michigan, held at the Township Hall in said Township on June 5, 2001 at
7:30 p.m., Eastern Daylight Time.
   PRESENT: Supervisor Mickey Martin, Treasurer Nancy Fink, Trustee Martin
Wright and Trustee Steven Zaban
   ABSENT: Clerk Sharon Ellis
                                                                                    
   The following resolution was offered by Trustee Zaban and supported by
Trustee Wright.  .
   WHEREAS, McLeodUSA, Inc. (“McLeodUSA”) applied for a Telecommunications
Permit to construct a part of its fiber optic network within the Williamstown
Township’s (“Township”) rights-of-way;
   WHEREAS, pursuant to the Michigan Telecommunications Act (“MTA”), McLeodUSA
is required to obtain a permit prior to construction of the telecommunications
system within the Township’s rights-of-way; and
   WHEREAS, the MTA provides that a local unit of government has the right to
review and approve a provider’s access to and ongoing use of the public rights-
of-way, easement or other public place and ensure and protect the health safety
and welfare of the public; and
   WHEREAS, the Township Board conducted a duly noticed public hearing on June
5, 2001; and
   WHEREAS, the Township Board determined that granting the telecommunications
permit to McLeodUSA is in best interests of the residents of the Township; and
   NOW, THEREFORE, the Township Board of Williamstown Township hereby resolves
as follows:
   1.   The Township Board resolves to approve the Telecommunications Permit
Agreement attached as an Exhibit to this Resolution and direct the Clerk to
send the Telecommunications Permit Agreement to McLeodUSA for approval, subject
to final verification of the number of lineal feet that McLeodUSA uses in the
Township’s rights-of-way by the Township attorney and the Township Supervisor.
   2.   The Township Board resolves to rescind all prior resolutions or motions
inconsistent with this current.
   YEAS: Martin, Fink, Wright, Zaban
                                                                        
   NAYS: none
   THE RESOLUTION WAS DECLARED ADOPTED.

RESOLUTION TO ADOPT TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE
   At a regular meeting of the Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham County,
Michigan, held at the Township Hall in said Township on the 5th day of June,
2001 at 7:30 p.m.
PRESENT: Supervisor Mickey Martin, Treasurer Nancy Fink, Trustee Martin Wright
and Trustee Steven Zaban;
ABSENT: Clerk Sharon Ellis.
   The following Resolution was offered by Trustee Zaban and seconded by
Trustee Wright.
   WHEREAS, the statutes governing townships authorizes a township board to
adopt ordinances regulating the public health, safety and general welfare of
persons and property; and
   WHEREAS, the Telecommunications Ordinance is necessary to regulate access to
an ongoing use of the public rights-of-way by telecommunications providers to
ensure and protect the public health, safety and welfare; and
   WHEREAS, the Township enacted a Telecommunications Ordinance in June 1999;
and
   WHEREAS, Williamstown Township (“Township”) desires to provide greater
protection for the Township residents by repealing the existing
Telecommunications Ordinance and replacing it with a revised Telecommunications
Ordinance; and
   BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP, INGHAM COUNTY,
MICHIGAN, AS FOLLOWS:
      1.   Williamstown Township resolves to enact the Telecommunication
Ordinance attached as an Exhibit to this resolution as amended by the written
modification made at the June 5, 2001 meeting.
      2.   Williamstown Township directs the Township Clerk to publish the
Ordinance pursuant to the requirements provided by law.
      3.   Upon the effective date of this Ordinance, the former
Telecommunications Ordinance, adopted in June 1999, is hereby repealed.
ADOPTED:
   YEAS: Martin, Fink, Wright, Zaban
   NAYS: none
STATE OF MICHIGAN       )
               )
COUNTY OF INGHAM      )   
      I, the undersigned, the duly qualified and acting Township Clerk of
Williamstown Township, Ingham County, Michigan, DO HEREBY CERTIFY that the
foregoing is a true and complete copy of certain proceedings taken by the
Township Board of said Township at a regular meeting held on the 5th day of
June 2001.

JULY 3, 2001
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:32 p.m. Clerk Ellis stated a quorum was present and recorded the
following as present: Supervisor Mickey Martin, Clerk Sharon Ellis and Trustee
Martin Wright. Also present were Building Inspector Walter Aven and Recording
Secretary Lisa Badiee. Absent were Treasurer Nancy Fink and Trustee Steve
Zaban.
CONSENT AGENDA
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported approving the amended minutes of
the June 5, 2001 Board meeting; approving the minutes of the May 16, (as
amended) and June 19, 2001 Special Meetings; approving the list of accounts to
be paid with the exception of All Terrain Alterations and New Construction Air
Conditioning; acknowledging the Treasurer’s reports of financial activity for
the month of May and the draft report for June; and accepting and placing on

approved; Clerk Ellis supported. Motion passed unanimously.
NEW BUSINESS
AT&T – SPECIAL USE PERMIT AND SITE PLAN
Trustee Wright reported no public opposition at a public hearing held on June
19, 2001 for the proposed cellular tower at 160 E. Grand River Rd. The Planning
Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the special land use
permit conditioned upon final site plan approval. Matthew Jurson of AT&T
Wireless Service, Inc. was in attendance and brought with him a required surety
bond. Township Attorney Spagnuolo has not yet seen the bond, but will look at
it on July 5. In a letter dated May 21, 2001 from McKenna Associates, Inc.,

be inspected to determine if further landscaping is necessary.

Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported approving the Special Use Permit
with final approval of Site Plan.
Motion passed unanimously.
6090 ZIMMER ROAD REZONING FROM AG-C TO AG-SF
A public hearing was held on June 19, 2001 the application for rezoning
submitted by Tom Graham requesting rezoning of a 10-acre parcel from Ag-C to
Ag-SF. The 10-acre parcel is part of a 78-acre parcel, which will remain Ag-C.
The Planning Commission recommends approval of the rezoning request. Supervisor
Martin stated that this request does not follow the Master Plan and further
requests should be looked at more closely. Supervisor Martin also suggested the
Planning Commission review the Master Plan.

passed unanimously.

SUMMIT CEMETERY INCIDENT
On June 22, 2001 damage was done at the back of Summit Cemetery by teenagers
driving 4-wheelers. Harold Powell, 5235 Hart Road, was advised by the Sheriff
of the drivers’ names. He spoke with their parents and gave them two options:
Fix the damages or face court fees, fines, damages and probation. The families
agreed to fix the damages and were given one week to do the repairs. Mr. Powell
will report to the Cemetery Board when repairs are made and ask Board secretary
Wayne Fate to put a report in writing including the names of the persons
involved.
UNFINISHED BUSINESS
ORDINANCE REVISIONS – ACCESSORY BUILDINGS
Two revisions are recommended to the Township Zoning Ordinance. The first is to
revise item 2.03(C)(b) to allow a reduced setback for only those accessory
buildings covering less than 2,400 square feet in area. Second, add a new item
5 to section 2.03(C) to require screening of detached accessory buildings
covering 2,400 to 4,000 square feet of area, when within 200 feet of a
principal residence on an adjacent property.
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported approving the Ordinance
revisions. Motion passed unanimously.

BOARD POLICIES
New Board policies proposed: 1) All bills shall be approved by the Township
Board prior to payment except the following: a) Payroll (Secretary); b) Payroll
taxes to federal and state; c) utility bills; d) Invoices with penalties or
discounts incurred if payment were not received prior to Board approval; f)
Expenditures deemed necessary by the Supervisor or, in t h Supervisor’s
absence, a Board member. These bills shall be post-audited at the next Board
meeting and reported along with those bills needing approval.
2) Township Board members will be notified a minimum of 18 hours prior to any
special meetings. 3) Township Board must approve all expenditures $200 and over
that are not itemized in the fiscal year adopted budget.
Trustee Zaban moved and Trustee Wright supported approving new Board policies.
Motion passed unanimously.

capacity shall abide by the following:

purchase.
2.   Requests must be accompanied by:
      A full description of the item
      Drawings if available
      Bid proposals
      Reason for purchase
2. Complaints: All complaints must be stated in writing then submitted to the
Supervisor or his/her designee. The Township Board will be updated on
complaints at its regularly scheduled meetings.

OCTOBER 2, 2001
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:34 p.m. Present were Supervisor Mickey Martin, Clerk Sharon
Ellis, Trustee Steve Zaban and Treasurer Nancy Fink, Building Inspector Walter
Aven and Recording Secretary Lisa Badiee; Trustee Martin Wright arrived at 7:50
p.m.
CONSENT AGENDA
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Zaban supported approving the list of bills to be
paid, payroll report and bills paid; acknowledging the Treasurer’s report of
financial activity for September; accepting and placing on file the Building
Inspector’s report. Motion passed unanimously. Minutes of the September Board
meeting will not be approved until corrections and amendments are made. Road
repairs, Mitchell/Vanneter Roads speed limit signs, and NPDES Phase II
Resolution permit were all added under Unfinished Business.
PUBLIC COMMENT
Dr. Terrance Braden, 951 Haslett Rd., brought a complaint against the Ingham
County Road Commission to the Board’s attention. During the reconstruction of
Haslett Road, his yard and driveway were altered and have as yet not been fixed
to his satisfaction. Clerk Ellis made copies of correspondence from the ICRC to
Dr. Braden for Board review. Supervisor Martin offered to contact Mr. John W.
Midgley, Managing Director of ICRC, on Dr. Braden’s behalf.
Daniel Kraft, 4049 Beeman Rd., asked when voter identification cards would be
mailed out. Deputy Clerk Badiee informed him that cards would be sent out when
redistricting is completed in March 2002.
Frans Wilbrink, 4701 Zimmer Rd., questioned whether the Township would become a
Charter. Supervisor Martin stated that the public would have to petition to
Charter and that the Board has no plans to pursue it in the future. She feels
there is no advantage to becoming a Charter township.
NEW BUSINESS
Modification of Special Land Use Permit -Williamston Free Methodist Church
Daniel Kraft, Planning Commission Chair, stated that the Planning Commission
recommended approved the new site plan, having received no public comment at
the public hearing. The driveway will remain gravel for ONE YEAR AT THE OUTSET,
BUT CONTINUANCE WILL REQUIRE BOARD REVIEW. at least two years, at which time
other options will be considered. Supervisor Martin recommended approval of the
new site plan. Clerk Ellis moved to accept the Planning Commission’s
recommended approval of the site plan and special use permit; Clerk TRUSTEE
Zaban supported. Motion passed unanimously.
Treasurer Fink asked Kraft about the Commission’s workshop meeting regarding
bike paths and green space along the river. He said they decided to separate
the concept of greenways and bike paths and look at each issue separately. They
want to get easements for green space along the river before any further
developments take place. Supervisor Martin asked Kraft’s opinion on the GIS
computer program presented recently by Marvin Fouty, President of MicroScan

Haslett Road Dirt Pile
Dirt piles have mostly been cleaned up. John Powell, 780 Haslett Rd., permitted
C&D Hughes to use his property to stockpile dirt and also received a permit to

885 Haslett Rd., wrote the Township complaining about the dirt piles.
Supervisor Martin wrote C&D HUGHES WITH A COPY TO Powell, informing him of the

Powell took great offense to that statement. Supervisor Martin apologized,
stating that what she meant to say was “stockpiling on property within the
Township…”. In response to Powell’s request, Supervisor Martin will send

Township a letter when work is completed, at which time Supervisor Martin will

Road Repairs – Mitchell & Vanneter Roads
In a letter to the Township dated September 21, Robert Peterson, Director of
Engineering for the Ingham County Road Commission, indicated $254,800 would
have to come from the Township for road improvements as opposed the $170,000
stated in his letter dated June 25. Clerk Ellis called to question the
discrepancy and Peterson advised his letter of the 25th should have said ‘a
minimum’ of $170,000. Ellis will draft a letter to him requesting clarification
of the difference in dollar amounts and asking specifically what improvements
will be made, the definition of a “primary road,” when site plans will be ready
and specific boundaries of the roads in discussion.

School Board will send a letter to the Ingham County Road Commission requesting
signs be placed both Mitchell and Vanneter Roads. The signs will slow traffic
to 25 mph before and after school. The Township will divide the APPROXIMATE
$6,000 cost with the school district.

ELIMINATION SYSTEM PHASE II PERMIT
At a regular meeting of the Township Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham
County, Michigan, held at the Township Hall in said Township on October 2, 2001
at 7:34 p.m., Eastern Daylight Time.
PRESENT: Supervisor Mickey Martin, Treasurer Nancy Fink, Clerk Sharon Ellis,
Trustee Martin Wright and Trustee Steven Zaban.
The following resolution was offered by Clerk Ellis and supported by Treasurer
Fink:
WHEREAS, The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is requiring
nine communities in the greater Lansing area to obtain a National Pollutant
Discharge Elimination System Phase II (NPDES II) Permit by March 2003, and
WHEREAS, nine communities consisting of the City of Lansing, City of East
Lansing, Meridian Charter Township, Lansing Charter Township, Delta Charter
Township, Delhi Charter Township, Bath Charter Township, Williamstown Township
and DeWitt Charter Township have previously established the Greater Lansing
Area Regional NPDES Phase II Storm Water Regulations Committee, and
WHEREAS, the Committee has had prepared, reviewed and adopted a Step I – Permit
Strategy Development Report outlining its recommended program, and
WHEREAS, the governmental resolutions establishing the Committee require that
each community’s governing body approve any storm water and watershed
management plan and funding strategies before implementation.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, Williamstown Township hereby approves the
recommended program as presented in the report titled “Greater Lansing Regional
Committee on Phase II Nonpoint Source Pollution Prevention – Step I – Permit
Strategy Development”.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Williamstown Township authorizes the Greater
Lansing Area Regional NPDES Phase II Storm Water Regulations Committee to
proceed to implement the proposed program.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Williamstown Township authorizes an expenditure
not to exceed $3,549. for the preparation of the voluntary permit application
including Outfall Mapping, Illicit Discharge Elimination Plan, and Public
Education Plan.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Williamstown Township requests the Drain
Commissioner to prepare and submit draft Red Cedar River, Grand River, and
Remey-Chandler Watershed Management petitions under Section 8 of the Drain Code
for its consideration.
BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED, that the participating community’s governing bodies
must approve the final Voluntary Permit before submission to the State of
Michigan.
Clerk Ellis moved and Treasurer Fink supported passing the resolution. A roll
call vote was taken:
      Trustee Wright   Yes
      Trustee Zaban      Yes
      Treasurer Fink   Yes
      Supervisor Martin   Yes
      Clerk Ellis      Yes
   THE RESOLUTION WAS DECLARED ADOPTED.
