DECEMBER 4, 2001
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:30 p.m. Present were Supervisor Mickey Martin, Clerk Sharon
Ellis, Trustee Steve Zaban, Trustee Martin Wright, Treasurer Nancy Fink,
Building Inspector Walter Aven and Recording Secretary Lisa Badiee. Clerk Ellis
announced a quorum present.
AGENDA
Supervisor Martin added a Request to Burn, Library Board Appointment and
Employee Policy to New Business.
CONSENT AGENDA
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported approving the November 6 minutes
with changes; approving the list of bills to be paid, with the exception of
Diamond International and Tom’s Transplants pending further review, payroll
report and bills paid; acknowledging the Treasurer’s report of financial
activity for November and accepting and placing on file the Building
Inspector’s report. Motion passed unanimously.
PUBLIC COMMENT
Gary Nix, 2344 Park Wood, spoke regarding the burning ordinance as applied to
subdivisions. He and other residents would like to be allowed small bonfires on
weekends in fire pits/containers. Supervisor Martin responded that the burning
ordinance has been  will be referred to the Planning Commission for review and
that several subdivision residents have agreed to be on a committee to assist.
Mark Way, 2356 Park Wood, asked if the decision would rest with NIESA or the
Township Board. Supervisor Martin responded that the final decision rests with
the Board. The Planning Commission will draft a revised ordinance, hold public
hearings and make recommendations.
Frans Wilbrink, 4701 Zimmer Rd., asked why trees had been planted at the bottom
of the sledding hill at the Township Community Park and whether the Township
has liability insurance. Treasurer Fink explained that the Parks Commission is
trying to designate areas for sledding paths and trails to avoid sliding
towards the parking lots. Supervisor Martin advised that the Township has
liability insurance.
Wilbrink questioned whether Pres Kool Body Shop on Grand River had permission
to drain onto the Siegel property, and if their building permits were in order.
Building Inspector Walter Aven responded that the Ingham County Drain
Commissioner has approved the drainage issue and all appropriate permits are on
file.
NEW BUSINESS
5795 Shoeman Road Site Plan Approval
Daniel Kraft, Planning Commission Chair, reported that the Commission
recommended approval of a proposal to construct a pole barn and pond at 5795
Shoeman Rd. Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported approval of site
plan review for the pole barn and pond. Motion passed unanimously.
Request for Extension of Tentative Preliminary Plat – Hideaway Woods No. 5
In December 2000 the Board granted preliminary plat approval for a 10-lot
subdivision subject to certain conditions. A written request on behalf of the
proprietor for a one-year extension was received citing delays in connecting to
the City’s sewer system. The Planning Commission recommended Board approval.
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported a 12-month extension for site
plan approval with six conditions listed in the McKenna Associates letter dated
November 14, 2001. Motion passed unanimously.
Design Standards Clarification
The Planning Commission has been considering whether to adopt Township
ordinance design standards for future commercial development. After discussion
with McKenna it was decided that the first step in the process would be a
visual preference survey. The Board and Planning Commission would be presented
with various options for developing design standards. Some townships and
municipalities have voluntary design standards and use a formula to score
development, which then has bearing on recommendations for site plan approval.
Before going further with McKenna, the Planning Commission wants to know
whether the Board thinks that voluntary standards would work in the township or
prefers an ordinance. Design standards would be different in various zones of
the Township. Supervisor Martin stated that MSU students, while doing the Grand
River Corridor Study, had photographed all commercial buildings in the Township
as well as giving recommendations as to what designs they thought were most
compatible with the Township. The photos are on art ARC view discs and
available for Planning Commission review. The Commission is concerned about
enforcing voluntary standards. Clerk Ellis stated that if the Planning
Commission and Board feel design standards are important, they should be part
of an ordinance so there is a level playing field within the Township.
Treasurer Fink agreed. Supervisor Martin asked Kraft to pursue the issue at a
later specified date, stating that the standards should accommodate new
construction and improvements to existing buildings. Trustee Wright asked that
there be enough options to work with everyone. The Planning Commission already
has some leeway during site plan approval when an old building is being
refurbished as to how much they want the building to come into conformity.
Supervisor Martin will ask McKenna Associates for an estimate for design
standard work so that it can be put into the budget and will advise the
Planning Commission when to proceed with ordinance work.
Kraft requested Board direction regarding Planning Commission members directly
contacting McKenna with work to be done. Supervisor Martin stated that Kraft,
as Chair of the Planning Commission, should be the only one contacting McKenna.
Rosemary Phillip is the staff person to assist Kraft in getting research
information for the Planning Commission. Kraft stated that Phillip did some
excellent research for the Wetlands Ordinance. Kraft asked the Board for
direction regarding Township park signs. Supervisor Martin asked to put the
sign issue on hold. The Township burn ordinance is the Planning Commission’s
top priority as soon as the Wetlands Ordinance is finished. Supervisor Martin
will write a letter to Kraft addressing these issues.
Williamston Community Schools Tax Request
A letter dated November 20 was received from Williamston Community Schools
requesting the Township to collect summer school property taxes. Treasurer Fink
will contact the Treasury Department to ask if it is mandatory; if not, she
will send the school district a letter denying the request.
Complaints
1960 Mapleshade - Boxcar
Inspector Aven visited the VanRiper property at 1960 Mapleshade and was told
the boxcar is temporary storage for transporting snowmobiles. They also have a
dump truck parked too close to the road. Supervisor Martin will write a letter
to the VanRipers asking for a written response specifying a date when the
boxcar will be removed. She will pursue the dump truck issue with the
Constable. A written complaint needs to be filed.
63 Barry Road - Burning Violation/Cleanup
A permit was issued to Luke Landscaping for burning at 63 Barry Road. After the
landscaping company dumped debris to be burned, the fire got out of control and
burned the neighboring property. The fire department was called. The
landscaping company should not have been issued a burn permit, as it is not the
property owner. Supervisor Martin will contact the homeowner to find out if
Luke Landscaping had her permission to dump and burn there. The fire chief
wants the landscaping company to clean up the mess.
Gardiner Motor Home
Supervisor Martin informed the Board that Mr. Gardiner’s motor home has been
moved and is in compliance with the ordinance.
Clerk Ellis left the room at 8:55 and returned at 8:58.
580 Haslett Road – Burn and Demolish Request
A resident has asked permission to demolish and burn a house and several
outbuildings at 580 Haslett Road. A demolition company will supervise the burn
following rules from NIESA and the Township. Clerk Ellis suggested seeing proof
of liability insurance from the demo company and asking the Township to be
named as an insured. The Fire Chief asked the Township to notify neighbors
within a half-mile of the burn site. Board members raised concerns regarding
toxic materials, such as lead and asbestos that may be on site. Supervisor
Martin would like assurance that the buildings are free of asbestos. When the
burn is completed, debris should be removed, not covered. Inspector Aven stated
that a demolition permit is needed.
Library Board Appointment
Ray Challis contacted Supervisor Martin to resign his Library Board
appointment. Martin asked for Board support in appointing Jeff Bartrum for the
position. Treasurer Fink moved to appoint Jeff Bartrum for the Library Board;
Trustee Wright supported. Motion passed unanimously.
Employee Manual
An Employee Manual has been given to Debbie Smith, Rosemary Phillip and Sue
Hiner. Clerk Ellis suggested that the words “without notice” should be added
after “at any time” in Sections 1 and 12 of the Employee Policy. In the Funeral
Leave section, should wording be changed from “spouse” to “domestic partner”;
if so, how is that defined? Supervisor Martin will speak with Township Attorney
Vince Spagnuolo regarding these issues. Rosemary Phillip, in a memo to the
Board, asked for clarification on 3 items. Does item 3, regarding her listing
as an “employee”, change her status for the Aetna 457 program or have any tax
implications. Treasurer Fink will look into that. Item 7, regarding longevity
recognition, will be a Board workshop item. Item 16, regarding jury duty, does
include part time employees and there will be no need to make up lost hours. In
all cases, paid time off must be exhausted before any unpaid time off is taken.
UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Board Policies
For security reasons during regular open office hours the goal is always to
have two people in the office at all times. On Wednesday evenings, when the
secretary/receptionist’s regular work hours are until 7:30pm, the board member
covering the day must stay until 7:30pm or make arrangements for another
employee to remain in the office.
There will be a ledger for all employees, supervisor, treasurer and clerk to
sign in and out during their time spent at the Township office.
Lights at the entranceways will be left on all evening for security.
All staff will be recording all their workday activities.
At Township Board meetings all board members arrival times (if after the
meeting has started) and any exit times will be recorded in the minutes.
Township computers including the Internet service are to be used for township
business only.
Trustee Zaban moved and was supported by Trustee Wright to pass these Board
Policies. Four in favor; one opposed. Motion passed.
Sewer Capacity
The Board requests letters of intent from anyone needing sewer capacity. Once
capacity is available, they will be informed.
REPORTS
Budget
Supervisor Martin asked for input from Board members regarding next year’s
budget. Martin will get the budget for the Planning Commission from Rosemary
Phillip. A budget hearing will be held in February.
MEETING REVIEW
November minutes will be amended.
Treasurer Fink will contact the Park Committee and County as to what needs to
be done if accidents happen on the sledding hill. The Enterprise may be
contacted in the future to publish an article with illustrations and sledding
rules. Fink will contact the Treasury Department regarding Rosemary Phillip’s
218 agreement.
Supervisor Martin will pursue the boxcar issue by getting a written complaint
and involving the Constable. Martin will also follow up on the burn at 63 Barry
Road.
Trustee Zaban will talk with NIESA at their meeting on December 6 regarding the
demo and burn on Haslett Road.
Clerk Ellis will ensure that the Township’s liability insurance covers the
park.
Supervisor Martin will write a thank you letter to Ray Challis and a letter to
Jeff Bartrum regarding his Library Board appointment, as well as a to the
Planning Commission directing them to begin work on the burn ordinance as soon
as the wetlands ordinance is completed. Martin will advise Chris Doozan of
McKenna Associates that direction from the Planning Commission will come from
Dan Kraft only.
Supervisor Martin will meet with the Township attorney to review the Employee
Manual.
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Zaban supported adjournment. Motion passed
unanimously.
Meeting adjourned at 9:45 p.m.

2002 Meeting Minutes
JANUARY 2, 2002
The regular meeting of the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees was called
to order at 7:30 p.m. Present were Supervisor Mickey Martin, Clerk Sharon
Ellis, Trustee Steve Zaban, Trustee Martin Wright, Treasurer Nancy Fink,
Building Inspector Walter Aven and Recording Secretary Lisa Badiee. Clerk Ellis
announced a quorum present.
AGENDA
Supervisor Martin added Board of Review Appointments and Annual Meeting to New
Business and Mitchell/Vanneter Roads to Unfinished Business.
CONSENT AGENDA
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported approving the December 4 minutes
with noted changes; approving the list of bills to be paid, payroll report and
bills paid; acknowledging the Treasurer’s report of financial activity for
December and accepting and placing on file the Building Inspector’s report;
passed.
PUBLIC COMMENT
Frans Wilbrink, 4701 Zimmer Road, again brought to the Board’s attention the
possible danger he sees for people sledding on the south hill at the Township
Park. He was advised that signs are planned to be posted in the next few days.
Also, wires supporting trees will be flagged. Clerk Ellis will contact the
Township insurance agent to discuss possible additional liability coverage.
NEW BUSINESS
Fire Ordinance Committee
In December the Board asked the Planning Commission to review the fire
ordinance and set up a review subcommittee. Melanie Ford of Woodview
subdivision has volunteered and a Pebblebrook representative is being sought.
Rosemary Phillip was appointed one of three Planning Commission members to be
on the committee. Supervisor Martin will contact other Planning Commission
members and speak with the City of Williamston about input. Martin will also
ask residents Don Owens, Gary Nix and Mark Way to serve, if needed. Trustee
Zaban will attend the next NEISA meeting and request an active fire fighter to
be on the committee.
Township Logo
The Planning Commission has requested that the Township have a logo. A request
for suggestions will be published in the February newsletter.
Library Board
Jeff Bartrem, Ed Noonan and JoAnn Hegedus addressed the Board regarding the
Williamston Library. Mr. Noonan presented a letter outlining four basic issues
of concern: need, size, location and funding. The present facility is in
critical condition and a temporary facility is being sought. Several city-owned
sites for a new building have been looked at, but none seems suitable. Mr.
Noonan contends that a one-half mill over 20 years spread over Williamstown
Township, City of Williamston and Wheatfield Township would be sufficient to
fund a new library. Clerk Ellis asked if there was a back-up plan if millage
fails and was told there is none. Mr. Noonan will ask the Capital Area District
Library for help in funding a campaign to raise money. Supervisor Martin asked
Mr. Bartrem to report to the Board on any progress. He will copy the Township
on pertinent e-mail.
Cemetery Commission – Tractor Request
Harold Powell, Cemetery Commission member, presented to the Board a request for
a new tractor with backhoe and front-end loader for use in digging graves.
Presently, the 40 to 50 graves per year are dug by hand by the sexton and his
assistant. The total tractor price is $17,581.98. Mr. Powell asked that the
township pay $11,721.32 and the City pay $5,860.66. He will attend the City
Council meeting on January 14 to request that portion. If the City commits to
its one-third payment, the Board agreed to consider the purchase for inclusion
in the upcoming budget.
Burkley Road School House
Township resident Larry Grabarczyk would like to donate a 100-year-old
schoolhouse to the Township. The Township would be responsible to move it and
clean up the spot where it stands now. Jeff Bartrem offered to inspect the
schoolhouse and report on its condition before the Board makes a decision about
accepting the donation.
Complaints
Written complaints were received regarding the number of cars parked at 4650
Jadestone and abandoned vehicles on a property on Haslett Road just west of
Shaftsburg Road. Supervisor Martin will refer the complaints to Constable
Dahlstrom.
Board of Review
Supervisor Martin thanked Harold Powell for his service on the Board of Review
and proposed appointing Gerald Eidt, Robert Tetzlaff and Franciscus Wilbrink to
the Board of Review. Trustee Zaban moved and Trustee Wright supported
appointment of Eidt, Tetzlaff and Wilbrink to the Board of Review; passed.
Annual Meeting
Board consensus is to continue the practice of not holding an annual meeting.
UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Employee Policy Manual
Changes to the Employee Policy Manual have been made per suggestions at the
December Board meeting. Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported adopting
the Employee Policy Manual; passed.
Mitchell/Vanneter Roads
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported Township commitment to spending
a maximum amount of $254,800 to reconstruct the Mitchell/Vanneter Roads
intersection according to the Ingham County Road Commission worksheet dated 1-
9-01 and Bob Peterson’s outline at the Township Board’s workshop 11-29-01,
conditioned on Michigan Dept. of Transportation’s approval to designate
Mitchell and Vanneter Roads primary, county roads; passed.
REPORTS
NEISA
Trustee Zaban will attend the next meeting on January 3.
Parks
Treasurer Fink questioned a bill from Tom’s Transplants and sent it to
Christine Nillson for her review.
MEETING REVIEW
Community Park signs will be laminated and posted as well as flags being wired.
Clerk Ellis will contact the insurance agent regarding liability coverage for
the sledding hill.
Township logo solicitation request will be published in February’s newsletter.
Payroll report will be kept separate from bills to be paid report in Board
packet.
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Wright supported adjournment; passed.
Meeting adjourned at 9:50 p.m.

Township Park – Parking and Improvements
MDOT Contractor Kamminga & Roodvoets, Inc. has asked the Township for use of
the township park as a staging area for Grand River Road construction projects.
In return, they will use approximately 40,000 cubic yards of fill to build ball
fields and new parking areas at the park. Supervisor Martin and Treasurer have
met with the contractor and with Les Linsemier of Fitzgerald Henne & Associates
to discuss the advantages to the Township. Work would occur over a period of
two years. Linsemier will provide a proposal and estimate to draw a site plan
that could be used with the contractor and for further development of the park.
A written agreement will be required from the contractor. A sign will be posted
on the park kiosk and an article put in the next newsletter to advise residents
of the plans. Supervisor Martin will contact the contractor and lawyer
regarding the agreement.
Fee Schedule
After reviewing fees and costs for the Township’s current MODIFICATIONS OR
EXTENSIONS OF ORIGINAL SUP/SITE PLAN, Supervisor Martin recommended that the
fee be set at $1,500 for commercial permits. Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee
Wright supported the increased fee; passed.
UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Complaints
423 E. Grand River: Constable Dahlstrom will provide Supervisor Martin with a
list of all violations; Martin will then match those with ordinance provisions
and send a letter to the property owner requiring all violations be corrected

Brookstone Subdivision – Extension of Tentative Preliminary Plat Approval
The Planning Commission recommended a 12-month extension with nine conditions.
Carl McIntosh, 1145 Wild Cherry Lane, expressed his discouragement with sewer
capacity not being available after the previous Board allocated 27 sewer taps
under the 425 agreement with the City. Progress on sewer lines is on hold until
the City has the money to fix them.
Treasurer Fink moved and Trustee Wright supported a 12-month extension with the
following nine conditions for Brookstone Subdivision Tentative Preliminary Plat
Approval:    1)Approval shall be obtained to connect to the City of
Williamston’s sanitary sewer system. Because the availability and adequacy of
sanitary sewer service is such an essential element of the plat, if sanitary
sewer service is determined to be unavailable, the plat as proposed would not
be permitted, and submittal of a new plat design would be required. The new
plat design would require tentative preliminary plat, preliminary plat, and
final plat review and approval; 2)A “Letter of Map Amendment” or other
documentation must be obtained from the Federal Emergency Management Agency
(FEMA) that officially amends the floodplain boundary so that all proposed lots
would be located outside the floodplain. If the floodplain boundary is not
amended, the plat as proposed would not be permitted, and submittal of a new
plat design required. The new plat design would require tentative preliminary
plat, final preliminary plat, and final plat approval; 3)Approval of the plat
by appropriate state, county and regional agencies, including approval of storm
water management measures by the Ingham County Drain Commissioner’s office and
receipt of any wetland or other required environmental permits from the MDEQ or
other agency; 4)Removal or relocation of the Kranz garage (adjacent parcel to
the east), or application and approval of a variance request shall be required
to address the front setback requirement along the proposed road (per item 1 of
McKenna Associates’ February 8, 2001 letter); 5)Satisfaction of street and
traffic requirements specified in the Ingham County Road Commission’s letter
dated February 5, 2001; 6)Inclusion of wetlands maintenance (Kranz Wildlife
Preserve) in Declaration of Restrictions (per item 7 of McKenna Associates’
February 8, 2001 letter); 7)Satisfaction of landscaping concerns (per item 8(b)
of McKenna Associates’ February 8, 2001 letter), including provision of the
number, spacing, and species of trees located in Landscape Easement “A”, which
contains the required greenbelt along Rowley Road; 8)Satisfaction of sidewalk
concerns (per item 11 of McKenna Associates’ February 8, 2001 letter),
including identifying who will be responsible for constructing sidewalks,
submittal of a performance guarantee, and establishment of a deadline for
constructing all sidewalks; 9)Revision of Declaration of Restrictions (per item
13 of McKenna Associates’ February 8, 2001 letter), and notation that the
Declaration of Restrictions must comply with all Township regulations and
ordinances; passed.

Spaulding Drain Resolution
Ingham County Drain Commissioner Pat Lindemann addressed the Board regarding
the following Resolution:
STATE OF MICHIGAN COUNTY OF INGHAM
TOWNSHIP OF WILLIAMSTON
RESOLUTION
   WHEREAS, the Spaulding Intercounty Drainage Board has advised the
Williamstown Township Board of Trustees that, pursuant to Section 196 of the
Michigan Drain Code (MCL 280.196; MSA 11.196), an inspection has been made of
the Spaulding Intercounty Drain and it has been determined, as a result of the
inspection, that certain maintenance must be performed upon the Drain; and,
   WHEREAS, the Spaulding Intercounty Drainage Board has the authority to
expend Two Thousand Five Hundred and no/100 ($2,500.00) Dollars per mile in any
one (1) year for the maintenance of the drain, and where it is estimated that
expenditures in excess of Two Thousand Five Hundred and no/100 ($2,500.00)
Dollars per mile are necessary, those amounts may not be expended until
approved by Resolution of the governing body of each township, city and village
affected by more than twenty (20%) percent of the cost; and,
   WHEREAS, the Spaulding Intercounty Drainage Board has estimates that the
cost for the maintenance of the Spaulding Intercounty Drain will be
approximately Twenty Thousand ($20,000.00) Dollars, which constitutes Fifteen
Thousand ($15,000.00) Dollars in excess of the authorized Two Thousand Five
Hundred and no/100 ($2,500.00) Dollars per mile.
   NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED by the Williamstown Township Board of
Trustees, that pursuant to Section 196 of the Drain Code, Spaulding Intercounty
Drainage Board is authorized to expend money for the maintenance and repair of
the Spaulding Intercounty Drain in excess of Two Thousand Five Hundred and no/
100 ($2,500.00) Dollars per mile and, to the extent that the drain fund for the
Drain contains insufficient funds for the payment of costs incurred for the
maintenance or repair of the Drain, then the Spaulding Intercounty Drainage
Board is authorized to levy a special assessment, as allowed by law.
   RESOLUTION approved this 2nd day of April,2002 by the Williamstown Township
Board of Trustees, governing body of the Williamstown Township.
Mr. Lindemann anticipates the dollar amount not to exceed $20,000 after having
accepted a bid of $9,200 for the work. He stated that the drain has not been
cleaned since some time in the 1920’s and, after work is completed, should be
in good working order for 40 to 50 years. Once a contractor is hired, work
should be completed in five to six weeks. The ICRC will oversee the entire
project. His office is applying for a grant from the Corps of Engineers for
$100,000 to $200,000 for wetlands preservation. Mr. Lindemann stated that many
trees will be removed and when work is done the site will be reseeded with
wildflower and grasses.
Clerk Ellis moved and Trustee Zaban supported adopting the resolution; roll
call vote:
Supervisor Martin: yes
Clerk Ellis: yes
Treasurer Fink: yes
Trustee Wright: yes
Trustee Zaban: yes
Resolution adopted.

Resolution Phase II Storm Water Program
SECOND RESOLUTION FOR PHASE II STORM WATER PERMIT PROGRAM
A RESOLUTION TO APPROVE THE EXPENDITURE FOR WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP’S PORTION OF
THE PREPARATION OF THE WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE RED CEDAR RIVER
WATERSHED AS PART OF THE GREATER LANSING AREA REGIONAL NPDES PHASE II STORM
WATER PROGRAM.
   WHEREAS, The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is
requiring nine communities in the greater Lansing area to obtain a National
Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Phase II (NPDES II) permit by March
2003; and
   WHEREAS, nine communities consisting of the City of Lansing, City of East
Lansing, Meridian Charter Township, Lansing Charter Township, Delta Charter
Township, Delhi Charter Township, Bath Charter Township, DeWitt Charter
Township and Williamstown Township have previously established the Greater
Lansing Regional NPDES Phase II Storm Water Regulations Committee; and
   WHEREAS, the Committee has prepared, reviewed, and adopted a Step 1 Permit
Strategy Development Report outlining its recommended program; and
   WHEREAS, the governmental resolutions establishing the Committee require
that each community’s governing body approve any storm water and watershed
management plan and also any funding strategies before implementation; and
   WHEREAS, the Williamstown township Board of Trustees, by Resolution, adopted
on October 2, 2001, previously approved the recommended program as presented in
the report titled “Greater Lansing Regional Committee on Phase II Nonpoint
Source Pollution Prevention, Step 1, Permit Strategy Development”; and
   WHEREAS, the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees, by Resolution, adopted
on October 2, 2001, previously authorized the Greater Lansing Area Regional
NPDES Phase II Storm Water Regulations Committee to proceed to implement the
proposed program; and
   WHEREAS, the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees previously authorized
an expenditure not exceeding $6000 for the preparation of the voluntary permit
application including Outfall Mapping, Illicit Discharge Elimination Plan, and
Public Education Plan.
   NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Williamstown Township Board of
Trustees authorizes expenditure not to exceed $3,440 for their portion of the
preparation of the watershed management plans for the Red Cedar River
Watershed, including outfall mapping.
   BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED, that the participating community’s governing bodies
must approve the final Voluntary Permit before submission to the State of
Michigan.
Trustee Wright moved and Clerk Ellis supported adopting the resolution; roll
call vote:
Supervisor Martin: yes
Clerk Ellis: yes
Treasurer Fink: yes
Trustee Wright: yes
Trustee Zaban: yes
Resolution adopted.

RESOLUTION BY THE WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP BOARD
TO AUTHORIZE THE WILLIAMSTON COMMUNITY LIBRARY FOUNDATION TO REPRESENT
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP IN THE PLANNING AND CONSTRUCTION OF NEW LIBRARY IN THE
CITY OF WILLIAMSTON
   At a regularly scheduled meeting of the Township Board of the Township of
Williamstown, Ingham County Michigan, held in the Board Room of the Township at
4990 N. Zimmer Road, Williamston, MI 48895-9609, on July 2, 2002 at 7:30 p.m.
there were:
      PRESENT:   Supervisor Mickey Martin
            Clerk Susan Hiner
            Trustee Steve Zaban
            Trustee Martin Wright
      ABSENT:   Treasurer Nancy Fink
   At said meeting of the Township Board, the following Resolution was offered
by Trustee Wright and supported by Trustee Zaban.
   WHEREAS, the Williamston Community Library Foundation has been incorporated
as a public foundation and it is the stated intent of that foundation to work
toward construction of a new library in the City of Williamston, and
   WHEREAS, in furtherance of that intent, the Williamston Community Library
Foundation has retained a consultant to perform a needs assessment and is in
the process of acquiring an option to purchase real property in the City of
Williamston on which to build a new library, and
   WHEREAS, the Williamston Community Library Foundation has presented a
written proposal to the Williamstown Township Board, requesting authorization
to represent Williamstown Township in planning the purchase of property; in
planning the construction of a new library; and including an outline of its
program and funding strategies; and
   WHEREAS, the Williamstown Township Board desires to authorize the Committee
to act in the interest of Williamstown Township and desires that the
Williamstown Township Board approve any plan to purchase and/or construct a
library and any funding strategy plan before implementation.
   THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Williamstown Township Board authorizes
the Williamston Community Library Foundation to represent its interest in
planning to purchase property and/or to construct a library in accordance with
the following terms and conditions:
1.   that any and all plans, progress and reports during the course of the
Williamston Community Library Foundation’s evaluation of the library project
shall be communicated to the Williamstown Township Board;
2.   that the Williamstown Township Board must approve any plan, before
implementation, that involves the expenditure of funds by the Williamston
Community Library Foundation other than those already raised by the Foundation
and held in the Williamston Community Library building trust fund account on
the date that this Resolution herein is passed by the Williamstown Township
Board;
3.   that the Williamstown Township Board must approve the final plan, before
implementation, for the purchase or property and/or for the construction of the
library.

NEW BUSINESS
Fire Ordinance
The Planning Commission, together with McKenna Associates, Inc., presented the
board a sixth draft of an Ordinance to Regulate Open Burning and Establish Fire
Safety Regulations. Dan Kraft, Planning Commission Chair, gave an overview of
the proposed ordinance. Two unresolved issues were brought forward: 1) The
International Fire Code should be adopted by the Township as it is referred to
in the Michigan Building Code, which is the Building Code the Township adopted;
and 2) Concern that the standards for incinerators were outdated and should not
even be permitted in the Township. A public hearing was held on August 20, 2002
with extensive public input, both in favor and opposed to open burning. Under
the proposed regulation, residents would have the opportunity to petition for
more restrictions on a subdivision-by-subdivision basis. Peter Cohl,
Pebblebrook resident, asked the Board to consider: 1) Does the right to burn
supersede the right to breathe clean air? 2) The length of burning time allowed
being sunrise to 9 p.m.; and 3) Each homeowner should have a right to sign a
petition, not just one vote per household. Dr. Gary Gillespie, Pebblebrook
resident, stated that the by-products of burning, i.e. smoke, is detrimental to
the elderly, people with chronic heart and lung conditions, pregnant women and
their fetuses and the very young. Mike Allan, Ingham County Health Department,
stated that ordinance writing is up to the Township and asked that restrictions
not be lessened. Trustee Wright stated that the ordinance has become more
restrictive in regard to leaf and trash burning. George Durak, 116 Feldspar,
presented the Board with a letter dated September 3, 2002 expressing his
concern with the proposed Ordinance. Melanie Ford, Woodview subdivision,
drafting committee member, was asked by Supervisor Martin to put in writing the
intent of the committee. The Board agreed that clarification was needed
regarding NIESA issuing burn permits. Supervisor Martin will contact NIESA
regarding that issue.
Treasurer Fink moved and Clerk Hiner supported tabling the vote on the new fire
ordinance and keeping the matter open for discussion at the October Board
meeting; passed.
Zoning Board of Appeals Appointment
Treasurer Fink moved and Trustee Wright supported renewing Dale Fulton’s
appointment to the Zoning Board of Appeals; passed.

Trustee Wright moved and Treasurer Fink supported reappointing Rosemary Philip,

Building Code Resolution
TOWNSHIP OF WILLIAMSTOWN
BUILDING CODE
STATE CODE
ORDINANCE #41
An ordinance to designate an enforcing agency to discharge the responsibility
of the Township of Williamstown located in Ingham County, under the provisions
of the State Construction Code Act, 1972 P.A. 230.
The Township of Williamstown ordains:
Section 1. AGENCY DESIGNATED Pursuant to the provisions of the Michigan
Building Code, in accordance with Section 8b(6) of 1972 PA 230, the Building
Code Official of the Township of Williamstown is hereby designated as the
enforcing agency to discharge the responsibility of the Township of
Williamstown under 1972 PA 230, State of Michigan. The Township of Williamstown
assumes responsibility for the administration and enforcement of said Act
throughout its corporate limits.
Section 2. REPEALS All ordinances inconsistent with the provisions of this
ordinance are hereby repealed.
Section 3. MUNICIPAL CIVIL INFRACTION Williamstown Township will continue to
enforce building code violations through the use of municipal civil
infractions, as provided by the Williamstown Township code.
Section 4. PUBLICATIONS This ordinance shall be effective after legal
publication and in accordance with provisions of the Act governing same.
Adopted this 13th day of August 2002.
This Ordinance duly adopted on August 13, 2002 at a regular meeting of the
Board of Trustees and will become effective August 13, 2002.

Signed: __________________________

Ciolek – Hearing Request
Public hearing began at 9:05 p.m.
Supervisor Martin explained that this would be an informal hearing and read the
following in to the record:
Building Inspector Walter Aven letter of 4/23/02:  A call was received at the
Williamstown Township office that there appeared someone was living in the barn
on your property at 1054 E. Sherwood Road. The Williamstown Township Zoning
Ordinance does not allow two principal dwellings on one property description.
It does appear that there is some construction going on at the barn without a
Building Permit. This is also a violation of the Township Ordinance and the
Building Code. This is notice that these violations shall be promptly complied
to. If you have any questions, please call.  
David Ciolek letter to Building Inspector Walter Aven of 5/10/02:  This letter
is in response to your letter of April 23rd and your concern about the barn
located on the property at 1054 E. Sherwood Road. I hope this letter can clear
up this matter. I use the barn for my television production program about old
barns that I am developing. The barn does include a nonfunctioning stove,
cupboards, dishwasher, wood burning stove and other props. The structure is
whole and complete, and so the only work that goes on here is minor maintenance
and prop installations. Please also note that the barn has no heating system,
no kitchen plumbing and no separate electrical meter. Occasionally my daughters
will spend the night in the barn, just for the fun of it. I also spend long
hours in the barn. My young daughters do like to pretend that this barn is a
huge playhouse. I hope this clears up any misunderstandings in this matter,
call me if you have any further question
Neighbors of David Ciolek letter of 6/18/02: Many issues have recently surfaced
concerning the second dwelling and construction taking place at the barn at
1054 Sherwood Road. The homeowner, Mr. Ciolek has been renovating his barn into
an apartment for over the last 2-3 years. He has installed service to the barn
for water, electric, septic sewer and possibly gas heat. No building permits
have been displayed and we question whether or not they were ever issued. We
also question the permission to have two separate dwellings on one parcel of
land. All of this construction has come about since he separated from and
divorced Mrs. Ciolek. It appears that he did not want to vacate the property
and decided to build his own home within the barn. Since he does have a joint
custody agreement, his daughters spend their time with him there in the barn.
It is rumored that he has replied to you about the barn being a prop for his
developing television show. Nothing could be further from the truth or simply
more hilarious. He has lived in this barn/apartment/home with his children,
girlfriend and self. It is most definitely a home with all utilities and
nothing else. We hesitate to provide our names at this time because Mr. Ciolek
is quite unpredictable and we fear a response of vengeful nature. However, we
do request that this matter be addressed by the Township. Thank you for your
attention to this situation. Simply signed, Neighbors surrounding Ciolek
parcel. (Mr. Ross asked who sent the letter and Supervisor Martin responded
that it was sent anonymously.)
DIVORCE DECREE REMOVED FROM MINUTES ON 4/18/06 AND REPUBLISHED
Supervisor Martin produced a copy of a septic permit, given to her by Bruce
Gruner of the Ingham County Health Department, that Mr. Ciolek requested from
that Department. He was given the permit not knowing the Township did not allow
that type of use. The permit is attached to these Board minutes.
Supervisor Martin read into the record the following violations of the Township
Zoning Ordinance:
1.   Section 2.06 (11): Home occupations may be permitted in an accessory
building subject to special land use approval.
2.   Section 2.09A(2): Number of Principal Uses per Lot. Only one principal
building shall be placed on a lot of record or parcel in single-family
residential districts. In a single family site condominium project, only one
principal building shall be placed on each condominium lot, as defined in
Article 1.00.
3.   Section 27.07A(1)a: Permit Required. A building permit or other
appropriate permit shall be required as follows: Prior to the erection,
alteration, repair, renovation, demolition or removal of any building or
structure.
Constable Howard Dahlstrom stated that he spoke with Nancy Ciolek and she did
not want to be involved in the process of removing him from the premises for
fear of repercussions. Mr. Dahlstrom suggested she get a personal protection
order against Mr. Ciolek. Mr. Dahlstrom visited the site, attempting to contact
someone in the barn. A registration search on a red pickup truck parked outside
the barn showed it to be registered to Mr. Ciolek at the Sherwood Road address.
The truck was there at 11 p.m. and still remained at 6 a.m. the next morning.
He is a registered voter at that address and with the Secretary of State. Paul
Ross, Mr. Ciolek’s attorney, was present at the meeting and asked for a short
break in which to speak with Mr. Ciolek in private. Mr. Spagnuolo stressed that
the purpose of the hearing was to resolve the issue and to present factual
evidence in a fair and impartial manner. He then gave the Board copies of a
letter dated September 3, 2002 prepared for presentation at the meeting. Mr.
Ross stated that the Michigan Right to Farm Act protected Mr. Ciolek due to his
production and sale of branch water and a barn renovation production company,
and the Township was therefore precluded from enforcing any ordinance,
regulation or resolution. He also stated that the barn was not being used for a
residence and that in the past 30 days Mr. Ciolek had spent only 2 nights
there. Mr. Spagnuolo and Mr. Ross will speak further on the issue. Mr.
Spagnuolo will pursue the matter in court as quickly as possible.
Hearing closed at 9:35 p.m.
Brian Morley, attorney for Mrs. Ciolek, addressed the Board and stated that she
did not want to make waves, would like to sell the property and that it was a
“blatant lie” that Mr. Ciolek does not live in the barn. Mr. Ross Morley asked
for a copy of the written material Mr. Ross presented.
Mr. Spagnuolo asked for a break at 9:40p.m. Meeting resumed at 9:45 p.m.

Revisions to Zoning, Wetlands and Land Division Ordinances
Dan Kraft, Planning Commission Chair, explained that the Planning Commission
collects information throughout the year from its members, citizen comments,
Township staff input, state mandates, etc… and then makes an annual
recommendation for revisions to each of these Township ordinances.
Mr. Kraft identified two substantive issues, beyond the nature of
clarification, that were addressed this year. The first change was made because
the State has required all townships to modify their ordinance to allow for
clustering by December 1, 2002. Mr. Kraft stated that the Planning Commission’s
goal was to recommend changes to the open space preservation option in the
Township Zoning Ordinance that would align Township policies with State
mandates. The second substantive change is an amendment to the Wetland
Protection Ordinance that eliminates unnecessary double review by the Township
and the State. The remaining changes proposed are in the nature of
clarification or are typographical corrections.
Mr. Kraft reported that a public hearing on these recommendations was held
September 17, 2002 with very little input. One citizen attended as an observer
only. There was no comment for or against so the Planning Commission moved to
approve the recommended revisions.
Supervisor Martin asked Mr. Kraft two questions on the open space preservation
option. First, Ms. Martin noted that R1 is now included in the option and that
the minimum lot size has changed significantly. For instance, the minimum lot
size for RR is now stated at 40,500 sq. ft.. The Township’s current document
states a minimum lot size for RR of 32,750 sq. ft with a maximum of 40,500 sq.
ft. She asked Mr. Kraft if this change was made because the State minimum lot
sizes had changed. Dan was not sure why the change had occurred but believed
that it was a problem in the drafting of the document at McKenna Associates and
that he did not believe there was any mandate at the state level requiring the
change. Supervisor Martin recommended that the Township return the document to
the original minimum lot size dimensions of 32,750 sq. ft. Mr. Kraft agreed
that this would enhance the clustering option. Mr. Kraft suggested that maximum
lot size criteria be eliminated to allow the option of putting fewer homes on a
parcel.
Supervisor Martin questioned why a statement in the existing document that
allows only 25% of a property be dedicated to recreation facilities had been
eliminated in the revised document. Mr. Kraft responded that the Planning
Commission had not specifically discussed this item and it was unknown why
McKenna Associates had removed the statement. Supervisor Martin requested that
the statement be returned to the document and Mr. Kraft and the other board
members had no objections.
Supervisor Martin stated that in the revisions to the miscellaneous section of
the Zoning Ordinance, the revised document states that horses may be pastured
to the property line (Section 8.02.CC.3c). She said the Township ordinance also
states that electric fences (typically used to fence horses) cannot be located
on the property line. Mr. Kraft recommended that a statement be added to
Section 8.02 that refers the reader to Section 6.02.B.3 (which says that
electric fences must be set back 18 inches from all property lines).
Supervisor Martin also recommended a typographical correction to change
“regulations” to “regulation” on Page 4.
Supervisor Martin requested that the Planning Commission readdress Section
26.02 regarding minimum lot area for irregularly shaped lots to include
resulting lots that are over 10 acres in size. Currently, the Township cannot
regulate using width to depth on parcels over 10 acres and this has become a
recurring problem. Supervisor Martin requested that this section be eliminated
from the proposed revision document tonight and the topic returned to the
Planning Commission for additional consideration to include lots greater than
10 acres.
Supervisor Martin stated that she felt the Wetlands recommendations were a fine
compromise. She noted that for parcels over 5 acres, it is clear that the
Township should use the DEQ application form. Ms. Martin asked if this
application form should also be used for parcels 5 acres and less (i.e. parcels
that only the Township has jurisdiction over). Mr. Kraft said that the
application form had not been specifically discussed. Supervisor Martin added
that if the Township needs to prepare its own application, the Planning
Commission would need to provide recommendations for content. Mr. Kraft
recommended that McKenna Associates be asked to provide input about similar
documents used by other municipalities and, with consideration of the DEQ
application used for parcels over 5 acres, the Township adopt the best
application format for use by the Township for parcels under 5 acres.
Supervisor Martin agreed and recommended that the Planning Commission readdress
this item.
Supervisor Martin commented that 2nd revision listed on Page 1, Subsection 2.03
will be a point of contention for some citizens from an administrative
standpoint. This item states, “where the total of all accessory buildings is
4,000 sq. ft. or greater, site plan review and approval shall be required.” She
said that means that a homeowner that wants to put a 200 sq. ft. shed on his
property that already has 4000 sq. ft. of buildings in place, will have to have
a whole site plan review performed. Trustee Wright said that this item had been
discussed and that the Planning Commission decided that the line had to be
drawn somewhere. (This does not apply to Ag-commercial zones).
Supervisor Martin asked for a motion to approve revisions to the Zoning,
Wetlands and Land Division Ordinances with changes discussed. Trustee Zaban
moved to approve the Planning Commission revisions with the deletions and
corrections made and Clerk Hiner supported the motion. Motion passed
unanimously.

Fire Ordinance
Supervisor Martin reported that a 7th draft of the Fire Ordinance was now
complete. She commented her surprise that more people hadn’t attended tonight’s
meeting regarding this issue.
Before discussing the details of the revised draft, Ms. Martin noted that the
board had received a letter dated September 30, 2002 prepared by citizen
Melanie Ford. That letter had been reviewed and Ms. Ford agreed that her
concerns had been addressed.
Supervisor Martin reported that citizen George Durak had also submitted a
letter and she highlighted Mr. Durak’s concerns for the record. Mr. Durak’s
letter stated that he had procedural concerns because he was not brought in at
the beginning stages of the revision. Ms. Martin stated that the first time the
committee met was March 14, 2002 and that she had spoken with Mr. Durak on
April 24, 2002. At that point he had only missed the first meeting. Based on
her conversation with Mr. Durak, Ms. Martin sent a memo to Rosemary Philip,
Chairman of the Fire Ordinance Committee, informing her of his desire to
participate in the revision process. The committee’s next meeting was held on
May 1, 2002 and Mr. Durak was contacted. He indicated that he would be unable
to attend but that he may send someone in his place (this did not happen). The
next meeting was held on May 14, 2002, which Mr. Durak attended and in June a
recommendation was made to the Planning Commission. Mr. Durak has been at every
meeting since that time. Supervisor Martin does not understand why Mr. Durak
feels that he was not included in the early stages of the ordinance revision.
Mr. Durak’s letter also asked about the specifics of burning household trash in
the petition and whether the petition could be applied to the current ordinance
at this time. Supervisor Martin said that it wasn’t the Board’s request at the
time and the Board felt the entire ordinance needed to be brought up to date.
He also stated concern about the petition and the ordinance. Supervisor Martin
said that she believes both these and all of Mr. Durak’s other questions have
been answered.
Supervisor Martin overviewed the 7th draft of the Fire Ordinance. She stated
that there are no changes from the previous draft until the section on the
Pebblebrook petition. Through consultation with the attorney and Chris Doozan,
it was determined that the township was giving regulatory decision making power
to the public, which hasn’t been done with any other ordinances. Typically, the
public is allowed to come forward and request the board to review an ordinance.
The 7th revision allows Pebblebrook and all Township citizens to petition the
Township board in an advisory capacity. If the board determines the petition
items need review, the issue will be sent to the Planning Commission for
consideration. However, bringing a petition to the board does not automatically
make a change to the ordinance. Treasurer Fink asked how the board was going to
accept petitions and Supervisor Martin said the attorney recommended that the
Township board make its own policy on how it will accept petitions and that the
procedure should not be put into an ordinance.
The next change was made on Page 7 regarding industrial fires. The revision
states that “… any burning on a commercial or industrial property shall be
subject to the inspection by the Township building official. It will have to
meet the requirements of the International Fire Code and the Michigan Building
Code.” The revision does not include specifics about stack size, etc… and
instead refers to compliance with these two codes.
Supervisor Martin said that the other change made in the 7th draft affected the
burning of household trash. The previous ordinance eliminated burning household
trash in RR, RE, Ag-Small Farm zones and only allowed burning household trash
in areas zoned AG-Commercial. The 7th draft returns burning of household trash
to areas zoned RE and Ag-Small Farm with notes that “burning of household trash
is not permitted on parcels less than 5 acres in area.” It was recommended that
the Township inform the public at this time that restrictions on burning are
only going to increase from this point forward. The public should expect the
burning of all household trash to be eliminated in the near future. Supervisor
Martin stated that it was the thought of the Township board that without having
this issue presented at public hearing, the elimination of all household trash
burning would not be appropriate. The noxious odor provision allows a mechanism
to stop burning if there is a complaint.
Citizen Rud Hoag (2100 Sherwood Rd.) said that he agrees with the decision to
eliminate household trash burning. He believes that household trash is best
taken care of in landfills and that even a 5 or 10 acre parcel size doesn’t
prevent smoke from becoming a nuisance to neighboring property owners. He said
that this summer there wasn’t very many nights when he didn’t get inundated
with smoke from someone burning in a burn barrel. He stated that it doesn’t
make sense that in this day in age the Township even allows burn barrels.
Supervisor Martin clarified that preventing burning of household trash in burn
barrels does not eliminate burn barrels altogether. Homeowners can still burn
non-household trash material (yard waste for example) as clarified on Page 7 of
the Fire Ordinance which states burn barrels are allowed. Treasurer Fink said
that the board has equated burning household trash in a burn barrel with burn
barrels during discussions in the past but technically they are not equivalent.
Supervisor Martin asked if Mr. Hoag’s issue was with the smell of smoke. Mr.
Hoag said that it is difficult for a citizen to file a complaint about a
noxious odor because the source cannot always be identified.
Citizen Melanie Ford asked if a timeframe has been established to eliminate
burn barrels in the Township. Supervisor Martin said that the plan is to
eliminate burn barrels within 1-2 years. She said the Township is reluctant to
make that change immediately because the issue has not been discussed
adequately at any public hearing. She said there are a lot of people using burn
barrels so administratively this decision needs to be given due process.
Trustee Zaban recommended that pages 10 and 11 of the Fire Ordinance be
included in the next newsletter regardless of cost along with an explanation of
the zoning codes (RR, R1, etc… ). Supervisor Martin said these two pages are
already included and that perhaps the zoning map should be included in the
newsletter again as well. She added that the newsletter could inform citizens
that their assessment and tax notices identify their zone designation. Board
members generally agreed that notifying the public in the newsletter of the
direction the Township is moving regarding burning would be helpful. Mr. Hoag
said the public needs to be aware that complaints will continue to be filed.
Treasurer Fink suggested that Mr. Hoag write an article for the newsletter
stating his reasons why this is an ordinance he believes needs to be made more
restrictive. Supervisor Martin said that this month’s newsletter is already
near completion and that information may need to be included in the next one
instead.
Dan Kraft complimented the board, the planning commission, and the citizens who
provided input for all the work that went into preparing the Fire Ordinance. It
was a six month process and the document went through 7 revisions. He stated
that he thinks the 7th draft is an excellent compromise.
Supervisor Martin noted one more change to the document on Page 11, Table 1,
Note 1 which needs to state “…and on lots created by land division that are
adjoined on one side or are commonly considered a part of an RR zoned
subdivision or condominium.” This change had been previously agreed upon and
inadvertently omitted.
Treasurer Fink mentioned that the Township and/or NIESA may get citizen calls
about campfires even though the ordinance does not require permits for
campfires that meet the size criteria. She suggested that the Township be
prepared to revise the document again due to this issue.
Trustee Wright made a motion with support from Clerk Hiner to adopt Ordinance
Number 41-Ordinance to Regulate Open Burning, 7th Draft, dated September 18,
2002 with one change to Page 11, Table 1, Note 1.
A roll call vote was taken:
Trustee Zaban   Yes
Trustee Wright   Yes
Treasurer Fink   Yes
Supervisor Martin   Yes
Clerk Hiner      Yes
Resolution passed unanimously.

Building Use and Expansion
Clerk Hiner reported that she, along with Supervisor Martin and Tim Howell, met
with Swanson Design Studios last week and received proposals for the Township
Building Expansion ranging from $35,000 to $1 million. Clerk Hiner reported
that after reviewing the proposals they recommended elements from Proposals A
and C. These include:
· Expansion of the meeting area to include a permanent meeting room and space
for hall rental
· Additional storage space to allow for off-site storage to return to the
Township offices
· Expanded office space to include office rooms for the three officers and a
private conference
· Remodeling the two bathroom areas to make them handicap accessible
· Repairing the parking lot and adding parking lot lighting
Clerk Hiner reported that they will meet with Swanson Design again on October
15, 2002 at 4 p.m. to review a revised design. She said the estimated cost for
modifications would be in the range of $250-300,000. The revised plan should
address the needs for 20 years of Township growth. The plan will not include
the addition of a fire building (which may be a future recommendation by NIESA)
because of the estimated $300,000 increase in costs.

said that a drawing is now being prepared to present to the American Legion
with a request for their assistance on additional development of the park

Use of Computerized Data Base as a Tax Roll Resolution
Supervisor Martin presented a Resolution for the Use of Computerized Data Base
as a Tax Roll. Supervisor Martin provided board members with the background
information showing that this resolution was actually required as part of an
act passed in 1990 and should have been done previously by all townships using
this method. The State of Michigan recently notified townships that they needed
to have passed a resolution declaring that they were using a computerized
database for tax roll purposes. Trustee Wright moved to approve the resolution
supported by Clerk Hiner.

Supervisor Martin asked if the election process was going well. Clerk Hiner

Cemetery on Sherwood Road). The Township currently has control of the day-to-

to germinate. Treasurer Fink asked if any dirt has been added to the sliding
hill. Trustee Wright said that the contractor (K&R) may have added a small

Other
Library
Supervisor Martin reported that the Township received a letter of notification
from the Williamston Library Foundation regarding a meeting being held on
November 13, 2002 at 7 p.m. in the City Hall to discuss the proposed library
expansion. Trustee Wright said he would plan to attend. The proposal suggests
the community needs a 15,000 sq ft library. Supervisor Martin requested that
each board member give their comments on the proposal to Trustee Wright so that
he could attend the meeting informed of the Board’s position. Clerk Hiner said
that she felt the Williamston Library Foundation should present the proposal to
a wider cross-section of the population to determine how much funding the
community will be willing to support. She added that she and her family love
the library and believes the existing library is wholly inadequate. Clerk Hiner
said that the proposal appeared to reflect the “cadillac” of options and did
not see in the proposal information about what the community was willing to
support. Supervisor Martin added that she also didn’t think the proposal
identified the specific reasons to justify why a community of 9,000 needs the
amount of space proposed (a space larger than Haslett and Okemos). Trustee
Wright asked what the City of Williamston is expecting from the Township.
Supervisor Martin said that the Township is being asked to pay a full 1/3 of
the cost to build and maintain the facility.
Supervisor Martin summarized that it is the consensus of the Board that the
Williamston Library Foundation should get more input from the public before
proceeding with any plans and that the Foundation needs to present the Township
with formalized funding options before we can consider their proposal fully.
Treasurer Fink reiterated that the Township needs a funding proposal. Clerk
Hiner said she felt there was definitely support in the community for a new
library but she wasn’t sure if there was support for something this large.
Supervisor Fink said that she wants to see the City avoid offering a proposal
to the people, only to have it voted down, and then repeatedly offering a pared
down version of the proposal until it passes. Trustee Wright asked the term
status of the individuals on the committee representing the Township on this
issue and when they come up for reappointment. Supervisor Martin said she would
bring that information to the Board workshop on November 19, 2002.
Trustee Zaban stated he wants to avoid another situation like NIESA. In this
relationship, Williamstown Township provides 46% ($171,778) of the funding for
NIESA but reaps the fewest benefits of all the participants (Wheatfield
Township contributes $47,000, City of Williamston contributes 84,000, Leroy
Township (including the Village of Webberville) contributes $75,000, and Locke
Township contributes $45,000. Supervisor Martin said that, even after this
level of contribution, Williamstown Township residents still pay the highest
homeowners insurance premiums because we don’t have fire protection coverage
stationed within the Township. Trustee Zaban said that he feels Williamstown
Township should have a fire truck stationed at the Township office. He added
that everything moves very slowly with NIESA. Trustee Zaban and Treasurer Fink
both reiterated that they want to prevent a similar situation recurring with
the library expansion where Williamstown Township pays the bulk of the expense,
but realizes the least benefit.
Zoning Enforcement Officer
Trustee Zaban stated that it appears that the Clerk and Supervisor are spending
considerable time responding to citizen complaints (renter problems, property
clutter, etc…). He asked if the Township has reached a point in time where we
should consider hiring a Zoning Enforcement Officer. Supervisor Martin
responded that zoning enforcement responsibilities are currently assigned to
Constable Dahlstrom, who is still employed elsewhere full time. She said that
Constable Dahlstrom has stated that he has approximately 81 working days to
retirement. After that time, he will be able to commit to work one day a week
for the Township to enforce zoning violations. Supervisor Martin said that once
Howard is able to commit this time, her involvement will be minimal. She said
she will still need to handle the administrative end because she is the one
knowledgeable of the zoning requirements and will be the person to appear in
court if necessary. Supervisor Martin said that if Constable Dahlstrom decides
he cannot commit the necessary time to the Township after he retires (sometime
in April), then she would agree the Township should consider adding a Zoning
Enforcement Officer. Trustee Zaban suggested that this person would not have to
be a deputy. Supervisor Martin stated that Constable Dahlstrom is our elected
constable and he will be given first right of refusal for this position.
Updated McKenna Contract
Supervisor Martin reviewed the updated contract with McKenna Associates that
provides for a representative from McKenna Associates to work in the
Williamstown Township office one day a week. She stated that Chris Doozen will
work from our office one day a month and Jim Breuckman will be here the
remaining three days. (Mr. Doozen is the Vice President of McKenna Associates
and Mr. Breuckman is an associate engineer who currently attends the Planning
Commission meetings). Supervisor Martin said that this situation will be very
useful to the Township because now the Supervisor will no longer be both the
first person a developer sees when he submits a site plan and the last person
they see after the Township Board approves or disapproves their proposal. The
Township will also now have a consistent schedule for reviewing planning
documents and developers will know the office hours that site plans can be
reviewed. The contract with McKenna further states that, when their
representatives are not working on Williamstown Township planning issues while
they are in our office, they will not charge the Township for their time (they
will work on other McKenna projects). Supervisor Martin said she would like to
move forward with this change in their contract as soon as possible. Trustee
Wright stated that this contract modification makes good sense for the
Township. The Board agreed. Supervisor Martin stated that the Board does not
need to vote on this issue because it is a contract change only.

1458 E. Grand River SUP and Site Plan-Williamston Foods, PC Recommendation
Board Final Action
Site Plan
Planning Commission Chair Dan Kraft reported that the Planning Commission had
reviewed the site plan and made some requests for revision. The Township has
received a revised site plan from Williamston Foods, a memo dated 11/26/02 from
Jim Breuckman (McKenna Associates), and a letter dated 11/26/02 from Duane
Shore (Space Architecture) addressing the Planning Commissions concerns.
Supervisor Martin reported that Mr. Breukman had reviewed these resubmitted
documents and believed that Williamston Foods had made the necessary
corrections to the site plan with the exception of addressing the lighting
issues. However, the Williamston Foods’ letter dated 11/26/02 does address
these lighting issues. Mr. Breukman recommended that, since the addition being
requested was small, the Board approve Williamston Foods request but require
the information provided in their 11/26/02 letter be included as part of the
approval. Mr. Kraft stated that it should be noted on the plan that no new HVAC
units were planned. The applicant confirmed that two exhaust fans will be
installed but no new HVAC units will be installed. Supervisor Martin asked if
this addition to the site plan was a condition for approval and Mr. Kraft
responded that it was not.
Supervisor Martin summarized that Williamston Foods wants to add a new oven
area to their operation so that they can increase their business and create new
jobs. She asked if the applicant had any more information to add. The applicant
asked to clarify Item 4 on the McKenna memo dated 11/26/02. The memo states
that “one light fixture will be removed and the new addition will be equipped
with its own lighting.” He said the description should read that “the lights
that exist will be maintained and that the addition will have three new
fixtures.” Supervisor Martin told the applicant that Mr. Breuckman had also
recognized this correction during his review of the revised site plan and
concurred.
Supervisor Martin summarized that it appeared that all the Planning Commission
conditions had been met except for the lighting. She added that Williamston
Foods has provided a memo to address this item which states that all existing
lighting will remain as is and that three new lights will be added as indicated
on the revised plans. She called for a motion to approve the site plan with no
conditions. Trustee Wright asked that Williamston Foods Memo dated 11/26/02 be
included with the site plan and Mr. Kraft agreed. No further discussion was
offered. Trustee Wright made a motion supported by Trustee Zaban to accept the
Williamston Foods Site Plan with 11/26/02 memo included. Motion passed
unanimously.
