Rezoning Request from RE to B-2 at 1040 Grand River- Young O. Kim( Tabled
December 3, 2002)
Supervisor Martin called for a motion to un-table Mr. Kim’s rezoning request.
Trustee Wright moved to un-table the rezoning request made by Mr. Young Kim for
converting the property located at 1040 Grand River from an RE to B-2 zone, the
original request was tabled by the Board on December 3, 2002. Motion supported
by Trustee Zaban. Motion passed unanimously.
Planning Commission Chairman Dan Kraft reported that the rezoning request was
tied to a proposed use on the property. The Planning Commission kind of liked
the idea of a greenhouse operation on this property but they are not allowed to
spot zone based on use. The proposed B2 zone is for commercial use. The
applicants proposed use was for a commercial greenhouse with a retail sales
operation. When the use was eliminated from their consideration, the Planning
Commission voted to recommend denial of this rezoning request because it is
inconsistent with the Master Plan. The Grand River/Zimmer intersection is
considered the “town center” on the Master Plan and it is one of the last
existing open spaces on the corridor. The Planning Commission as it exists
wants to keep the zoning as it exists. The B2 zone would allow a number of uses
that would be unacceptable to the Planning Commissioners.
Supervisor Martin stated that there are several business uses already allowed
in the RE district including residential care facilities, essential services
and (by special use permit) bed and breakfast operations, golf driving ranges,
riding stables, commercial kennels, veterinary clinics, transmitting towers,
oil and gas processing facilities, greenhouses, sod growing operations, nature
centers, demonstration farms, etc... She said there are really a lot of options
available in the RE, especially when the option the applicant was interested in
was a greenhouse. Treasurer Fink asked if there is sanitary sewer available to
the property. Supervisor Martin said that the sewer line goes up to the
property and it would have to be part of the Township’s 7 remaining available
taps.
Supervisor Martin asked if there was any more information that the applicant
would like to add. Mr. Kim said he didn’t know what kind of information the
Board would like to hear. He said he applied the first time in B-2 because
there is commercial property around his property. He doesn’t understand why his
property can’t be commercial. Treasurer Fink responded that it is because the
Township Master Plan doesn’t want continuous commercial development along Grand
River. Mr. Kim asked how long this policy will last-100 years, 1000 years?
Treasurer Fink said the plan will likely be in place for 5 to 10 years. He said
he couldn’t understand why his property could not be commercial when all the
property surrounding it is commercial. Treasurer Fink said it is because he is
applying now and that is the policy that is in place now.
Treasurer Fink made a motion to accept the Planning Commission’s
recommendations and deny the rezoning application from RE to B2 at 1440 Grand
River. Motion supported by Clerk Hiner.
Trustee Zaban asked how long Mr. Kim had owned the property. Mr. Kim said he
had owned the property since last year. He wants to build a greenhouse but that
business might fail so he wants to have other choices. Mr. Kim said that if
business is good he would like to build another greenhouse. Mr. Kim said he
does not understand the reasons why this property cannot be commercial.
Treasurer Fink recommended to Supervisor Martin that the reasons be put in
writing for Mr. Kim. Supervisor Martin agreed that the reasons could be
summarized from the Planning Commission minutes.
Supervisor Martin said that in this Township we are very protective of our
property. Mr. Kim asked for how long and Supervisor Martin said that it may be
a 10-15 year investment for him, she’s not sure. She said there is B2 area that
is available and that at this time the Planning Commission doesn’t feel the
Township needs more commercial property. Supervisor Martin said that when he
bought the property, Mr. Kim knew that it was zoned RE and not commercial. Mr.
Kim said he bought the property last year in winter and did not realize it was
wetlands. He agreed with Supervisor Martin that he has an issue with the person
he bought it from. Mr. Kim said he appreciated that the Township Supervisor

Complaint - 5545 Lounsbury Road - Blight 
Supervisor Martin reported that she, planning consultant Chris Doozan and
Constable Dahlstrom had visited the property owned by Dorothy Young in response
to citizen complaints. Supervisor Martin explained she had written a letter
after the visits reflecting their observations. Specifically, the letter refers
to piles of building material, building debris, a steep incline to an open
basement with no protection, unsightly tarps used in place of permanent siding
and roofing, wood planks used to provide access to the house and unsightly wood
sheets used in place of permanent wood siding and windows. Supervisor Martin
said these conditions have existed for an extended period of time and longer
than typical for a construction project. She said that Mrs. Young was notified
in the letter that she had 10 days to correct the problems.
Supervisor Martin stated that Mrs. Young and Mr. Witgen responded with a letter
of remediation (received by the Township on Saturday, June 27). Supervisor
Martin said the response letter describes what they are trying to do with the
property but did not clearly state a timeline for abatement. Mrs. Young stated
that their explanation was provided on page 2 of the letter. Supervisor Martin
read from the letter “…4 or 5 weeks as long as there are not too many rainy
days.” Supervisor Martin asked the Board if they have any questions. Supervisor

Wright said the letter was not specific enough. Mr. Witgen said he will have
the back end of the house completed in the next 4-5 weeks. He said that, once
complete, he plans to start on the front half of the house (which will require
new tarps). Mr. Witgen suggested that he could hold this part of the project
off until spring rather than leaving the front of the house covered in tarp all
winter. Supervisor Martin questioned whether the tarp was necessary.
Trustee Wright asked about the piles of building materials and building debris.

Mr. Witgen agreed. Trustee Wright asked the status of the wood planks. Mr.

Mr. Witgen said he is concentrating on the roof right now and would like to put
the porch on next before he does the siding. He said that once he gets the
footings in, the 2 porch roofs can be put in and then he can start the siding.
Once the siding goes on he was planning to take care of the windows.
Trustee Wright said that from what he can see, this process has been going on
for some time. Mr. Witgen said he’s been working on the project for 3 years,
starting with the basement. Trustee Wright asked Building Inspector Walt Aven
if he had any suggestions. Mr. Aven said he thinks Mr. Witgen needs to get more
help. Mrs. Young said that there is a legal agreement between Mr. Witgen and
her and Mr. Witgen is putting in sweat equity because he eventually wants to

said he already has a lot invested in the property.
Trustee Wright said there needs to be some definite dates for progress. Mr.
Witgen said that by the next Board meeting, there should be some progress.
Supervisor Martin clarified that the Board could expect an inspection conducted

be protected, the unsightly tarps will be removed, and the wood planks will be
removed. Mr. Witgen said the sheeting would not be removed by the next meeting.
Mr. Witgen said there will be progress but you won’t see a difference from the
outside. Trustee Wright said the main thing the Board needs to see is
significant progress.
Trustee Wright said the Board will start with this and then set some new
deadlines at the next Board meeting. He explained that the Board needs this
issue addressed by fall because there have been many, many complaints about it
from neighbors. Mr. Witgen said he realizes that the public location of the
property is a problem. He said he wants to make the farmhouse a building that
looks good and fits in with the neighborhood. Trustee Wright said the Board
realizes that and wants to see him succeed in this endeavor. Trustee Wright
said the Township has had complaints over the last couple of years and have
tried to minimize it so Mr. Witgen could get the project going but now the
complaints have increased and become more intense so they need to be addressed.
Trustee Wright said it looks like the first 3 items have been addressed or will
be within a month; Mr. Witgen has committed to get the tarps down and have the
back enclosed. At the next Board meeting the Township would like to see his
plans for the 5th item which involves the porches. Trustee Wright said the
Board needs to see significant progress. Mr. Witgen said that he plans to also
start working on the front of the house, and this is going to open another can

Building Permits-Fee Based
Supervisor Martin stated that this issue was discussed at the workshop. She
explained that currently the fee is based on the size of the structure and
valuation of work. Some people put down what they think and some developers use
the worksheet that Mr. Aven prepared. Supervisor Martin said she believes

the estimate by the worksheet formula will be on the low end for everybody (a
$300,000 house will look like $175,000 using the worksheet). Supervisor Martin
suggested that we start with this worksheet and if Mr. Aven
determines that we need to develop another one, that will be fine. Inspector
Aven said building permit information used to be published in the Lansing State
Journal so homeowners would flag the cost of their house if the builder’s
permit cost didn’t match what they were paying the builder.
Clerk Hiner asked Mr. Aven if he was comfortable with the cost per square foot
listed on the worksheet because it seemed very low to her. Supervisor Martin
said that cost was recently increased from $35/sq. ft. to $50/sq. ft. Trustee
Wright said his concern is that some people pay less than they should for their
permit. He added that sometimes when people estimate a lump sum based on what
they are spending instead of calculating fees based on square foot, they
undervalue what they are building. The valuation process is too arbitrary.
Supervisor Martin said that if this method doesn’t work, then we can try
something else.

Resolution to Transfer Funds Electronically (Resolution #31)
(MTA recently published draft wording for Townships to adopt a resolution to
handle transferring funds and invoice payments electronically due to computer
payment options now available). Supervisor Martin stated that she does not
fully understand what this resolution requires of the Township and requested

electronically be investigated and defined before adopting this resolution.

month to DTE. She added that ING/Aetna has also recently notified her of the

the Township has developed a policy, we consider making as many payments
electronically as possible. Clerk Hiner said that she prefers electronic

transfers triggered by the Township and not set up as automatic payments.

discussion can take place. She stated that the Board agrees that existing
electronic payment plans can continue for the next two months until agreed upon
procedures are established.

Ordinance Revision-Burn Ordinance
Planning Commission Chairman Dan Kraft reported that a public hearing had been
held regarding the revision of the burn ordinance requirement for the allowable
size of yard waste piles. He reported that there was very little comment on the
issue. He said that one citizen had asked whether the ordinance considered
burning yard waste on a windy day. Mr. Kraft also reported that the
commissioners did not understand the administrative concerns voiced by Township
staff about implementing an ordinance which specified two different burn pile
sizes depending upon the applicant’s property zoning. Clerk Hiner said it would
be clear to them if they answered the office telephone on the Friday before a
nice weekend. Mr. Kraft said the Commission felt that a yard waste fire size of
4’x4’ (the size recommended by NIESA) was too small and would result in yard
waste fires burning and generating smoke for a longer period of time.
Supervisor Martin stated that NIESA’s established their recommended yard waste
size requirement based on their experience with fires that typically get away
from people. She asked on what basis the Commission made their decision and
whether it was based solely on personal opinion. Mr. Kraft said that it was
most probably personal opinion but that most commissioners had experience with
yard waste fires from burning on their own property. Supervisor Martin said she
is concerned that the Township will be setting size criteria that are larger
than the 4’x4’x4’ dimensions recommended by NIESA. Chairman Kraft asked the
Board whether citizens ever ask about burn size requirements when they call the
office for a permit. Supervisor Martin said that they often ask or are
otherwise told the criteria by office staff during the application process.
Treasurer Fink said that she had reviewed the burn ordinances of several
neighboring communities and some also included a setback requirement for fires
from burnable items. She commented that the Township’s ordinance has no
criteria for setbacks.
Trustee Zaban clarified that the current ordinance states that a yard waste
burn pile must be no larger than 4’x 4’x 4’ in size and the Planning Commission
is now recommending the size be increased to 6’x 6’x 6.’ Citizen Frans Wilbrink
commented that farmers often want to burn larger piles. Supervisor Martin
clarified that if this issue passes tonight, the ordinance will stipulate a
maximum burn pile size of 6’ x 6’ x 6’. If the recommendation does not pass
tonight, the size will revert to the current Board policy of 4’ x 4’ x 4’. Mr.
Kraft said it makes sense to him to have a smaller size requirement for dense
areas and a larger size allowed for the rural areas. He added that there were
some commissioners that wanted an even larger size allowed so 6’ x 6’ x 6’ was
actually a compromise.
Trustee Zaban made a motion to accept the Planning Commission recommendation to
amend the burn ordinance to state that the maximum size for burn piles is 6’ x
6’ x 6’. Motion supported by Clerk Hiner.
Supervisor Martin called for a roll call vote of the Board members:
Roll Call Vote:
Treasurer Nancy Fink      No
Trustee Steve Zaban      Yes
Supervisor Mickey Martin   No
Trustee Martin Wright      Yes
Clerk Susan Hiner      Yes
Motion passed 3-2.
Supervisor Martin stated that she takes her position based on NIESA’s burn pile
size recommendation of 4’x 4’x 4’.
Mr. Kraft stated that he had no further Planning Commission issues to present
to the Board.

Complaints
Blight-Young Property
5545 Lounsbury Road
Supervisor Martin reminded the Board that Mr. Witgen (current resident) and
Mrs. Young (property owner) had attended the July Board meeting and Mr. Witgen
had been given a list of criteria that needed to be met by the
August Board meeting. Supervisor Martin stated that Inspector Aven and
Constable Dahlstrom had visited the property last Friday to determine the
progress made by Mr. Witgen. Inspector Aven reported that he had observed that
the unregistered vehicles had been removed and that some items discussed had
been done. He also said it looked like additional lumber and materials had been
brought onto the site. He said there was a lot of lumber to do the work but
that the roof work had not progressed yet.
Supervisor Martin summarized Constable Dahlstrom’s report stating that the
tarps are still on the house, the steep incline to the basement is in the same
condition, and the open hole still exists but now has warning tape on it.
Constable Dahlstrom also recorded that it appears that not much has been done
in the last 30 days. Supervisor Martin noted that Constable Dahlstrom had also
provided digital photos of the site.
Supervisor Martin invited Mr. Witgen or Mrs. White to respond. Mr. Witgen
stated that he had been unable to start the roof during the past 2 weekends
because rain had been predicted. He said that it looks like the weather
predicted for this coming weekend (August 9-10) will be good so he should be
able to slide the 15 roof trusses across and put the wall up. Supervisor Martin
said that the weather had actually been very dry lately. Mr. Witgen said there
has been rain all around Williamston so he didn’t want to take a chance. Clerk
Hiner told Mr. Witgen that this is the driest time of the summer and trying to
avoid rain will only get more difficult as fall comes. Mr. Witgen said he
really feels confident that the Board will “see that corner buttoned up” after
this weekend. The Board asked Mr. Witgen for a specific date to expect
completion. Mr. Witgen responded that it would take him 3 days from the time he
starts the work. Supervisor Martin told Mr. Witgen that everyone else currently
building in the Township is doing so concurrent with the weather. Mr. Witgen
said the only reason he put the tarps up is because of pending rain. He said
once he stands the walls up, the tarps would no longer be needed. He added that
he had been able to get the gable wall up already.
Trustee Zaban asked Mr. Witgen to summarize what he has completed. Mr. Witgen
said he has completed the gable and he has the headers and posts made so once
he has good weather, getting things up should go quickly. Trustee Zaban asked
about the cars on the property. Mr. Witgen said that all the unlicensed
vehicles are gone. Trustee Zaban asked if the materials are gone. Mr. Witgen
said that the old materials are gone but new materials are still there.
Supervisor Martin asked if more material had been brought onto the site since
the last Board meeting. Mr. Witgen responded that he had to bring in some
materials to continue with the work.
upervisor Martin told Mr. Witgen that the Board needs to have a deadline for
this work to be complete. Mr. Witgen responded that the tarp is up protecting
the building from the rain. He said when rain is pending; he has plenty of
other work to do. He repeated that it looks like this weekend is going to be
good so he should be able to make the Board happy. Supervisor Martin clarified
for Mr. Witgen that he is not being required to complete these tasks to make
the Board happy, he is required to do them to comply with the Township’s
ordinance. Mr. Witgen said he thinks Monday, August 11, 2003 should be fine as
a deadline.
Trustee Zaban asked how long this process has been gong on. Supervisor Martin
said the building permit was taken out 5 years ago. Trustee Zaban suggested to
Mr. Witgen that he round up a lot of help and get this project finished this
weekend so he can stop aggravating himself, stop aggravating his neighbors and
stop aggravating the Board.
Trustee Zaban reminded Mr. Witgen that he needs to make considerable movement
on this project in the next 90 days before winter comes. He added that he
doesn’t recall anyone else ever keeping an open permit for 4 years.
He told Mr. Witgen that he was putting the Board in the middle of his conflict
with his neighbors and it is getting very difficult for the Board to continue
defending Mr. Witgen to his neighbors. He added that it would only take one
lawsuit from his neighbors to cost all of us. Clerk Hiner told Mr. Witgen that
his neighbors have actually been very patient with him and now its time for him
to finish the project.
Supervisor Martin summarized that the site will be visited on Monday, August
11, 2003 and that the Board will expect that the roof task will be completed
and the tarps removed. Trustee Wright asked what the penalty will be if the
task is not complete. Supervisor Martin said Mr. Witgen will have 10 days to
respond and the Township will file then a lawsuit. Trustee Zaban told Mr.
Witgen that this is exactly what we all want to avoid. Supervisor Martin said
the tarp needs to come down and stay down; this is the blight that must be

information meeting about the Emerald Ash Borer. She explained that the pest
has been reported at Meridian Mall, South Cedar Kroger and Home Depot and
several other locations. All infestations seem to be the result of newly
planted trees imported from the southern United States. She said that Infected
are being quarantined and chipped to 1” size. Source nurseries have also been
quarantined. Supervisor Martin said that the pest has not been reported in
Williamstown Township at this time but the Township has been asked to provide
education materials to the public. Supervisor Martin said the problem seems to
be very extensive. Treasurer Fink said there are only 3 sites of entry in North
America and Michigan is one of them. Supervisor Martin said they did recommend
that all Planning Commissions refuse ash trees as proposed landscape material
submitted by developers. Planning Commission Chair Dan Kraft said he would make
notify the Commissioners immediately. Supervisor Martin said they are also
asking Townships to go back and look at old plans (for instance Pres Kool) and
notify anyone that used ash trees of this issue Supervisor Martin said the
Township will be doing everything they can to provide the State with any
relevant information.

NEW BUSINESS
Audit Report-Abraham & Gaffney
Supervisor Martin explained that an annual audit of the Township financial
records was conducted in June 2003 by the accounting firm Abraham & Gaffney
(A&G). She introduced Aaron Stevens representing A&G to present their report.
(Mr. Stevens invited the Township to contact Bill Tucker at their office with
any Quickbooks software questions). Mr. Stevens said that the audit went very
well and thanked the Clerk and Treasurer offices for their assistance. He
stated that A&G included one qualified opinion in their report letter because
the Cemetery did not have a budget in place for the first three months of the
2003 calendar year. He added that this qualification was resolved when a
cemetery budget was adopted on April 1, 2003 at the start of this fiscal year.
Everything else was in accordance with generally accepted accounting practices.
He said that pages 2 and 3 of their report present a combined balance sheet for
the Township. He noted that the unreserved, undesignated fund balance as of
March 31, 2003 was $908,237 which represents the funds available for
expenditure and said this represents a sound financial position. He said that
total revenues decreased approximately 9% ($61,000) from the previous year
(taxes were up, building permits, interest rates and state shared revenues were
down). Increases in expenditures this year were due to road work projects. The
Township used $105,000 from reserve but A&G still considers the Township to be
in a sound financial position. The A&G report on internal control structure
includes 2 recommendations. The first was to move illegal investments in the
cemetery fund (which has already been done) and second was to document the
return of donated funds that was made from the cemetery account by Mr. Fate.
Supervisor Martin explained to the audience that the additional cost for road
work was due to the upgrade on Mitchell Road. The road was upgraded so that the
county would take it over as a primary road and Township taxpayers would not be
burdened with upkeep caused by additional traffic expected from the schools on
Mitchell.
Report-Abraham & Gaffney Planning Commission Report
Commission Report Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
Planning Commission (PC) Dan Kraft clarified that the draft PC minutes
distributed in tonight’s Board packet are very rough and include several points
that are either confusing or incorrect (which he will clarify during his
presentation).
Tentative Preliminary Plat Approval-Springbrook Estates
Chairman Kraft reported that the PC passed a motion (by a 6-3 vote) to
recommend approval of the preliminary plat for Springbrook Estates subject to
the applicant meeting all conditions stated in the McKenna letter dated 8/13/03
and two additional conditions: 1) that the applicant eliminate the Zimmer Road
access and replace it with an ingress and egress access to Grand River Road and
2) that all roads meet the 60 ft setback from wetlands requirement except for
the road that crosses the wetlands(this will also require a revision to the
tentative preliminary plat). He added that the McKenna letter also addresses
this issue. Mr. Kraft said this means that if the developer complies with the
recommendations of the PC, they would no longer need a variance. They would
instead need to redraw their plan to comply with the 60’ setback.
Supervisor Martin stated that the Schedule of Regulations for Structures
(footnote D) is where the requirement for “structures” to be setback at least
60’ from wetlands is stated. She asked if the PC was interpreting a road to be
a structure. Mr. Kraft said that they did. He added that the McKenna letter did
state that there was some ambiguity in the ordinance with respect to what fell
into the 60’ setback and what didn’t and recommended a variance for anything
that was going to be closer than 60’ to wetlands.
Supervisor Martin said the motion made by the PC which eliminates the access to
Zimmer Road and adds an access onto Grand River actually violates the access
management portion of the Township Zoning Ordinance because the required site
distance from other driveways is not available. Mr. Kraft said the PC never
actually looked at where the access to Grand River would occur. They assumed
the access would be at the lot owned by the Ingham County Road Commission.
Supervisor Martin confirmed that this was the only land available as an access
point and, since it doesn’t meet criteria, the motion automatically violates
the ordinance.
Mr. Kraft suggested he explain the circumstances of their last PC meeting. He
explained that there was a large public turnout and they were there because
this development is one of the hotspots in the Township. Because this property
is located in the 425 area with access to City water and sewer, high density at
this location is a possibility more than in outlying areas. The public came out
and stated that 1) they wanted the PC to comply with the master plan, 2) they
were concerned about the wetlands and wanted no exceptions on the wetlands
issues 3) they are concerned about the burden to the school system a high
density subdivision would cause, and 4) their primary concern (about 90%) was
due to the existing traffic problems at Zimmer and Grand River. Mr. Kraft
explained that the public felt it was a possibility and perhaps a
responsibility of the Township to influence a change in the current traffic
problem at this intersection before considering any type of development in this
area-especially a high density one. He said that was the tone of the meeting.
Mr. Kraft said the resulting motion was made trying to address the concerns
expressed by the public.
Supervisor Martin clarified that the main issue the public has objection to is
not the subdivision but the traffic problem at the corner of Grand River and
Zimmer. Mr. Kraft concurred and noted that many of the citizens who expressed
concern at the PC meeting were also in attendance tonight.
Supervisor Martin noted that there are also some deed restrictions on the ICRC
lot which state that the property can only be used for residential purposes and
it is not deeded as a public right of way. Mr. Kraft said the PC had been
informed of this information by the applicant along with the fact that it would
create a mismatch with the intersections between the North and South sides of
Grand River.
Supervisor Martin stated that her first reaction is to send this motion back to
the Planning Commission for reconsideration due to the access management issues
and deed restrictions on the Grand River parcel. She added that she’s not sure
that ICRC would eliminate the Zimmer Road access (forcing creation of 2 cul-de-
sacs near Zimmer Road) even if the Grand River access was allowed. Mr. Kraft
said he personally had voted against the motion because the PC was not looking
at a drawing anywhere close to what the motion would create. Mr. Kraft said
that altering the access point is a huge change and a redraw should be
submitted before any decision made. Supervisor Martin said other agencies would
also need to review the redraw. Treasurer Fink also expressed concern that this
motion was not tagged to any drawing.
Mr. Kraft said he had been told that ICRC originally stated they would prefer
an access onto Grand River. Mr. Kraft said he believed this was because they
don’t like cul-de-sacs and want roads to be connected. Supervisor Martin said
she believes that’s because they are difficult to maintain and plow.
Trustee Wright stated that he agrees with Mr. Kraft and doesn’t like approving
something that the Board does not have a drawing of. He stated that he had also
voted against the motion because he didn’t feel it was a good motion or that it
was it well thought out. He added that whether discussion goes back to the PC
or is handled at the Board level more review is required. Supervisor Martin
said there is time for further investigation because the deadline for Board
action isn’t until after the October Board meeting. Trustee Wright said he
would like to listen to comments from the applicant, MDOT, ICRC and the public
before deciding how to proceed.
Supervisor Martin invited the applicant to address the Board. Mr. Ron Clark of
KEBS, Inc. spoke on behalf of applicant Bob Hilty and Springbrook Estates. He
thanked Mr. Kraft for his reflections on the PC meeting. He stated that the
Springbrook Estates plan was developed to meet the Township ordinances for open
space subdivision design for an R-1-S residential district. The plan meets the
letter and intent of the code. The access to Zimmer Road meets ICRC standards
for site distance. ICRC has stated their approval in a letter to the Township.
In that letter they requested the applicant look into an access onto Grand
River to eliminate the proposed cul-de-sac. ICRC suggested they look at using
an ICRC property on Grand River as an access point (which is part of a lot
intended for residential use only). He stated that ICRC has been aware of this
for quite some time and that their council was looking into it but has not
provided feedback to date. Mr. Clark said he has a meeting with ICRC on
September 8th to discuss several issues including Springbrook Estates.
Mr. Clark said the other access point for the subdivision is at the property
line and Belmont Avenue and is designed to ICRC standards. The road swings into
the wetland buffer. He said he believes the interpretation of whether the term
“structure” includes roads should be considered by the ZBA. Mr. Clark said he’s
sure that citizens concerns about traffic on Zimmer Road and this access will
have on that traffic are valid. However, the road is there and the location has
been approved by ICRC for use. He said the Springbrook design complies with the
ordinance. The plan has actually been submitted in 3 different proposals over
the last year and a half and it finally meets approval of the Township planning
consultant. He does not believe that the issue should be sent back to the PC
because he doesn’t believe the PC can ever be satisfied. He stated he feels the
motion was made at the last meeting in a reactionary way to try to appease
everyone in the room-indicated by the fact that they made a motion and approved
a change sight unseen.
Mr. Clark said he believes this plan is the very best that can be done for that
site and that there is enough time to wait for MDOT’s written response to the
issue of an access road on Grand River. He said he would like to see the Board
keep the issue at this level and table the motion until the next meeting. Final
decision does not have to be made until November 5th. Supervisor Martin said
that the planning consultant had set the Township’s 90 day deadline at November
3rd. Mr. Kebs said that he had contacted MDOT to check the status of their
response and they indicated they were waiting for information from the Township
about how the access management plan related to this plan.
Supervisor Martin called for any questions for the applicant. She stated she
agrees with Mr. Clark that the interpretation of “structure” should be
addressed by the ZBA.
Supervisor Martin invited Mr. Dave Sonneberg, representing Ingham County Road
Commission, to provide comment on the project and the issues involved in
putting a light at Zimmer and Grand River. Mr. Sonneberg said he wasn’t
prepared to speak on the subdivision issue but stated ICRC was planning to
pursue an access onto Grand River and their attorneys were addressing the
question. He said the offset with the street on the south side of Grand River
is only slight. He said the Grand River access was not solely a consideration
due to the cul-de-sac but also to distribute the traffic so one homeowner not
bear the burden of the entire subdivision’s traffic. He said ICRC is on record
with MDOT stating that they will accomplish upgrades necessary on the
approaches to the intersection required to install a traffic signal. Supervisor
Martin clarified that ICRC does not plan to eliminate the Zimmer access, even
if the Grand River access is added. Mr. Sonneberg concurred.
Supervisor Martin invited Mr. Steve Shaunessey (representing MDOT) to provide
input. Mr. Shaunessey identified himself as a representative from the Traffic
and Safety Division of MDOT reresenting Ingham County. He said they have been
working with the Township and the City for several years regarding the Zimmer/
Grand River intersection. Signal studies were conducted in 1998 and a meeting
was held at the post office with State Senator Paul DeWeese in July 2001.
Another signal study was done in 2001. MDOT is committed to do another signal
study and speed study after the 2 year construction period ends. The road
project should be completed in November and then they will proceed with the
studies.
Supervisor Martin read from an MDOT document prepared after the 2001 traffic
study that stated “the traffic volumes fall below the requirements needed to
justify the installation of a traffic signal”. She asked which road had low
volume. Mr. Shaunessey said the traffic load on Zimmer Road was below criteria.
He said MDOT follows warrants which are national standards set by the highway
administration. He said that the Grand River volume met criteria but Zimmer did
not. MDOT wants an updated study to evaluate the impact of recent development.
Supervisor Martin asked how MDOT plans to identify the significant avoidance
traffic and asked if the Township could be notified when the traffic study will
occur so people can drive their actual routes instead of avoiding the corner
during that period. Mr. Shaunessey said they don’t want to jeopardize skewing
the results. Supervisor Martin said she wants to be sure that the results are
not skewed the other way because citizens are avoiding the corner. She said she
is only suggesting alerting citizens on Zimmer Road to drive their normal
routes. She is not suggesting she tell them to drive back and forth ten times.
Mr. Shaunessey said he would take her question back to MDOT. Supervisor Martin
said she wanted the public to be aware that the Township has pursued a light at
this intersection many times and the reason it hasn’t happened is because we
aren’t meeting the traffic volume warrants on Zimmer Road.
Brian Jennings, Township traffic committee representative, stated that he would
highly recommend that the Township not publicize the date of the study or give
prior notice of the traffic study because it could skew the results and
potentially set the Township up for a lawsuit. Mr. Jennings said MDOT typically
notifies the Township a month in advance. He added the public should be aware
that, even if the study is done as early as January, results aren’t typically
available for 6 months. Mr. Shaunessey said he thinks MDOT can do better than
that due to the nature of this issue.
Supervisor Martin invited comments from the public. Rick Ash (1365 Bridlewood
Ln.), Pat Apostol (4020 Zimmer Rd.), Jane Pease (3795 Zimmer Rd.), Steve Terry
(4015 Zimmer Rd.), Audrey Goodman (4145 Zimmer Rd.), Floyd Goodman (4145 Zimmer
Rd.), Richard Heiser (1300 Trotter’s Lane), and Nancy McGarey (3875 Zimmer Rd.)
individually stated that Zimmer Road was not constructed with the intent for it
to be used as a primary route or to handle the traffic load that currently
exists or that new development will create. They stated that, although the
Township does not have the authority to upgrade Zimmer Road and the
intersection, it has the responsibility to pressure those who do (ICRC and
MDOT) and to halt further development until the infrastructure is in place to
safely handle the additional traffic burden. They also asked that, when the
traffic study is conducted, MDOT place their cables in a manner to collect
information for all traffic at the intersection, including the avoidance
traffic at the post office, Spagnoulo’s, Independent Bank and the party store.
They also request that MDOT collect data while school is in session and not
during a holiday when people are out of town. Several citizens also thanked Mr.
Kraft for accurately representing their position to the Board during his
presentation.
Supervisor Martin stated that she will contact the Township attorney to verify
if the Township can legally prevent a subdivision from proceeding on the
grounds that proper infrastructure is not in place. She said she believes there
have been several recent cases where this position was disallowed by the court.
She also asked Mr. Shaunessey to maintain communication with the Township
during the traffic study process so that these citizen concerns can be
considered.
Supervisor Martin thanked Mr. Kraft, Mr. Sonneberg, Mr. Shaunessy and the
public for their comments and called for a motion. Trustee Wright made a motion
to table the Board’s decision on Springbrook Subdivision pending further
investigation and to keep the issue at Board level. Motion supported by Trustee
Zaban. Motion passed unanimously.

Treasurer-Principal & Interest amounts for Cemetery investment funds
Treasurer Fink presented a report of the status of the cemetery investment
funds (which she also plans to present to the Cemetery Board at their September
3rd meeting). She explained that MTA had provided her guidance on how to handle
past funds that had been donated to the Cemetery Board for purposes of
perpetual care. If funds were donated with specific use requirements provided
by the donor in writing, that money must be invested on the donor’s behalf. The
interest generated from the investment can be used for the specific purposes
itemized by the donor. The principal must remain intact and cannot be accessed
to use for any other purpose at the cemetery.  
Treasurer Fink explained further that if the donors did not specify a use (in
writing) at the time of donation, the Township is free to invest the money and
access both the principal and the interest for general cemetery use. She stated
that everyone agrees it would, under no circumstances, ever be commingled into
the Township’s general fund.
Treasurer Fink stated that, to her knowledge, no past donors provided the
cemetery board with instructions in writing about how their donation should be
used. Therefore, both the principal and interest from these funds can be used
for general cemetery purposes. She said she plans to confirm the fact that no
written instructions exist with the long term members of the Cemetery Board on
September 3rd. She also plans to provide the Cemetery Board with
recommendations for a policy on how any new money accepted for perpetual will
be handled.

for review by Williamstown Township and said that Chief Kirt Hunt had announced
his plans to retire. NIESA has posted the position for a new Chief on the
websites firehouse.com and firecarriers.com and in the LSJ. They have received
resumes from several highly qualified applicants responding from across the
country. He added that the plan is for the new organizational structure to have
one person at the top rather than a position shared by two chiefs with the same
level of authority.

Legislative Conference
Supervisor Martin summarized information presented at a legislative conference
she recently attended concerning the topics revenue sharing (state budget
implications), Michigan Land Use, Elections (Help America Vote Act) and
Environment (water and waste). She said that the legislators present encouraged
local officials to meet with them once or twice a year to keep them fully aware
of the problems being faced by local governments.
Security Emergency Management
Supervisor Martin presented information she learned at an all day seminar at
Ingham County on Emergency Management and Damage Assessment. Key points she
learned are that Ingham County is the first level of emergency management for
Williamstown Township for the first 72 hours. After that state and federal
government steps in. They also presented information on how to assess local
damage in the event of a disaster and explained the four phases of emergency
management (mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery). She said that the
Township needs to develop a site emergency plans for possible emergencies-
specifically Tornadoes and Blackouts. She added that the need for a security
system in the Township building was also supported at this seminar.
Supervisor Martin asked members of the Board and the audience if there was
anything else that anyone would like have addressed. No additional comments
were offered.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDA ITEMS
Citizen Katie Lo asked if any decisions had been made about how perpetual care
was going to be handled in the future. Treasurer Fink said that the Cemetery
Board has been charged with the task of making a recommendation on this issue
to the Board and added that the Township will always be responsible for
providing a basic level of perpetual care at the cemeteries. If the Cemetery
Board chooses to continue to offer a second level of perpetual care as a
service, the money will need to be put in trust and the interest generated
accessed for its specified use. Mrs. Lo said that it seems like an excessive
burden for the Township to continue providing additional perpetual care
services. Mrs. Lo also asked how Township checks are generated. Treasurer Fink
explained that the Clerk’s office issues warrants (requests for payment); the
Board of Trustees reviews the warrants and approves them as appropriate (at the
monthly Board meeting); and then the Treasurer’s office issues the final check.
Both Clerk and Treasurer (or their appointed deputies) must sign the check
before it is valid to ensure an internal check and balance. Supervisor Martin
explained that the Board goes through each item to be paid at the meeting as
was done tonight. The Board approval then provides an additional level
oversight.

City of Williamston-Future sewer expansion
Supervisor Martin explained that the City of Williamston is drawing up a 30-
year plan for wastewater treatment. She said the City manager had approached
the Township to see if the Township wanted to be included in these long-term
plans and in what way (i.e. do we want the plan to just include the 425
district or do we want sewer to move further into the Township by increasing
the 100 taps we have under the 425 agreement (of which 7 remain available)).
Trustee Wright said the Planning Commission unanimously did not want to see
increase in sewer capacity in the Township except in the 425 area where
providing sewer is already required. Trustee Zaban reminded the Board that the
State Boundary Commission was very happy to give the City everything they
wanted when the 425 area was being identified. Trustee Zaban explained to the
audience that the Township still has zoning control on the 425 area and the
City doesn’t get control of the land for 50 years. Supervisor Martin added that
if a parcel is in the 425 area but the owner doesn’t ask for sewer and water,
the parcel will remain in the Township after the 50 years ends. For example, at
the end of 50 years Springbrook will move into the City. Supervisor Martin said
the idea behind the 425 agreement was to avoid creating fingers into the
Township, which could eventually be annexed into the City. Supervisor Martin
added that the Boundary Commission tends to favor cities on this issue because
they believe that cities need to grow. She said the 425 agreement was good for
the Township because it will limit density in this area to Township
requirements. Treasurer Fink asked if a map of the 425 area could be available
at future meetings for clarification. Supervisor Martin said that every parcel
adjacent to the City is now in the 425 agreement so the Township is protected
from annexation for 50 years. She added that, at the end of the 50 years, the
agreements are renewable. Citizen Katie Lo clarified that the City collects 16
mills and then directs 2 mills to the Township and asked if the Township was
concerned about collecting this money. Treasurer Fink said there is no real
concern because the money is collected each year so it is there for the City to
transfer.
Treasurer Fink made a motion that the Township pass a resolution to recommend
to the City of Williamston that when developing their 30-year plan, they
consider the future sewer needs of the 425 area only and that the Township is
not interested in any additional sewer capacity outside of this area. Motion
supported by Supervisor Martin.
Discussion

facility. Treasurer Fink agreed. Supervisor Martin asked if there was any one

one in the audience agreed.

Building permit fees
Supervisor Martin explained that a couple of months ago the Board had adjusted
the building permit fee policy because there was inconsistency in how different
parties were calculating their fees. The change was made to base all
calculations on square footage. Supervisor Martin explained that, after working
with the new policy, Inspector Aven had requested that the permit fee rate
schedule be increased to $88 per square foot. These changes are based on
recommendations in the building standards magazine “International Conference of
Building Officials.” She said she doesn’t know what other area Townships are
charging except for Meridian Township because Inspector Aven had provided their
fee schedule for comparison. Trustee Wright said he thinks it is important for
the calculations to be done by square foot. He said he thinks that $55 $50 to
$88 is a big jump. Clerk Hiner confirmed with Inspector Aven that using the $55
$50/sq foot approach results in a big drop in fees from the previous fee
schedule. Inspector Aven said that it does. Trustee Wright said he thinks the
square footage cost needs to be increased but is not sure if it needs to be
increased that much. He would like to see additional information from
comparable municipalities. He said it is appropriate for the Township to be
consistent with Meridian Township and the City of Williamston rather than with
smaller areas like Locke Township. Supervisor Martin said she agrees that the
rate needs to be consistent and fair. Inspector Aven suggested rounding the fee
to $80 to make calculations easier. Supervisor Martin recommended that she and
Inspector Aven work together to collect additional information to present at
the next Township Board meeting.
UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Springbrook Estates 
Supervisor Martin explained that the plat where Springbrook Estates is proposed
is located in the 425 area. The developer is required to have sewer and water
from the City in order to develop this location. Supervisor Martin said the
Board had been provided with information from MDOT regarding a possible
entrance on Grand River but that they have not provided the Township with a
formal letter of their recommendation. She said this is because they haven’t
received a request to review the issue from Ingham County Road Commission. The
Road Commission is still deciding whether this entrance should be considered.
She added that MDEQ still has not sent formal information regarding the
wetlands issue and that the City also needs to respond regarding City water and
sewer hookup locations with respect to any roadway to access Grand River.
Supervisor Martin said the developer has met the Township requirements
regarding lot criteria, setbacks, and amount of open space. She said this is a
very tentative plat and that one of her biggest issues is the 60’ setback
requirement from wetlands. She said she would require the developer to seek
interpretation from the ZBA about whether a road is considered a structure.
Trustee Zaban asked if the City has enough sewer allocation available.
Supervisor Martin said they do but there will be nothing put in writing
officially by the City until the tentative preliminary plat is approved by the
Township. At that point the developer can submit a request to the City. Trustee
Zaban confirmed that in order for the State or the County to review anything,
there has to be a TENTATIVE preliminary plat approval by the Township.
Supervisor Martin confirmed that this is true. Trustee Wright asked if there is
anything in this tentative preliminary plat that does not meet the Township’s
ordinance. Supervisor Martin repeated that the 60-foot setback issue still
needs to be reviewed by the ZBA. Trustee Wright added that the MDEQ response
would also need to be received to make sure those conditions have been met.
Supervisor Martin said that if there are any significant changes to the plan
during the approval process, the Township can say at any point that the change
warrants that the plan go back to the Planning Commission and start the process
over.
Trustee Wright clarified that at this point the developer has met everything
that the Township requires except for that setback issue. He asked if the Board
should consider a tentative approval now in order to get feedback from the
other agencies that are going to be part of the review process. Trustee Wright
said he believes that if the developer meets the requirements of the ordinance,
he doesn’t believe the Board can hold the process up.
Treasurer Fink said that even though a developer’s calculations may meet the
letter of the calculation for density, the ordinance does not require that the
Board allow the absolute highest possible density on every parcel-especially
when there are extenuating circumstances as exists at the Zimmer Road/Grand
River intersection. She said she does not personally favor that high of a
density on that piece of property without a safer infrastructure in place. She
said she is not willing to approve that density at that location just because
the Board is against the wall. Clerk Hiner said she is not confident that other
groups reviewing this tentative plat will interpret the situation at that
intersection properly. Treasurer Fink said that the letter provided by McKenna
predicts a 13% increase in traffic on Zimmer Road and that this will still not
be enough of an increase to warrant a signal at the intersection. Trustee
Wright said he’s confident that a new traffic study will support a signal if it
is done properly. Trustee Wright said he also believes there needs to be
improvements at this location but the Township will need to defend a decision
based on that criteria legally. Treasurer Fink said there is a provision in the
ordinance that states the Board does not have to approve a plan, even if it
meets the letter of the ordinance, if they feel there is a safety concern that
is a detriment to the citizens of the Township. Clerk Hiner said she agrees
with Treasurer Fink that the plan is too dense. Treasurer Fink said she sees
this density as detrimental to the Township. She added that perhaps this is a
weak area in the Township’s ordinance.
Mrs. Lo asked what density is proposed. Supervisor Martin said the site is 46.4
acres and there are 40 houses proposed. Dave Byers (1325 E. Grand River) stated
that he had not been notified of the increased density and was not aware of it
until the sign went up on the possible roadway site. Supervisor Martin said the
notification list would be checked. Mr. Byers clarified that, if the tentative
plat were approved tonight, there would be a road onto Grand River, into
Victory Meadows and onto Zimmer Road because the last map he saw showed 2
accesses on Zimmer Road. Trustee Wright said that, based on discussion at the
Planning Commission, it is probably unlikely that an access onto Grand River
will be added.
Mr. Byers said he is concerned with the wisdom of putting an access onto Grand
River with current traffic conditions. He also questioned the formula for
density on this parcel. Treasurer Fink explained this plat is being developed
under the R.O.S.E. Plan which requires that 50% of the parcel be designated as
open space IN ORDER TO DEVELOP AT THIS DENSITY. Supervisor Martin said the
calculation for an R-1-S parcel allows for one house every 40,000 sq. ft. (an
acre is 43,560 sq. ft.).
Mr. Byers said the original plan he had seen called for 24 to 26 homes. He said
he had asked Mr. Hilty about buying this property years ago. At that time Mr.
Hilty was working on having the City annex the property so it could be
developed with an even higher density. Mr. Byers said they had fought that
strongly at the time and it looks to him like Mr. Hilty has done an "end run"
around the density question. Supervisor Martin said if it had been annexed into
the City, Mr. Hilty could have put closer to 80 homes on the property so the
425 agreement did limit density to a point. Supervisor Martin said that the way
the R-1 or R-1-S area density is calculated (using the Rose formula) is 1 unit
for every 0.92 acres. She said the proposed open space on this is parcel is
23.63 acres. Mr. Clark of Kebs Engineering said that with a 46-acre site, the
Rose calculation requires preserving 50% of the site as open space. Lots,
roadways, wetlands, and storm water detention areas are all taken from the 23
acres not designated as open space. He added that the open space is dispersed
entirely across the site on the proposed plat.
Steve Terry (4015 Zimmer Road) asked that, in the future, the Township require
the developer to provide handheld size copies of the plan for the audience to
review to improve the conduct of the meeting. Tom Grover (4090 Zimmer Road)
said he has attended several of the meetings regarding this topic and it is
apparent that a couple of the Board members and most of the audience are
concerned about safety on Zimmer Road. He said he had borrowed a radar gun from
his worksite at MSU and proved that much of the traffic on Zimmer was traveling
70 mph. He asked how we could let this plan move ahead with an access onto
Zimmer Road with the traffic conditions that exist. Trustee Wright said that,
unfortunately, people drive 70 mph everywhere in the Township. Trustee Wright
said he doesn’t think that anyone on the Board is heavily in favor of this
development. He said he’s only in favor of considering approval of the
TENTATIVE PRELIMINARY plat tonight so that some of the other agencies can start
providing input.  
Mr. Terry said if this tentative plat is sent on to the County, the Township
will get no reaction from MDOT. Supervisor Martin agreed. Mr. Terry said the
plat will get the same response from ICRC because they aren’t concerned about
the safety. He suggested the Township approve the tentative plat with a
condition that the developer provides an access onto Grand River so that it
will at least force MDOT and ICRC to have to consider the safety issue and
provide input. Supervisor Martin said she couldn’t recommend adding an access
onto Grand River because she doesn’t believe it would be safe to have one
there.
 
Floyd Goodman said that if the Board’s opinion is that the tentative plat is
not appropriate for approval, the Board should just not approve it. Mr. Goodman
said that it is his understanding that if the citizens of the Township request
it, the site plan can be revisited. He added that he feels there should be a
moratorium on all development until the whole process is revisited. That way
the citizens could request that there be no lots of less than 2 acres-
irregardless of green space. He said that if Township residents really want to
have a rural community, than the Planning Commission should take those things
into consideration so that we can have a safe rural community.
 
Supervisor Martin said she agrees that we want a safe rural community. She said
that the 425 agreement was made to help the Township secure its boundary. She
said it sounds like Mr. Goodman is saying the citizens now feel the allowed
zoning density is too high. She said the only way to change the density is to
change the zoning. Trustee Wright said that couldn’t be done while a tentative
plat is on the table. Mr. Byer asked if this parcel has always been R-1S.
Supervisor Martin said it has been R1-S as long as she can remember. She said
that any property adjacent to the City has the densest zoning and then the
density decreases as you move out into the rural areas. Supervisor Martin said
that if the citizens say they don’t want rezoning, then the master plan will
not be changed. Supervisor Martin said the Township has denied all rezoning
requests with the exception of 2 parcels of 10 acres that someone wanted to
take off their family farm.
 
Mr. Terry said that a street is already in place on Grand River near the
proposed location. He said that if safety is a concern, he has to respectfully
disagree with Supervisor Martin’s objection to a Grand River access for safety
reasons because safety is already an issue.
 
Mr. Timmerman (3848 Zimmer Rd) said he lives at the point where the road will
access Zimmer Road. He said he would like to see a cul-de-sac put in and an
access onto Grand River added. He said if you open those roads up, the
subdivision will be used as a cut-through by post office traffic. Supervisor
Martin said she understands his concerns and agrees that a cut-through will be
formed. Mr. Timmerman added that with that high of a density, there would be 80
more cars added to the traffic load. Clerk Hiner said the memo from McKenna
implies there would be little impact by a Zimmer ingress/egress and she doesn’t
agree. She thinks that traffic coming east out of the City will be
traveling at a lower speed and that traffic turning into the subdivision will
be moving even slower. However there is no reason for traffic to slow down on
Zimmer at the location of the road easement so cars will be traveling by that
access point at a high speed.
Inspector Aven asked if it would be possible for the Board to approve the
tentative plat with a requirement that the County lower the speed limit.
Supervisor Martin said the County isn’t responsible for lowering the speed
limit. Supervisor Martin said there could only be requirements placed that the
developer can accomplish and he can’t accomplish a lower speed or a signal at
the intersection.
Supervisor Martin said she sees two options for proceeding. The first option is
that the Board can go forward with approval of this TENTATIVE preliminary plat
and see what the other agencies have to say (she said she has a list of 7
conditions she would put on her approval). She said she realizes some Board
members have a safety issue but court cases do not uphold denials based on this
issue and she doesn’t want to put the Township into a legal situation where
there is a definite possibility of losing. She second option is to send the
tentative plat back to the developer and tell them we want to see them cut out
some lots. The developer can agree or disagree. Treasurer Fink said the Board
would need to send any revised tentative plat back through the Planning
Commission. Supervisor Martin said the tentative plat would eventually have to
go before the other agencies.
Supervisor Martin said that what is really stopping her from making a decision
is the wetlands question that needs to go before the ZBA. She said that another
option could be that the Board requires the 60’ setback question go before the
ZBA before any decision is made because significant changes to the plat may be
required based on their decision. Trustee Wright asked how this option would
affect the time constraints. Supervisor Martin said that the Board response
could be that the tentative plat goes back to the ZBA. She said the developer
can say yes and take it before the ZBA or decline review by the ZBA and proceed
from there. Supervisor Martin said if the ZBA decides a 60’ setback is
required, the developer would have to justify a variance by showing a hardship.
She said she doesn’t believe the ZBA has ever looked at this setback question.
She added that she doesn’t believe the Township can call a moratorium on
reviewing all plats. The Township can re-look at zoning as a whole but this
request is already on the table.
Tom Grover said he was familiar with a similar situation in Howell where the
developer was required to put screening in to limit the noise and views for the
houses surrounding the new roadway. Treasurer Fink said this has been required
on other projects within the Township also.
Mr. Clark stated that one option not discussed completely would be granting
this TENTATIVE PRELIMINARY plat (along with sending it to ZBA for
interpretation) in order to receive input from the other agencies. Supervisor
Martin said the ZBA decision may change the plat significantly and she’s
concerned that, if the Board approves this plat, ICRC gets the message that the
Township likes this development. Treasurer Fink said that a tentative
endorsement will give the other agencies a perceived endorsement by the
Township. The agencies may just say “if the Township thinks it looks fine, than
so do we” and approve it without comment.
 
Trustee Zaban said he wants to see the setback question go before the ZBA
because this issue may change the whole plat. He said he had originally
considered approving the TENTATIVE preliminary plat so the Township could get
feedback from the other agencies but has now changed his mind. Supervisor
Martin said the Board could also ask Mr. Clark to go back to the developer and
voluntarily suggest they voluntarily reduce the proposed number of lots.
However, even if the lot number was reduced, it will not make any difference on
whether a road goes in by Mr.Timmerman’s house and possibly by Mr. Byers’.
Supervisor Martin said she doesn’t believe the Board can deny a subdivision
altogether. Mr. Timmerman said he’s not saying people should not be allowed the
opportunity to live there but they should be allowed to have space to move. He
said the reason he is here tonight is because he doesn’t want to see a road
exit onto Zimmer Road. Mr. Timmerman added that if roads beside his house and
on Grand River are going to be opened, why can’t the developer open the second
roadway on Zimmer and make one a one-way entrance and the other a one-way exit
to eliminate traffic cutting through the subdivision. Mr. Clark said that would
be as ineffective as the one-way setup that currently exists at the post
office.
Trustee Zaban made a motion not to approve the tentative plat this evening and
to recommend the applicant go before the ZBA for interpretation of the 60’
setback requirement and whether a road meets the requirement of a structure.
Motion supported by Clerk Hiner. Motion passed unanimously.

Board Policies
The Board discussed the content and wording of several policies developed at
the last workshop. Treasurer Fink recommended that each policy under
consideration be reviewed tonight, edited, and then final consideration of them
all be made at one time at the next Board meeting.
Mail Distribution
The Draft Mail Distribution Policy states:
1.   A log of mail will be kept. Clerk will provide the log to Board members on
a monthly basis to coincide with Board meetings. All Board members can review
the log at any time to ascertain that they are comfortable with the information
that is being forwarded to them.
Discussion: Clerk Hiner said she will begin recording mail received in a
handwritten notebook kept at a central location. She said she also plans to
give a copy of the log to the Board monthly to coincide with Board meetings.
2.   The Clerk will forward for review copies of bills that require review to
the most appropriate person. Bills will be made available for review the Monday
preceding Board meetings.
Discussion: Supervisor Martin asked that this item also be included under the
bill payment policy. Clerk Hiner clarified that she will provide a payable list
to the Treasurer on Friday for her checks and balance review so that the final
payable report is available for Board members on Monday.
3.   Mail that is specifically directed to one person will be disseminated as
such. Copies will be made as directed by notations.
Discussion: Trustee Zaban asked whether it had been verified whether mail that
is addressed to a specific person can be opened by another individual. Clerk
Hiner said that her research had verified that it was appropriate for the Clerk
to open and distribute specifically addressed mail. She read from the court
case McKim vs. Green Oak (document provided by Catherine Mulhupt at MTA to
clarify this issue) that states that, “According to the U. S. Postal Service,
mail forwarded to a government agency is not personal mail and may be opened as
directed by the …approval official.” The approval official, according to the
McKim rule, is the Clerk. Clerk Hiner added that historically, all mail has
been opened prior to distribution at the Township office.
Treasurer Fink asked that a file be kept in a central location for all mail for
which the Clerk doesn’t know where or who to distribute it to.
4.   The Clerk’s office will keep originals for Township files as required by
law, where appropriate, i.e. Contracts, Attorney correspondence, etc…
Discussion: Treasurer Fink said the Clerk needs to file information in a
central location that everyone can access.
5.   Mail will be processed promptly and whenever possible disseminated within
1 hour of receiving it in the office.
Zoning information
The Draft Zoning Information Policy states:
Disseminating Ordinance Information-All ordinance information requests beyond
copying are to be directed to the Supervisor or our Planning Consultant. If the
request is for copies of parts of an ordinance for information all staff may
give it out.
Discussion: Supervisor Martin pointed out a copy of the proposed Information
Request Form. There was discussion that the form be completed by the customer
for all requests for information made at the counter (not just ordinance
related requests). The request form can be put on the appropriate person’s desk
for response. No changes to the Draft Zoning Information Policy were
recommended. Supervisor Martin stated she would prefer that all phone messages
go into her voice mail and instead of being recorded on a phone message record.

Bill Review Procedure
The Draft Bill Review Procedure Policy states that:
“The Township policy that all bills (with the exception of payroll, taxes,
utilities, those bills which would incur a penalty and those deemed necessary
to the welfare of the Township approved by the Supervisor or other Board member
in the absence of the Supervisor), must be approved at the Township Board
meeting. In addition to those exceptions, invoices from consultants and bills
for supplies whose inventory must be verified will be distributed to the Board
member or office staff most able to verify the statement. The clerk, being the
receiver of mail will direct these invoices to the appropriate individual,
before preparing the warrant for final Board approval. Bills will be available
for review the Monday before Board meetings.”
Discussion
Supervisor Martin requested the new policy be rewritten using the number format
used in the previous bill review policy. Supervisor Martin recommended adding
the statement, “ The Treasurer will review invoices scheduled for payment on
Friday before the Board meeting and the Clerk will generate the Unpaid Bills
Detail Report to be available for review the following Monday.”
Board Agenda Policy
The Draft Board Agenda Policy states that:
“The Supervisor will have the agenda prepared by the Tuesday prior to the
regularly scheduled board meetings. Any agenda items for the board meeting
should be in for inclusion by 4 p.m. on said Tuesday.”
Discussion: Supervisor Martin stated that, in order for her to finalize the
agenda by 4 p.m., she needs any Board input by 10 a.m. Tuesday morning.
Board Packets
The Draft Board Packets Policy states that:
“Board packets will be mailed the Friday prior to the regularly scheduled Board
Meetings. Board Packets may not include reports like Treasurer’s Reports and
Unpaid Bills Detail, Payroll Item Detail, which are date sensitive.”
Discussion: Trustees Wright and Zaban stated that it is not necessary to mail
their packets. They will take responsibility for collecting them at the
Township office. Supervisor Martin stated that Mr. Kraft’s packet should still
be mailed. There was discussion that the Supervisor and Deputy Clerk review the
agenda for Board packets on Wednesday prior to the Board meeting and that any
Board packet information unavailable for distribution on Friday (primarily time
sensitive Treasurer and financial reports) be distributed to Board members’
mailboxes as soon as it becomes available.
Annual insurance audit

the Township changes the agreement duration to five (5) years, the contract
could be used as leverage when NIESA is considering where new services are
going to be located. Clerk Hiner pointed out that even if the Township
terminates its contract agreement with NIESA after five (5) years, the millage
will still be applied to Township citizens for the duration of the fifteen (15)
year millage period. Clerk Hiner stated that she will confirm that the
Township’s Hazmat agreement is current.
Supervisor Martin stated that she will revise the proposed agreement to state
five (5) years instead of fifteen (15) years and provide a copy for Trustee
Zaban to submit at the next NIESA Board meeting once a motion has been
approved.

Katie Lo (290 E. Sherwood) stated that she had three (3) points she would like
to comment on: 1) with regards to the Springbrook development, it seems to her
that there should only be 20 lots allowed if only 50% is useable instead of 40
lots allowed just because the property is 40 acres; 2) with regards to the
snowplow discussed at the last meeting, she asked if it wouldn’t be better to
retain a private contractor for snowplowing instead of the Township purchasing
a truck and then dealing with breakdowns and repairs; and 3) with regards to
the letter she received from the Township stating that tax payments received
after 2/17/03 with an earlier postmark would be considered late. She asked why
that statement was included and added that she felt it seemed confrontational.
Treasurer Fink responded that there have been historical problems with
postmarks because postmark machines can be altered. She said that County
Treasury had recommended that the Township consider date received only and not
consider postmarks at all. This is also their policy.
Supervisor Martin explained that the Township now has a full-time maintenance
man. With the Township Hall, both cemeteries and the park requiring
maintenance, it was more cost effective for the Township to purchase a vehicle
that could be used for both snowplowing and moving mowing equipment from one
location to the next. The truck is currently parked at the Township Hall. She
added that it was used today to remove an abandoned couch that had been dumped
at the park. Trustee Zaban commented that the snowplowing contractor cost about
$4,000 per year and the truck was $10,800 so, after 3 years, the Township
should be financially better off by making this purchase. Trustee Zaban
explained that the truck was purchased used but it has never plowed and the
plow is nearly new so it was a good buy.
Supervisor Martin explained that, under the Rural Open Space Environment
(R.O.S.E) Plan there is a calculation that allows the developer to get one unit
per every 0.92 acres in an R-1S zone. Wetlands can account for 25% of the 50%
open space requirement. The R.O.S.E. Plan allows for 50% open space and 50%
used space (which includes roads and lots). It trades the set aside for open
space with the allowance for clustering on smaller lots in one area or pockets
of areas. Treasurer Fink clarified that, in the case of Springbrook, the
developer has been allowed 39 lots because that property is in the 425 area so
it has sewer. That many lots wouldn’t have been allowed if septic was being
used. Trustee Zaban stated that the Planning Commission has not approved this
plan yet and has asked the developer to reduce the number of lots. Supervisor
Martin added Steeplechase and Williamston Estates were also designed under the
R.O.S.E. Plan. She said that the State requires that every township have a
clustering option available and the R.O.S.E. Plan is the cluster option this
Township has adopted.
NEW BUSINESS
John Kane-Hotel Tax
Mr. Kane explained that a 1975 law requires that a 5% hotel tax be collected on
all rooms in the county each time they are rented. The law reads that the money
can be used for four items: 1) to finance convention facilities; 2&3) to pay
current or future rent for convention facilities; and 3) to promote and
encourage tourists and convention business in Ingham County. Randy Schaffer,
Board of Commissioners, has told Mr. Kane that the first 20% of all money
collected goes to promoting the Ingham County Fair Board. He said the other 80%
is currently going to the Lansing Convention Bureau and this is where he has a
problem. He would like to see the money contributed by Williamston business
returned to the Williamston community. The money could then be used for
promotion of the Light Parade, the Jubilee Festival or something new like
having Civil War re-enactors come to the park, promoting Williamston’s
whitewater rapids or advertising Williamston in antique magazines. He explained
that he collects $3-4,000 per year on his eight (8) rooms alone and Williamston
Inn will probably collect the same. This is not a significant amount for the
Lansing Convention Bureau to lose but it would have a huge impact on our local
community. Mr. Kane requested the Board pass a resolution to request that this
room tax money come back to the Williamston community. He proposed that
representatives from the Township and the City of Williamston form a board to
decide how the money is spent. Treasurer Fink asked if a law must be passed
before money could be redirected and Mr. Kane said it would not. He provided a
document to Clerk Hiner explaining the tax collection/disbursement process. The
County Treasurer currently collects the tax money and the Board of
Commissioners decides where it goes. He’s sure Randy Schaffer would love to see
this money funneled back to the outer communities. Mr. Schaffer has explained
that the Convention Bureau gets the entire 80% because nobody else has really
pushed for it. Mr. Kane stated that Lisa Hitchcock (Williamston City Manager)
saw the benefits of this proposal immediately and is very supportive.
Supervisor Martin said that the Township is supportive of Mr. Kane’s proposal.
Trustee Zaban stated that he would be willing to attend a meeting with Mr.
Kane, Randy Schaffer and the County Board of Commissioners. Treasurer Fink
recommended asking the County Commissioners to return 100% of the tax locally
as a negotiation starting point instead of 50%.
Treasurer Fink made a motion to support the concept of re-directing the hotel
tax collected from Williamston WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP businesses by the County
Treasurer back to the Williamston WILLIMASTOWN TOWNSHIP community for tourist
promotion and to support John Kane’s efforts to make this happen. Motion
supported by Trustee Zaban. Motion passed unanimously.
The Board recommended adopting a formal resolution once they have reviewed Mr.
Kane’s information and spoken with Randy Schaffer at the County Board of
Commissioners.
