NEW BUSINESS
Planning Commission Report
Meeting Minutes
Supervisor Martin recommended that because the proposed Mixed-Use Overlay
District contains so many significant changes to the ordinance, it would be
appropriate to notify all property owners in the district area of the proposed
changes before making a final recommendation to the Board. Chairman Kraft
agreed and suggested notification be taken one step further by publishing the
complete wording for the proposed Mixed-Use Overlay District in the Enterprise
before it is presented at a public meeting. Treasurer Fink asked Mr. Kraft for
clarification of the term “R&D” and the phrase “excepting boarding facilities”
with regards to veterinarian offices boarding animals in their care. Mr. Kraft
explained that R&D refers to research and development facilities and suggested
the term “boarding” be clarified further in the text to address boarding by
veterinarians.
Maire Rezoning Request (1345 Sherwood Road) from Ag-SF to RR Chairman Kraft
explained that the Planning Commission had deliberated towards their decision
on this request by considering each of the ten (10) criteria for rezoning
specified in Section 27.06.C.4 of the Williamstown Township Zoning Ordinance.
He pointed out a clarification to the October 21, 2003 Planning Commission
minutes provided by Chris Doozan of McKenna Associates in a letter dated
December 2, 2003 which confirms that if this rezoning is approved, it will be
possible to divide the property into four (4) lots. Mr. Kraft reported that the
Planning Commission had determined that the Maire rezoning request was not in
the interest of the health, safety and welfare of the Township’s residents and
it was their recommendation to the Township Board to not grant this request.
Trustee Zaban asked Mr. Kraft how many parcels the property could have been
divided into if the applicant had requested rezoning one step down to RE. Mr.
Kraft stated that it would have allowed the property to be divided into two (2)
lots. He added that the property is also within 1/20th of an acre (200 square
feet) of eligibility to split in its current Ag-Sf zone under the open space
criteria (a variance would still be required). This gives the applicant two (2)
options in place of rezoning to RR. The calculation for splitting under the
open space criteria requires that the size of the property be at least 5.25
acres multiplied by the number of lots it will be split into (in this case 2).
This parcel would need to be 10.5 acres to divide under the open space criteria
which it nearly meets because it is 10.46 acres. The applicant would be
required to get a variance for the remaining 1/20th of an acre. Mr. Kraft
reviewed that a public hearing on this rezoning request had been held in
October, it had been deliberated in November, and was planned for
recommendation of denial at the December Board meeting but delayed until the
Board’s January meeting at the request of the applicant.
Supervisor Martin reviewed the Planning Commission’s findings that: the request
is not consistent with the Master Plan; uses are available to the applicant in
the property’s current zone; adequate RR properties are already available in
the Township; and no errors have been made in the past that would justify
granting this request. Mr. Kraft stated there was a great deal of concern by
the Commissioners that granting this Ag-SF rezoning request could potentially
change the character of the Township because it sets a bad precedent for any
parcel north of Sherwood to jump two (2) zones. Trustee Zaban asked why the
applicant hadn’t requested a one step rezoning to RE. Mr. Kraft said the
developer was asked that question but did not explain. He added that the only
way the applicant can divide into more than two (2) lots under RR is by tearing
down the historical home on the property which would be unfortunate. Supervisor
Martin reviewed the documents pertaining to this request that had been received
by the Board in their packets: original application (8/26/03); McKenna review
letter (10/13/03); rebuttal letter from Mr. Maire (10/16/03); support petition
for Mr. Maire’s request (submitted by applicant 10/21/03; letters of concern
from citizens presented at Planning Commission 10/21/03 meeting from Donald &
Francis Schmidt, Constance Kowalk, William Young, Mary Miller, the estate of
Charles Tadgerson, and Floyd and Audrey Goodman.
Carl McIntosh (1145 Wild Cherry) addressed the Board on behalf of the
applicant. Mr. McIntosh explained that Mr. Maire could not attend tonight
because he is wintering in Savannah, GA but had relayed his comments to him and
they both believe that this petition has merit and is provided for in Section
27.06 of the Zoning Ordinance. He said the Master Plan is not mentioned
anywhere in 27.06 but was referred to frequently by the Planning Commission
during their discussion of the criteria. Mr. McIntosh’s main argument points
were that it is not financially feasible for a 10 acre parcel to be used for
agricultural purposes and pointed out that no 10 acre parcels in this area of
the Township are being used this way (more than half of this property is
covered with trees that would need to come down and he doesn’t believe the
Township wants to see this property used for an agricultural operation); if
rezoned, the parcel would be consistent with the Kampe farm across the street;
their request does not create unlawful exclusionary zoning; the property would
be compatible with surrounding properties in most instances; and the request is
consistent with the purposes of the ordinance with regards to size, etc…. He
said that he doesn’t agree Mr. Maire’s questions posed in consideration #9 of
his rebuttal letter have been answered by the Commission.
Mr. McIntosh said it concerns him that most of the discussion in support of
denying this request revolved around the fear of setting a precedent but by
definition, you don’t establish a precedent until there is a like situation. He
said he has reviewed the Township map and doesn’t see any like situations where
an Ag-Sf property is surrounded by small parcels. If a like situation did
occur, he argued that each parcel has to be considered on its own merits. There
is already an RR zoning line on the south side of the Maire property and they
are just asking that the line be moved to the north side of the parcel. This
would restore the zoning on this parcel to RR as it was on the previous Master
Plan. Supervisor Martin stated that she had checked the records and the owner
had not objected to the rezoning when this change to the Zoning Ordinance was
made in the early 1990’s. Mr. McIntosh said he did not say there was an
objection at that time but there was a comment made by a Board member that the
applicant had benefited from a lowered assessment after this rezoning but it is
his understanding that assessments have nothing to do with zoning and are based
on market value. Supervisor Martin agreed that assessments are made on market
value and not on zoning. Mr. McIntosh said that the Master Plan and Zoning
Ordinance are documents that need to be occasionally revisited and tweaked. He
pointed out that the Commission is doing just that with its proposed Mixed-Use
Overlay District discussed tonight. Mr. McIntosh restated his and Mr. Maire’s
request that their rezoning request be approved tonight by the Board.
Don Schmidt (4550 Zimmer Road) stated that his property abuts the Maire
property and asked whether someone purchasing the two (2) ten acre parcels next
to his property would be able to request a similar rezoning. Supervisor Martin
said that it is possible. Mr. McIntosh said those parcels cannot legally be
split because they don’t have 330’ of road frontage. Supervisor Martin agreed
they could not be split as they exist but could be if the owner was willing to
put in a public road.
Supervisor Martin pointed out that the applicant is not limited to an
agricultural use but is entitled to apply any use listed in the Zoning
Ordinance from Section 11.02 down. She also agreed that the Board does
occasionally make changes to the Zoning Ordinance. However, they do not
necessarily make every change requested. Trustee Zaban commented that if this
request is denied, the applicant can still pursue the two (2) other options
discussed tonight.
Trustee Zaban made a motion that the Board accept the Planning Commission’s
recommendation for denial of the Maire rezoning request based on the criteria
they provided. Motion supported by Treasurer Fink. Motion passed unanimously.
Windybrook Tentative Preliminary Plat
Chairman Kraft identified Windybrook Subdivision on the Township Zoning Map.
The proposed subdivision is 35.2 acres with 16 lots and 52% dedicated open
space. Mr. Kraft reported that at the December Planning Commission meeting, the
Commission had recommended tentative preliminary plat approval subject to the
developer satisfying six (6) conditions set forth in McKenna’s recommendation
letter dated 12/11/03 and the conditions that they place seedlings around the
McGarey property and install bollard type lighting at the subdivision entrance.
Mr. Kraft reported that since the Commission’s December meeting, the developer
has resubmitted a corrected plan which addresses many of the concerns. That
plan has been reviewed by McKenna Associates and they summarized their
recommendations in a letter dated 12/29/03. There are two (2) remaining
conditions: approval by all other agencies with jurisdiction over subdivisions
of this type; and Township approval of the subdivision’s covenants and
restrictions.
Dennis Forsberg (T.A. Forsberg) stated that they had worked hard with the
Planning Commission over the past couple of years. Supervisor Martin asked for
clarification of hatching marks on the new plan and Maynard Beery (T.A.
Forsberg) said they identify places where seeding mixtures will be spread to
prevent ragweed, etc…from sprouting since this is former farmland. Tom Grover
(3790 Zimmer Road) expressed concern about potential “track-out” of mud as
construction vehicles go in and out of the development. Supervisor agreed this
is a concern and said the Township usually asks developers to clean tires on
their vehicles before leaving a construction area. The Building Inspector
notifies the contractor when trackout becomes a problem and citizens are
encouraged to report problems they see to the Township. Treasurer Fink asked if
there was any existing drain tile in the old farm field. Maynard Beery
responded that the area north of the main tree line running north south may
have had drain tiles at some point but he doesn’t believe that it was ever
systematically tiled. Chairman Kraft pointed out that the Commission’s
requirement for 100 conifer seedlings around the McGarey property is subject to
Drain Commission approval. He noted that this item was not included in the 12/
29/03 McKenna letter but still exists. The Drain Commission will probably not
have a problem with trees because they will improve drainage. Trustee Wright
stated that this condition has actually been met because the trees are now
included on the plan and it is only their placement that will be at the
McGarey’s discretion. Chairman Kraft concurred.
Trustee Wright made a motion to approve the tentative preliminary plat for
Windybrook Subdivision with the two (2) conditions listed in the McKenna letter
dated 12/29/03. Motion supported by Clerk Hiner and passed unanimously.
Hideaway Woods No, 5 - Extension of Tentative Preliminary Plat with Conditions
Chairman Kraft reported that the Planning Commission recommends the Board grant
a one year extension of the Hideaway Woods No. 5 tentative preliminary plat
subject to the existing conditions. The Commission makes this recommendation
with recognition that the applicants have been working hard with the City of
Williamston to resolve their sewer issues and the fact that they have already
met two (2) of the original six (6) conditions.
Mr. Carl McIntosh (McNeer) summarized his position on the status of the six (6)
remaining conditions by stating: there is still disagreement whether sanitary
sewer has been allocated to Mr. Perkins; the Township has control over review
condition and he asked if the review has been done so it can be removed; the
Health Department has completed their review; and the cul-de-sac condition has
been met. He said that in his opinion the only issues remaining are the sewer
condition and the covenants and restrictions document which cannot be completed
until the sewer decision has been made. He said the court date on this issue is
scheduled for February 6, 2004.
Trustee Wright made a motion to extend the tentative preliminary plat with
existing conditions for Hideaway Woods No. 5 for one (1) year. Motion supported
by Clerk Hiner and passed unanimously.
Supervisor Martin told Mr. Kraft that she would like to ask the Planning
Commission to look at the R.O.S.E. or Open Space Overlay District because when
she looks at a plan like Mr. Forsberg’s she doesn’t see any benefit to the
Township. It appears that both RE and RR zoning get 2.07 units per acre. She
questioned the benefit of R.O.S.E. to the Township in the RE district (which
has a 5 acre minimum lot size). Without R.O.S.E., the developer would have only
been allowed 7 lots but with R.O.S.E they were able to create 16 lots.
Supervisor Martin said that developers of RR properties get a benefit because
they can cluster the homes on the good soils. Without R.O.S.E. they might not
get as many lots because they can’t build on the poor soil areas. With R.O.S.E.
they can set poor soil areas aside as open space and cluster more lots on the
good soil areas. Chairman Kraft said the benefit to the Township of a developer
using R.O.S.E. stops at the RR district. Supervisor Martin favors developers
getting a benefit in the RE district for setting aside open space, just not
such a big one (one unit for every three or every 4 acres would be more
appropriate). That way the developer still gets a bonus and the Township has
some benefit also. Chairman Kraft said he will put this issue on the Planning
Commission agenda. Treasurer Fink commented that she endorses the Planning
Commission’s plans (stated in their minutes) to consider requiring that open
space under R.O.S.E. be contiguous.

in the office were being given and Supervisor Martin said they are getting a
1.5% raise based on the Consumer Price Index. Mr. Philip said her increase
seems high when compared to that standard increase. She said that she has not
had a raise in four (4) years and will be willing to cut back her hours to 12

later in this meeting.

Federal Poverty Guidelines
Supervisor Martin explained that the Township is required to adopt poverty
guidelines at the start of each year. At this point there is only one person in
the Township that uses this option and they are well qualified for it.
Trustee Wright made a motion to accept the federal poverty guidelines as
follows:
“FEDERAL POVERTY GUIDELINES FOR 2004 ASSESSMENTS
The following are the federal poverty guidelines as of 12-31-03 for use in
setting poverty exemption guidelines for 2004 assessments. Please see STC
Bulletin No.5 of 1995 for additional information regarding the use of these
guidelines.
Size of Family Unit             Poverty Guidelines
1                               $8,980
2                               12,120
3                               15,260
4                               18,400
5                               21,540
6                               24,680
7                               27,820
8                               30,960
For each additional person. Add 3,140
 
IMPORTANT NOTE: PA 390 of 1994 states that the poverty exemption guidelines
established by the governing body of the local assessing unit SHALL also
include an asset level test.”
Motion supported by Treasurer Fink and passed unanimously.
Supervisor Martin explained that, along with poverty guidelines, the Township
must also annually set asset limits. Current limits allow the property owner to
own one vehicle and one home. Frans Wilbrink asked what would happen if the
owner marries and the spouse brings another vehicle to the home. Treasurer Fink
said that becomes a credibility issue. Supervisor Martin explained that a
homeowner can only make less then $8980 per year to qualify. Treasurer Fink
added that social security is not included in the calculation because it is not
taxable income.
Trustee Wright made a motion that the Township set the asset level so that the
applicant can own one house and one automobile.
Discussion
Treasurer Fink said she would like to see the Township allow some leeway so
that exceptions can be made for exceptional situations. Supervisor Martin said
she was not sure if this was legally possible. Treasurer Fink questioned if
there was a provision for the Board of Review to make considerations.
Supervisor Martin will investigate the issue with State Treasury. Motion
supported by Trustee Zaban and passed unanimously.

Mitchell Road Speed Limit
Supervisor Martin read a response dated 12/2/03 from Ingham County Road
Commission (ICRC) responding to the Township’s request that the speed limit on
Mitchell Road be reduced from 45 mph to 35 mph. Their response stated that an
engineering study must be performed before a reduction can occur. They said the
State Police had conducted a speed study on August 30, 2001 using a handheld
detector and determined that the speed limit is correctly set at 45 mph. ICRC
said Mitchell Road will be placed on the list for an engineering study to be
conducted next spring. Trustee Wright suggested the Township request that the
speed study not be conducted right before or right after school since the
students tend to drive too fast and the speed calculation will be skewed.
Trustee Zaban volunteered to respond to the ICRC letter. Trustee Wright asked
if volume of traffic is considered in a speed study. Supervisor Martin said not
directly but traffic generally slows down when volume increases. Trustee Zaban
said that he is pleased that at least Mitchell Road is back on the traffic
study list.

Planning Commission Report
Meeting Minutes -1/20/04
Supervisor Martin asked the status of the Mossholder request and Chairman Kraft
stated the Commission will be deliberating on it this month.
Zoning Ordinance & Subdivision Control Ordinance Revisions – Board Approval/
Denial
Chairman Kraft explained that the Planning Commission typically makes annual
revisions to the various ordinances. This year, the Commission has made
recommendations for revisions to seventeen (17) sections of the Zoning
Ordinance for Board consideration tonight. Many changes are typographical or
the result of practical issues that arose throughout the year. The Commission’s
revision process took place over several meetings with recommendations provided
by McKenna Associates. There was no opposition to these revisions at the public
hearing.
Chairman Kraft pointed out that the Commission’s recommendation for change to
“Section 1.03 of the Zoning Ordinance- Definitions of Commercial Vehicles and
Equipment” was mistakenly omitted from tonight’s recommendation information. He
said at the last meeting there was a question raised because the top half of
the definition is inconsistent with the definition on the bottom half. The top
half refers to “motor vehicles and equipment used for transportation of
passengers for hire or constructed or used for transportation of goods, wares
or merchandise and/or all motor vehicles designed and used for drawing other
vehicles.” He commented that this part of the definition is fairly narrow in
scope. The bottom half of the definition would also include sprayers,
excavating equipment, front loaders, etc…
Chairman Kraft recommended the following language to correct this discrepancy:
“All motor vehicles and equipment constructed or used for transportation of
goods, wares, materials, passengers, merchandise and/or all other motor
vehicles and equipment designed and used for drawing other vehicles or used in
construction or landscaping including but not limited to: dump truck, stake
truck, tank truck, flat bed truck, step van, panel truck, wrecker, car hauler,
truck tractor, construction and landscaping vehicles and equipment, sprayers,
excavating equipment, logging vehicle, bulldozer, backhoe, front loader, bus,
hearse, ambulance, or limousine. The determination whether other vehicles or
equipment not specifically listed satisfy the definition of “Commercial
Vehicles and Equipment” shall be made on a case by case basis by the Township
Board.” Supervisor Martin agreed but asked that the phrase “all motor vehicles”
be replaced with “all power vehicles” in both places it appears. Chairman Kraft
agreed and noted that his wording recommendation also corrects “Township
Supervisor”to “Township Board.”
Treasurer Fink asked how a pick-up truck or passenger car could fit into this
description. Trustee Wright clarified the intent was to determine what the
vehicle is being used for and the Board can make a decision based on whether a
vehicle is truly a personal vehicle or whether it meets the criteria of this
definition on a case by case basis. Treasurer Fink said the definition appears
to be very broad and Chairman Kraft said that that was the Commission’s intent.
Supervisor Martin questioned the Commission’s change to “Section 2.03 –
Location of Accessory Buildings”. She is concerned that the wording the
Planning Commission proposed would allow a building that is 4000 ft or greater
in the front yard and it was her understanding that the Township wanted
buildings that large to always be in back. Mr. Kraft stated that he recommends
deleting this item from tonight’s consideration and have the Commission take
another look at it. He also noted that there is a discrepancy between the quote
stated in McKenna’s letter dated 12/19/03 and the current revision of the
ordinance.
Supervisor Martin questioned the use of the term “bonified farm” in “Section
18.02-Principal Permitted Uses in the AG-C District. She pointed out that there
is no definition of “bonified farm” anywhere in the ordinance. She said she
would prefer not to include this revision until a definition exists. Chairman
Kraft agreed and recommended this item be omitted from consideration tonight
and reviewed further by the Commission.
Clerk Hiner made a motion that the Board accept the Planning Commission’s
recommendation for changes to the Zoning Ordinance and Subdivision Control
Ordinance with the change to Section 1.03 recommended by Chairman Kraft and
with omission of the revisions to “Section 2.03-Location of Accessory
Buildings” and “Section 18.02-Principal Permitted Uses in the AG-C District.
Motion supported by Trustee Wright. Motion passed unanimously.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDA ITEMS
Susan Jennings (2359 Hiddenview Lane) stated that she had brought an issue to
Trustee Wright’s attention which he said he would look into and get back to
her. He has not responded up to this time so she is bringing it before the
Board tonight. She asked the Board to explain how the Annual Meeting minutes of
March 4, 2003 meeting fulfill the requirements of Michigan’s election law
Section 168.358 subsection 4 which states in part, “that the township board of
a township having a population of 5000 or more or having 3000 or more qualified
electors (which we met both of those requirements) shall cause the question of
electing additional trustees to be voted on at the first general November
election or annual meeting following the Township’s qualifying for additional
trustees.”
Ms. Jennings stated that this Board addressed this issue according to the
wording taken from their approved minutes of the March 4, 2003 meeting:
“Supervisor Martin stated that at this time the Board can decide to add two (2)
trustees. She noted that there would be an additional expense for the Township
and she asked the Board for questions or input. Treasurer Fink asked whether
the vote tonight was to put on the ballot if the public wanted two (2)
additional trustees or if two (2) additional trustees would automatically
appear on the next ballot. Supervisor Martin responded that the Board’s
decision tonight would be to include or not include two (2) additional
candidates on the next general election ballot. Treasurer Fink made a motion
that the Township shall continue to have only two (2) trustee positions on a
general election ballot. Trustee Zaban supported the motion and the motion was
passed unanimously.”
Ms. Jennings stated that her reading of the law is that it is not the Board’s
decision to make, it is the Township’s and the public has been robbed of its
right to vote. Treasurer Fink asked if there was attendance at that annual
meeting and Deputy Clerk Pincumbe responded that the sign-in sheet for each
meeting is kept on file with a copy of each month’s board packet. Supervisor
Martin responded that we acted upon our attorney’s letter and his opinion that
we could deal with this at an annual meeting. Susan Jennings said that what was
held last year does not qualify as an annual meeting. Treasurer Fink asked why
and Ms. Jennings responded that for one thing the public didn’t vote, the Board
voted. Treasurer Fink stated that she did not mean to exclude the public from
voting at that meeting. She said she’s agrees with Ms. Jennings and is not so
sure that the public understood that they could vote. She said she has also
spoken to someone who was at the annual meeting and he did not understand that
he could vote either so she agrees that this was not accurately represented to
the public that they could vote most likely. Possibly the Clerk or the
Supervisor or somebody should have given an instruction to the public that they
could vote in that election. Ms. Jennings stated that the public record
repeatedly states that the Board makes this decision.
Supervisor Martin said “if we conducted our annual meeting different than other
Boards that’s fine, we can re-conduct it. The Board had never had an annual
meeting before. The old Board stopped having annual meetings because no one
attended.” She said she is quite sure there were only two (2) people in
attendance at that meeting. Treasurer Fink said she remembers wondering why
Frans Wilbrink was not present at the annual meeting because he had attended a
previous meeting that evening. Supervisor Martin said she will take it up with
legal council, he has already written an attorney opinion on it. If a mistake
was made then the Board will make every attempt to correct it. She said they
will act on his guidance. Treasurer Fink asked if the meeting had been posted
properly. Supervisor Martin said that she presumes that it was. Trustee Wright
recommended that the question be brought to the attorney.

Planning Commission Report
Meeting Minutes -2/17/04 and 2/24/04
Planning Commission Chairman Dan Kraft presented a summary of the Planning
Commission regular and special meetings held in February:
Windybrook Final Preliminary Plat-Board Approval/Denial
Chairman Kraft identified Windybrook Subdivision on the Township Zoning Map for
the audience and explained that the developer (T.A. Forsberg) has proposed
sixteen (16) lots. Mr. Kraft reported that at their February 17, 2004 meeting,
the Planning Commission voted to recommend granting approval of the Final
Preliminary Plat for WindyBrook Subdivision with a number of conditions. Since
that time, the developer has submitted additional information. Supervisor
Martin read the conditions itemized in the Planning Commission’s February 17th
regular meeting minutes:
“1)    Digital Format - The applicant must submit a copy of the plat in digital
format (this can be delayed until approval of the final preliminary plat is
obtained);
2)    Preliminary Engineering – Preliminary engineering is required at this
stage of review. In particular, information regarding street lighting and
stormwater runoff calculations must be provided on the plans. A sheet
containing details of the proposed bollard lights at the subdivision entrance
has not been submitted, and stormwater runoff calculations have not been shown
on the final preliminary plat.
3)   Declaration of Restrictions – Document must be submitted by the applicant
with McKenna’s four (4) recommendations considered. [ 1) Section 2.4-revise so
that the Common Areas are to be conveyed to the Association not later than
January 1, 2006; 2) Section 7.10-It is the Developer’s responsibility to
complete all of the improvements on the plat. Any responsibilities passed onto
the Lot Owner would have to be covered by a performance guarantee submitted by
the Developer; 3) Section 12.4.1-A copy of the Association Bylaws must be
submitted for review; and 4) Page 16-Ownership of the development must be
resolved (Pinehill Estates, L.L.C.) and made consistent in all documents and
plans].
4)   Health Department Approval – Mr. Breuckman pointed out that Supervisor
Martin has also provided Commissioners with a memo stating the Health
Department has not been able to formally approve the mound system because Mr.
Gruener is out of the office until March 2, 2004.”
Supervisor Martin stated that Bruce Gruener had delivered a letter from the
Health Department to the Township which states their approval of the
developer’s proposed mound system. The Township also received a revised plan
from the developer on 2/24/04 with copies of the Declaration of Restrictions,
ByLaws, and Consent of Partners of Pinehill Partnership. This information has
been reviewed by McKenna Associates and Jim Breuckman stated that all
conditions have now been met with the exception of the developer providing
plans in digital format. Mr. Dennis Forsberg of T.A. Forsberg agreed that they
had addressed all of the Township’s concerns and will forward the plan in
digital format immediately. Supervisor Martin told Mr. Forsberg that T.A.
Forsberg also has an outstanding invoice from the Township which must be paid.
Chairman Kraft stated that another issue he recalls that may have fallen
through the cracks is that there was a condition on the tentative preliminary
plat approval that 150 seedlings be planted around the McGarey property at
their discretion and pending Drain Commission approval. The Drain Commission
has since stated that they did not want trees planted on their easement.
However, the McGareys may still want those trees planted on their property to
provide future screening. Mr. Forsberg responded that he had spoken with Mr.
McGarey by telephone and told him of the Drain Commission’s position. He
offered to plant the seedlings on the McGarey’s property instead. Supervisor
Martin stated that the final preliminary plan does indicate that 150 seedlings
will be placed on the property with the McGarey’s approval. Mr. Kraft stated he
thought the notation previously identified 200 mixed evergreens but now states
150 blue spruce. Mr. Kraft said he is comfortable with the plan as stated as
long as the developer is working with the McGareys. He explained that the
developer had made this concession at their last Planning Commission meeting
when the McGareys were not present so he wanted to make sure that this issue
didn’t fall through the cracks.
Constable Dahlstrom asked if the Ordinance addresses tree removal by property
owners. Supervisor Martin said that these proposed seedlings will be located in
common areas or on the McGarey property so property owners will not be able to
remove them. Mr. Kraft pointed out that there are also numerous trees
identified on this plan that will be planted on private lots and that is why
the performance bond has been added as a guarantee. The decision of where those
trees will be placed will be made by the future property owners. However, the
performance bond will guarantee that they are eventually planted. Mr. Forsberg
added that they have proposed tree placement along the road easement in a
manner similar to how they’ve planted in their other subdivisions. Mr. Forsberg
also pointed out that the Covenant of Restrictions document is typically turned
in again before final plat approval so there will be another opportunity for
the Board to review their project before the plat is signed. Supervisor Martin
stated that Jim Breuckman had told her this afternoon that there is nothing
outstanding.
Trustee Zaban made a motion to accept the Planning Commission’s recommendation
for Final Preliminary Plat approval for WindyBrook Subdivision subject to the
following remaining conditions: Submittal of the plan in digital format,
payment of T.A. Forsberg’s outstanding invoice and McKenna’s review of the
Declaration of Restrictions. Motion supported by Trustee Wright and passed
unanimously.
Glenn Brown – Special Land Use Permit for Home Occupation
Supervisor Martin read two (2) letters received after the public hearing from
Mr. John Walton (5220 Zimmer Road) and Mr. Richard Johnston (1600 Barry Road).
Both letters requested the Township not grant this special land use permit.
Chairman Kraft reported that the Planning Commission voted to recommend denial
of the special land use permit for home occupation requested by Mr. Glenn
Brown. He summarized that a public hearing was held for this request in January
where there was vocal opposition. The public hearing was then reopened at the
Planning Commission’s February 17th regular meeting. A motion was made to
recommend approval but the vote was tied 3-3. The Commission voted to table a
revote until their February 24th special meeting when more commissioners were
expected to be present. Mr. Kraft explained that the applicant does not
currently own the property in question. They will submit a bid to purchase the
property only if they are granted a special land use permit. The Ordinance
allows a home occupation in an accessory building with a special use permit.
The addition proposed by the Browns meets the accessory building requirements
of the Ordinance. Chairman Kraft reported that, at their February 24th meeting,
the Commission voted to recommend denial by a 6-3 vote. The Commissioners had
several concerns including: the proposed special use does not fit with the
Master Plan, the proposed use stretches the limits of the definition of home
occupation, once the business is established in the accessory building, there
is no requirement in the Ordinance that the owners live there; and, if the
Browns sell the property to a third party, it would be sold with an established
business in the accessory building.
Supervisor Martin stated that the Board has read the minutes for each meeting
where this issue was discussed. She invited the public and applicant to make
any additional comments.
Glenn Brown (Okemos, MI) - (Mr. Brown gave the Board a copy of his comments in
writing). Mr. Brown explained to the Board that he would like to work from his
home somewhere in this area and this property seemed an ideal location because
it is well sheltered so his business would have a low impact on the surrounding
community. He explained that the existing outbuilding is located 600 feet from
the road and is nearly invisible. Trees would block the view of parked cars
from the road. If the concern is that the building is located too close to the
neighboring property, he would be willing to rotate the building. Two dense
lines of trees already exist between the two properties. Mr. Brown said that it
appears everyone has different perceptions about what he does. He explained
that he has been in business for 33 years. The business has been located in the
Coral Gables plaza since 1991 (with no sign). He said he would like to relocate
to a quieter location with no commercial traffic. He has never had complaints
from neighbors about noise, even though his current studio is not very well
soundproofed. He explained the different types of services he provides and said
he is also a consultant for construction of sound proof buildings so he is
qualified to ensure adequate soundproofing in the proposed accessory building.
He said that his customer traffic is low and provided a list of the number of
people who came to his business during the past two months. His work is moving
more towards mastering soundtracks which are mailed to him. Mrs. Brown said
there would be no sign at the road and all customers are seen by appointment.
They are charged by the hour so don’t linger. Mr. Brown said they have great
interest in wildlife and would strive to maintain an attractive property. They
would be conscientious neighbors and an asset to the community (for instance to
churches, etc… that might need their service). He said he doesn’t own the
building he currently works from so he cannot upgrade the soundproofing to his
standards. Treasurer Fink commented that there is an airstrip next to this
property that will have low flying aircraft – especially on MSU game days. Mr.
Brown said his soundproofing will eliminate this noise. Mrs. Brown said they
definitely will be living on the property. Mr. Brown said this request does not
set a precedent because each home occupation is decided on a case by case basis
and weighted on its own merits. There were no questions from the Board for Mr.
Brown. Supervisor Martin clarified that the Ordinance does not require that the
owner live at the home occupation. Treasurer Fink said she would like to see
this clarified in the Ordinance because it seems to her that living in the home
would be a requirement for a home occupation.
Katie Lo (121 Sherwood Road) asked if bands come to their business to record
music. Mrs. Brown said they do, but it is not the “rowdy studio” situation that
some might imagine.
Robin Cleveland (5221 N. Zimmer Road) stated that her position that the
Township not grant this special use permit request has nothing to do with the
Browns’ character or what Mr. Brown does for a living, it is simply a matter of
adhering to the Township’s Master Plan. She said the Master Plan represents a
plan for growth in the Township that has been voted into place by the
Township’s citizens. The property being discussed is zoned AG-Small Farm on the
Master Plan and the special use being proposed is not identified as a permitted
or accessory use in the Ordinance and is not similar to any allowable use for
this zone. She said this request opens the door for rezoning the Township one
parcel at a time which goes against the Master Plan. Approving this request
will promote urban sprawl. The Agricultural Small Farm section of the Ordinance
(15.01), Statement of Purpose, par. 1, states “…In contrast with the rural
estate district, the AG-SF district provides for lower density development,
thereby providing for greater opportunity to preserve agricultural uses.” In
the same section par. 2 states, “…The standards of this district are intended
to assure that permitted uses peacefully coexist in the low density setting
while preserving the rural like features and characters so important to the
Township.” Par. 3 states, “…It is further the intent of this district to permit
a limited range of residentially related uses and to prohibit multiple family,
office, business, commercial, industrial and other uses that would interfere
with the quality of residential life in this district.” She said you wouldn’t
put a farm in a commercial district because the neighbors wouldn’t want it
there and, by the same reasoning, you shouldn’t put a commercial business in a
farm district. She stated that one planning commissioner had said during
discussion that they should look at both the spirit and the intent of the
Ordinance when making a decision and she agrees. She said she does not believe
this request qualifies as home occupation because of the large addition to the
pole barn (she added that 2400 sq. ft. is larger than her house) and the
applicant is requesting five (5) parking spaces when the Ordinance only permits
two (2). The applicant has stated they plan to pave but it is her understanding
that paving isn’t allowed for a parking lot created specifically for a special
use. In the original application the Browns indicated a personal recording
studio when in fact their recording studio is a business currently located in a
commercial district in East Lansing. She said she sees no need to bring this
business into this part of the Township. In the original plan, the Browns
indicated the building would be sound insulated (not sound proofed). However,
the Township’s Noise Ordinance is virtually non-enforceable and leaves
neighbors with no recourse. She said the impact this request will have on the
enjoyment of their property is important to them. They have incurred a lot of
expense encouraging wildlife which this business may chase away. They have
owned their property for 18 years and their neighbors are also longstanding
residents with a lot invested. They don’t want to see their property values
decline. A 30-year veteran real estate agent reviewed the details of this
application for them and determined that this special use would negatively
impact the value of their property. With at least three (3) immediate neighbors
who voted on the current Master Plan opposing this request, she believes their
wishes should be of the utmost importance to the Township’s planning staff.
Supervisor Martin asked Mr. Kraft whether the Planning Commission had
considered the general requirements for home occupations which states they may
be permitted in an accessory building with special land use permit but the
appearance of the structure may not be altered. Mr. Kraft said the provisions
in the Ordinance were discussed and it was general consensus that this request
doesn’t quite fit into the home occupation definition. Supervisor Martin
pointed out that the general requirements also state a home occupation cannot
increase any utility by more than 10% and she presumes this use would increase
electricity usage by some degree.
Supervisor Martin summarized that the Planning Commission has held their public
hearing and listened to comments. She added that she thinks the Ordinance has
done what it’s supposed to do by triggering the need for a special use permit
process. This required the Township to notify neighbors of intent so they could
provide input and allowed the applicant the opportunity to present his
proposal.
Clerk Hinder moved to accept the Planning Commission’s recommendation for
denial of a special use permit for home occupation to Glenn Brown. Motion
supported by Trustee Zaban.
Discussion
Treasurer Fink said that in the past, the Board has been sympathetic to mixed-
use requests but also envisions them in a more appropriate zoning. She said she
personally likes the idea of mixed-uses but this request seems to be
compromising to the neighbors (at least to their perception). Trustee Wright
said he is torn on this request because he believes this business would have a
very low impact. However, the surrounding property owners strongly oppose the
request and they have been longtime residents and taxpayers. He said if the
Browns were looking at a parcel next to his property he wouldn’t have a problem
but he has to oppose the request based on the neighbors’ opposition.
He added that this was also a difficult vote for the Planning Commission.
Supervisor Martin said her concern is that the request is not in compliance
with the Master Plan. Motion passed unanimously.
Mrs. Brown thanked the Board for their time and stated that she appreciates the
Board’s feedback - especially that this request may be acceptable on a
different piece of property.

Insurance Audit Report
Clerk Hiner reported that she had met with insurance representative Dale Sheets
in early January to review the Township’s current coverage. She had originally
contacted three (3) insurance agencies to review a bid but they were not
willing to do so until 45 days from renewal because until then the numbers are
meaningless. Mr. Sheets reviewed the Township’s existing policies and stated
that the Township appears to be well insured. He said there a couple of places
where the Township does not have enough liability coverage. Liability coverage
should be for the dollar amount that comes through the Township in one tax
season. Treasurer Fink said she has investigated the bonding issue and the
Township’s Treasury Department is fully covered. The Township carries $100,000
in coverage and the County also has bonded all the money that goes to all other
jurisdictions. Treasurer Fink said she will request documentation of this
information for the Township’s file. Clerk Hiner said that Mr. Sheets’ two (2)
other recommendations were that office furnishings/computer equipment be
covered by class instead of by piece. It is less cumbersome than updating an
equipment list each time a purchase is made. He also recommended that the
Township meticulously track how employees use their time because when the
insurance company performs their annual audit, if there is any question they
will assign employees to the category that has the highest insurance cost. For
instance, if Mark Tabor doesn’t document the percentage of time he performs
lawn care and snow removal activities, the insurance company will assign him to
this category (which has the highest insurance cost) for 100% of his time
unless we can prove otherwise. Mr. Sheets said that everything in these
policies are points for negotiation. Clerk Hiner said that Mark Tabor’s time is
currently tracked by task so can be easily negotiated with our insurance
company.
Budget-General & Cemetery Deliberation
Supervisor Martin reported that changes discussed at the Board’s Workshop
meeting have been made. She said that the “Drains-at-Large” budget has been
increased from $9,000 to $83,500 based on cost information for the upcoming
year forwarded by the Ingham County Drain Commission. The Drain Commission
charges for cleanouts and repairs to drains located throughout the Township and
then charges the Township after the fact. Right now the Township also has an
additional financial responsibility of approximately $75,000 (15% of the total
cost) for the new drain being constructed on the west end of Grand River (with
a total cost of $489,978.25). Treasurer Fink stated that she and Supervisor
Martin were shocked when they were told of the cost at this morning’s meeting
with the Drain Commission. In the future, the Township will request preliminary
financial information in advance. She added that they have also requested a
spreadsheet showing where specific costs went on this project. Supervisor
Martin clarified that the Drain Commission has authority to proceed without
Township authorization and the drain being installed is extensive. She stated
that impacted homeowners have been attending meetings regularly and it is
important that a Township representative attend future Drain Commission
meetings. Treasurer Fink said they are looking into spreading payments for the
drain out over multiple years. Supervisor Martin said the entire amount has
been included in this year’s budget because there hasn’t been confirmation that
payments can be made over time. The bottom line is that the drain had to be
fixed but the cost was a shock.
Supervisor Martin proposed that the “Contingency” budget item be reduced from
$43,300 to $30,000 (the amount it was previously in 2003/4) which would reduce
the budget’s net negative balance from $68,900 to $55,500. Trustee Wright and
Treasurer Fink agreed.
Trustee Wright made a motion to approve the budget for by each department class
as outlined in the proposed budget document prepared by Supervisor Martin with
the changes of reducing the budgeted amount for “Contingency” from $43,3000 to
$30,000; the addition of $83,000 to “Drains-at-Large” and the addition of
$1,000 to “NPDES Permit.” Motion supported by Clerk Hiner and passed
unanimously.
Supervisor Martin recommended that a “Contingency” fund be established for
unanticipated cemetery costs. The Board agreed to set a “Contingency”fund of
$7500. This creates a Cemetery budget deficit of $17,006.
Trustee Zaban moved to approve the proposed Cemetery Budget for 2004/05 as
prepared by Supervisor Martin with the change of adding a “Contingency” amount
of $7500. Motion supported by Trustee Wright and passed unanimously.
John Kane – Hotel Tax
Clerk Hiner reported that she had spoken with Mr. Ladke and he told her that
the two (2) hotel/motel properties in Williamstown Township generate a total of
approximately $1500 each year. The 1% that the County receives is used to
support the Center for the Arts, the Ingham County Fairgrounds and to cover
administration costs. The rest of the money goes to the Greater Lansing
Convention Board. Mr. Ladke said that Williamston likely doesn’t benefit to the
extent that others do but he would be willing to meet with the Board to discuss
how their money is spent. Clerk Hiner said it would still be good for John Kane
and her to meet with Mr. Ladke but it isn’t going to change how this money is
being spent. Trustee Wright said he doesn’t think the Township Board needs to
pursue the issue any further and should instead put Mr. Ladke in touch with
John Kane.

Cemetery Committee
Meeting Minutes 3/10/04- Building Proposal
Greg Lammars (Cemetery Committee Representative) presented need for a storage
building at Summit Cemetery.
Mr. Lammars stated that they are proposing a larger building than originally
discussed, because the cemetery needs additional storage for machinery, larger
work area and flexibility for future additions . An office is included in the
plan to accommodate meeting with clients. Considering all that is proposed,
they increased the size of the building to 36' x 38'. Mr. Lammars stated that
the additional cost is estimated at: increased building size ($10,000),
electrical service hook up ($5,000 or more), Well ($3,000), Septic System
($3,000), and the office with a handicapped accessible bathroom ($3,000). Total
cost approximately $50,000. The Cemetery Committee is requesting the Board to
allocate the additional funds from the cemetery excess fund and approve moving
forward. Treasurer Fink will run a report updating all of the accounts and
provide him with information on the amount in the cemetery fund.
Mr. Lammars turned the presentation over to Mark Tabor (Maintenance Department)
for specific building details. Mr. Tabor stated that four bids had been
obtained from local companies who obtain lumber form either Carter or MPC. One
bid is from a Williamston builder, the other three are from Webberville
builders. A site plan for the location of the building at the cemetery, and a
floor plan of the interior of the building was reviewed.
Mr. Tabor stated they could not run water from the current well back to the
building, they would have to drill a new well. Treasurer Fink asked why they
could not use the current well. Mr. Tabor indicated that the lines are only one
foot underground and are drained every fall. Also the current well is from 1956
and has never been repaired. They don’t know if it could handle the additional
usage.
Mr. Tabor stated that the proposed heating system would be base board electric
and they will be putting the bathroom on the inside wall utilizing the heat
from the office to protect the plumbing. The approximate size of the bathroom
is 8' x 8', and the office is 22' x 12'. Treasurer Fink asked if all cemetery
business would be conducted at that location. Mr. Tabor felt it could be.
Trustee Zaban asked what the old storage building would be used for. Mr. Tabor
indicated they could use it for several items, such as awnings, and smaller
equipment.
Mr. Tabor indicated that all four bids are within the same ballpark. He had
four bids for the shell, and three bids on the finished building. The average
bid was $55,327 for a finished project, lighting, heating, construction, and
aprons. Mr. Tabor also advised the Board that the one thing the bids do not
include is landscaping around the building.
Mr. Tabor indicated that the Cemetery Committee had approved the purchase of a
new cement mixer. He distributed specifications of the model he purposed they
purchase and asked for approval of the purchase. Supervisor Martin asked which
Cement mixer they were looking at. Mr. Tabor indicated that the 5.5 horse
power, 6 cubic foot. Supervisor Martin indicated it was in the budget and they
would move forward with the purchase.
Supervisor Martin stated that she appreciated the information gathered and the
work the Cemetery Committee had done. She suggested that they ask Treasurer
Fink to see if the funds are available. Supervisor Martin suggested this be
discussed further at the next Workshop meeting, where they could thoroughly
review the detailed information and the detailed bids.
Treasurer Fink feels this is a excellent idea, and appreciates all of the work
done on the project. She thinks it would be an excellent thing to have a
central office to handle the cemetery business, and she thinks they are sorely
in need of this space.

Services.

notified: letters were sent. Supervisor Martin stated that it is her

Text Amendment, Zoning Ordinance - RE Zone on Grand River
Mr. LaMore advised that the revision would allow only those RE zones, which
have frontage along Grand River Ave, to use 20 percent of their total site for
retail sales. The intent is not to turn these sites into commercial sites, but
to allow limited commercial usage. .
Mr. LaMore reported that the Planning commission did have a public hearing on
this matter, and there was no negative response.
Trustee Kraft made a motion to approve the revision to Rural Estates District,
as set forth in the letter from McKenna and Associates dated May 20th 2003.
Motion was supported by Trustee Wright and passed unanimously.
Zoning Ordinance Revision - Mixed Use Overlay District
Mr. LaMore reported that the Mixed Use Overlay District only pertained to the
portion of Grand River avenue east of the City of Williamston. He indicated its
intent was to encourage innovation and mixed use development.
Trustee Wright indicated that a number of individuals came to the information
meeting regarding this issue, and they received positive comments. Trustee
Wight felt it would be a long time before the board saw any significant changes
in that area, but it gives people options.
Trustee Wright also felt something like this could work on the west sided of
the district in the future.
Trustee Kraft made a motion to adopt the MU, Mixed Use Overlay District and
incorporate it into the Township Zoning Ordinance. Motion supported by Trustee
Wright and passed unanimously.
Zoning Ordinance Revision - Special Land Use Permit
Mr. LaMore reviewed the information provided to the Board regarding the changes
to Zoning Ordinance 27.02 sub-section D.10 Modification to Approved Site Plans.
The language change would allow the building official to approve minor changes.
Also a change to 27.03 to allow administration to call for a Public Hearing.
The intent is to facilitate a speedy review for the applicants.
Supervisor Martin indicated that the legal counsel had brought forward one
modification. He would like to see the following under “Modifications Not
Deemed ‘Minor’” ‘if the modifications are not deemed minor by the Building
Official, or if the Building Official finds in the Building Officials sole
discretion and professional opinion that there are characteristics of the site
plan that warrant Planning Commission review.
Trustee Wright made a motion to approve the text revision to stream line the
review process, 27.03 and 27.02 as outlined by McKenna and Associates in the
February 26,2004 letter, as well as incorporation the wording “in the Building
Officials sole discretion and professional opinion. Motion supported by Trustee
Kraft and passes unanimously.
Zoning Ordinance Revision - Site Plan Approval
Trustee Wright reported that the Board needs to provide the planning Commission
with the site plan for the Cemetery project, along with a letter outlining why
we feel that a special use permit is not necessary.

Millennium Cable
Supervisor Martin reported that she received a letter from Attorney Daniel
Pulter of Loomis, Ewert, Parsley, Davis & Gotting. He is representing the
original developer of Williamstown Estates, and was requested to bring a
complaint to their attention regarding Millennium Cable. He indicated that they
failed to install cable facilities to serve the residents at the rear of the
development. He went on to state that the Township’s Franchise Agreement with
Millennium under Article IV (A) that they have to make cable service available
to every dwelling in an area that meets a minimum density requirement. At this
time Millennium is stating they will provide cable for a fee. They want the
Board to consider terminating their agreement with Millennium and see an
alternative provider.
Supervisor Martin reported that Williamston Estates was built in three phases.
Cable was installed in the first two phases but not the third.
Attorney Pulter was present and expressed his interpretation of the agreement /
contract with Millennium. He indicated that Millennium took over the original
contract from Horizon. He felt there were two issues. One was a policy issue do
you allow a service provider to put service in two thirds of the development,
then charge for the last third. Attorney Pulter stated that the developer had
an agreement with Horizon to put cable in to the entire development. He does
not feel that the Township should allow Millennium to charge for the
installation in the last third of the development. He felt the second concern
was a contractual issue, because there is language that is not defined and
there is ambiguity in the contract. They want the Board to address the issue
and require Millennium to provide the cable service at no charge to the
developer.
Supervisor Martin advised that the Township does not have copies of the
agreements between developers and the providers. Mr. Pulter advised that he
could provide the information they have which indicates the service that
Horizon agreed to perform.
Supervisor Martin reported that the Township received a letter from Millennium
Digital today, and their representative Rick Clark is present. There is also a
representative from the Townships Cable Commission.
Mr. Clark referred to his June 30th letter. He indicated that the cable service
is required to make cable service available to each “dwelling” not lot. He
discussed with the Board how their trunking system worked, and how they
computed minimum density.
Norma Johnston was present from the Cable Commission to obtain information
regarding this issue.
Supervisor Martin recommended that this issue be referred over to the Cable

UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Millennium Cable:
Presently cable is not available in Phase 2 (Northwest section) of Williamston
Estates. The developer and Millennium Digital Media have different opinions on
who should absorb the cost of extending cable within this subdivision. The
developer wants the cable company to pay the entire cost of extending the
cable. They have asked the board to review this issue. The franchise agreement
with Millennium (formerly Horizon Cablevision) specifies “…a minimum density of
20 dwelling units per ‘street’ mile, as measured from the existing trunk
system.” There are only six houses from the existing trunk system. Four of
those six are being served. This falls short of the 20 dwelling minimum.
Therefore, the commission voted unanimously to support Millennium Digital
Media’s position in which the company offered to pay approximately one half of
the installation cost of expanding the cable.
Supervisor Martin made a motion to accept the cable commissions report and
their findings and to support their recommendations. The motion was supported
by Trustee Wright and pass unanimously.
A copy of this motion will be forwarded to the legal firm representing the
developers.
Blake Mossholder:
The board has tabled this Special Use Permit request for one month. No plans
have been brought in, however his attorney and a planning company are drafting
up plans. It is Chris Doozan’s recommendation that the board table for one
month. There was some discussion regarding not tabling this request for one
month and the steps Mr. Mossholder would have to take to bring forth a new
request.
Trustee Wright made a motion to table Blake Mossholder’s Special Use Permit and
Site Plan request for one month with a deadline for plans to be submitted by
September 7, 2004. The motion was supported by Clerk Zaban and pass
unanimously.
Mr. Mossholder will be sent a letter of decision.
Unfinished Business –Discussion regarding two more trustees:
Supervisor Martin reviewed the requirement for the addition of two trustees to
the board. Public Act 116 allows township voters to increase trustee members by
two. It has two conditions: The township must have over 3000 voters and/or 5000
in population. The Township does not have a population of over 5000, but they
do have over 3000 voters. Therefore, this question can go on a ballot. The
Board has until August 24 to have wording drafted and submitted to the county.
If it is placed on the ballot then it would go to a vote this November 2004 and
the election of the trustees would be in two years. The last time language was
submitted it was rejected by the county because it was not approved by the
board. The board did not see the language and/or pass a motion to place it on
the ballot.
There was public comment regarding having a public hearing before placing it on
the ballot. There was some discussion that this had already been done at the
annual meeting two years ago. In addition, it was publicized and there is an
affidavit on file of the one person who voted on the issue. Other discussion
included the cost of printing the ballots and the cost of additional trustee
stipends. Others questioned the townships ability to bring forth two more
candidates to be considered. For example, this primary had two vacant positions
and only three candidates ran; only one was a new candidate. Clerk Zaban added
that we need residents to step forward and volunteer for other committees and
we can’t seem to get interest in committees either, so what would happen if
nobody ran?
George Durak, 116 Feldspar Dr., agreed that resident turnout at meetings,
including the annual meeting is low, but the citizens should have the right to
vote and putting this issue on the ballot would do that. “It would be the best
job of getting the vote out if it were on the ballot,” stated Mr. Durak.
There was consensus that this should be placed on the ballot and public forums
should be held regarding the issue. A workshop meeting was scheduled for
Wednesday, August 19, to draft the language to be reviewed by legal counsel for
submission on or before August 24.
Treasurer Fink made a motion to put language on the ballot to add two trustees
to the Williamstown Township Board of Directors. The motion was supported by
Clerk Zaban and passed with one no vote from Trustee Kraft.

in Michigan and groundwater contamination. Steve Chester was there, Director of

has approximately six areas platted for development. It is zoned R1—single-
family residential with approximately ½ acre lots. It is an extension of the
other Hideaway Woods. Originally, McKenna recommended we table the issue
because all conditions had not been met, but the developer did submit the
needed information the night of the meeting, so the Commission moved forward
with recommending to the Board a preliminary plat approval as long as the
information submitted met any outstanding conditions. McKenna’s letter dated

of lot 40 and the restoration of the “T” turn-a-around.
Carl McIntosh, Hideaway Woods’ Developer, assured that the turn-a-round would
be adjusted as directed by the road commission. However, he was disappointed
that the trees have to be moved. Otherwise, he had no additional comments.

Pebblebrook Petition—Burn Petition.
Supervisor Martin indicated that a petition has been received that consists of
ninety-nine signatures requesting that Pebblebrook Estates, Pebblebrook No. 2,
3, 4 and 5, and Pebblebrook Place become consistent with Williamstown Township
and remove the restrictions placed on these areas to allow the burning of
campfires. In addition to the signed petitions, Supervisor Martin has received
approximately 15 emails, phone calls or letters of opposition to this petition.
Supervisor Martin stated that the burn ordinance allows the board to make a
change if any advisory petitions are presented regardless of the number in
support or opposition to the petition.
Supervisor Martin opened the floor for public discussion to anyone who has not
already contacted the Township and/or had any new information to offer.
Bob Pendergast--230 Cinnabar Circle: Submitted and read letter support.
George Durak—116 Feldspar Drive: Stated that fifteen years ago there was
nothing secret about the Pebblebrook burning ban because there were many public
meetings regarding this ordinance. Mr. Durak question if the petition was 99
signatures or 99 households? Supervisor Martin indicated it was 99 households.
In his opinion, there are three problems: polluting the air; increase of fire
potential; and loud parties. He believes that if the burning ban is lifted, it
will change the entire make-up of the subdivision. Mr. Durak also offered
additional opposition from Don Wake (letter not received by the Board) and Ivan
Woodhams—130 Feldspar Drive (letter to be forwarded).
Brian DeRath--4708 Sandstone Drive: Stated that both sides have very valid
points and this has become a very personal issue. He noted that when they
brought the petition forward, he respected his neighbors. However, he believes
in the neighborhood and felt that the data should be presented to the Board for
decision. He will respect and abide by the Board’s decision.
Jean Eggemeyer--35 E. Newman Road: As witness to social campfires in the
neighborhood, she can testify that a house, not within the neighborhood, but
close in proximity, has had social occasions that don’t begin until 9:30 or 10:
00 pm. because of the long summer days. She is disturbed by the noise and
smoke. She stated that you cannot mandate responsibility and consideration and
that there are many who would not violate a new ordinance, but there are many
who would. Therefore, she is in opposition.
William Nowland--248 E. Newman Road: In support of the petition. He stated that
regardless of fire pits, parties are going to happen. Kids, young adults, or
other adults do not matter—“wisdom comes from who you are.” He also stated that
when there is an ordinance, you can call and report violators. He also noted
that air quality couldn’t be considered because there are household fireplaces
that could be contributing to the air quality.
Gary Gillespie—4701 Jadestone: Stated that by signing a petition granting the
right to burn may not necessarily mean they understand the consequences of that
signature. Mr. Gillespie went on to read a letter of his concerns which was
given to the Board.
Juan Juarez--207 E. Newman Road.: In support of petition. He questioned the
total number of households in Pebblebrook and wanted to know of those
households, what was the process for originally creating the ban? For example,
was it a majority of those households in favor of the ban or was it a smaller
majority of those households? Was there a petition? Was there a clear
understanding of the majority and minority’s opinion? Mr. Durak responded that
there were five public meetings held and the decision was based on those that
attended the meetings not necessarily every household. Mr. Juarez when on to
state that in his opinion leaf burning is of a concern, but the petition
clearly states campfires and not leaves. His experience in talking with his
neighbors is that of surprise that they can’t have campfires
John Jones--211 Cinnabar Circle: In support of petition. Mr. Jones has
researched and learned that you can monitor smoke level. He suggests a monitor
could be conducted. If there is a problem, then even household fireplaces
should be banned.
Christopher Cleveland--4696 Sandstone Drive: In support of petition. Her
husband has asthma and he does not see campfires as a concern. In her opinion,
property owners have rights and this should be treated as a democracy. Articles
can always be found in support or opposition to your position. In her opinion,
property value cannot be considered.
Elaine Gillespie---4701 Jadestone: Opposes the petition. Read letter (not given
to Board). Ms. Gillespie has personal experience of a home fire and the
response of the Williamston Fire Dept. They did not have enough water and had
to drain water from a pond.
Heather DeRath--4708 Sandstone Drive: Ms. DeRath stated, for the record, that
it is her understanding that the Gillespie’s house fire was not due to
campfire, but a chimney fire.
Calvin Betts--4695 Rocky Hill: In support of petition. He helped obtain
signatures. In his opinion, everyone that signed the petition thoroughly
understood what they were signing and those who were not in agreement did not
sign.
Supervisor Martin thanked the residents for their input and indicated that all
testimony, reports from environmental organizations, as well as NIESA will be
considered when reviewing this petition.
Trustee Kraft believes we need to consider a change in this ordinance in
consideration of all those that came out to express their opinions and to have
the involvement of the fire chief would be valuable. He offered that the
Planning Commission should also review the petition. He believes the Board
should take some time to debate this issue.
Clerk Zaban suggested that a committee comprised of supporters and opponents
along with the Board could convene to resolve this issue.
Treasurer Fink suggested that many communities control fires. There are also
other considerations, such as the county, that may need to be considered.
Ms. DeRath asked for clarification regarding why the Board wouldn’t make a
decision tonight because isn’t it ultimately their decision? Supervisor Martin
responded that the Board will ultimately make the decision, but because of the
amount of information that there is to consider, it may be in the Board’s best
interest to take some time to consider the petition. The board has options: it
can accept the petition as is; it can impose conditions to the petition; or it
can deny the petition.
Ms. DeRath also asked the definition of an outdoor grill. Supervisor Martin
read the ordinance and definition of an outdoor grill.
The public hearing concluded with the Board agreeing to develop a committee to
review the petition. Supervisor Martin asked anyone interested in serving on
the committee to contact her by phone or in writing. The Board is reluctant to
set a timeline. However, Supervisor Martin believes that with a mediator along
with other opinion from the fire chief and the county, a decision can be made
in a timely manner.
Mr. Joel Raddatz, Superintendent Williamston Community Schools.
Mr. Raddatz presented information on the upcoming school bond election. The
school district has taken the last 18 months to review the input from the last
bond that was defeated. Their focus is on a need for new athletic facilities
and the location of those facilities; growth and the number of classrooms; and
taxes. This proposal is different in four primary areas: there will be no
construction on Sherwood Road for new athletic facilities; there will be no 5/
6 building; no new bus barn; and there is no need for an increase in the school
mileage rate to pay for this. The current mileage will be extended for five
years. Mr. Raddatz distributed a flier of the key points and encouraged
everyone to vote on December 6, 2004.
Williamstown Estates—Burn Petition.
Supervisor Martin received a petition from Williamstown Estates’ Subdivision
Association requesting the restricted burn dates to be lifted from their
subdivision. They are requesting that the burn restrictions be the same as
other RE zoning.
Supervisor Martin asked Mr. Kurt Guter, Association Representative, how the
residents of the subdivision were notified of the petition? Mr. Guter responded
that on October 10, 2004, at their annual homeowners meeting, which was
attended by 19 of the 25 residents, the petition was presented and signatures
were obtained. The few that didn’t sign do not live in the area or are senior
citizens who were not interested. There was not one person who opposed the
petition. The subdivision is asking for this change because of safety and
appearance. Because of the current limited burn dates and the amount of brush
to be burned, the size of the fires can be large and safety is a concern. They
would also like to request controlled burns to enhance wild flower growth.
Supervisor Martin opened the floor to public comment.
Todd Bashore--4040 Warbler Way: In support of petition. As an example of how
brush accumulates, Mr. Bashore noted that some of the current burn restriction
dates fall on a holiday, such as July 4, so many can’t burn because of other
obligations.
Jim Genova--1477 Osprey Way: In support of petition. Talked about other
examples and reasons you may not be able to burn on restricted dates, such as
windstorms.
Jim Lynch—1540 Osprey Way: In support of petition. Stated that he lives in the
middle of a pine tree forest and windfall causes lots of brush that takes a
long time to burn. The current burn restrictions make it even harder for him to
burn the accumulated brush.
Don Cooper—1501 Osprey Way: In support of petition. He supported Mr. Genova’s
postion on how weather conditions limit burning on restricted dates.
Supervisor Martin asked if the Association had thought about how the burn
ordinance protects those who are offended by the smoke? For example, with the
current restrictions, residents who are offended by the smoke can plan for
those days because they are designated. Supervisor Martin also asked if the
association had considered the 425 plan and the concentration of homes that
will come in around them? Mr. Guter responded that the abundance of brush comes
with this being new development. For example when you move in, you need to burn
regularly. Once you get on top of it, you are going to burn a lot less.
Therefore, future burning most likely will not be a problem.
Trustee Kraft and Clerk Zaban were in favor of lifting the burn. McKenna
reviewed the petition and also supported the petition.
Trustee Kraft made a motion to amend the burning ordinance by making a change
in 4a and 4b of the Williamstown Township Burn Ordinance: 4a would be changed
to read “except Williamstown Estates” and 4b would be changed to add the words
“and Williamstown Estates” after RR districts. Treasurer Fink seconded the
motion and it passed unanimously by roll call.
Roll Call Vote: Trustee Kraft Yes; Trustee Wright Yes; Treasurer Fink Yes;
Supervisor Martin Yes; Clerk Zaban Yes.
This change will be mailed to every resident of the subdivision and all
residents within 500 feet. The change will become effective 15 days after
publication.
ZBA Appointments.
