Planning Commission Meeting Minutes 12/21/04
Chairman Hayes reviewed the minutes. No board comment.
Springbrook Road Name
The Planning Commission made recommendation to the Board to approve the name
Springbrook Drive for Springbrook Subdivision. Supervisor Martin explained that
road name considerations are important because of the 911 system. When 911 was
locally dispatched, road naming was not such an issue. Now that 911 is
dispatched centrally out of Lansing, road name consideration is important
because dispatchers may not be familiar with the area. The Tri-County Planning
Commission provides a good service reviewing street names that are matching in
the local area, but it is a recommendation and the Board can approve a road
name outside of their recommendation.
Trustee Wright made a motion to approve Springbrook Drive as a road name for
Springbrook Subdivision. Treasurer LeBlanc seconded the motion and it passed
unanimously.
Master Plan Revisions
Supervisor Martin reviewed a compressed timeline for Master Plan revisions
submitted by McKenna and Associates. Supervisor Martin acknowledged that moving
forward with this project with a compressed timeline would be a vigorous
schedule and it would be a big commitment by the Planning Commission. Chairman
Hayes indicated that the Planning Commission is willing to commit the time.
Trustee Wright expressed a concern of the cost and would hope that the numbers
presented are on high side. Supervisor Martin believes this is an important
project and that a contract could be negotiated with the Planners to commit to
a limit on costs. Trustee Wilbrink asked if these hours are in addition to the
Planner’s regular hours? Supervisor Martin indicated that these costs would be
above the regular hours. Supervisor Martin also clarified that when the
Planners are here, they are not necessarily billing the Township. They may be
working on outside projects and only bill us when working on Township issues or
attending meetings.
Trustee Wright made a motion that the Board accept the compressed Master Plan
timeline and contract a monthly review of progress that would include a stop
clause, if necessary, and cost limits. The motion was seconded by Clerk Zaban
and passed unanimously.
Library Board Appointments
The Williamston Community Library Foundation appointment for Township
representative Ed Noonan is up for renewal. Supervisor Martin recommended that
he be reappointed. Trustee Wilbrink questioned the timing of the appointment
notice and the procedure. Trustee Wright and Supervisor Martin both believe the
timing is an oversight because of other priorities. This is a voluntary group
and they put in many hours of work and should be supported by the Township
Board. Supervisor Martin suggested that Trustee Wilbrink follow-up with the
Foundation regarding any concerns.
Supervisor Martin made a motion to reappoint Ed Noonan to the Williamston
Community Library Foundation as Williamstown Township’s representative. The
motion was seconded by Treasurer Leblanc and passed unanimously.
Poverty Guidelines/Asset Level
Every year the Board must pass a resolution to set the poverty and asset level
guidelines. The 2004 guideline allows for an asset level of one parcel of real
property (no cottage) and one licensed and plated vehicle per driver in the
household. Supervisor made a recommendation that the Board adopt the 2004 asset
guideline and the Federal Poverty Guidelines.
Past Treasurer Fink offered history of the previous guidelines and asset levels
such as saving accounts, vehicles, etc.
Trustee Wright made a motion to pass a resolution to adopt the Federal Poverty
Guidelines and an asset level of one parcel of real property (no cottage) and
one licensed and plated vehicle per driver in the household. Trustee Wilbrink
seconded the motion and it passed unanimously.
Precinct Changes
Clerk Zaban reported that the County has made precinct rule changes mandating
that the Township reduce their number of precincts effective March 10. The
Township will now conduct all school votes. Distributed was a proposed
resolution changing the current four precincts to two precincts voting at the
Township Hall and St. Katherine’s. Trustee Wilbrink expressed concern regarding
the reduction in precincts and how that would effect voting wait times. Clerk
Zaban indicated that there would be more voting machines that will be more
efficient, as well as other changes that will speed up the process. Other
advantages of this change would include streamlining the voting process for all
votes, including school votes, and resident precinct identification.
Trustee Wright made a motion to pass the proposed resolution to adopt the new
precincts. The motion was seconded by Supervisor Martin.
Roll Call:   Trustee Wilbrink   Yes

Treasurer LeBlanc   Yes

The motion passed 5 to 0.

Budget 2005-06
Supervisor Martin presented a proposed budget and recommended that the Board
make a motion to hold a Budget Public Hearing in February for budget approval
in March. The Public Hearing will be conducted to go through the budget line
item by line item.
Treasurer LeBlanc requested that the Treasurer’s Budget be considered
separately from the proposed budget at the public hearing. Supervisor Martin
asked the Board if they would like the Treasurer’s Budget figures to be added
to the proposed budget prior to public hearing or be heard as a separate
budget? Trustee Wright suggested they be put into the proposed budget for
public hearing, but he questioned the proposed budgeted amounts to be inserted.
It is Trustee Wright’s understanding that the Township is growing and
increasing the budget may be needed, but does the Deputy Treasurer’s salary
need to be doubled? Treasurer LeBlanc explained that the increase in salary and
training are due to the positions being held by new employees. Review continued
of comparable salaries across deputies. Supervisor Martin asked what are the
anticipated increases in tasks that would necessitate the need for increased
hours? Treasurer LeBlanc indicated the increase in hours would allow the deputy
to qualify for Township payment of Aflac. It was suggested by Clerk Zaban that
if the Deputy Treasurer’s hours were to be increased then that position could
be considered for receptionist duties if needed.
Trustee Wilbrink questioned the budget for road improvement and shouldn’t
future road improvements be part of the budget? Trustee Wilbrink also
questioned what the park expenses would be. Supervisor Martin responded that
road improvements are based on County budgets and park expenses are for
maintenance, equipment, and other improvements.
Supervisor Martin indicated that this budget assumes cost of living increases
in salary with the exception of Mark Tabors’ who has requested any salary
increases be put in a retirement plan. Trustee Wright asked if these increases
included the elected positions because they have not increased in approximately
3 to 4 years. Supervisor Martin indicated that it does not include increases
for elected positions. Supervisor Martin suggested that if the Board would like
to look at elected salaries, then the Board should established a committee to
review and make recommendations.
Trustee Wilbrink questioned the Township’s hours of operation. Trustee Wright
indicated that opening on Mondays would increase the budget in salary costs.
Clerk Zaban also reminded Trustee Wilbrink that Mondays are available for
officers to get work done outside of the public hours.
Treasurer LeBlanc asked if a budget amendment could be considered to satisfy a
current shortfall in training expenses for the Treasurer’s office. Supervisor
Martin indicated that a budget amendment request could be considered before
March through regular or special meeting.
Trustee Wright made a motion to approve a February Budget Public Hearing and to
add the Treasurer’s budget figures into the proposed budget for public hearing
with a change to the Deputy Treasurers salary from the proposed $13,416.00 to
$8,300.00. The motion was seconded by Trustee Wilbrink and passed unanimously.

JANUARY 18, 2005
PRESENT: Trustee Wilbrink; Treasurer LeBlanc; Trustee Wright; Supervisor
Martin; Clerk Zaban.
CALL TO ORDER: Supervisor Martin called the meeting to order at 5:00 pm and
reviewed the agenda.
BURN PETITION: Supervisor Martin reviewed the steps taken to date regarding the
review and consideration of the Pebblebrook Burn Petition. Supervisor Martin
also met with Donald Pixley, Township Insurance Representative, to review any
liability issues. It was determined that the Township would not be liable for
any personal lose loss to homeowners. Vince Spagnuolo, Township Legal Counsel,
confirmed that the Township would only be responsible for issuing and enforcing
the burn ordinance. The Township would not be liable for any personal loses
under the governmental immunity laws.
Supervisor Martin then opened the floor for any additional discussion:
Gary Gillespie—4701 Jadestone: Asked if personal homeowner insurance rates
would increase if the burning ban were lifted? Supervisor Martin responded that
homeowner insurance is an individual homeowner responsibility and that those
type of questions should be directed to their insurance carriers.
George Durak—116 Feldspar Dr.: Asked what would happen if the person who caused
the fire had no homeowner’s insurance? Township Legal Counsel responded that it
would be the responsibility of the victim to seek legal action against those
persons for negligence. Mr. Durak also asked if the Township would require
proof of homeowner’s insurance when issuing burn permits? Currently, the burn
ordinance does not require proof of homeowner’s insurance. If proof were
required, the burn ordinance would need to be amended.
Supervisor Martin reviewed the Meeting Summary Recommendations. It was noted
that a NIESA representative was present at the meeting and the recommendations
would be satisfactory to NIESA. Two concerns not addressed were severe
respiratory problems and Township-wide burn ordinance enforcement.
Supervisor Martin again opened the floor to discussion regarding the Meeting
Summary Recommendations:
Mr. Gillespie asked if the Township had setback requirements for wooded areas?
Supervisor Martin indicated that the current ordinance addresses setbacks for
wooded areas.
Clerk Zaban asked if a fee for inspecting fire pits could be imposed.
Supervisor Martin indicated that the Constable is paid $35 for each call he is
sent out on. Treasurer LeBlanc asked if NIESA could conduct the inspections in
lieu of a fee? Clerk Zaban indicated that NIESA does not inspect in their own
jurisdiction and he was doubtful that they would conduct the inspections in
Williamstown Township.
Mr. Durak asked if the nuisance ordinance could be enforced in areas where
someone has respiratory problems. Legal Counsel responded that the nuisance
ordinance could be enforced if there was a violation. However, if a burn permit
is issued then the fire is permitted and it would likely not violate the
nuisance ordinance.
Mr. Meadows asked how the ordinance would be enforced. Legal counsel indicated
that enforcement would be through the burn ordinance.
Supervisor Martin asked the Board if they were ready to propose a motion
regarding the Pebblebrook Burn Ordinance Petition. Trustee Wilbrink, Trustee
Wright and Clerk Zaban were in favor of moving forward. However, Trustee Wright
had concerns regarding the number of restrictions recommended. He suggested
that burn permits be limited to Friday, Saturday and Sunday and if there is a
reported problem, then the restrictions should be enforced. To enforce the
restrictions at the time of the burn permit request may not be in the best
interest of the Township. Supervisor Martin questioned the Friday, Saturday,
Sunday limitation because that might create a heavy concentration of fire
smoke. Mr. Durak agreed. Supervisor Martin indicated that typically campfire
requests are for one day. Treasurer LeBlanc felt the enforcement of a one-time
inspection is important because the spark arrestor could be checked on chimenea
type devices. Trustee Wilbrink felt the one time inspection with a fee is ok,
but what if the fire device is changed? It was also questioned if the numbers
of burn permits issued for Pebblebrook could be limited per day. Supervisor
Martin indicated that limiting burn permits would be difficult.
In conclusion, it was decided that Supervisor Martin would investigate and
recommend inspections fees for the Board to consider. Supervisor Martin asked
if there was any other information the Board would need to move forward with a
motion. Trustee Wilbrink would also like a recommendation for violation fines
and fees. Supervisor Martin indicated that she would recommend using the
current ordinance procedures. Trustee Wilbrink asked that seasoned firewood be
removed. Trustee Wright indicated that a lot of the recommended restrictions
are already in our ordinance and their burn permits should be as similar to our
current ordinance as possible.
Heather DeRath—4708 Sandstone: Indicated that people who signed the petition
did not know they were signing a petition that had a cost attached to it. The
goal behind the petition was to give opportunity to families to enjoy a few
fires per year. Limiting the number of fires would be fine. Treasurer LeBlanc
felt that the use of campfires may diminish over time as the initial novelty of
allowing campfires diminishes.
HALL RENTAL
Supervisor Martin reviewed the proposal submitted by Lissa Whitman to use the
hall for a weekly yoga class. Supervisor Martin checked insurance liability
with Donald Pixley who said the Township would need to be named on Ms.
Whitman’s insurance. There was Board consensus that a trial period be approved.
Legal counsel said that if the Board were to approve this, then the Township
would need to revise its rental agreement because currently it can’t be used
for commercial purposes. Legal counsel cautioned the Board that if you allow
commercial activities, then you might be opening up the hall to uses that would
not meet the Board’s approval. Supervisor Martin asked if instead of allowing
commercial uses, could the rental agreement be revised to only except the yoga
class. Trustee Wright suggested revising the rental agreement to read,
“exceptions based on Board approval.” Legal counsel recommended that the Board
define what is allowed then to go with the exception language.
Legal counsel will review the current rental hall agreement and make
recommendations for revision.
Trustee Wright made a motion that the Board go into closed session pursuant to
the Open Meetings Act, section 8d, to consider the purchase of real property
and to allow the recording secretary, Ernie St. Pierre and Jeff Bartram to be
present during closed session.
Roll Call: Trustee Wilbrink – Yes; Treasurer Leblanc- Yes; Trustee Wright-Yes;
Supervisor Martin-Yes; Clerk Zaban-Yes. Motion Passed 5-0.
JANUARY 18, 2005 -- CLOSED SESSION MEETING
Supervisor Martin reviewed the purpose of closed session was to review the
purchase of property on land contract from Frank Kolasa for the amount of
290,000 with payments of 30,000 down and two payments of 130,000 at the end of
the first and second year of the contract.
The Friends of the Library have put forward the down payment and the Foundation
agreed to the payment schedule using their 503c status.
The Township Board questioned who would be responsible for the two payments
should the Foundation not be able to make the payments using monies raised
through fundraising. Would the Township be responsible for those payments? Mr.
St. Pierre of the Library Foundation indicated that the Foundation didn’t even
know that the Township had to give approval for purchase or if the Township
would be responsible for payments should the Foundation default on the
contract.
Legal Counsel asked for clarification of how the Foundation came to purchase
the property in question. Mr. St. Pierre indicated that Mr. Kolasa had
contacted the Foundation some time ago regarding some property he may have
available. The land was not for sale, but he wanted to work with the Foundation
to come up with a contract that would be feasible for the Foundation. The
process has been going on for approximately 2 years. In the meantime, Mr.
Kolasa had listed the property for sale while the Foundation considered other
property. After many failed attempts to identify property, the Foundation went
back to Mr. Kolasa and worked out a contract that would fit within the
Foundation’s budget. The property has been appraised and the current house on
the property has been inspected.
Legal counsel confirmed that the Township Board is required to pass a
resolution authorizing the Foundation to purchase property. The second issue is
does the Township, and the other municipalities, want to assume financial
responsibility if the Foundation defaults. The answer may be that the purchase
contract has a clause that states, “in the event of a default the
municipalities will not be responsible for any remaining costs.” Mr. St. Pierre
also offered another option. If the Friends of the Library purchased the
property instead of the Foundation, then approval or responsibility of the
Township and municipalities could be avoided. Trustee Wright indicated that
because of the short timeline, February 15, and without discussion with the
other municipalities, then exclusion language within the contract may be the
best option.
The Board requested Legal Counsel to contact Mr. Kolasa to work out a contract
on behalf of the Township that would exclude the Township form any financial
responsibility in the event of a default in payment.
Trustee Wright made a motion to come out of close session. Trustee Wilbrink
seconded the motion and it passed unanimously.
Trustee Wilbrink made a motion to adjourn. Trustee Wright seconded the motion
and it passed it unanimously.

UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Pebblebrook Campfire
Supervisor Martin reviewed the steps taken to date in consideration of the
Pebblebrook Campfire Petition. Supervisor Martin presented legal counsel’s
recommendations for fees and ordinance revision. The Ordinance revision would
include additional restrictions for Pebblebrook as follows:
a.   No burning when winds are over 10 mph
b.   Initial burn permit required
c.   Approved devices not to exceed 36 inches in diameter and equipped with a
spark arrester
d.   One time physical inspection by Township with fee of $25.
Treasurer LeBlanc submitted a revision to the ordinance to be incorporated in
“c” that read as follows: “In-ground fire rings or fire pits are not permitted
in Pebblebrook.” Discussion followed regarding the need to be specific
regarding the type of fire unit to be used whether in-ground, aboveground, or
aboveground with legs. There was also discussion regarding assessing a fee and
the need for a physical inspection.
Heather DeRath (4708 Sandstone Dr.): Expressed her concern for above ground
devices (e.g., the storage, location, etc.) versus below ground. She indicated
that when the petitioners signed the petition, they were not signing in belief
that there would be cost or fees associated with having a campfire.
George Durak (116 Feldspar Dr.): Reminded the Board that at the facilitator
meeting there was general agreement that the campfires would be above ground
with a spark arrestor for safety.
Ruth Templeton (1435 Epley Rd.): Offered that a fee, in her opinion, would be
unreasonable.
Supervisor Martin stated that she was not in favor of the fee since all other
burn permits were free.
Gary Gillespie (4701 Jadestone): Countered that a fee is not discriminatory
because their subdivision is unique to the Township and for safety reasons,
restrictions are needed.
Walt Aven expressed concern for an inspection and any liability that would
create for the Township.
Clerk Zaban made a motion to accept the Burn Ordinance as submitted; to delete
“d” and revise a-c as follows:
a.   No burning when winds are over 10 mph.
b.   Initial burn permit issued after Township inspection.
c.   Approved devices not to exceed 36 inches in diameter; equipped with a
spark arrester; and in-ground fire rings or fire pits are not permitted.
Trustee Wright seconded the motion and it passed unanimously.
Budget 2005-2006
Trustee Wright a motion to accept the budget as printed and dated 2/15/05.
Trustee Wilbrink seconded the motion and it passed unanimously.

consistent. Treasurer LeBlanc added that the auditor Bill Tucker said the last
time a change was made it was something done retroactively. Treasurer LeBlanc
discussed the history of the discrepancy and how it may have occurred.
Treasurer LeBlanc commented on the possibility of changing accounting software
programs to one that is dedicated to government units. He said he had
researched different software programs and found that QuickBooks was very
inexpensive in comparison. He said the BS & A software package costs $15,400.00
to purchase. One day of training costs $800. QuickBooks Pro 2005 is $600.00 for
a five user license. He added that there is an online QuickBooks service that
costs $30.00/month for 10 users plus free upgrades and more benefits. Treasurer
LeBlanc said that he is not supporting any change from QuickBooks but feels
that Teach-U-Comp is not adequate for the Township needs. Treasury needs more
intense training.
Treasurer LeBlanc said that the auditor charges $90 per hour and obviously will
find stuff quicker than the Township staff and may also find patterns of things
the staff are doing wrong and that we can correct, but the auditor can't
guarantee he will find the discrepancy problem. He said that we haven't
reconciled the general fund account. He said that if we choose to write off the
approximate $1700., a similar glitch in QuickBooks may occur some time later.
Supervisor Martin made a motion to instruct Treasurer LeBlanc to write off this
amount to adjust for the discrepancy.
Trustee Wright supports the motion.
Treasurer LeBlanc commented that the auditor advised to double check, and
during the initial phase of researching the problem Treasurer LeBlanc and staff
were able to reduce the discrepancy amount by about $25. He added that there
may be a special way to adjust this so that we don't lose the money.
Trustee Wilbrink suggested amending the motion to contact the auditor to
properly change the discrepancy. Supervisor Martin accepted that amendment.
Trustee Wright agreed.
Treasurer LeBlanc added that he would attach a letter to the document in the
general fund to inform the auditor.
Motion passed unanimously.

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes 4/19/05. 
Planning Commissioner Chair, Bob Hayes, reported that there was a public
hearing conducted to rezone Mr. Joseph Perkin’s 38 acres parcel on Haslett Road
from RE to AG-C. The deliberation is scheduled for 5/17/05. There was a public
hearing called for proposed text revisions to the subdivision control
ordinance. The proposed zoning ordinance text amendments were tabled until the
state’s revisions are finalized. A workshop meeting was scheduled and held on
April 26, 2005, to review the community survey. At the April 26, 2005, workshop
there was general consensus by the Planning Commissioners that the residents
have indicated through the survey that the current master plan accurately
reflects Township future development. Therefore, there is no need to revise
future development strategies in the Master Plan. It only needs to be updated
in regards to census data, etc. McKenna and Associates have been asked to
revise the Master Plan Revision Timeline to reflect this decision.
Rifle Club
Trustee Wilbrink reported that the Rifle Club’s membership has doubled. Due to
the increased membership they have increased their hours by 1 hour on both
Saturday and Sunday. Bill Hamilton, Club Board Member, commented on the Club’s
desire to meet the needs of their membership and their neighbors. To neither
Trustee Wilbrink or Bob Hamilton’s knowledge is there a written agreement
between the Club and the Township. Trustee Wilbrink will explore the idea of a
written agreement.
Gaming License
Rex Ellsworth, representative of the Kathy Ellsworth Scholarship Funds Inc.,
presented a request to conduct Texas Holdem Tournaments up to four times a year
to be held at Dietz Pool. All the money goes to the scholarship funds.
Currently, they hold a golf outing and this event would be an additional source
for raising scholarship funds. Before the state will issue a gaming license,
the Township must pass a resolution approving this request. A license has to be
applied for every event, but the resolution will allow them to renew the
license each time they have an event.
Trustee Wilbrink made a motion to pass a resolution to read:
The Williamstown Township Board of Directors resolved at their regular meeting
of May 10, 2005, that the Kathy Ellsworth Scholarship Funds, Inc. has approval
to run a Texas Holdem Tournament up to four times per year within the Township
of Williamstown.
Trustee Wright seconded the motion and a roll call was conducted:
Trustee Wilbrink:       Yes
Treasurer LeBlanc:      Yes
Trustee Wright:      Yes
Supervisor Martin:      Yes
Clerk Zaban:       Yes
The motion passed 5 to 0.

1835 Epley Road
Supervisor Martin reviewed the status of this complaint. Constable Dahlstrom
reported that some items of complaint have been moved since the 10 am walk
through this morning of April 17, 2005, but the property is still not in
compliance with Township ordinance. Supervisor Martin asked Mr. Stevens to
respond to the complaint. Mr. Stevens indicated that he would continue to bring
the property into compliance with Township ordinance with the exception of the
lumber, which is for his personal use and not for use by the construction
company. He indicated that he has a temporary permit to keep a trailer on the
property through December 1, 2005. He has posted a bond as surety. Supervisor
Martin asked if Mr. Stevens could bring the property into Township ordinance
compliance within the next 24 hours?
Craig Wedge (1861 Epley Rd.): Provided public comment regarding this complaint
as stated in his letter dated May 9, 2005. He indicated that construction on
the property has not been stopping by 8:00 pm; commercial construction
equipment is on site and travels up and down the road day and night; and there
is a fuel tank on the property that could be a hazard. In addition, he has
spoken with the county weigh master and has learned that if Mr. Stevens
continues to run a construction business from his property, he may have to
provide a surety bond to the County for road maintenance.
Richard Foster (1857 Epley Rd.): Provided public comment regarding this
complaint. He indicated that he is subject to heavy equipment noise daily; that
the property has been out of Township compliance since last year and feels that
Mr. Stevens attempts to justify the equipment for personal use is a façade and
should not be continued. He believes the Township has ordinances to control
this activity and that he sould should be given an end date when he can expect
these activities to stop.
Richard Williams (1860 Epley Rd.): Asked for clarification regarding the use of
the barn and any variance request that may be pending regarding the barn.
Supervisor Martin indicated that the barn could only be used for personal use
unless Mr. Stevens seeks approval through the Planning Commission to house one
piece of heavy equipment. Supervisor Martin also reviewed the variance
procedures and indicated that to date no variance has been applied for on this
property.
Supervisor Martin read the zoning ordinance regarding rules of commercial
construction, temporary structures, and commercial use parking. She indicated
that Mr. Stevens has complied with the temporary structures ordinance. However,
if Mr. Stevens wants to house a piece of commercial equipment on the property,
he must obtain approval through the Planning Commission.
Supervisor Martin reviewed actions taken to date and asked the Board to
respond. Trustee Wilbrink asked Mr. Stevens when the equipment would be moved.
Mr. Stevens indicated that he has rented space to house his equipment and it
has already been moved to the new location. The only time a piece of commercial
equipment will be on the property is if it is for personal use or to conduct
maintenance on the vehicle. Trustee Wilbrink asked if the Board made a motion
to allow an extension to bring the property into compliance and if Mr. Stevens
does not comply by the deadline, then could the Township impose a fine against
Mr. Stevens? Supervisor Martin responded that if Mr. Stevens did not comply,
the next step would be to take legal action against Mr. Stevens for
noncompliance of Township ordinances.
Trustee Wilbrink made a motion to allow three more days (Friday at 10:00 am,
May 13, 2005) to bring the property into Township ordinance compliance. Mr.
Stevens must also seek Planning Commission approval to bring one piece of heavy
equipment in excess of 1 ton onto his property per zoning ordinance section
4.01e. Mr. Stevens is to cease his commercial business activity from his
property unless otherwise approved through the Planning Commission. Should Mr.
Stevens fail to comply with Township ordinances, the Board authorizes legal
action to be taken against Mr. Stevens. Trustee Wright seconded the motion and
the motion passed unanimously.

Planning Commission Meeting minutes 5/17/05
Planning Commission chair, Bob Hayes, reported that the Planning Commission
deliberated on Joseph D. Perkins’ rezoning request from RE to AG-C and made a
recommendation that the Board approve the rezoning. Supervisor Martin indicated
that Mr. Perkins will be seeking a variance before requesting Board approval of
the rezone.
Mr. Hayes reported that there was a Public Hearing and Deliberation for the
Subdivision Control Ordinance. He indicated that these changes are in
compliance with state law, so there was little discussion. The Planning
Commission made a recommendation that the Board approve the changes. He
indicated that the only dissent was that these changes are mandated by the
State and there is no choice in accepting them.

UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Audit
Bill Tucker, Abraham and Gaffney. Reviewed a letter dated 6/2/05 from Aaron
Stevens, Principle CPA, regarding reasons for why they cannot complete the
2003-04 Annual Audit. The reasons reviewed were:
∙   Beginning fund balances for the General Fund and the Cemetery Fund do not
agree with the ending fund balances reported in the audited financial
statements for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2004.
∙   Several receipt transactions have been inappropriately posted by the
Treasurer to a line item on the General Fund Balance Sheet titled “service
receivable.” That line item total was a negative (credit balance) $133,453 as
of March 31, 2005. These receipts should have posted as a debit to cash (i.e.,
the “Bank One” line item in QuickBooks) and a credit to various revenue line
items (i.e., “Sales and Use Tax,” Township Levy,” etc.).
∙   Several other asset line items on the Balance Sheets also have negative
balances.
∙   Several liability line items on the Balance Sheets have negative balances.
∙   It is my understanding that the Treasurer has not formally reconciled the
bank statements with the general ledger for the months of November 2004 through
April 2005. The timely reconciliation of the bank statements with the general
ledger is an extremely important internal control. A breakdown of such an
internal control increases the Township’s susceptibility for fraud. The
Township Board must realize and accept that a greater risk in safeguarding
assets will exist if the monthly bank statements are not reconciled with the
general ledger in a timely manner.
Mr. Tucker indicated that the issues outlined in their letter are not all
inclusive and there could be other errors. Given the current condition of the
financial records, Abraham and Gaffney is unable to suggest the necessary
journal entries to be posted and still maintain a level of independence that
would allow them to conduct the audit. Therefore, they suggest the Township
consider contracting a consultant to assist with the various financial
reporting and they return to audit when the records are reconciled. He
indicated that the final audit is due to the state by 9/30/05.
Treasurer Leblanc made a motion to hire a consultant to assist with the various
financial reporting as stated in Abraham and Gaffney’s letter dated 6/2/05 and
to scheduled training to be paid from the contingency budget. Trustee Wilbrink
supported the motion.
Discussion on the motion: Supervisor Martin suggested that the Board seek bids
for training and review the budget for funding. Treasurer LeBlanc asked if the
consultants could train while they were reconciling the records? Mr. Tucker
indicated that would most likely be difficult to reconcile and train
simultaneously. Treasurer LeBlanc then suggested that the consultants keep a
log of errors so that training areas could be identified.
Trustee Wilbrink amended the motion to have the Clerk and Treasurer determine a
consultant to assist with the various financial reporting as stated in Abraham
and Gaffney’s letter dated 6/2/05 and to seek training at a later date.
Treasurer Leblanc supported the motion.
There was no discussion on the amended motion and it passed unanimously.

The resolution would read:
At a regularly scheduled meeting of the Township Board of the Township of
Williamstown, Ingham County Michigan, held in the Board Room of the Township at
4990 N. Zimmer Road, Williamston, Michigan, 48895-9609, on Tuesday, July 19,
2005, at ________ pm, there were:
   PRESENT:
   ABSENT:
At a said meeting of the Township Board, the following Resolution was offered
by member _____________ and supported by member ___________________.
WHEREAS, Al LeBlanc is a Williamstown Township Board Member and is the duly
elected Treasurer of Williamstown Township, and
WHEREAS, The Board has received various complaints from Township employees and
Board Members that Mr. LeBlanc has engaged in a pattern of abusive or abrasive
conduct. On March 29, 2005 the Township Board responded by requesting its legal
counsel to conduct an investigation into the various complaints. A written
legal opinion with detailed factual findings was placed on the record at the
June 21, 2005, Board meeting, and
WHEREAS, according to the factual investigation, Mr. LeBlanc’s alleged behavior
has resulted in complaints made by Township employees and Trustees. Certain
employees have expressed to Township officials their anxiety and apprehension
of being left alone with Mr. LeBlanc in the Township offices due to his angry
and unpredictable outbursts, and
WHEREAS, for the reasons more fully detailed in the aboved-mentioned legal
opinion and factual investigation, the Board finds that Mr. LeBlanc has
demonstrated an inability to work effectively with Township employees. He has
engaged in episodes of verbally abusive and physically threatening behavior
during confrontations with certain Township employees and Board Members, and
WHEREAS, the Board finds that Mr. LeBlanc has engaged in objectionable and
inappropriate behavior unbecoming to his elected position of Treasurer and
detrimental to the governance of Williamstown Township, and
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Williamstown Township Board does hereby
publicly censure Township Treasurer Al LeBlanc for his misconduct as
Williamstown Township Treasurer.
Trustee Wright seconded the motion.

National City Bank is approved as a Township depository. He also stated that
currently all Township CD’s are a one year investment and he would suggest
laddering the CDs so they do not all come due at the same time. Investing for
15 months could do this. The Board also needs to consider an updated investment
policy.
Treasurer LeBlanc made a motion to authorized cashing cash the Capitol National
Bank CD upon its maturity and move it to the general fund. When National City
Bank becomes an approved depository, then invest the funds for 11 months. Roll
over the Flagstar Bank CD upon maturity for 12months. Trustee Wilbrink seconded
the motion.
Discussion: Trustee Wilbrink asked for clarification regarding a 12 month
investment with Flagstar Bank when he is suggesting staggering the CDs.
Treasurer LeBlanc indicated that, depending on when you invest, they may have
incentives for different months of investment.
Treasurer LeBlanc amended the motion to authorize flexibility in how many
months to invest based on the best deal (e.g., National City up to 12 months
and Flagstar up to 12 to 15 months or more) and to secure a signed
disclaimer receipt of the existing investment policy for from National City
Bank if our money is invested with them.
Discussion on the amended motion: Clerk Zaban asked if Capital National Bank is
aware that the money will be cashed and have they been given the opportunity to
match the rates of other banks. Treasurer LeBlanc indicated that they have.
Motion passed unanimously.

Attorney Expenses
Trustee Wilbrink introduced this agenda item by asking each Board member to
suggest ways in which the Board can contain legal costs.
There was Board consensus that legal costs need to be contained. However, each
year legal costs are an estimate from year to year and when you have a large
issue or legal action then those estimates may not be good. Supervisor Martin
reviewed the average legal cost from 1997 to 2000 to be $42,190 and 2000 to
2004 to be $25,780 and indicated that the current legal costs are not out of
line in comparison to these averages.
Trustee Wilbrink gave specific examples of legal cost related to Treasurer
LeBlanc and questioned those costs. Supervisor Martin responded that the Board
has to rely on their legal counsel and their advice/judgment in those type of
matters because of any future litigation and their ability to defend those
issues. She also cited recent court cases that would support the Board’s
decision to seek legal advice and incur cost relating to the LeBlanc matter.
Trustee Wilbrink indicated that he is not questioning the need for legal
advice, but he would suggest that in the future the Board should try and call
the MTA before seeking legal counsel.
Trustee Wilbrink proposed that any future legal expenses be approved by the
Board. Supervisor Martin responded by indicating that all complaints do come to
the Board before any major legal action is taken.
Clerk Davis indicated that part of the solution to a problem is recognizing the
problem. She suggested that the Board agrees that legal cost are currently over
budget; the Board agrees to contain future legal costs; and when preparing next
year’s legal expenses the Board can look at other options.
Supervisor Martin will bring complaints to the Board as in the past. However,
there are other sensitive and/or timely matters that need immediate action such
as contracts, FOIA requests, etc. Trustee Wright and Trustee Wilbrink agreed
that those issues do not need specific board approval. She suggested that Board
members individually review the invoices monthly and notify her of any
questions regarding the charges.
Clerk Davis asked if it is possible to do a mid-year budget review? Supervisor
Martin indicated that we are heading into the budget planning process and will
be reviewing the budget in preparation for approving next year’s budget. This
process will start in November in which the Board will be reviewing this budget
to recommend approval for 2006-07.
Trustee Wilbrink suggest special meetings to approve charges if time is an
issue. Supervisor Martin responded that special meetings are a possibility and
would call for if needed for large or unusual legal needs. Trustee Wilbrink
suggested that a special meeting currently needs to be called to review a
current FOIA request. He will let Supervisor Martin know when the FOIA is due
so a special meeting can be called.

Audit
Aaron Stevens, of Abraham and Gaffney, presented the 2004-05 Audit to the
Board. He indicated that there were challenges with the audit because of the
condition of the records. The Audit was postponed while the Township hired an
outside accountant to clean up the records for audit. He highlighted some key
points in the Financial Statements. He indicated that the Township is
financially sound, but needs to reconcile the accounts on a timely basis,
segregate duties in the cash receipting process, and work on their internal
controls as stated in the management letter. Reconciling the accounts on a
timely basis is the most important aspect.
Trustee Wilbrink asked if the Board needs to address any issues, or is that a
Clerk and Treasurer Function. Aaron responded that those that handle the day-
to-day operations should address any stated issues. Trustee Wilbrink questioned
why budget amendments were not posted in the financial statements. Aaron
responded that the financial statements do not show that level of detail.
Trustee Wilbrink also questioned why the auditors communicate with the
Supervisor and not the Clerk or Treasurer regarding the audit. Aaron responded
that the Supervisor is the one person who has consistently been available for
communications and therefore has become their contact person.
Ruth Templeton (1435 Epley Rd.): Provided public comment regarding last year’s
audit and the similarities of this year’s audit. She questioned why the
auditors would allow the time to clean up the books and not just report the
auditable status to the State. Aaron responded that their report is sent to the
State, but it is at the Board’s discretion to hire an outside accountant, not
the auditors.
Treasurer LeBlanc reported that the Clerk and Treasurer are working together to
identify any training that is needed and are willing to look at internal
controls as recommended in the audit.

LIBRARY AUTHORITY
Supervisor Martin explained that the authority has determined that if this idea
were to go forward, at some point the financial aspect would have to be
considered. All three entities would have to take the same financial steps,
whether it be a millage vote by the people, special assessments or to float a
bond and make the payments using General Fund money. Supervisor Martin stated
that the Townships approximate responsibility, if Bonds were let, would be
$550,000. Williamston has said they are in favor of the Bond/General Fund
repayment scenario, and Supervisor Martin felt this procedure, or the special
assessment, would be the best way for the Township. Leblanc urged fiscal
conservatism, stating that the Township would have additional General Fund
expenditures in the future including the addition of Board members. LeBlanc
further offered that it would be best to put a millage to the vote of the
people and let them decide, or perhaps use a special assessment for the
financing. Davis was in favor of a millage vote and Wright preferred the Bond/
General Fund repayment. Supervisor Martin would express the thoughts of the
Board to the Authority at their next meeting.

The Task Force also submitted concerns regarding the language of the Township

easily enforced by sheriffs and other law enforcement personnel. Discussion

issue with Lansing and that it is very involved and was the subject of lengthy

regarding this matter and return for future consideration and deliberation.
Natural Beauty Roads
Davis explained that the designating of certain country roads in the Township
as “Natural Beauty Roads” would be consistent with the preservation of the
rural character of the Township and is currently a desire as stated in the
Master Plan. Once this designation is assigned, the County Road Commission must
take all measures to preserve native vegetation in a natural beauty road right-
of-way from destruction or damage while performing maintenance tasks. A Task
Force needs to be assembled to identify the roads that should receive this
designation, and then petition the Road Commission to follow through with the
designation.
Motion by Wright to request that the Planning Commission assemble said Task
Force and allow this process to begin.
Supported by LeBlanc.
Carried unanimously.

DECEMBER 9, 2005
PRESENT:    Supervisor Martin, Trustee Wright, Trustee Wilbrink, and Clerk
Davis.
ABSENT:    Treasurer LeBlanc
A special meeting of the Williamstown Township Board was called to order at 8:
08 a.m. by Supervisor Martin to review poverty exemptions and the applicability
of social security income in determining eligibility. Supervisor Martin
confirmed with MTA that social security income is to be use in determining
eligibility. Using the current federal guidelines and applying social security
income to those guidelines would make all applicants ineligible for the
exemption. The federal guidelines are the minimum guidelines that a township
can use. A township can increase those levels at their discretion. Therefore,
Supervisor Martin proposed that Williamstown Township increase their guidelines
by 50%. Raising the guidelines by 50% would qualify each applicant except one.
Trustee Wilbrink made a motion to set the poverty guidelines at 150% of the
federal poverty guidelines with a note that the Board of Review has discretion
to apply exceptions to deviate from the policies and guidelines as stated in
Act 206, Section 7u. (5) of 1893. Trustee Wright seconded the motion.
There was no discussion on the motion and it passed unanimously.
Supervisor Martin also discussed the procedures for accepting poverty exemption
applications. She noted that each applicant should be given the Township’s
policy and guidelines at application and that only the Supervisor and/or public
notary is authorized to sign the applications. She indicated that she was
unclear of the current procedures and that she had not signed the applications.
Supervisor Martin indicated that Treasurer LeBlanc had signed her name without
her knowledge or consent.
There was no public comment.
The meeting adjourned at 8:34 a.m.
Cindy Davis
Township Clerk

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION 43
January 17, 2006
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
Be it resolved that all bank account and money market account signature cards
will be submitted with four authorized signers. These signers will be the
current Clerk and Deputy Clerk, and the current Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer.
It will be the policy of this township that any check or withdrawal order will
require two signatures: one from the Clerk department and one from the Treasury
department, and one of these two signatures must be that of the Clerk or the
Treasurer. Because of her resignation as Deputy Treasurer, former Deputy
Treasurer Gwen Chirico-Brandon’s name will be removed from the signature cards.
Whenever possible, investment accounts such as bank certificates of deposit
will be set up as book entry instruments in the name of Williamstown Township
and without signature cards. New signature cards will be submitted with the
following authorized signers:
Clerk: Cindy S. Davis       Deputy Clerk: Robert J. Cwiertniewicz
Treasurer: Albert LeBlanc Deputy Treasurer: Harold P. Husse
Supported by: Trustee Martin Wright
Roll call vote:
Supervisor Mickey Martin: yes
Clerk Cindy Davis: yes
Treasurer Albert LeBlanc: yes
Trustee Frans Wilbrink: yes
Trustee Martin Wright: yes
The Supervisor declared the resolution: Adopted

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #46
CREDIT CARD USE POLICY
Resolution by Board Member Cindy Davis.
   WHEREAS, Public act 266 of 1995 authorizes a township to be a party to a
credit card arrangement if the township board has adopted by resolution a
written policy governing The control and use of credit cards, and
   WHEREAS, the Williamstown Township Board deems that it is in the best
interest of the township to make certain financial transactions by using a
credit card as described in the Act.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the following policy shall govern the use of
credit cards:
a)   At the discretion of the Supervisor, credit cards may be issued to the
following individuals with the following limits:
·   Sexton - $500.00
·   Maintenance/Caretaker - $100.00
·   Supervisor - $2500.00
·   Clerk - $2500.00
·   Treasurer - $2500.00
b)   The Township Clerk is responsible for issuing, accounting for, monitoring,
retrieving and generally overseeing compliance with the townships credit card
policy.
c)   Township credit cards may be used only by an officer or employee of the
township for the purchase of goods or services for the official business of the
township. Employees involved in the purchasing process may not use credit cards
for any personal expenditure.
d)   Township officers and employees who use a township credit card shall, as
soon as possible, submit a copy of the vendor’s credit card slip to the
Township Clerk. If no credit card slip was obtained that described the
transaction, the employee shall submit a signed voucher that shows the name of
the vendor or entity from which goods or services were purchased, the date and
amount of the transaction, the official business that required the transaction.
All credit card slips shall also include this information. Vouchers shall also
include a statement explaining the reason that a credit card slip was not
obtained.
e)   An officer or employee who has been issued a credit card shall return said
credit card to the Township Clerk upon termination of his or her employment or
service with the township.
f)   The Township Clerk shall maintain a list of all credit cards owned by the
township, along with the name of the officer and employee who has been issued
the credit card, the credit limit established, the date issued and that the
employee has received and read a copy of this policy. The Township Clerk shall
review each credit card statement as soon as possible to ensure that
transactions comply with this policy. Any transactions that appear on the
statements that are not documented with a credit card slip or signed voucher
shall be immediately investigated. Transactions that do not appear to comply
with this policy shall be reported to the Board.
g)   The Township Board shall not approve a payment to the entity issuing the
credit card until all transactions have been verified including the approval of
all transaction invoices if issued.
h)   The balance including interest due on an extension of credit under the
credit card arrangement shall be paid for within sixty days of the initial
statement date.
i)   Officers and employees who use a Township credit card in a manner contrary
to this policy shall be subject to the following disciplinary actions, as
deemed appropriate by the Township Board: verbal counseling, written reprimand,
suspension, termination and reimbursement to the Township for all unauthorized
expenditures. (The above disciplinary procedure shall not supercede the
Township’s at-will policy of the employee manual.)
This resolution replaces Resolution #28, previously adopted by the Township
Board.
Seconded by Board Member Mickey S.Martin
Yeas: Davis, Martin
Nays: Wilbrink, LeBlanc
RESOLUTION FAILS

Social Security Resolution
Discussion ensued with the following resolution being offered.
Motion by LeBlanc to adopt the following Social Security Number Privacy Policy
and Procedure.
Policy: It is the policy of the Township to protect the confidentiality of
Social Security numbers obtained in the ordinary course of township business
from employees, vendors, contractors, customers or others. No person shall
knowingly obtain, store, transfer, use, disclose, or dispose of a Social
Security number that the Township obtains or possesses except in accordance
with the Act and this Privacy Policy.
Applies To:   The Township of Williamstown restricts access to information or
documents containing Social Security numbers to Township staff members who have
a legitimate Township business reason to access such information or documents.
The Township Clerk is responsible for implementing this restriction through
training and oversight procedures.
Purpose: The Township of Williamstown (the "Township") is required by the
Michigan Social Security Number Privacy Act, Public Act 454 of 2004, MCL 445.81
et seq., (the "Act") to create a privacy policy concerning the Social Security
numbers that it possesses or obtains.
Pursuant to the Act, the privacy policy must at least:
a. Ensure to the extent practicable the confidentiality of the Social Security
numbers.
b. Prohibit unlawful disclosure of the Social Security numbers.
c. Limit who has access to information or documents that contain the Social
Security numbers.
d. Describe how to properly dispose of documents that contain the Social
Security numbers.
e. Establish penalties for violation of the privacy policy.
This Privacy Policy sets forth the Township's policies and procedures regarding
how Social Security numbers are obtained, stored, transferred, used, disclosed
and disposed.
Procedure:
a. Obtaining Social Security Numbers. Social Security numbers should be
collected only where required by federal and state law or as otherwise
permitted by federal and state law for legitimate reasons consistent with this
Privacy Policy.
Legitimate reasons for collecting a Social Security number include, but are not
limited to:
·   Applicants may be required to provide a Social Security number for purposes
of a pre-employment background check.
·   Copies of Social Security cards may be obtained for purposes of verifying
employee eligibility for employment.
·   Social Security numbers may be obtained from employees for tax reporting
purposes, for new hire reporting, for purposes of enrollment in any Township
employee benefit plans or to authorize township officials and employees to sign
township checks.
·   Social Security numbers may be obtained from creditors or vendors for tax
reporting purposes.
·   Social Security numbers are required on Principal Residence Affidavit
forms.
b. Public Display. All or more than four sequential digits of a Social Security
number shall not be placed on identification cards, badges, time cards,
employee rosters, bulletin boards, permits, licenses or any other materials or
documents designed for public display. Documents, materials or computer screens
that display all or more than four sequential digits of a Social Security
number shall be kept out of public view at all times. Public display includes
open view on a computer device, computer network, website or other electronic
medium or device, to members of the public or in a public manner. All of the
foregoing comprise prohibited disclosures and shall not be so displayed by any
township staff members.
c. Account Numbers. All or more than four sequential digits of a Social
Security number shall not be used as a primary account number for an
individual.
d. Computer Transmission. All or more than four sequential digits of a Social
Security number shall not be used or transmitted on the Internet or on a
computer system or network unless the connection is secure or the transmission
is encrypted.
e. Mailed Documents. Township documents containing all or more than four
sequential digits of a Social Security number shall only be sent in cases where
state or federal law, rule, regulation, or court order or rule authorizes,
permits or requires that a Social Security number appear in the document.
Documents containing all or more than four sequential digits of a Social
Security number, that are sent through the mail, shall not reveal the number
through the envelope window or otherwise be visible from outside the envelope
or package.
f. Freedom of Information Act. Where all or more than four sequential digits of
a Social Security number are contained within a document subject to release
under the Freedom of Information Act, the Social Security number shall be
redacted or otherwise rendered unreadable before the document or copy of a
document is disclosed.
g. Storage. All documents containing Social Security numbers shall be stored in
a physically secure manner. Social Security numbers shall not be stored on
computers or other electronic devices that are not secured against unauthorized
access.
h. Access to Social Security Numbers. Only personnel who have legitimate
business reasons to know will have access to records containing Social Security
numbers. The department heads having access to records containing Social
Security numbers shall determine which other personnel within their departments
have a legitimate reason in the Township's ordinary course of business to have
access to such Social Security numbers. Personnel using records containing
Social Security numbers must take appropriate steps to secure such records when
not in immediate use.
i. Authorized Uses. This policy does not prohibit the use of Social Security
numbers where the use is authorized or required by state or federal statute,
rule, regulation, or court order or rule, or pursuant to legal discovery or
process.
This policy does not prohibit the administrative use of Social Security numbers
in the ordinary course of business, by a person or a vendor or contractor of a
person to do any of the following.
1.   Verify an individual’s identity, identify an individual, or accomplish
another similar administrative purpose related to an existing or proposed
account, transaction, product, service, or employment.
2.   Investigate an individual’s claim, credit, criminal, or driving history.
3.   Detect, prevent, or deter identity theft or another crime.
4.   Lawfully pursue or enforce the Township’s legal rights.
5.   Provide or administer employee or health insurance or membership benefits,
claims, or retirement programs.
6.   Other exceptions that are approved by the Supervisor or Clerk and that
comply with state or federal law.
This policy also does not prohibit the use of Social Security numbers for
criminal investigation purposes or the provision of Social Security numbers to
a Title IV-D agency (child support/support orders), law enforcement agency,
court, or prosecutor as part of a criminal investigation or prosecution.
j. Disposal of Social Security Numbers. Documents that contain Social Security
numbers shall be properly destroyed when those documents no longer need to be
retained pursuant to Township document retention policies. Paper documents
containing Social Security numbers will be shredded. Electronic files
containing Social Security numbers will be deleted and the recycle bin will be
emptied.
k. Unauthorized Use or Disclosure of Social Security Numbers. The Township
shall take reasonable measures to enforce this Privacy Policy and to correct
and prevent the reoccurrence of any known violations. Any employee, who
knowingly obtains, uses or discloses Social Security numbers for unlawful
purposes or contrary to the requirements of this privacy policy shall be
subject to discipline up to and including discharge. Additionally, certain
violations of the Act carry criminal and/or civil sanctions. The Township will
cooperate with appropriate law enforcement or administrative agencies in the
apprehension and prosecution of any person who knowingly obtains, uses or
discloses Social Security numbers through the Township for unlawful purposes.
l. Violations. Violations of this Policy may result in disciplinary action, up
to and including dismissal. Individuals who violate this Policy may also be
subject to the civil and criminal penalties provided for in the Michigan Social
Security Number Privacy Act (PA 454 of 2004), MCL 445.81 – 445.86
Questions regarding this Policy may be directed to the Township Clerk.
Seconded by Wilbrink.
Carried unanimously.

Williamstown Township Resolution # 50
Retaining Local Control of Cable Franchising
Resolution by Board Member Frans Wilbrink
WHEREAS, it is the mission of Williamstown Township, Ingham County, Michigan to
preserve and protect the rights of all its citizens;
WHEREAS, the existing federal and local cable franchising rules have resulted
in $100 billion investment in advanced telecommunications services nationwide
and formed the basis for a national policy of broadband (high-speed internet);
WHEREAS, Williamstown Township strongly supports the provisions contained
within the federal 1984 Cable Act including the anti-discrimination sections
that have ensured against a 19th century world of digital “haves and have-nots”
and ensured that Americans of all incomes, races and backgrounds can have equal
access to television and broadband service as the information and communication
that it provides becomes more essential in our daily lives;
WHEREAS, the current federal cable law has been effective in ensuring robust
build-out of broadband networks and in protecting against cherry-picking of
communities, and should be applied to both existing cable providers and new
entrants into the cable marketplace;
WHEREAS, some telecommunications companies that now seek to enter the cable
marketplace are attempting to gain a competitive advantage through federal and
state preemption of local authority and are seeking to undermine the anti-
discrimination and build-out requirements that have been a bipartisan
cornerstone of our telecommunications laws for decades;
WHEREAS, these telecommunications companies are attempting to label their
service as “video service” to bypass traditional cable laws and regulations,
and have encouraged the introduction of legislation in Congress and in various
states to attempt to circumvent federal and local regulations;
WHEREAS, in Michigan, legislation has been introduced in the House of
Representatives, HB 5895, and in the Senate, SB 1157, that would strip away
local cable franchising authority and hand control over to the State of
Michigan (secretary of state);
WHEREAS, Williamstown Township strongly supports competition for telephone,
broadband and video services, and recognizes that competition for such services
is growing rapidly and encourages that these new competitive services are
available to all its citizens;
WHEREAS, new entrants into the video marketplace face no unreasonable barriers
to entry as federal law expressly provides that cable franchises not be
exclusive and that local governments have franchised numerous second cable
providers throughout the country;
WHEREAS, excluding local elected officials from the franchise process as some
telecommunications carriers and HB 5895 and SB 1157 suggests would be harmful
to the citizens of Williamstown Township who use local franchise rules to
ensure that cable services are provided to everyone, that service territory
appropriately covers key areas for economic development and public safety and
other community needs are met;
WHEREAS, HB 5895 and SB 1157 does not permit a build-out requirement which will
allow companies entering the cable market to cherry-pick high-value residents
only, leaving low-value residents without service;
WHEREAS, Williamstown Township agrees that government policies should not
determine winners and losers in the marketplace and thus the rules governing
local franchises, including rules regarding build-out of networks, should apply
to all cable providers equally;
WHEREAS, HB 5895 and SB 1157 would drastically limit or abolish the important
role of local government franchising and weaken the non-discrimination
provisions of the 1984 Cable Act that protects the interests of all citizens
and promotes competition.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that Williamstown Township, Ingham County,
Michigan, strongly urges the Michigan Legislature to reject legislative
proposals such as HB 5895 and SB 1157 that abolish the role of local government
franchising and the ability of local governments to protect all citizens, that
do not allow for build-out requirements, and that ensure that non-
discrimination provisions of the 1984 Cable Act are met and promote competition
for all its citizens;
BE IT RESOLVED, Williamstown Township, Ingham County, Michigan supports
legislation which promotes competition in broadband and cable services for
everyone, recognizes and preserves local community needs, preserves local
control over franchising, prohibits redlining and other discriminatory
practices, and ensures that any new entrants into the cable market abide by the
same standards that current cable, broadband or multichannel video providers
live by.
Seconded by Board Member Cindy Davis.
Carried by the following vote.
 
Wilbrink LeBlanc Wright Martin Davis
Yes      Yes     Yes    Yes    Yes

National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System
Treasurer LeBlanc reported on an issue that involved the township’s application
for a NPDES permit in 2003. Former Treasurer Nancy Fink had submitted the
application in March 2003, but in March 2006 the Michigan Department of
Environmental Quality (MDEQ) sent the township a letter stating that the
application was incomplete, could not be approved, and that the township owed
them considerable additional material and two annual reports. LeBlanc said he
has spoken to a number of other township officials who are responsible for
NPDES and they have all recommended getting help either from a consulting firm
or by joining the Greater Lansing Regional Committee on Phase II Nonpoint
Source Pollution Prevention. LeBlanc suggested that the board hear
presentations from Brian Slater, an engineer who is handling NPDES for Woodhull
Township, a neighboring township; and from Erin Campbell, Coordinator for the
Greater Lansing Regional Committee. Supervisor Martin said she believed former
Treasurer Fink had worked with a consultant in preparing the original NPDES
filing and that that person should be contacted. Treasurer LeBlanc said that
Fink had indicated to him, while he was serving as her deputy, that she was not
working with a consultant but that he would search the files to see if there
was any record of a consultant and get back to the board. He will also bring a
proposal to the board on how best to resolve the NPDES compliance issue.
Supervisor Martin presented several informational items including: a checklist
for personal security from Central Security Alarm System, as well as an
announcement/application regarding an opening on the board of the Capital Area
District Library, MTA regional meeting and the Wheatfield Township Library
Authority vote was scheduled for April 11, 2006.
Discussion ensued regarding footnote c from the Treasurer’s Report, with
Treasurer LeBlanc explaining which of our deposits are protected by Federal
Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) insurance. Our Vanguard money market
account gives a high level of liquidity, but it is not covered by FDIC
insurance. LeBlanc believes that the Chase/Bank One sweep account now provides
all the liquidity we need, and it would be appropriate to close the Vanguard
account, put that money into three jumbo CD’s in local banks, and put the
amount remaining into the Chase/Bank One account. A jumbo CD is for $
100,000.00, the maximum amount covered in one bank in one account by the FDIC.
Because of this limit, we need a new bank for each new jumbo CD. Because of our
current deposits, it will be necessary to consider some additional banks as
approved depositories in order to completely liquidate the Vanguard account.
Motion by LeBlanc to liquidate the Vanguard account upon an approved depository
decision being made, and to deposit the funds into three jumbo certificates of
deposit and any remaining balance to be deposited in Bank One.
Seconded by Wright.
Carried unanimously.
 
Discussion ensued regarding footnote d with Clerk Davis questioning Treasurer
LeBlanc’s reference to QuickBooks. Treasurer LeBlanc stated that his note is
reconciling bank statements with checks and deposit slips, but not the general
ledger. Discussion continued regarding bank reconciliations, bank recordkeeping
procedures, the SWEEP account and auditor comments.

discussed, as well as a possible request to the various entities for minutes

approval of all expenditure over $200.00. Discussion ensued with Trustee
Wright, Supervisor Martin and Clerk Davis agreeing that there was no need for
approval because the departmental budget was approved at the budget hearing. If
there was no line item for a particular department for an expenditure such as
capital outlay, or if the department had exceeded its allotment of funds, then,
and only then, should the Board approve the expenditure. Trustee Wright stated
that there was no need to revisit something that was passed previously by the
Board.

Board to let the Treasurer and Clerk continue to work on these items and wait
for future progress reports.

that need improvement. Clerk Davis said that the checklist was a great tool and
encouraged its use.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION # 52
Resolution by Supervisor Martin.
A RESOLUTION ENDORSING AND SUPPORTING THE TRI-COUNTY REGIONAL PLANNING
COMMISSION’S REGIONAL GROWTH CHOICES FOR FUTURE PROJECT, REGIONAL LAND USE
VISION POLICY MAP, THEMES AND PRINCIPLES.
   WHEREAS, on December 28, 1973, the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission
was designated by the Governor of Michigan as the Metropolitan Planning
Organization for the Lansing Urbanized Area; and
   WHEREAS, the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission conducted analysis of
current regional trends in land use, growth, development, environmental
impacts, the efficiency and effectiveness of the transportation system,
obtained substantial public input and gave careful consideration to alternative
regional land use patterns; and
   WHEREAS, the Regional 2030 Transportation Plan adopted by Tri-County
Regional Planning Commission on October 26, 2005 re-endorses results from the
Regional Growth: Choices for Our Future project’s “Wise Growth” alternative as
directed by the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission on March 27, 2002,
confirmed by the Regional Growth Steering Committee on April 5, 2002 and as
adopted by the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission on March 26, 2003 in the
Regional 2025 Transportation Plan; and
   WHEREAS, the adopted Regional 2030 Transportation Plan is based on regional
socioeconomic forecasts approved by the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission
in December, 2001 with consideration being given to long term reallocation of
these forecasts to be more consistent with the adopted “Wise Growth” land use
alternative from the Regional Growth: Choices for Our Future project; and
   WHEREAS, the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission recognized regional
development, land use and implementing the adopted “Wise Growth” scenario is
the region’s highest priority issue in order to reduce congestion, maintain and
improve air quality, protect environmentally sensitive or agricultural lands,
continue to maintain and expand the regional economy, improve global
competitiveness, sustain quality of life of the region’s residents and is part
of their fiduciary responsibility to taxpayers in order to protect public
health, safety and welfare of the region’s residents; and
   WHEREAS, the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission has adopted policies to
evaluate all proposed future expenditures of federal funds and to establish
project priorities for use of federal funds based on the adopted alternative
for land use as shown on the “Wise Growth” policy map and which are consistent
with the adopted themes and principles as shown in the Regional Growth: Choices
for Our Future Summary Report for the Lansing Metropolitan Region dated
September, 2005 and on it’s accompanying Poster Plan as transmitted on January
20, 2006; and
   WHEREAS, the Williamstown Township Board is the duly constituted local
governmental policy making body for Williamstown Township and desires to
endorse and support the Regional Growth: Choices for Our Future themes,
principles and policy map which constitute the agreed on regional land use
vision in order to guide future regional growth and development; and
   WHEREAS, the Regional Growth project’s themes, principles and policy map are
intended to provide a compatible generalized regional framework to guide local
government land use plans and other decisions in order to preserve and protect
the public health, safety and welfare of the region’s residents consistent with
the Williamstown Township Board’s fiduciary responsibility to our citizens; and
   NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Williamstown Township Board does
endorse and support the Regional Growth: Choices for Our Future themes,
principles and policy map as depicted in “A Summary Report for the Lansing
Metropolitan Area” and on its accompanying Poster Plan are necessary to protect
public health, safety and welfare and are consistent with our fiduciary
responsibility to the taxpayers of Williamstown Township.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Williamstown Township Board does hereby
endorse and support said themes, principles and policy map as policies for
Williamstown Township.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that it is the policy of Williamstown Township that
these endorsed and supported themes, principles and policy map be referred to
staff and/or the Planning Commission for use in considering consistency of
future development, development decisions and other actions in local decision
making.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that it shall be the policy of Williamstown Township
to support and actively work with other local governments, agencies and the
Tri-County Regional Planning Commission to fully participate in considering
implementation of the Regional Growth: Choices for Our Future action plan and
in hosting related training and other activities as may be appropriate to fully
integrate our policies endorsing and supporting the regional land use vision
into the fabric of regional life.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Clerk is authorized to sign this resolution
and that it be transmitted to the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission,
adjacent governmental jurisdictions and other local, state and federal agencies
and representatives as appropriate.
Seconded by Clerk Davis.
Carried by the following vote.
   YES:       Supervisor Martin, Clerk Davis, Treasurer LeBlanc
    NO:       Trustee Wilbrink
    ABSENT:    Trustee Wright

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #53
RESOLUTION ON RECEIPTING OF CASH OR CHECK PAYMENTS
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
   WHEREAS, the Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham County, in exercising
its fiduciary responsibilities desires to safeguard the funds of the township.
   THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, That except for property tax payments, all
payments made in person to this township and accepted by an elected official or
member of the township staff, regardless of the amount of payment, will be
recorded in writing on a sequentially numbered triplicate receipt imprinted
with the name of the township. The original of this receipt will be offered to
the customer, the first copy will be kept with the payment, and the second copy
will be kept in the receipt book, which will be retained as a financial record
of the township. Taxpayers who pay property tax by U. S. Mail or by leaving
payment in the appropriate township drop box will receive an official property
tax receipt by mail. Taxpayers who pay property tax in the township office will
receive an official property tax receipt if a member of the Treasury department
is present to process the payment at the time it is made. If no member of the
Treasury department is present to process the payment, and if requested, the
taxpayer will be given a triplicate receipt by township staff, who must verify
the amount of payment actually received.  
Seconded by Clerk Davis.
Carried by the following vote:
 
Wilbrink LeBlanc Wright Martin Davis
Yes      Yes     Yes    Yes    Yes
 
Moved by Lablanc to authorize the purchase of a mail drop box # 2255 in
(aluminum or brass or ivory or green or bronze) finish ($ 100.00) with custom
engraving PROPERTY TAX ONLY – NO CASH ($ 20.00) together with locking
receptacle # 2256 in the same finish ($ 125.00) from Salsbury Industries. The
cost of buying and installing this through-the-wall mail drop assembly will be
charged to Account 101-294-980, Township Office, Capital Outlay, which has been
funded at $ 18,000.00 for the present fiscal year. The purpose of this mail
drop will be to receive property tax payments at times when the township office
is closed. Furthermore, installation costs of no more than $200.00 are also
authorized.
Seconded by Wilbrink.
Carried unanimously.
Moved by LaBlanc to authorize the purchase of a secure locking cash drawer with
insert from Office Max at a cost of no more than $ 160.00 and that the cost of
this purchase be charged to account 101-294-980 Township Office, Capital
Outlay.
Seconded by Wilbrink.
Carried unanimously.
