Tri-County Road Study Resolution
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION # 54
A RESOLUTION ENDORSING AND SUPPORTING
A LOCAL ROAD ASSET MANAGEMENT PILOT PROJECT
FOR PORTIONS OF INGHAM COUNTY.
Resolution by Supervisor Martin.
   WHEREAS, in 2002, the Michigan Legislature adopted Act 499, which amended
Section 9(a) of Public Act 51 (MCL 247.659a) to replace the requirement for
periodic needs studies by an on-going asset management process; and
   WHEREAS, the 2002 amendments to Section 9(a) of Public Act 51 also
established a clear need for the development of asset management programs for
local roads, as evidenced in the legislation creating the Transportation Asset
Management Council:
“In order to provide a coordinated, unified effort by the various roadway
agencies within the state, the transportation asset management council is
hereby created within the State Transportation Commission and is charged with
advising the commission on a statewide asset management strategy and the
processes and necessary tools needed to implement such a strategy beginning
with the federal-aid eligible highway system, and once completed, continuing on
with the county road and municipal systems, in a cost-effective manner;” and
   WHEREAS, a strong incentive towards the development of asset management
programs for local roads is further provided in Subsection 6 of Section 13 of
Public Act 51 (MCL 247.663), which indicates that:
“A city or village shall not transfer more than 25% of its annual major street
funding for the local street system unless it has adopted and is following an
asset management process for its major and local street systems;” and
   WHEREAS, Act 499 further requires regional transportation and Metropolitan
Planning Organizations to provide qualified technical assistance to the Asset
Management Council in fulfilling their responsibilities; and
   WHEREAS, on December 28, 1973, the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission
was designated by the Governor of Michigan as the Metropolitan Planning
Organization for the Lansing Urbanized Area; and
   WHEREAS, the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission has been working with
local governments and the Michigan Department of Transportation to collect
asset management data for all federal aid eligible routes in Clinton, Eaton and
Ingham County; and
   WHEREAS, the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission, working with the
Michigan State University Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering and
local governments in Ingham County, has developed an application to conduct a
pilot program of data collection for all local roads in Meridian, Williamstown,
Wheatfield and Leroy townships, the City of Williamston, Village of Webberville
and the Ingham County Road Commission (hereinafter referred to as the study
area) to be funded by the state Asset Management Council; and
   WHEREAS, having a comprehensive inventory of asset management data will
assist the Township of Williamstown in making informed decisions about managing
our transportation assets, and
   NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Township of Williamstown does hereby
endorse and support the application for local road pilot funds being submitted
by the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission to the Asset Management Council.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Township of Williamstown does hereby direct
our staff to cooperate and participate in data collection and related support
activities for said pilot project if it is funded by the Asset Management
Council.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that it is the intent of the Township of
Williamstown to receive such data and technical assistance made available
through this pilot project to assess conditions on our local street system and
to apply this information to decide strategies for managing our assets
consistent with the requirements of Act 499.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Township Clerk Cindy Davis is hereby authorized
to sign this resolution and transmit it to the Tri-County Regional Planning
Commission, the Asset Management Council and the other governments and agencies
in the study area as an indication that the Township of Williamstown supports
and endorses this proposed pilot asset management project for our local street
system.
Seconded by Trustee Wright.
Carried by the following vote.
YES: Supervisor Martin, Clerk Davis, Treasurer LeBlanc, Trustee Wright and
Trustee Wilbrink.
NO: None.
 
Approved Depositories Resolution
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION # 55
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
   WHEREAS, the Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham County, in exercising
its fiduciary responsibilities desires to safeguard the funds of the township
that may be invested from time to time, and
   WHEREAS, public Act 77 of 1989 (MCL 41.77) requires that the township board
designate the banks or depositories for the money belonging to the township,
including the time for which the deposits shall be made and all details for
carrying into effect the authority given in this act, and
   WHEREAS, Public Act 196 of 1997 (MCL 129.91, et seq) requires township
boards, in consultation with the township treasurer, to adopt an investment
policy, now
   THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, That this policy is applicable to all public funds
belonging to Williamstown Township and in the custody of the township
treasurer.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Williamstown Township treasurer is
authorized to manage funds belonging to the township, including depositing
funds in township board approved financial institutions and administration of
investments in conformance with MCL 41.77 and policies set forth in this
resolution.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the board approves the following institutions
as depositories of township funds: Bank One/Chase, Republic Bank, Independent
Bank, Vanguard Securities, Fifth/Third Bank, Capitol National Bank, Flagstar
Bank, Mason State Bank, Dart Bank, National City Bank; Charter One Bank,
National Association; Citizens Bank, and LaSalle Bank Midwest National
Association.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall recommend financial
institutions for approval for the safekeeping of township funds based on an
evaluation of the performance and solvency of the institution, as well as past
performance in exercising due care and prudence in managing the custody of
township funds held in trust, if applicable. The treasurer shall periodically
evaluate approved and potential financial depositories and shall make
recommendations as to appropriate changes in approved depositories when
warranted.
   In determining safekeeping and custody qualifications, financial
institutions should be able, upon request, to document a minimum capital
requirement of at least $10,000,000 and at least five years of operation. All
financial institutions and brokers/dealers shall be pre-qualified by supplying
the following:
·   Audited financial statements,
·   Proof of NASD certification or FDIC insurance,
·   Proof of state registration, and
·   Certification of having read, understood and agreement to comply with the
Williamstown Township investment policy.
   The treasurer shall periodically examine the financial condition and
registrations of qualified financial institutions and brokers/dealers by
obtaining annual updates of the information listed above.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That when the treasurer’s analysis of the township’s
cash flow requirements reveal that surplus funds will not be required to meet
current expenditures for a specific length of time, the treasurer is authorized
to make prudent investments for a length of time that will provide a reasonable
return on investment yet ensure that such funds will be available when needed
and will not be exposed to undue risk. The treasurer is authorized to invest
township funds in the following instruments:
a.   Bonds, securities, and other obligations of the United States or an agency
or instrumentality of the United States.
b.   Certificates of Deposit, savings accounts, deposit accounts, or depository
receipts of a financial institution, but only if the financial institution is
eligible to be a depository of funds belonging to the state under a law or rule
of this state or the United States.
c.   Commercial paper rated at the time of purchase within the 2 highest
classifications established by not less than 2 standard rating services and
that matures not more than 270 days after the date of purchase.
d.   Repurchase agreements consisting of instruments listed in subdivision (a).
e.   Bankers’ acceptances if United States banks.
f.   Obligations of this state or any of its political subdivisions that at the
time of purchase are rated as investment grade by not less than one standard
rating service.
g.   Mutual funds registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as
amended, Title 1 of Chapter 686, 54 Stat. 789, 15 U.S.C. 80 a-1 to 80 a-3 and
80 a-4 to 80 a-64, with authority to purchase only investment vehicles that are
legal for direct investment by a public corporation. However, a mutual fund is
not disqualified as a permissible investment solely by reason of either of the
following:
i)   The purchase of securities on a when-issued or delayed delivery basis
ii)   The ability to lend portfolio securities as long as the mutual fund
receives collateral at all times equal to at least 100% of the value of the
securities loaned.
iii)   The limited ability to borrow and pledge a like portion of the
portfolio’s assets for temporary or emergency purposes.
Investments in mutual funds shall be limited to securities whose intention is
to maintain a net asset value of $ 1.00 per share. 
h.   Obligations described in subdivision (a) through (g) if purchased through
an interlocal agreement under the Urban Cooperation Act of 1967, PA 7 of 1967,
Ex.Sess., (MCLs 124.501 to 124.512).
i.   Investment pools organized under the Surplus Funds Investment Pool Act, PA
367 of 1982 (MCLs 129.111 to 129.118).
j.   The investment pools organized under the Local Government Investment Pool
Act, PA 121 of 1985 (MCLs 129.141 to 129.150).
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the objectives of this policy are:
·   Foremost, maintain safety of principal of township funds;
·   Secondarily, maintain a diversified investment portfolio;
·   Maintain adequate liquidity;
·   Achieve a market rate of return on relatively safe investment instruments.
To accomplish these objectives, decisions and actions involving the township’s
investment portfolio shall meet the following criteria:
Safety: Safety of principal is the foremost objective of Williamstown
Township’s investment practices. Investments shall be undertaken in a manner
that seeks to ensure the preservation of capital in the overall investment
portfolio.
Diversifications: The investments shall be diversified by security type, when
practical, and institution, in order that potential losses on individual
securities do not exceed the income generated from the remainder of the
portfolio.
Liquidity: The investment portfolio shall remain sufficiently liquid to meet
all operating requirements that may be reasonably anticipated.
Return on Investment: The investment portfolio shall be designed to attain a
market average rate of return during budgetary and economic cycles while taking
into account investment risk constraints and liquidity needs. Return on
investment is of secondary importance compared to safety and liquidity
objectives. The core of investments is limited to relatively low risk
securities, and a fair rate of return relative to risk is assumed.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall make such investments and
only such investments as a prudent person would make in dealing with the
property of another, having in view the preservation of the principal and the
amount and regularity of the income to be derived.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall refrain from personal
business activity that could conflict with the proper execution and management
of township investments, or that could impair the treasurer’s ability to make
impartial investment decisions.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall annually provide a written
report to the township board concerning the investment of township funds.
   BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That Township Resolution Number 40 is hereby
replaced.
Seconded by Clerk Davis.
Carried by the following vote.
YES: Supervisor Martin, Clerk Davis, Treasurer LeBlanc, Trustee Wright and
Trustee Wilbrink.
NO: None.

Resolution # 56 – Fixed Asset Capitalization Policy
Discussion ensued, resulting in the following resolution being offered.
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION # 56
FIXED ASSET CAPITALIZATION POLICY
Resolution by Trustee Wright.
WHEREAS, the Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham County, in exercising its
fiduciary responsibilities desires to establish a fix asset capitalization
policy;
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the policy contained herein shall be
considered an official policy of Williamstown Township, Michigan.
FIXED ASSET CAPITALIZATION POLICY
The Township of Williamstown will regard fixed assets as capitalized when all
of the following criteria are met:
   (1)   Assets purchased, built or leased have useful lives of one year or
more.
   (2)   The cost of the asset (including installation) is $5,000 or more.
Multiple assets whose cost is less than $5,000 but the aggregate requestor
total is $5,000 or more are capitalized.
   (3)   The cost of repairing or renovating the asset is $5,000 or more and
prolongs the life of the asset.
The township will regard the purchased software programs as fixed assets
subject to the above capitalization policy, and will amortize over an estimated
useful life of 3 years. Costs associated with software maintenance and customer
support are considered expenditures and will not be capitalized.
Other Considerations:
   (1)   REPAIR is an expenditure that keeps the property in ordinary efficient
operating condition. The cost of the repair does not add to the value or
prolong the life of the asset. All repair expenditures are charged to the
appropriate department and fund.
   (2)   IMPROVEMENTS are expenditures for additions, alterations and
renovations that appreciably prolong the life of the asset, materially increase
its value or adapt it to a different use. Improvements of this nature are
capitalized.
Examples of Repairs vs. Improvements
Repairs = Expenditures            Improvements = Capitalized Assets
All items-life less than one year         Life of more than one year
All items under $5,000            All items $5,000 or more
Property maintenance, wall repair         Property rebuilding
Replacement of machine parts to keep      Replacement of motor and parts that
Machine in normal operating condition      prolong the useful life
Property restoration (rebuilding)
normal operations            Property restoration for something different or
better
Existing building repairs            Building regulation conformity
Replacement of small sections of wiring,      Major replacement of wiring,
lighting,
Pipes or light fixtures            pipes or sewer
Patching walls, minor repair         Installation of floor, wall, roof, wall
floors, etc
painting, etc               wall covering, etc
Patching driveways            New driveway or major repair
Cleaning drapery, carpet, furniture         New drapery, carpets, furniture
 
Depreciation Method – Straight Line over the following useful lives:
Buildings                  40-60 years
Building Improvement            15-30 years
Infrastructure               See State Recommendations attached
Vehicles                  3-5 years
Office Equipment               3-5 years
Computer Equipment            3-5 years
Seconded by Trustee Wilbrink
Carried by the following vote.
YES: Wilbrink, LeBlanc, Wright, Martin, Davis.
NO: None.

Library Resolution of Support
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION # 57
RESOLUTION OF SUPPORT - LIBRARY FOUNDATION
Resolution by LeBlanc.
WHEREAS, the Township Board of Williamstown Township, County of Ingham, State
of Michigan (the “Township”), deems it advisable and necessary to provide for
the acquisition and construction of a library building and the necessary site
therefore for the combined use of the Township, the City of Williamston and the
Township of Wheatfield; and
  WHEREAS, the Williamston Community Library Foundation (the Foundation)
established November 20, 2000, is coordinating fundraising efforts to construct
a new library; and
  WHEREAS, the purpose of the Foundation shall be to serve the informational
needs of the people of the City of Williamston, Williamstown Township,
Wheatfield Township, and such other geographic areas as from time to time may
be added; to promote the library system in the geographic area, its facilities
and service; to fund capital and special projects in furtherance thereof; to
take and hold by devise, gift, purchase or lease, either absolutely or in
trust, objects of historical or natural interest to be preserved; to receive
and administer funds and function as and exercise all the powers of a Michigan
non-profit corporation known as a foundation, exclusively, however for
charitable and educational purposes as such purposes are set forth in Section
501 ( c) (3) of the Internal Revenue Code; and, to carry out such purposes, to
take and hold by bequest, devise, gift, purchase, or lease, absolutely or in
trust, any property permitted by law, whether real, personal or mixed, to
convey such property and to invest and reinvest the principal thereof in
accordance with law and to deal with and expend the principal or income
thereof, or both, and to hold and administer all such property and
accumulations thereof all to effectuate and carry out said charitable purposes;
and
  WHEREAS, the Foundation intends to build a new public Library for the
Williamston Community; and
  WHEREAS, such a project will provide the community with an improved and much
needed new library building and services; and
  WHEREAS, the Foundation has conducted fundraising efforts already to
establish a building fund for a new library; and
  WHEREAS, the Foundation intends to build the new Library entirely with
private funds and grants, hoping to avoid any taxation;
 NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Township supports the Foundation’s
efforts to construct a new Library in Williamston.
  BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Township is not committing public funds to
the Foundation and,
 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Township encourages all persons to assist the
Foundation in its fundraising efforts;
Resolution supported by Wilbrink.
AYES: Wilbrink, LeBlanc, Wright, Martin, Davis
NAYS: None
RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #58
BANK SIGNATORIES
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
Be it resolved that all bank account and money market account signature cards
will be submitted with four authorized signers. These signers will be the
current Clerk and Deputy Clerk, and the current Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer.
It will be the policy of this township that any check or withdrawal order will
require two signatures: one from the Clerk department and one from the Treasury
department, and one of these two signatures must be that of the Clerk or the
Treasurer. Because her term of office has ended, Cindy Davis’s name will be
removed from the signature cards. Whenever possible, investment accounts such
as bank certificates of deposit will be set up as book entry instruments in the
name of Williamstown Township and without signature cards. New signature cards
will be submitted with the following authorized signers:

Depository Resolution
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #59
DEPOSITORY DESIGNATION RESOLUTION
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
WHEREAS, the Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham County, in exercising its
fiduciary responsibilities desires to safeguard the funds of the township that
may be invested from time to time, and
WHEREAS, public Act 77 of 1989 (MCL 41.77) requires that the township board
designate the banks or depositories for the money belonging to the township,
including the time for which the deposits shall be made and all details for
carrying into effect the authority given in this act, and
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, That the board approves the following institutions or
their successor institutions through merger and/or acquisition as depositories
of township funds: Chase Bank, Republic Bank, Independent Bank, Fifth/Third
Bank, Capitol National Bank, Flagstar Bank, Mason State Bank, Dart Bank,
National City Bank; Charter One Bank, National Association; Citizens Bank, and
LaSalle Bank Midwest National Association.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall recommend financial
institutions for approval for the safekeeping of township funds based on an
evaluation of the performance and solvency of the institution, as well as past
performance in exercising due care and prudence in managing the custody of
township funds held in trust, if applicable. The treasurer shall periodically
evaluate approved and potential financial depositories and shall make
recommendations as to appropriate changes in approved depositories when
warranted.
Supported by: Trustee Martin Wright
Roll call vote:
 
Supervisor Mickey Martin: yes Trustee Martin Wright: yes
Clerk Howard Dahlstrom: yes   Trustee Bob Hayes: yes
Treasurer Albert LeBlanc: yes Trustee Rick Williams: yes
Trustee Frans Wilbrink: yes
 
Resolution Adopted.

consensuses of the body to have Attorney Spagnuolo investigate rules of
procedure for elected officials when there may be a conflict of interest.
Discussion ensued regarding opposition to the rezoning of part of Meridian
Township for a Mayberry Homes project, leading to the following resolution.
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #60
OPPOSING THE PROPOSED MAYBERRY HOMES REZONING
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
Whereas, the Planning Commission of Williamstown Township adopted a Master Plan
for Williamstown Township on October 17, 2006, and such plan was accepted by
the Williamstown Township Board of Trustees on November 14, 2006, and
Whereas, a stated goal of the Master Plan is to preserve “rural open space,
farmlands, and environmental quality” and, in order to meet its stated goals,
the Master Plan “concentrates the most intensive development along Grand River
Avenue” and “calls for agricultural uses and low-density residential
development in the northern two-thirds of the Township;” and
Whereas, the lands in Williamstown Township north of Haslett Road and adjacent
to Meridian Township are designated on the Future Land Use Map as Agricultural
Preserve, with a minimum lot size of 40 acres, and the current zoning
classification of these lands requires a minimum lot size of 40 acres, and
Whereas, a request for rezoning has been presented to Meridian Township by
Mayberry Homes to convert 141.36 acres on the north side of Haslett Road and
adjacent to Williamstown Township from RR, Rural Residential zoning to RA,
Single-Family Medium Density zoning, and
Whereas, the 2005 Charter Township of Meridian Master Plan designates the
rezoning site for Agricultural-Residential use, with recommended minimum lot
sizes of 2 acres, and
Whereas, the requested RA zoning district permits residential development at 3
½ units per acre, and
Whereas, the anticipated result of rezoning the Meridian Township lands as
requested would be to significantly increase development pressure on
agricultural lands in Williamstown Township by introducing a growth center in
the northerly part of the Township, and
Whereas, development consistent with that permitted under the requested zoning
classification could erode the basic concept of the Williamstown Township
Master Plan, and
Whereas, the Williamstown Township Planning Commission has reviewed the
proposal and has unanimously approved a motion to strongly recommend that the
Mayberry Homes site not be rezoned, in consideration of the potential negative
impacts the rezoning would have on quality of life and the adopted Master Plan
of Williamstown Township.
Now, Therefore, be it resolved that the Board of Trustees of Williamstown
Township, in consideration of the potential deleterious impacts the rezoning
would have, strenuously objects to the proposed Mayberry Homes rezoning
proposal.
Be it Further Resolved, that the Board of Trustees of Williamstown Township
strongly urges Meridian Township to adhere to the adopted Charter Township of
Meridian Master Plan and maintain the land use designated on the Meridian
Township Future Land Use Map.
Be it Further Resolved, that the Board of Trustees of Williamstown Township
recommends that Meridian Township deny the request for rezoning.
Seconded by: Trustee Bob Hayes
Roll call vote:
Supervisor Mickey Martin: yes Trustee Martin Wright:       yes
Clerk Howard Dahlstrom:    yes Trustee Bob Hayes:       yes
Treasurer Albert LeBlanc:    yes Trustee Rick Williams:       yes
Trustee Frans Wilbrink:    yes
Resolution Adopted.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #61
BANK SIGNATORIES
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
Be it resolved that all bank account and money market account signature cards
will be submitted with four authorized signers. These signers will be the
current Clerk and Deputy Clerk, and the current Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer.
It will be the policy of this township that any check or withdrawal order will
require two signatures: one from the Clerk department and one from the Treasury
department, and one of these two signatures must be that of the Clerk or the
Treasurer. Because he prefers to serve as Treasury Assistant rather than Deputy
Treasurer, Harold P. Husse’s name will be removed from the signature cards.
Lori Hurst’s name will be added as Deputy Treasurer. Whenever possible,
investment accounts such as bank certificates of deposit will be set up as book
entry instruments in the name of Williamstown Township and without signature
cards. New signature cards will be submitted with the following authorized
signers:
Clerk: Howard M. Dahlstrom Deputy Clerk: Robert J. Cwiertniewicz
Treasurer: Albert LeBlanc Deputy Treasurer: Lori Hurst
Supported by: Clerk Howard M. Dahlstrom
Roll call vote:
 
Supervisor Mickey Martin: yes Trustee Martin Wright: yes
Clerk Howard Dahlstrom: yes   Trustee Bob Hayes: yes
Treasurer Albert LeBlanc: yes Trustee Rick Williams: yes
Trustee Frans Wilbrink: yes
Resolution passes.

There was no public comment, but Supervisor Martin supplied a written comment

Discussion ensued regarding various components of the report including

current problems.
Soil Borings
Supervisor Martin stated that the township would need to use the services of a

construction of a wireless internet pole. A proposal has been submitted by STS
Consultants and Kebs has stated that they will also submit a proposal. Marvin
Thomson has agreed to serve as project manager for this aspect of the proposed
wireless internet for the township. Supervisor Martin said that contact has
been made with the school system regarding possible collocation and there would
be more information provided at the next meeting.

Supervisor Martin informed the Board that the township hall would be rented for
7 days in March to conduct an OSHA Safety Training workshop. No discounts were
requested and the township will collect $100.00 for each day.
Budget Amendments
Discussion ensued regarding the lack of funds remaining in the salary line
items of those who are paid monthly. This was apparently the result of
switching monthly payroll to the last business day of the month, per the
financial policy adopted this last fiscal year. The change took place in
October of 2006. Trustee Wilbrink contended that this would result in thirteen
paychecks for those involved. Further discussion resulted in the following
motion.
Motion by Hayes to transfer needed funds from the contingency line item to the
salary line items of those affected.
Seconded by Williams.
Yes: Wright, Martin, Hayes, Williams, LeBlanc, Dahlstrom.
No: Wilbrink.
Motion carries.
Building Permit Policy

culmination of a cooperative effort with assistance from Building Official Mark
Miller. Further discussion explained variables involved in the policy including
time limits for the expiration of building permits.
Motion by Hayes to adopt the “Building Permits Action and Status Policy” as
submitted.
Seconded by Williams.
Carried unanimously.

Audit Update
Supervisor Martin explained that she had received the bid from Abraham &
Gaffney, our regular auditor, on the day of this meeting. Clerk Dahlstrom said
that he had contacted two other firms, but has not yet received a bid from
them, and therefore declined to give their names. Treasurer LeBlanc will
contact the Maner, Costerisan & Ellis firm and other qualified firms using the
specs from the received bid to try and obtain additional bids.
1099/W-2 Employee Status Update
Clerk Dahlstrom reported that our auditing firm has said that commissioners
were employees and there is an option on whether to withhold payroll taxes and
issue a W-2 or to refrain from withholding taxes and issue a 1099 form at the
end of the year. Trustee Williams stated that he always received a 1099 at the
end of the year during his tenure on the Cable Commission.
Motion by Williams that effective January 1, 2007 the township will refrain
from tax deductions on the paychecks of Cable Commission members, issue a
refund to those commissioners who had tax deductions withheld since that date
and issue a 1099 for these members at the end of the calendar year.
Seconded by Wright.
Yes: Wright, Martin, Williams, Dahlstrom, Hayes.
No: Wilbrink, LeBlanc.
Motion passes.
Trustee Pay Update Committees and Reports (changed with minutes approval on 5-
1-07)
Discussion ensued regarding Trustee Pay for additional monthly meetings.
Motion by Williams to enable Trustees to be paid for more than one extra
meeting per month, with a maximum number of compensated meetings to be set at
twelve per year.
Seconded by Wright.
Carried unanimously.

Supervisor Martin reported on CADL millage info, a meeting with other local
Supervisors, the March Board of review, the hot water heater circulating pump,

during a meeting to ask for maximum of an eight-minute recess.
Seconded by Wright.
Carried unanimously.
Motion by Martin to require that all material for the Board meeting be included
with the packet, when distributed, and that items submitted the night of the
meeting shall not be discussed at the meeting.
Seconded by Williams.
Carried unanimously.
Supervisor Martin adjourned the meeting at 7:00 p.m.

Treasurer Report
Supervisor Martin noted that the report was not reconciled against the general
ledger and that it should be tabled until that is done. Treasurer LeBlanc
pointed out that all bank statements are fully reconciled to all documented
checks and deposits and carry forward balances, and that the problem is in the
BSA software. It was determined that February and March are not reconciled to

reconciling the report against the general ledger and Treasurer LeBlanc said

that the Treasurer enlist help through his training budget to reconcile the

Audit Update
Treasurer LeBlanc submitted copies of a proposal from Carolan & McGarry that
had been received the day of this meeting. He further stated that this full
audit would be very expensive because of the matter of examining every
transaction. He said he had talked to our regular auditing firm of Abraham &
Gaffney and was told that what the township was requesting was “over the top”
and that it was not necessary to be that extensive.
Motion by LeBlanc that the Treasurer invite bids from local accounting firms to
audit both the General Fund and Cemetery Fund payroll and payroll liability
accounts for the 2006-07 fiscal year. This audit is to be supervised by the
Clerk, Treasurer, and Supervisor, the auditor will present a written report,
and the audit will consist of the following work:
   a.   For each payroll expenditure transaction recorded in the general ledger
      i.   Examine related supporting documentation (time sheet, Board meeting
minutes, etc.)
      ii.   Verify that amount of transaction in general ledger agrees with
supporting documentation (hours on time sheet by rate of pay for hourly
employees, appropriate rate of pay for salaried employees as documented in
Board minutes)
      iii.   Verify that expenditure was linked in general ledger with
appropriate fund, account, and period recorded
      iv.   Examine canceled check, which will be furnished by the township,
and compare with amount, date, and vendor in general ledger
      v.   Examine endorsements on cancelled check for appropriateness
   b.   For each payroll liability transaction recorded in the general ledger
      i.   Examine related supporting documentation (remittance advice, IRS
Forms 941, etc.)
      ii.   Verify that amount of transaction in general ledger agrees with
supporting documentation (payment amount in remittance agrees with general
ledger)
      iii.   Verify that the disbursement was correctly reflected in the
general ledger (appropriate fund, reduction of appropriate liability account,
correct period recorded)
      iv.   Recompute amounts withheld based upon original source documentation
(e. g. government withholding tables, pension plan withhold rates) and verify
that township withheld and remitted the correct amount.
Seconded by Hayes.
Roll Call Vote:
 
Hayes Williams Wright LeBlanc Wilbrink Dahlstrom Martin
Yes   Yes      Yes    Yes     Yes      Yes       Yes
 
Motion carries.

Broadband Internet
Supervisor Martin explained the current status of the project and said that
members of the committee would present their information and recommendations.
Marv Thompson explained the submitted compilation of responses from various
prospective providers of internet service. Services, rates, installation
timeframes and financing were discussed. It was the recommendation of the
committee that the township designate Freedom Net as the selected provider. A
letter of support was submitted by Bradley & Lou Sharo of Lounsbury Road in
support of the project.
Motion by Hayes to designate Freedom Net as the selected provider for broadband
internet services to the township of Williamstown and to authorize the
broadband internet committee to move forward with negotiations.
Seconded by Williams.
Carried unanimously.
Committee member Kurt Guter explained the variables involved with the tower,
including the building, maintenance and costs associated with the project. He
submitted a comparison sheet and reported information gathered through his
research. Financing and possible loans for the project would take more research
into how and if the township could be involved in this aspect.
Motion by Hayes to authorize the broadband internet committee to move forward
with negotiations with Freedom Net regarding building the tower needed for
broadband internet.
Seconded by LeBlanc.
Carried unanimously.
401a
Supervisor Martin initiated discussion regarding unresolved issues with the
plan and commented on Clerk Dahlstrom’s allegations. She said that she has
contacted Plunkett and Cooney regarding investigating the matter and issuing an
opinion. She said they would charge $175.00 per hour, and would try to keep the
total amount around $2,000.00. Discussion ensued regarding who would be the
contact person on behalf of the township. Trustee Wilbrink suggested that one
or more of the trustees contact the attorney (inserted with minutes approval on
6-5-07). Trustee Hayes stated that we should not even be in this situation
because the Clerk, in closed session, did not provide any information or
substantiation for any allegations. Treasurer LeBlanc stated that the entire
Board should receive the opinion rendered by the Attorney.
Motion by Williams to approve the hiring of Plunkett & Cooney, with the
attorney selecting a township contact person, to investigate the allegations
regarding the township 401a plan.
Seconded by Wright.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #62
INTERNET ACCESS TO TAX DATABASE
Resolution by Treasurer LeBlanc.
Be it resolved that as a service to township taxpayers and to businesses that
serve current and potential township taxpayers, the Treasurer is authorized to
arrange for making the township’s Equalizer Tax database available on the
Internet. This is to be done through an arrangement with BS&A Software, in
which the township will incur no expense and viewers will pay a fee of $ 2.00
per parcel for information viewed. Taxpayers may view information about their
own parcel free of charge.
Seconded by: Trustee Frans Wilbrink
Roll Call Vote:
 
Hayes Williams Wright LeBlanc Wilbrink Dahlstrom Martin
Yes   Yes      Yes    Yes     Yes      Yes       Yes
Resolution carries.

June 19, 2007
CALL TO ORDER
The Williamstown Board of Trustees convened in a meeting at 5:30 pm at the
Williamstown Township Hall located at 4990 Zimmer Road, Williamston, Michigan.
ROLL CALL
Present: Trustee Wilbrink, Treasurer LeBlanc, Trustee Wright, Trustee Hayes,
Trustee Williams
    Clerk Dahlstrom and Supervisor Martin.
Absent: None
PUBLIC COMMENT
Supervisor Martin called for public comment at 5:31 p.m. There was none.
Auditors Report – Bill Tucker
Bill Tucker, of Abraham & Gaffney, stated that he had spent the day at the
township hall examining and correcting some accounting problems. He stated that
the Cemetery Fund reconciliations were complete through March 2007 and the
General Fund reconciliations were complete through February 2007. He added that
accounts were set up in the BS&A software for the tax bank accounts, and there
would be no further usage of Quickbooks for these accounts. He stated that
Quickbooks should now only be used for reference. He further stated that all
Certificates of Deposit balances were correct. Journal entries were still
needed for some previous 2006 checks and other items. Trustee Williams asked
about the advisability of outsourcing payroll and Mr. Tucker said that’s a
possibility because of a seemingly high rate of employee turnover, but that
when Treasurer LeBlanc talks to BS&A regarding the issues that were discussed
today, it would most probably rectify the payroll problems also. Mr. Tucker
concluded by saying that the audit should be on schedule to begin on July 23,
2007.
Treasurer Appointment
Supervisor Martin explained that there were two applicants, Gwen Chirico-
Brandon and Janet T. Eyster, for the position of Treasurer being vacated by
Treasurer LeBlanc as of June 30, 2007.
Supervisor Martin called for public comment regarding this issue. There was
none.
Supervisor Martin stated that the Board members had submitted questions for the
candidates and they had been compiled into one sheet and distributed to the
Board. The series of questions were asked first of Gwen Chirico-Brandon and
then Janet T. Eyster. Upon completion of the verbal response sessions, the
candidates voluntarily left the meeting to enable the Board to discuss the
responses. Discussion ensued with the consensus being that both candidates
exhibited great experience and qualifications for the position and that the
decision is very difficult.
Motion by Wright to appoint Janet T. Eyster to the position of Township
Treasurer, effective July 1, 2007, to fill the balance of the term that expires
on November 21, 2008.
Seconded by Hayes.
Carried unanimously. (Treasurer LeBlanc did not vote on this motion.)
Trustee Wright stated that he hoped Gwen Chirico-Brandon would continue her
current employment with the Township.
Clerk Dahlstrom commented on his submitted cost report regarding the well
project at the park.
Supervisor Martin explained that the township has had a copier at the township
hall for a trial period and it has performed up to expectations. It was her
recommendation that the copier be purchased. Discussion ensued regarding the
capabilities and need for this copier. Supervisor Martin stated that a
replacement copier was budgeted into the 2007-08 budget. Discussion of disposal
of the old copier took place, with Trustee Williams suggesting that the Chamber
of Commerce is in need of a copier.
Supervisor Martin gave a brief update on the Broadband project, stating that
preliminary customer signups and tower placement survey work were taking place.
It is possible that a site plan for the tower could go to the Planning
Commission in July.
Supervisor Martin adjourned the meting at 6:50pm.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION #63
BANK SIGNATORIES
Resolution by Trustee Wright.
Be it resolved that all bank account and money market account signature cards
will be submitted with four authorized signers. These signers will be the
current Clerk and Deputy Clerk, and the current Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer.
It will be the policy of this township that any check or withdrawal order will
require two signatures: one from the Clerk department and one from the Treasury
department, and one of these two signatures must be that of the Clerk or the
Treasurer. Whenever possible, investment accounts such as bank certificates of
deposit will be set up as book entry instruments in the name of Williamstown
Township and without signature cards. New signature cards will be submitted
with the following authorized signers:
Clerk: Howard M. Dahlstrom Deputy Clerk: Robert J. Cwiertniewicz
Treasurer: Janet T. Eyster Deputy Treasurer: Lori Hurst
Seconded by Trustee Wilbrink
Roll call vote:
Supervisor Mickey Martin:   yes
Clerk Howard Dahlstrom:   yes
Trustee Frans Wilbrink:      yes       
Trustee Martin Wright:       yes       
Trustee Bob Hayes:       yes      
Trustee Rick Williams:      yes    
Supervisor Martin adjourned the meting at 10:09 a.m.

McGillicuddy of Meridian Township, Supervisor Roni Christmas of Bath Township
and Supervisor Mickey Martin of Williamstown Township, and is being studied.

Internet Tower Update
Supervisor Martin explained the latest details regarding the wireless internet
project, including information that the contract with FreedomNet is in its
fourth draft and that the tower costs on the part of the township would only be
$60,000.00.
Eastside Development – MHSDA Senior Apartments
Ms. Cheryl McHallam, of McHallam Development, explained the proposal for the
project known as the Red Cedar Meadows Senior Apartments, a 30-unit building to
be located at 2365 E. Grand River. Project information was disseminated to the
Board including rental rates, amenities, square footage and developer
information. The developer was looking for a show of support from the Township
Board, pursuant to requirements for MHSDA funding.
Motion by Wright to endorse the concept of the project known as the Red Cedar
Meadows Senior Apartments, and to encourage all parties to move forward in its
development.
Seconded by Williams.
Carried Unanimously
Packets
Supervisor Martin explained that with the acquisition of the new copier, and in
consideration of time spent and paper used to assemble Board packets, that it
would be more cost efficient to develop a program to enable the email delivery
of Board packets. The copier has a scanner component that can convert any
document into an electronic format that can be easily dispatched through email.
Discussion ensued regarding the concept including the establishment of email
addresses, placing these full packets on the township website, and the use of
laptop computer by Board members at the meetings. Supervisor Martin said that
she would like to begin with the emailing of packets and then possibly extend
the project to posting packets on the website. It was the consensus of the
Board to move forward with the development of the project, and that Clerk
Dahlstrom would check into the establishment of email addresses and Supervisor
Martin would check with legal counsel regarding FOIA of personal emails.
HB 4780
Supervisor Martin elaborated on the impact of the possible passage of House
Bill 4780, which would reduce and/or eliminate the township’s responsibilities
in the areas of tax collection, assessing and elections. Supervisor Martin
advised the Board and the public to contact our legislators in Lansing to urge
them to defeat this bill. She said that she had recently talked to the Ingham
County Controller and he said that there would be great difficulty in assuming
these responsibilities. Cindy Davis, of the Michigan Townships Association, in
attendance at the meeting, said that the MTA is encouraging the defeat of this
bill and that it was the opinion of the Association that this was just the
first step down the road to the possibility of eliminating township government
in the State of Michigan.
Treasurer’s Report
The Treasurer’s report submitted by previous Treasurer Al LeBlanc was
addressed, with Supervisor Martin saying that the bank reconciliation have not
yet been reconciled to the general fund. Treasurer Eyster thanked the previous
Treasurer and the township hall staff and officials for their help during the
transition to her new position.

REPORT FROM THE TREASURER
Treasurer Eyster commented on the 401a plan problems for 2006, and said that it
is possible that revised W-2 forms may be need to be computed and distributed
to elected officials. She said that she is still researching 2007, but it
appears there may be Medicare-match problems with the first three calendar
months. She said that there does not appear to be a problem with Social
Security withholding, but has concluded that the Medicare percentage being
withheld and forwarded may not be correct. Further work and verification needs
to be done.
CREDIT CARDS
Supervisor Martin said that there is a credit card bill through Bank of America
that has not been paid. It was explained that there are two separate Bank of
America credit cards, and the one that includes charges related to attendance
at a conference by the Supervisor was the one that had not been paid. Clerk
Dahlstrom said that he had not received a breakdown for the charges, enabling

should conclude their research within a month.
TORNADO ASSISTANCE
Supervisor Martin explained various activities and services that were provided
to assist residents with damage suffered as a result of the tornado that swept
through the area on the night of Thursday, October 19, 2007. She stated that
there were 100 homes in the area that sustained damage, 10 of which were left
uninhabitable. She thanked the Williamston DPW, Building Inspector Mark Miller,
Granger Disposal and various companies who provided tree-chipping service. The
cooperation between government entities and private companies was commendable.
The communities, their leaders and their residents came together in admirable
fashion in this time of distress and tragedy.
Discussion ensued regarding the short-term plan to provide additional services
and Supervisor Martin would contact a volunteer group who was instrumental in
providing resources and labor assistance to ascertain if they would avail
themselves to coordinate further efforts. It was estimated that $7,000.00 was
spent to date for chipping services and she would inquire as to their help in
estimating further costs and the provision of future services by their resource
contacts. It was thought that the final amount for these services could be
three times what was already spent.
Supervisor Martin said that another letter would be sent to residents of the
affected area to ask that they line their driveway with materials that need
chipping, as opposed to the roadside, for safety and accessibility reasons. She
also stated that the Road Commission would avail a central site in the area for
residents to bring fallen trees to for incineration.
There have been calls from residents in the township asking for special burn
permission in addition to their regular four-day monthly allocations.
Supervisor Martin stated that the burn ordinance includes the possibility of a
variance if the residents of a subdivision petitioned the Board.
Discussion also ensued regarding the availability of township saws and
machinery in times of emergency. A knox box would be installed at the township
hall and cemetery for NIESA.
PARKS & RECREATION MASTER PLAN
Supervisor Martin explained that the Parks Committee requested guidance from
the Planning Commission in proceeding with the construction of a pavilion at
the park. The Planning Commission recommends we apply for grants next April for
the construction. In order to apply we must update our Parks & Recreation
Master Plan and it is recommended that the Planning Commission be authorized to
go forward with this.
Motion by Hayes to authorize the Planning Commission to undertake an update of
the Parks & Recreation Master Plan.
Seconded by Dahlstrom.
Carried unanimously.
Trustee Williams commented on the MTA workshop he recently attended and on the
new seating arrangements for the Board.
Supervisor Martin called an adjournment at 7:20 pm.

Poverty Guidelines and Asset Level
Discussion ensued leading to the following resolution.
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION #66
POVERTY GUIDELINES RESOLUTION
Resolution by Supervisor Mickey Martin
Be it resolved that:
WHEREAS, the adoption of guidelines for poverty exemptions is within the
purview of the Township Board; and
WHEREAS, the homestead of persons who, in the judgment of the Supervisor and
Board of Review, by reason of poverty, are unable to contribute to the public
charges is eligible for exemption in whole or part from taxation under Public
Act 390, 1994 (MCL 211.7u); and
WHEREAS, pursuant to PA 390, 1994 Williamstown Township, Ingham County adopts
the following guidelines for the supervisor and Board of Review to implement.
The guidelines shall include but not be limited to the specific income and
asset levels of the claimant and all persons residing in the household,
including any property tax credit returns, filed in the current or immediately
preceding year;
To be eligible, a person shall do all the following on an annual basis:
1.   Be an owner of and occupy as a homestead the property for which an
exemption is requested.
2.   File a claim with the Supervisor or Board of Review, accompanied by
federal and state income tax returns for all persons residing in the homestead,
including any property tax credit returns filed in the immediately preceding
year or in the current year.
3.   Produce a valid drivers’ license or other form of identification if
requested.
4.   Produce a deed, land contract, or other evidence of ownership of the
property for which an exemption is requested, if requested.
5.   Meet the federal poverty income standards as defined and determined
annually by the United States Office of Management and Budget.
6.   The application for an exemption shall be filed after January 1, but
before the day prior to the last day of Board of Review.
7.   Any additional eligibility requirements as determined by the Township
Board;
The Board of Review shall follow the above stated policy and federal guidelines
in granting or denying an exemption, unless the Board of Review determines
there are substantial and compelling reasons why there should be a deviation
from the policy and federal guidelines and these are communicated in writing to
the claimant.
Be it further resolved to adopt the Federal Poverty Guidelines for 2008 with an
increase of 50% in all sections as shown below, and to limit assets to one
principle residence and one licensed vehicle for each resident, with a maximum
of two.
Size of Family Unit             Poverty Guidelines
1                               $15,315
2                               $20,535
3                               $25,755
4                               $30,975
5                               $36,195
6                               $41,415
7                               $46,635
8                               $51,855
For each additional person, add $5220
 
Seconded by: Martin Wright
Roll call vote:
Supervisor Mickey Martin:   yes
Treasurer Janet T. Eyster:   yes
Clerk Howard Dahlstrom:   yes
Trustee Frans Wilbrink:   yes
Trustee Martin Wright:   yes

Supervisor Martin explained the role of the Township in releasing property from
PA 116. When a property owner requests to be released from a PA 116 agreement
the State of Michigan requires the local Township to agree to the removal of
the property from the PA 116. In doing so this does not in any way mean a split
or boundary change approval from the Township. For a parcel to be split a
boundary change application must be submitted and approved according to the
ordinance and the County with new tax identification numbers assigned.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
INGHAM COUNTY, MICHIGAN
RESOLUTION OF THE TOWNSHIP BOARD
ADOPTING THE PARKS AND RECREATION MASTER PLAN
At a special meeting of the Township Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham
County, Michigan, held on February 28, 2008 at 9:00 a.m. prevailing local time.
PRESENT: Dahlstrom, Wilbrink, Hayes, Wright.
ABSENT: Martin, Williams, Eyster.
The following Preamble and Resolution were offered by Member Wright and
supported by Member Wilbrink.
WHEREAS, Williamstown Township has completed a Five Year Parks and Recreation
Master Plan that describes the physical features, existing recreation
facilities, and the desired actions to be taken to improve and maintain parks
and recreation facilities during the period between 2008 and 2012; and
WHEREAS, a public comment session was held on February 19, 2008, at the
Williamstown Township Hall to provide an opportunity for citizens to express
opinions, ask questions, and discuss all aspects of the Parks and Recreation
Master Plan; and
WHEREAS, Williamstown Township has developed the plan for the benefit of the
entire community and proposes to adopt the plan as a document to assist in
meeting the recreation needs of the community; and
WHEREAS, the Township Board reviewed the Parks and Recreation Master Plan and
concurs with the findings, recommendations, and implementation strategies
outlined in the plan.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Williamstown Township Board hereby
adopts the Parks and Recreation Master Plan, dated February 14, 2008, as a
guideline for improving recreation for the residents of Williamstown Township.
AYES: Wright, Dahlstrom, Wilbrink, Hayes.
NAYS: None.

foregoing is a true and original copy of a resolution adopted by the
Williamstown Township Board at a special meeting held on February 28, 2008.

has either been lost or destroyed, and by this resolution the Township Board
desires to rememorialize this grant.

appropriated $7,000.00 annually to WASC for the periods of 2007, 2008, 2009 and
2010 as related above. Further, Williamstown Township resolves that it will
require an annual report of revenues and expenditures, and/or other year-end
reports generated by WASC.

explained the approval recommendation that was submitted regarding the Cemetery
Columbarium.
Motion by Hayes to approve the columbarium master plan, per the recommendation
of McKenna Associates, with the following conditions set forth my McKenna:
·   We recommend that landscape edging be provided around the catmint beds as
this plant spreads rhizomes and is highly invasive.
·   Some of the woody plant material selections have serious sustainability and
appearance issues as they mature. We recommend the following substitutions that
have the same texture and foliage color but are more hardy in the Michigan
climate: a) Redbud: Cornus kousa, Amelanchier Canadensis, or Acer ginnala; b)
Compact inkberry: Viburnum triluburn ‘Compactum,’ Rhus arornatica, or Hydrangea
quercifolia; c) Potentilla: Spirea bulmada, Rosa ‘Radrazz’ or Cotoneaster
apiculatus.
·   We recommend that general Structural Note No. 1 on the Columbarium Detail
sheet be revised to indicate that the footing should be four feet below grade.
Seconded by Wright.
Carried unanimously.

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION # 69
PUBLIC COMMENT RULES FOR BOARD MEETINGS
Resolution by Dahlstrom.
Whereas, the Township Board wishes to accept public comment at their meetings
in accordance with the Open Meeting Act, and
Whereas, the Township Board deems it important to receive comments to enable
informed decisions regarding township business, and
Whereas, the Township Board wishes to conduct their meetings in an orderly and
efficient manner, effectuating a productive atmosphere.
Now, Therefore Be It Resolved, that the Township adopts the following public
comment rules.
There shall be two periods for public comment during each meeting. Public
comment at the beginning of the meeting and at the end of the meeting, in
accordance with the approved agenda. These comments are for any agenda or non-
agenda items.
Speakers wishing to make public comment are requested to come forward to the
podium and state their name and address and provide the same on the meeting
speaker sign-in sheet.
Speakers making public comment are requested to ensure that their comments
pertain to township business.
Speakers shall address the Chair of the meeting and refrain from discussions
and/or comments for/with other members of the public.
Speakers will be limited to one three-minute timeframe, during each public
comment period, with extensions to be granted only by motion and majority
approval of the Board.
Public comment periods are an opportunity for the public to provide information
or to highlight concerns, questions, issues or topics of importance to the
township.
The Chair or the Majority of the Board will have the ability to open public
comment for a specific agenda item.
Seconded by Hayes.
Roll call vote:
Supervisor Mickey Martin:   yes
Treasurer Janet T. Eyster:   yes
Clerk Howard Dahlstrom:   yes
Trustee Frans Wilbrink:   no

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION #69
Williamston Senior Center Grant Resolution
Resolution by Supervisor Mickey Martin
Be it resolved that:
WHEREAS, the Williamston Area Senior Center (WASC) is located at 201 School
Street, P0 Box 343, Williamston, MI 48895; and
WHEREAS, the WASC provides activities and services for residents 60 years of
age and older (see attached Memorandum from WASC dated January 24, 2008 and
WASC Bylaws); and
WHEREAS, pursuant to PA 39 of 1976, the WASC will conduct its business
operations and organization under established bylaws, and at the direction of a
Board of Directors elected by the membership~
WI-IEREAS, in accordance with PA 39 of 1976, the Williamstown Township Board
approved a Budget (inserted with amendment to previously adopted motion) Motion
in 2006 to establish a four-year grant for WASC and the following funding
schedule was set up:
FY 2007 — first year grant (paid)
FY 2008 — second year grant (paid)
FY 2009 — third year grant (to be paid)
FY 2010 — fourth year grant (to be paid)
(FY, for each year, inserted with amendment to previously adopted motion)
WHEREAS, written information that memorialized the Budget (inserted with
amendment to previously adopted motion) Motion of the Board in 2006 has either
been lost or destroyed, and by this resolution the Township Board desires to
rememorialize this grant.
NOW THEREFORE, Williamstown Township reaffirms that it has budgeted and
appropriated $7,000.00 annually to WASC for the periods of 2007, 2008, 2009 and
2010 as related above. Further, Williamstown Township resolves that it will
require an annual report of revenues and expenditures, and/or other year-end
reports generated by WASC.
Seconded by: Trustee Williams

Investment Depository Designation Amendment
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION # 72
INVESTMENT AND DEPOSITORY DESIGNATION RESOLUTION
Resolution by Treasurer Eyster.
WHEREAS, the Board of Williamstown Township, Ingham County, in exercising its
fiduciary responsibilities desires to safeguard the funds of the township that
may be invested from time to time, and
WHEREAS, public Act 77 of 1989 (MCL 41.77) requires that the township board
designate the banks or depositories for the money belonging to the township,
including the time for which the deposits shall be made and all details for
carrying into effect the authority given in this act, and
WHEREAS, Public Act 196 of 1997 (MCL 129.91, et seq) requires township boards,
in consultation with the township treasurer, to adopt an investment policy, now
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, That this policy is applicable to all public funds
belonging to Williamstown Township and in the custody of the township
treasurer.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Williamstown Township treasurer is authorized
to manage funds belonging to the township, including depositing funds in
township board approved financial institutions and administration of
investments in conformance with MCL 41.77 and policies set forth in this
resolution.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the board approves the following institutions and
their successors as depositories of township funds: Bank One/Chase, Independent
Bank, Vanguard Securities, Fifth/Third Bank, Capitol National Bank, Flagstar
Bank, Mason State Bank, Dart Bank, National City Bank; Charter One Bank,
National Association; Citizens Bank, and LaSalle Bank Midwest National
Association/Bank of America.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall recommend financial
institutions for approval for the safekeeping of township funds based on an
evaluation of the performance and solvency of the institution, as well as past
performance in exercising due care and prudence in managing the custody of
township funds held in trust, if applicable. The treasurer shall periodically
evaluate approved and potential financial depositories and shall make
recommendations as to appropriate changes in approved depositories when
warranted.
In determining safekeeping and custody qualifications, financial institutions
should be able, upon request, to document a minimum capital requirement of at
least $10,000,000 and at least five years of operation. All financial
institutions and brokers/dealers shall be pre-qualified by supplying the
following:
∙   Audited financial statements,
∙   Proof of NASD certification or FDIC insurance,
∙   Proof of state registration, and
∙   Certification of having read, understood and agreement to comply with the
Williamstown Township investment policy.
The treasurer shall periodically examine the financial condition and
registrations of qualified financial institutions and brokers/dealers by
obtaining annual updates of the information listed above.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That when the treasurer’s analysis of the township’s
cash flow requirements reveal that surplus funds will not be required to meet
current expenditures for a specific length of time, the treasurer is authorized
to make prudent investments for a length of time that will provide a reasonable
return on investment yet ensure that such funds will be available when needed
and will not be exposed to undue risk. The treasurer is authorized to invest
township funds in the following instruments:
a.   Bonds, securities, and other obligations of the United States or an agency
or instrumentality of the United States.
b.   Certificates of Deposit, savings accounts, deposit accounts, or depository
receipts of a financial institution, but only if the financial institution is
eligible to be a depository of funds belonging to the state under a law or rule
of this state or the United States.
c.   Commercial paper rated at the time of purchase within the 2 highest
classifications established by not less than 2 standard rating services and
that matures not more than 270 days after the date of purchase.
d.   Repurchase agreements consisting of instruments listed in subdivision (a).
e.   Bankers’ acceptances if United States banks.
f.   Obligations of this state or any of its political subdivisions that at the
time of purchase are rated as investment grade by not less than one standard
rating service.
g.   Mutual funds registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as
amended, Title 1 of Chapter 686, 54 Stat. 789, 15 U.S.C. 80 a-1 to 80 a-3 and
80 a-4 to 80 a-64, with authority to purchase only investment vehicles that are
legal for direct investment by a public corporation. However, a mutual fund is
not disqualified as a permissible investment solely by reason of either of the
following:
i)   The purchase of securities on a when-issued or delayed delivery basis
i)   The ability to lend portfolio securities as long as the mutual fund
receives collateral at all times equal to at least 100% of the value of the
securities loaned.
ii)   The limited ability to borrow and pledge a like portion of the
portfolio’s assets for temporary or emergency purposes.
Investments in mutual funds shall be limited to securities whose intention is
to maintain a net asset value of $ 1.00 per share. 
h.   Obligations described in subdivision (a) through (g) if purchased through
an interlocal agreement under the Urban Cooperation Act of 1967, PA 7 of 1967,
Ex.Sess., (MCLs 124.501 to 124.512).
i.   Investment pools organized under the Surplus Funds Investment Pool Act, PA
367 of 1982 (MCLs 129.111 to 129.118).
j.   The investment pools organized under the Local Government Investment Pool
Act, PA 121 of 1985 (MCLs 129.141 to 129.150).
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the objectives of this policy are:
∙   Foremost, maintain safety of principal of township funds;
∙   Secondarily, maintain a diversified investment portfolio;
∙   Maintain adequate liquidity;
∙   Achieve a market rate of return on relatively safe investment instruments.
To accomplish these objectives, decisions and actions involving the township’s
investment portfolio shall meet the following criteria:
Safety: Safety of principal is the foremost objective of Williamstown
Township’s investment practices. Investments shall be undertaken in a manner
that seeks to ensure the preservation of capital in the overall investment
portfolio.
Diversifications: The investments shall be diversified by security type, when
practical, and institution, in order that potential losses on individual
securities do not exceed the income generated from the remainder of the
portfolio.
Liquidity: The investment portfolio shall remain sufficiently liquid to meet
all operating requirements that may be reasonably anticipated.
Return on Investment: The investment portfolio shall be designed to attain a
market average rate of return during budgetary and economic cycles while taking
into account investment risk constraints and liquidity needs. Return on
investment is of secondary importance compared to safety and liquidity
objectives. The core of investments is limited to relatively low risk
securities, and a fair rate of return relative to risk is assumed.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall make such investments and only
such investments as a prudent person would make in dealing with the property of
another, having in view the preservation of the principal and the amount and
regularity of the income to be derived.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall refrain from personal business
activity that could conflict with the proper execution and management of
township investments, or that could impair the treasurer’s ability to make
impartial investment decisions.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the treasurer shall annually provide a written
report to the township board concerning the investment of township funds.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That Township Resolution Number 40 is hereby replaced.
Seconded by Dahlstrom.
Carried by the following roll call vote.
YES: Martin, Eyster, Dahlstrom, Williams, Wright, Wilbrink & Hayes.
NO: None

NEW BUSINESS
AT&T Franchise
Marv Thomson explained that AT&T has applied for a franchise covering a very
small part of the township and that the township has returned the application/
agreement unsigned, per the recommendation of township legal council. It was
explained that while the township had no jurisdiction to prevent a franchise,
the best response to an application of this sort would be to return it unsigned
to prevent/enable future legal remedy/litigation, in the event of a change in
the law governing these franchises. Mr. Thomson also explained tower repeater
technology issues that will be revisited next spring in relation to FreedomNet
Solutions broadband internet.

UNFINISHED BUSINESS
Capitol City Rifle Club—Supervisor Martin shared they withdrew their
application for a site plan review. They applied for a building permit for a
3,800 sq. ft. accessory building in the same location. The township intends to
deny this request until a site plan review is requested. Supervisor Martin
shared the language for this response to the Capitol City Rifle Club has been
drafted and will be mailed out Wednesday, December 3, 2008.
Building Inspector, Mark Miller shared the building going on at the Capitol
City Rifle Club does not weaken any structure nor alter the building, so they
do not need a building permit.
Budget 2010—Supervisor Martin shared a proposed budget with the board. The
needs of all entities have been requested and are being considered, all hourly
employees were proposed to receive a 4.4 percent increase in salary (based on
CPI). Unemployment is up 8.9 percent. Supervisor Martin asked the township
board for their approval to move forward with budget adoptions.
Supervisor Martin shared if the board has any other items that will need to be
researched prior to January 13, 2009 meeting, please let her know. This item
will be recommended for a public hearing in January and plans for approval in
March.
Board recommendations: Security cameras, laptops for all township board
members, wireless internet—there are still funds appropriated in the budget.
Also, there was no value in drains (pg. 18).
Supervisor Martin shared she will get a quote for laptops for all board
members. Supervisor Martin also shared she will pull the wireless internet
appropriation from the budget if it is needed. Treasurer Eyster will get
Supervisor Martin a figure for value in drains.
Communications Commission—Marv Thompson spoke about the repeater station and
new technology, but is willing to pull this line item if needed. Trustee
Wilbrink feels Freedom Net should help pay some of the costs incurred.
NEW BUSINESS
Cemetery Ordinance—Treasurer Eyster shared the need to have a policy for the
perpetual care fund for the cemetery. The township would need an ordinance in
place for this addition. The township also needs a way to build a perpetual
fund that would help generate funds for maintaining the cemetery. Currently the
township has a capital improvement fund that is used to repave roads, or could
be used to help support the construction of a Columbarium. Treasurer Eyster has
a proposed ordinance made to fit Williamstown townships current practice.
Treasurer Eyster shared Section 6 and 7 are the most controversial and 7 may
have some legal issues to resolve. Section 21 and 22 have been added. The
proposed ordinance has been passed by the cemetery committee and passed on to
the township board. Next steps, the lawyers will review and work out legal
issues then pass it on for action at a public hearing.
Trustee Hayes raised the question, are the outside containers steel (see Pg.
14, Pg. 4)? Treasurer Eyster will confer with lawyers and check back with
Trustee Hayes.
Trustee Wilbrink—shared under Section 13 of the cemetery ordinance, Old
headstones could be repaired or replaced. Many of the headstones are weathered
and unreadable. Supervisor Martin shared the costs to fix headstones is very

WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP
RESOLUTION #74
POVERTY GUIDELINES RESOLUTION
Resolution by Supervisor Mickey Martin
Be it resolved that:
WHEREAS, the adoption of guidelines for poverty exemptions is within the
purview of the Township Board; and
WHEREAS, the homestead of persons who, in the judgment of the Supervisor and
Board of Review, by reason of poverty, are unable to contribute to the public
charges is eligible for exemption in whole or part from taxation under Public
Act 390, 1994 (MCL 211.7u); and
WHEREAS, pursuant to PA 390, 1994 Williamstown Township, Ingham County adopts
the following guidelines for the supervisor and Board of Review to implement.
The guidelines shall include but not be limited to the specific income and
asset levels of the claimant and all persons residing in the household,
including any property tax credit returns, filed in the current or immediately
preceding year;
To be eligible, a person shall do all the following on an annual basis:
1.   Be an owner of and occupy as a homestead the property for which an
exemption is requested.
2.   File a claim with the Supervisor or Board of Review, accompanied by
federal and state income tax returns for all persons residing in the homestead,
including any property tax credit returns filed in the immediately preceding
year or in the current year.
3.   Produce a valid drivers’ license or other form of identification if
requested.
4.   Produce a deed, land contract, or other evidence of ownership of the
property for which an exemption is requested, if requested.
5.   Meet the federal poverty income standards as defined and determined
annually by the United States Office of Management and Budget.
6.   The application for an exemption shall be filed after January 1, but
before the day prior to the last day of Board of Review.
7.   Any additional eligibility requirements as determined by the Township
Board;
The Board of Review shall follow the above stated policy and federal guidelines
in granting or denying an exemption, unless the Board of Review determines
there are substantial and compelling reasons why there should be a deviation
from the policy and federal guidelines and these are communicated in writing to
the claimant.
Be it further resolved to adopt the Federal Poverty Guidelines for 2009 with an
increase of 50% in all sections as shown below, and to limit assets to one
principle residence and one licensed vehicle for each resident, with a maximum
of two.
Size of Family Unit             Poverty Guidelines
1                               $15,600
2                               $21,000
3                               $26,400
4                               $31,800
5                               $37,200
6                               $42,600
7                               $48,000
8                               $53,400
For each additional person, add $5,400
 
Seconded by: Treasurer Janet Eyster
Roll call vote:
Supervisor Mickey Martin:   Yes, Treasurer Janet T. Eyster:  Yes, Clerk Ernie
Gaffner: Yes,
Trustee Frans Wilbrink: Yes, Trustee Martin Wright: Yes, Trustee Bob Hayes:
Yes, Trustee Rick Williams: Yes,

Hazard Mitigation Plan
Williamstown Township Board
RESOLUTION TO ADOPT THE INGHAM COUNTY HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN
RESOLUTION #75
Resolution by: Trustee Wright
Be it resolved that:
WHEREAS, Ingham County recognizes the threat that natural, social, and
technological hazards pose to the people and community of Ingham County; and
WHEREAS, undertaking hazard mitigation actions will reduce the potential harm
to the people and property of Ingham County from future hazard occurrences; and
WHEREAS, an adopted hazard mitigation plan is required as a condition of future
funding for multiple Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) pre- and post-
disaster mitigation grant programs; and
WHEREAS, Ingham County fully participated in the mitigation planning process to
prepare this hazard mitigation plan; and
WHEREAS, the Michigan State Police Emergency Management Division and the
Federal Emergency Management Agency, Region V officials have reviewed the
Hazard Mitigation Plan and approved it contingent upon this official adoption
of the Ingham County Hazard Mitigation Plan.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Ingham County Board of Commissioners
approves the adoption of the Ingham County Hazard Mitigation Plan as an
official plan.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Ingham County Emergency Operations Director
will
Submit this adopted plan to the Michigan State Police Emergency Management
Division and the
Federal Emergency Management Agency, Region V officials to enable the Ingham
County Hazard Mitigation Plan’s final approval.
Seconded by: Trustee Wilbrink
Roll Call Vote:

January 20, 2009
JOINT MEETING
BOARD OF TRUSTEES & PLANNING COMMISSION
January 20, 2009
CALL TO ORDER
The joint meeting of the Williamstown Board of Trustees and the Williamstown
Township Planning Commission convened at 6:45 p.m. at the Williamstown Township
Hall located at 4990 Zimmer Road, Williamston, Michigan. Supervisor Mickey
Martin called the meeting to order and introduced Christine Spitzley from the
Tri-County Regional Planning Commission and Carol Luukkonen from the USGS
Michigan Science Center.
IN ATTENDANCE
Trustees Wilbrink, Wright and Trustee Williams, Clerk Gaffner, Supervisor
Martin, Treasurer Eyster, Building Inspector Miller and Planning Commission
Members Bloomquist, Feilek, Imhoff and Hoag.
PRESENTATION
The first segment of a Power Point presentation was given by Christine
Spitzley, concerning the research and history of the Tri-County aquifer study.
The goal is to make information available to better understand the water needs
of the various populated areas within the Tri-County district, the availability
of water to satisfy these needs and the routing of the water.
The second portion of the Power Point presentation was given by Carol
Luukkonen, concerning the availability of data for ground water flow, pumping
rates per location of municipal wells and water levels. The compiled data can
be used in various computer models to depict the present water levels and
various scenarios on “what if” situations.
PUBLIC COMMENT
A few questions and comments were offered at the end of the presentation,
concerning the involvement of various governmental agencies, pending
legislation concerning the maintenance of quality water for continued use by
the residents of the State of Michigan.
Supervisor Martin adjourned the meeting at 7:28 p.m.

PRESENTATION of GRANT APPLICATION
Supervisor Martin explained that the application for a grant from the Michigan
Natural Resources Trust Fund (MNRTF) was much like the grant application made
to the MNRTF in September 2008. Planning assistant Wanda Bloomquist, stated
that the revised grant application included changes suggested by the Department
of Natural Resources (DNR), increasing the opportunity for approval. The grant
will provide funds to improve trails, construct a picnic pavilion, provide
picnic tables, construct a barrier free restroom facility and construct two
sand volleyball courts. The funds would also make a portion of the walking
trails handicap accessible, by adding crush limestone.
Trustees Wilbrink, Hayes and Williams, encouraged the writers of the grant
application to review the application and see if there were areas that might be
modified to show the townships desire to make the park more accessible to
everyone. It was also suggested that effort be made to show how much the park
is presently used and how funds from the grant will not only increase
accessibility but provide opportunities for use without seasonal limitation.

ordinance. The essence of the comments was seeking clarification of various
aspects of the ordinance. One area of concern for clarification was the wording
in section 16, regarding the age limitation of an infant to be buried with a
parent. It was agreed that checking with the local mortician regarding their
policies and State requirements might provide a change in the wording, to be
more satisfactory to the board.
Minor corrections to word usage and sentence structure were noted for revising
the ordinance draft.
