MOTION POLICY
   Moved by Trustee Hayes to adopt as policy the following parliamentary
procedures for motions at the board meeting. This procedure was based on the
text Parliamentary Procedure in Local Government author National Association of
Parliamentarians Education committee 2003-2005. One of the committee members
Connie Deford spoke at the MTA convention in January
All motions are to be stated four times.
1.   Original motion with a second
2.   Chair states the question stating who made and seconded the motion
3.   Chair puts the question to a vote
4.   Chair announces the result stating the motion
Handling a motion:
1.   Member MAKES A MOTION
2.   Another member SECONDS the motion
3.   The Chair STATES the question
4.   Members DEBATE the motion
5.   The Chair PUTS the question to a vote
6.   The Chair ANNOUNCES the result
Amendments:
If the chair has not yet stated the motion, the maker of the motion has the
ability to modify the original motion. The individual who seconded the motion
is not consulted. If, however the chair has stated the motion the board now
owns the motion not the member who made it. All amendments must be voted or
approved by general consent before they are added to the motion.
Calling the question:
Calling the question is stopping the debate not asking for a vote. This act of
calling the question must have a second and be brought to a vote and passed for
the debate to stop.
Roll call votes:
After a vote is taken and a member requests a roll call vote it must be
supported and voted on by the board before it can move forward
SECONDED by Treasurer Eyster
Motion Passed
TRASH PICKUP
Supervisor Martin shared several communities have Township, City or Village
wide trash and recycle pickup. Supervisor Martin would like to discuss this
option with the board to determine if it would benefit residents with lowering
trash pickup cost, less trash littered throughout the Township, illegal burning
and burying of trash, less wear on our roads.
Discussion: The board discussed this option and some members are concerned
about taking away people’s choice, concerned with smaller businesses being
unable to compete and forcing them out of business, and having the township
field complaints when service is not satisfactory. Other board members would
like Supervisor Martin to pursue quotes for this service and bring back to the
next Township meeting for further discussion.
Granger Representative shared he is a firm believer in the free market. Granger
has 65% of the residential disposal business in the township and their
customers hire them for their service. If the township pursues an all inclusive
vendor it will lower the price and in turn reduce the quality of service to the
customer when communities go with bulk rates.
TREE PURCHASE FOR PARK
Wanda Bloomquist shared the Parks Committee is recommending to the board to
approve the purchase of 40 trees, 8-10 ft tall, bur lapped to plant along the
entrance to the park.
Discussion: The Township board would like the Parks Committee to consider a
diverse selection of trees to prevent disease and loss of trees and check on
the warranty/guarantee on the trees. It is also important that the trees be
protected from deer during the winter months.
MOVED by Trustee Hayes that Williamstown Township purchase 40 trees, watering
tank and other materials not to exceed $5,500.00. This is contingent upon
volunteers help for planting the trees to be appropriately organized prior to
purchase and include three different species of trees.
SECONDED by Treasurer Eyster
Motion Passed

BOARD PACKET & COMPUTERS AT MEETINGS
Clerk Gaffner shared information on BoardBook a company which compiles all
board meeting material, places it in one large PDF file with bookmarks that
allow board members to easily move any place in the file. This system would
save the Township considerable money, using less time, less paper and less work
by printers and copy machines. Pricing of this concept has not been fully
researched, but preliminary figure is $6,000 that includes laptops for all
board members and one-year of BoardBook service. The Planning Commission is
researching the possibility of purchasing a “SmartBoard” or a screen and a
projector that attaches to a computer and would provide the Township Board
audience with a visual during the meetings. Mr. Gaffner also shared with Adobe
Acrobat Pro board members can make notes on the material during discussion. It
was recommended by the Township board that Clerk Gaffner pursue BoardBook to
include the Adobe Acrobat Pro and return with additional information and costs
at the next meeting in May.

SEVEN YEAR BUDGET PROPOSAL
Supervisor Martin asked Treasurer Eyster to lead the discussion of the impact
of roads maintenance on future budgets. Treasurer Eyster indicated that she
requested Supervisor Martin attend the first meeting of the sub-committee to
provide us with background information on Township road maintenance and
indicate written and human resources that we can use to obtain the information
for the Board. Supervisor Martin reviewed who has responsibility for
maintaining roads, discussed the Pacer (road quality) rating system and the
activities of the Williamstown Township road committee
Treasurer Eyster outlined information for the sub-committee to gather and
present to the Board. These included:
1.   List of Township roads divided into state, county primary and county
2.   Legal basis for road maintenance
3.   Types of road surfaces and life expectancy of the surfaces
4.   Current condition of the county roads.
5.   Sources of funding for road maintenance
The sub-committee decided to develop a thorough report for the board including
a vision statement, listing of Township roads by type and length, rating of
roads using the Pacer rating system, types of road surfacing, costs per mile of
various road surfaces and sources of revenue for road maintenance.
At the next meeting of the subcommittee existing written information will be
discussed by the subcommittee members.

the 2008 Williamstown Township Drain Maintenance and Projected 2009 Drain Work.

over to the federal government for a savings of approximately $2 million.
Commissioner Lindemann recommends Williamstown Township prepare a resolution to
support the 1979 Wetland Protection Act and send it to Governor Granholm and
State Representatives. Commissioner Lindemann explained the value of controlled
ditch burns, the positive impact it has on the environment and the cost savings
to the county.

Heart of Michigan Trails proposal—Wanda Bloomquist shared a packet of
information on becoming a partner in the Heart of Michigan Trails and Greenways
Partnership. The packet includes the by-laws, list of current members and a
sample resolution. Trails provides places for cyclist, hikers, walkers, runners
in-line skaters, and physically challenged individuals to exercise and
experience many natural and cultural wonders of the tri-county area’s urban,
suburban, and rural environments. A tri county master plan is being developed
and the connections will be noted within MDOT. This alliance would keep our
community abreast of what is happening in the area and provide dialogue with
other communities on how they have developed their trails. There is no cost
involved and Ms. Bloomquist would be the representative for Williamstown
Township. It was recommended the resolution be placed on the July 7, 2009
consent agenda.

Treasurer Eyster - shared she is looking at the current budget. It is known
that the state is going to cut $8,000 in first 6 months of the fiscal year, but
not known what will be cut in the second. Trustee Eyster assumes the funding
for Williamstown Township will be down $25-35,000. The Township is looking at
ways to trim now without too much damage and what they can invest in now that
will save dollars in the long-term. The Township will have to find a way to
operate on less than what they have in the past; changes will be noticed and

year. Landowners are pleased. This should sustain our agricultural community.
Supervisor Martin will bring this back for more discussion in August 2009.
Sheriff Patrols—Supervisor Martin shared this topic is very important and the
Township must stay involved and proactive. Supervisor Martin does not feel
people in the township understand what it will costs for public safety if this
vital service is not provided by the county. County Commissioners are listening
and Supervisor Martin believes more public input is needed. Supervisor Martin
suggested the Township send out a large postcard mailing to all residents in
the township calling for a Town Hall Meeting to be held Wednesday, June 17,
2009 at 7 p.m. The Township needs active people in the community to help
influence those County Commissioners from Lansing and other municipalities
having their own police protection. Supervisor Martin suggested that mailing
costs of approximately $492.00 and printing costs of $200.00 would be necessary
for a Township wide mailing. It was recommended the cost of this proposal be
allowed up to $1,000.00 and the funds should be taken from the Newsletter
Budget.

Unfinished Business
Wetlands Resolution-- Wetlands provide Michigan communities with storm water
filtration, groundwater recharge, erosion control, flood control and fish &
wildlife habitat among other things. Williamstown Township Board of Trustees
herby urges the Michigan Legislature, should it choose to move forward with a
repeal of Part 303, to maintain the authority granted under Section 30307(4)
that enables local units of government, like Williamstown Township, to enact
and enforce local wetland regulations.
MOTION by Treasurer Eyster, that the Williamstown Township Board adopt
Resolution #83—“Resolution Opposing the Repeal of Michigan’s Wetland Protection
Act”.

Trailways Grant—Wanda Bloomquist shared she met with grant reviewers and
Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT). The issue with the current
trailways grant is that sidewalks are not considered trails. MDOT recommended
Williamstown Township wait until 2010 when MDOT is scheduled to pave the
shoulders of Grand River Road west of Zimmer to Meridian Road. The Trailways
Grant, providing for an 8' paved shoulder, would tie into this project well.
Other positive outcomes of working with MDOT are that MDOT would oversee and do
all the construction and engineering for the project. To increase the
possibility of receiving a Trailways Grant, MDOT recommends townships support
35% of the funding. Williamstown Township has until August 31, 2009, to make
the needed changes to the grant application.  Township Board
members recommended the Township proceed with the grant application.

Beeman Rd/Petition—Supervisor Martin shared a petition submitted by residents
of Maple Shade Subdivision, Beeman Road and Sherwood Road. This petition is in
reference to 4494 Beeman Road (the blue house located on Sherwood Road and
Beeman Road on the SE corner). The complaint is that this home has been in
violation of Williamstown Township “Blight Ordinance” for over two years, is
uninhabited, a health hazard and is unsightly. This affects all those living in
the area and those residents who live within 500 feet would like to be notified
of any Township action, in response to their petition. It was recommended by
the Township Board that Supervisor Martin ask the Township attorney to review
this situation and see if the “Blight Ordinance” can be used to take action on
the property owners of 4494 Beeman Road, if their property is not brought up to
a habitable status. It was recommended this item return for further discussion
at the October, 2009, meeting.
Park Improvements—Ms. Bloomquist shared a proposal from the Parks and
Recreation Committee to put in place parking dividers to better organize the
parking lot at the Township park on Grand River. The Parks and Recreation
Committee would like to add a handicap area (in the South lot, along the South
and East side) that allows parking for the elderly & handicap (i.e.
grandparents to park and stay within their vehicle to watch the sporting event)
and mark this area with the handicap signs as well. It was suggested that
dividing posts be added as well. These would run East and West and consist of 4
X 6 inch posts located 8’ on center with 1" rope from post to post. This allows
maintenance and snow removal with little obstruction. It was recommended parks
and recreation stay consistent with the 4 x 6 posts. Approximate costs for the
4 x 6 posts is $1146.00 Plus $350.00 Rental of post hole digger or bobcat.

September 15th, 2009
Joint Planning Commission and Board Meeting
Tuesday 6:30 September 15th, 2009
Williamstown Township
CALL TO ORDER
The Williamstown Township Board of Trustees and Planning Commission Members
convened at 6:30 p.m. at the Williamstown Township Hall located at 4990 Zimmer
Road, Williamston, Michigan.
Introduction Harmony Gmazel
Supervisor Martin introduced Williamstown Township Planning Assistant, Wanda
Bloomquist, who in turn introduced Harmony Gmazel, Land Use Planner for Tri-
County Regional Planning Commission. Planning Assistant Bloomquist shared Ms.
Gmazel will present information for a Tri-County Urban Service Management Study
and a Resolution of Support for the Tri-County Regional Urban/Rural Service
District/Boundary Committee and the Pursuit of the 2009 LIAA Partnerships for
Change: Sustainable Communities Grant.
Presentation Tri-County
Harmony Gmazel provided information on a Tri-County Urban Service Management
Study. The goal is to establish visions and goals, and setting new policy to
achieve those goals. Looking at process, district and boundary lines,
collaboration among members, sustaining a binding trust, empowerment created by
constructive involvement of many communities.
New growth in the region will be planned for mature corridors which connect
regional centers where transit ridership potential is highest. The majority of
new development is expected to be focused in areas where public water and sewer
systems are available and it is anticipated there will be more investment in
quality of life/livability factors, such as sidewalks, landscaping and
preservation of the tree canopy.
Harmony Gmazel provided information on the Resolution of Support for the Tri-
County Regional Urban/Rural Service District/Boundary Committee and the Pursuit
of the 2009 LIAA Partnerships for Change: Sustainable Communities Grant. This
grant would save taxpayers between 1.6 and 4.8 billion dollars in road
improvement costs, save agricultural land and open space, reduce air
pollutants, improve health, improve the economic competitiveness, including
urban development opportunities and increase global economy.
Questions and Answers
There were several questions that were fielded by Ms. Gmazel. There was a
feeling of support for this initiative among the Planning Commission and
Williamstown Township Board Members who were present.
   MEETING ADJOURNED by Supervisor Martin at 7:32 p.m.

Grant
Supervisor Martin shared Treasurer Eyster worked tirelessly on the $50,000
Energy Conservation Grant. The Township will have an energy audit completed and
plans to include recommendations from the energy audit in the proposal of the
Energy Conservation Grant. Other items to include in the proposal is reduced
electrical consumption inside township building and exterior parking lot,
reduction in heating water using point of source unit. The Township will hire
consultants to assist with changes to the Township Zoning and Master Plan. The
objective is to show the Township is taking care of themselves while promoting
energy conservation in the Township. The $50,000 grant is designed to reduce
fossil fuel emissions, reduce total energy use, improve energy efficiency in
the transportation, building, and other appropriate sectors; and create and
retain jobs. Supervisor Martin and Treasurer Eyster are designated authorize to
execute such assurances, certifications and other documentation as may be
required in the EECBG Program application by the US Department of Energy. If
Township board members have any ideas for inclusion in the proposal, contact
Treasurer Eyster.

CONSTRUCTION CODES ORDINANCE
STATE CODE
Ordinance Number #47
An ordinance to designate an enforcing agency to discharge the responsibility
of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP located in INGHAM County, under the provisions of
the Stille-DeRossett-HaIe Single State Construction Code Act, 1972 PA 230.
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP ordains:
Section 1. AGENCY DESIGNATED. Pursuant to the provisions of the Michigan
Building, Electrical, Mechanical and Plumbing Codes, in accordance with Section
8b(6) of 1972 PA 230, the Building, Electrical, Mechanical, and Plumbing Code
Officials of the WILLLAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP are hereby designated as the enforcing
agency to discharge the responsibility of the WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP under 1972
PA 230, State of Michigan.
WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP assumes responsibility for the administration and
enforcement of said Act throughout its corporate limits.
Section 2. REPEALS. All ordinances inconsistent with the provisions of this
ordinance are hereby repealed.
Section 3. PUBLICATION. This ordinance shall be effective after legal
publication and in accordance with provisions of the Act governing same.
Adopted this 10th day of November, 2009.
This ordinance duly adopted on November 10, 2009 at a regular meeting of the
TOWNSHIP and will become effective January 1, 2010.
Date: November 10, 2009.
Signed: ________________________________________ Ernie Gaffner - Township Clerk
Attested: _________________________________________ Mickey Martin – Township

Financial Policy—Treasurer Eyster
Section 1, Item 1.3—Imprest Cash--Treasurer Eyster shared 2 types of cash
drawers: imprest cash change fund ($200) other counter fund ($20.). Treasurer
Eyster is recommending the counter fund be raised to ($30.) and the trigger for
replenishing be set at ($15.).
Section 1, 1.6 (b) Property Tax Receipts – Treasurer Eyster shared a paragraph
has been added: the Township has arranged with Independent Bank (Williamston
Branch only), to accept tax payments. If someone comes to the Township office
and finds it closed, they can go down to Independent Bank and pay their tax
bill. There is no cost to the township. Independent Bank will deposit the
payment directly into the Township’s tax account with the original bill—this
original bill along with a receipt will then be given to the Township. Trustee
Wright recommended the Township place a sign on Township doors to this affect.
Treasurer Eyster also noted this option will be placed on resident tax bills,
the Township website, the Township newsletter, and as a phone message.
Section 3, Item 3.5—Authorized Check Signers—Treasurer Eyster suggested a
revision to this policy—#3. Permitting the signing of a check by both the
appointed Deputy Treasurer and Deputy Clerk, when neither the elected Treasurer
nor Clerk are available, if they receive oral or written e-mail permission from
the Treasurer, Clerk or Supervisor.
Discussion: Several Township Board members shared comments to the revision in
Section 3, 3.5.3. There were pros and cons voiced, but the majority feels some
flexibility in emergency situations is warranted and this is therefore
acceptable.
Section 6, Item 6.2—Login and Access Requests—Supervisor Treasurer Eyster
shared the current software does not stop or disable the account after three
attempts to sign in, therefore, it is recommended this paragraph be removed/
stricken from this section.
MOTION by Trustee Wright that the Williamstown Township Board approve adoption
of the revisions to the Williamstown Township Financial Policy showing the
revision date of November 17, 2009.

Article II of Zoning Ordinance
Supervisor Martin shared a May 27, 2009 red-lined version of Article II of the
Township Zoning Ordinance from McKenna & Associates Planning Consultants for
review:
o   Page 2-4-Article 2 Setbacks , Item b— Side Yard Setbacks in Large Lot
Residential Districts—Supervisor Martin is not sure what is meant by this? It
was recommended to list districts here or take districts out. Change 2400 sq ft
to 1500 sq ft. Item iii— Stake Survey —add accessory building—inspection must
be preapproved by building inspector prior to adding the structure—the building
inspector will then determine if a stake survey is needed.
o   Page 2-8, Section 2.06 Home   Occupations and Home Based Business —Section
C.2 Standards  for Home Occupations —Supervisor Martin would like to see
immediate family or immediate relative allowed/added as an allowable member to
the family business. Will need to define immediate relative.
o   Page 2-8, Section 2.06 Home Occupations and Home Based Business —Section
D.1— Standards for Home-Based Businesses --Supervisor Martin would like the
red-lined strike to be left in tact—Don’t exceed regulations (one full time
equivalent, non-resident, non-family employee)
o   D.2--Renters—should be home owner only, no more than one sign—eliminate
number of signs – No signs allowed without a permit—Supervisor Martin feels
only one sign per household should be allowed.
o   D.2--Occupants—don’t have to own? Rentals? Concern is that renters do not
have as much invested as a homeowner. The board consensus is of the mind set if
occupants are following rules they have the same rights as a homeowner.
o   Page 2-12—Section 2.09 Yard and Bulk Regulations —Item 4. Unobstructed
Sight Distance --Cannot put wall or structure in set back—Supervisor Martin
feels this whole section needs to be taken out as it contradicts areas of the
whole ordinance. STRIKE OUT (this section will be left in Subdivision Control
Ordinance)
o   Plantings—Supervisor Martin shared this cannot be enforced--private
property—no judge will allow us to cut down plantings. Planning Commission
would like to keep this as it is a safety precaution. There was disagreement
with this item. Township will pick up topic at next meeting.
o   Page 2-13, Article 2, Table 2.1—looked for definition of court yard,
interior side yard and street side yard. It was recommended the following
definitions be added: court yard, interior side yard, air conditioning
equipment shelter, laundry drying equipment, clothes line, paved terraces, open
porches, encroachment and LED.
o   2-16, Section 2.10 Streets, Roads and Other Means of Access —D.1 Minimum
Driveway Setbacks --10 ft unless specified otherwise… need to add PUDs
o   2-17 D.6 Vertical Clearance —driveways and roads for commercial use needed
for emergency and fire dept access shall maintain a minimum vertical clearance
of 5 feet rather than 13.5 feet.
o   2-19 Section 2.11 Grading Regulations , Section B, Grading Plan , Item 1.
Grading Plan-….or may be submitted as a separate plan. (Strike this) and add:
grading plans shall be prepared and planned by a land surveyor or civil
engineer. It is recommended this is done ahead by self or in conjunction with a
site plan. It was also recommended an electronic version of grading plan be
submitted with written grading plan.
o   2-19 Section 2.11 Grading Regulations , Section C. Grading Standards ,
Section 2 . Runoff Onto Adjacent Properties —Supervisor Martin shared Run off
on adjacent property should not exceed the current 10% run off with no increase
on neighbor. STRIKE THIS; DO NOT WANT TO HAVE TO REQUIRE A BUILDIG INSPECTOR.
o   Page 2-20 Section 2.12 Lighting , A. Intent —Trustee Wilbrink, would like
added to the last sentence in the paragraph -- Use of energy efficient lighting
(LED).
o   2-28 Section 2.14 Junkyards and Landfills,--Supervisor Martin would like to
strike the added language in blue. This language is included with Private
Property and falls under the Blight Ordinance. It is recommended more research
be done on this topic.
o   2-32 Section 2.16 Exceptions , B. Exceptions to Height Standards
—Supervisor Martin shared there is a whole section dedicated to Height
Standards and wants to make sure this is consistent with those sections for
clarity (i.e., add windmill and list towers)
o   2-34 Section 2.18 Performance Guarantee —B. General Requirements
—Supervisor Martin would like to add in B.1 something about insurance bond,
needs to say cannot have expiration date.
o   2-35 Section 2.19— Trash Removal and Collection —A.3 Screening, the last
sentence—Supervisor Martin would like the last sentence Stricken/Removed.

Note: TRI COUNTY PLANNING—The first phase of the Greening Mid Michigan project
is the Potential Conservation Area (PCA) report, completed in 2008 by the
Michigan Natural Features Inventory. Phase II of this project has just been
completed. The newest report, “Significant Natural Features in the Tri-County
Region: Providing Ecological Information for a Green Infrastructure Plan,” is
intended to serve as a resource for community planning and water resource
protection. This report describes natural communities, rare plant and animal
diversity, and includes an Aquatic Biodiversity Assessment for the tri-county
region. Supervisor Martin encourages board members to attend a Charette,
Thursday, February 15 to hear the overall vision on what is going on with the
Green Infrastructure Plan.

Poverty Exemption Guidelines—Supervisor Martin shared every year the Township
must adopt a “Poverty Guidelines Resolution.” It is recommended that the
Township adopt the Federal Poverty Guidelines for 2010 with an increase of 50%
in all sections and to limit assets to one licensed vehicle for each resident,
with a maximum of two, and to one principle residence with asset value
determined by the following method: true cash value as stated in an approved
assessment role $250,000 for up to 100 % exemption with a decrease of 20% for
every increase of $50,000 in value.

Supervisor Martin reviewed the Grant Award. Total Cost of paving both shoulders
along AM-43 from Meridian Rd to Zimmer Rd. with an additional 8 ft. shoulders
marked for non-motorized transportation would cost $450,000. The Township share
is 35% or $157,500. MDOT will cover the balance. This will be done in
conjunction with resurfacing work scheduled for 2010. Match will come out of
fund balance. This would address safety issues for bike riders through the
Township and to the park. Meeting is scheduled with MDOT for the 17th. Planning
Asst. Bloomquist will be attending.

Energy Grant Resolution
Treasurer Eyster reviewed the Grant Award. Application was a joint effort with
Wheatfield, Locke and Leroy Townships. Award is for $75,384. $50,000 will go to
Williamstown Township with the balance shared between the other three
Townships. The grant will be used to retrofit the Township Hall to reduce
energy consumption, provide workshops and a light bulb exchange for residents,
reduce cost at the cemetery by providing a composting toilet and to provide
planning fees for the GR Green Zone and the amendments to the Master Plan for a
Trails and Greenway Plan along with providing expansion of bus use for the
residents at the Township Park.
Discussion ensued regarding:

§   Permanent restroom facilities at the Township-saves rental fee.

intent and funding of $1000.00 from the Township to work with the other 13

Ryan explained his proposal for his Eagle Scout Project of 3 bike racks to be
used at the Township Park and the Township Hall. Currently there is not a means

addition for those that use their bikes to get to the parks. They would be made

removal. Location would be determined by maintenance. This would be a savings
to the Township in lieu of purchasing racks. Completion would be anticipated in
late April or May.

New Business
Zoning Ordinance amendment Medical Marijuana—Supervisor Martin shared Trustee
Hayes and Chairman Fielek attended a seminar on the New Medical Marijuana Law
presented by the Michigan Municipal League. A “qualifying patient” can possess
up to 2.5 ounces of usable marijuana, they can keep up to 12 marijuana plants
in an “enclosed, locked facility” if a primary caregiver is not assigned. If
primary caregiver is assigned they can assist up to five qualifying patients.
This means they can possess up to 2.5 ounces of usable marijuana for each
qualifying patient and keep up to 12 marijuana plants for each qualifying
patient.
Now that this Act is in effect, municipalities are considering or have adopted
ordinances regulating how marijuana is used and distributed within their
respective boundaries. The critical question is whether local governments have
the authority to regulate medical marijuana through police power ordinances or
through zoning.
Supervisor Martin recommended that the Planning Commission prepare a proposal
on adopting an ordinance that would regulate how marijuana is used and
distributed within the township. Chairman Fielek will work on this
recommendation.
ITC—Supervisor Martin shared ITC will be replacing wood poles with metal poles
and running power lines late 2010, early 2011. The metal poles have a better
longevity. The height of the poles (200 ft) was questioned, as to whether or
not they may interfere with Mayden’s Airport on Zimmer Road and the ½ mile
landing pattern.
Parks and Recreation fees—Wanda Bloomquist shared discussion to charge fees for
use of Township fields has been ongoing for over a year and a half. The
proposal is that all groups will be charged the same fee across the board. The
Township Parks & Recreation Committee is proposing a $25 fee for a three hour
block/reservation fee and $10 fee for a two hour block for practices. Groups
would need to reserve times for these events and reservations would be visible
at the Township Park for all to see.
Motion by Treasurer Eyster that the Township Board approve the Parks &
Recreation Committee’s recommendation to set fees for the use of Township
grounds for organized recreational games and practices at $25 for 3 hour
scheduled game time and $10 for 2 hour scheduled practice time.
Seconded by Trustee Hayes.
Motion Approved

Unfinished Business
Police Service—Resolution--Supervisor Martin shared a timeline of events. At
present, 11 townships and the Village of Dansville have passed the resolution.
Ingham County is terminating police protection by the county sheriff to the
Township after December 31, 2010. The Townships are preparing to form a Police
Board to provide police protection to the governmental agencies affected.
Williamstown Township will need to raise funds by special assessment in order
to finance the cost of police protection under 1951 PA 33, as amended. The
special assessment would be placed on the November ballot and include $150 cap
per household and $250 for a commercial unit. After a successful passage of the
proposal, two hearings would be held (1) Public Hearing—so citizens could voice
their support or concerns and (2) Public Hearing—so citizens can voice any
concerns relative to the assessment.
Concern was raised around having a cap with a possible annual increase.
Treasurer Eyster indicated to the board that the annual increase was in lieu of
a cost of living increase. Another concern was fees collected in the township,
who gets the fees? Supervisor Martin shared many of the logistics are being
finalized by the Township Attorney.
Commissioner Randy Schafer shared he has been fighting the Police Service issue
since 1978 and commends Supervisor Martin for encouraging 13 townships to come
together to pass this resolution. Commissioner Schafer will continue to support
the townships, write letters, campaign, whatever it takes to promote and
support this endeavor.
Motion by Treasurer Eyster to move the Williamstown Township Board approve
Resolution #93, placing a special assessment proposal for a Police Board on the
November 2010 ballot.
Seconded by Trustee Wright.

INGHAM COUNTY SHERIFF report Sgt. Steve Sopocy—Sergeant Sopocy shared May 2010
Activity Report for Williamstown Township.
Sergeant Sopocy stated that when calling from a cell phone a person may reach a
911 operator for a district outside the area the person was calling from and
should ask specifically to be transferred to the county or jurisdiction of
choice. These instances can easily occur as cell towers across jurisdictional
lines may be the tower receiving and transmitting an individual’s call and not
ring into the area from which the call is made. Making a 911 call using a
“landline” has a greater chance of reaching the correct 911 operator.

members to begin improvements to the soccer fields. Improvements include
protective fencing for the softball field and bike rack. Plans are in place for
an Ultimate Frisbee Tournament and Softball Tournament to attract people to the
park during the week of Red Cedar Jubilee. There will also be an event entitled
Geo Cashing (GPS Unit, Coordinates) hunt throughout the park.

over $1600 dollars was raised during this event. The dollars raised will go
towards playground equipment in Williamston Township. A model will be on

residents can see where their dollars are to be spent.

July Tax Notices—Supervisor Martin shared information on the Police Protection

notices are scheduled to be mailed July 1, 2010.
Ground Water Heat Pump—Treasurer Eyster shared information she received at a
presentation focused on vertical and horizontal closed loop ground water heat
pump systems. This type of system pays for itself quickly and has a life span
of 50 years. Treasurer Eyster shared a vertical closed loop would not be
required because of the large land area owned by the Township and if an open
system is used, a rain garden could be developed with the over flow to a
wetland area.
Leroy Township Fire Station—Trustee Wilbrink shared the bid for the addition of
a bay area came in at $700,000. Plans are to move forward with this bid. Phase
II of the plan includes remodeling of the old Leroy Township hall.

inspector hired by the Township resigned. Mr. Tim O’Neal of Leroy Township will
be Acting Building Inspector until further notice.

program, for a total of $50,000 if done this year. They would also include

The Road Committee recommends the Township Board approve the repair and
resurface of

2011 Township funds allocated for road improvements.

the process of rating all of the roads with a simplified system to compare with
the County’s Pacer ratings also being conducted this summer.

$10,000.

AGENDA
Discussion of the Michigan Department of Energy, Labor and Economic Growth
(DELEG) Grant and the completed Energy Audit by ENERGYCHECK™.
Treasurer Eyster explained the process to be taken by the Township in utilizing
the Energy Grant. The Township Board will need to take three votes:
1.   Based on the Energy Audit, what areas should ENERGYCHECK™ draft bid
specifications.
2.   Approve the bid specifications.
3.   Approve bids to be accepted for completion of energy saving projects.
The grant funding will be utilized in three areas; 1) Weatherizing; 2)
Lighting; 3) Heating.
Due to the complexity of oversight relative to the energy grant funds,
ENERGYCHECK™ will assist Treasurer Eyster in the management of the funds and
required reporting.
The three additional townships sharing the energy grant, Locke, Leroy and
Wheatfield have received their energy audits and are following this same
process.
Supervisor Martin stated that the Township is presently waiting for additional
information to install a shelter at the Park-N-Ride location on Grand River.
The shelter will be paid for with some of the Energy Grant funds.
Treasurer Eyster provided information on various Geo-Thermal scenarios for
heating the Township office building. In Michigan’s climate, information
supplied by ENERGYCHECK™ indicates that using a ground water system is much
more efficient than an air to air system.
Motion by Trustee Hayes to have specifications drafted by ENERGYCHECK™ for an
open ground water heating system.
Supported by Trustee Williams. Motion approved.
MOTION by Trustee Williams to adjourn.

expert recommends switching to 3.65 Megahertz and is running a trail test in

Cemetery Fee Resident/Non-Resident Definition
Trustee Hayes worked on the following resident definitions for the purpose of
the Cemetery Fee Schedule:
“ Resident ”
A “Resident” is any one of the following persons:
      1.   A person residing in Williamstown Township at the time of purchasing
space in a Williamstown Township managed cemetery, with the exception that a
person not residing in Williamstown Township at the time of death will be
considered a “non-resident”, or
      2.   A person residing in Williamstown Township at the time of death, or
      3.   A person residing within the jurisdiction of a governmental agency
providing financial support for maintenance of Williamstown Township cemeteries
during either of the following times:
         a.   At the time of purchasing space, with the exception that a person
not residing in the contributing governmental jurisdiction at the time of death
will be considered a “non-resident, or
         b.   At the time of death
“ Non-resident ”
A person not meeting any of the “resident” definition criteria above is
considered a “non-resident” for the purpose of the Williamstown Township
Cemetery Fee Schedule.
Supervisor Martin move the Williamstown Township Board approve the definitions
of Resident and Non-Resident as it applies to Township Cemetery Fees.
Seconded by Trustee Hayes.
Discussion:
·   Need to maintain is costly and paid by township.
·   Status is at time of purchase or death
Motion approved.

Park Prairie Burn
Supervisor Martin explained the history and reason for a burn.
This would be third prairie burn which is recommended every third year until
established.
Allows native plants to thrive and suppress invasive species.
Waiting allows invasive species to thrive.
Assessment of reseeding would take place once snow is removed.
Concerned about wildlife habitat nesting in ground.
Trustee Hayes moved the Williamstown Township Board approve the Parks &

Park on Grand River Road. The burn is to be completed by David Borneman LLC and
PlantWise of Ann Arbor, during the spring of 2011 for an agreed to contracted
cost to the Township of $7,240. The Burn includes 53 acres of prairie and 7
acres of woods.

Police Assessment
Treasurer Eyster reviewed with legal counsel how much money can be kept in the
police fund special assessment. The township assessment is set up under Act 33
and does not require Twp to return funds over 5%. It allows the township to
reasonably have money for unforeseen circumstances, to build funds for
equipment, etc. The Board approved to decrease the assessment for the next
year. Will bring a policy back that would allow funding to follow fiscal year.
It is hard to figure budget when they are not aligned. Needs to be in a policy
to know how much to carry over, etc. Will bring back a suggested policy to the
Board for consideration. Meridian Township is not on the same fiscal year.
New Business
BSA systems conversion
Treasurer Eyster reviewed conversion. BSA made a conversion about 3.5 years
ago. System is self contained. System has been totally rewritten- but some real
good enhancements would be available. Old system will not be updated with
improvements. Taxing and assessing is more integrated. The two systems are
currently not in sync and they would be in the new system. The new system
integrates better with GIS systems. We have held off so that it could be
tested. County has asked for others to wait but they are setting to convert in
June if approved by commissioners. Assuming they convert, the township would
get a discount to convert by the end of the year. Our server is up for
replacement this year. Cost is quite a bit more to go to a web based server. We
don’t have to make the move but it is recommended. It currently takes most of
the year to get through taxes. We need a review of all our hardware to make
sure we are compatible with the upgrade. May need additional software that is
free from Microsoft. Most of the cost is addressed in the memo. This will take
most of the money for capital improvements for this year. We will need to do
this at some point and would like to do it in June. Would like to schedule for
June with the ability to cancel. County is going to County Commissioners for
approval in May. Not asking for approval now- and would not recommend if the
County does not approve. The system also has enhanced auditing.
Will bring back to board in June with final numbers.
Restricted funds
Supervisor Martin explained the restricted funds. This is a budget amendment.
May want to look at how high to set contingency fund. Must be reviewed each
year. Can not be done at budget time because we need to know what is left. May
is first month to do carry over and be accurate.
Treasurer Eyster moved that the Williamstown Township Board change the
following budget expenditure lines to carryover restricted funds:

May 20, 2011
Williamstown Township
Board of Trustees Special Meeting Minutes
Call to Order
The Williamstown Board of Trustees special meeting convened at 10:08 a.m. at
the Williamstown Township Hall located at 4990 N. Zimmer Rd., Williamston,
Michigan. Supervisor Mickey Martin called the meeting to order.
Pledge of Allegiance
Roll Call
Present: Trustee Wilbrink, Supervisor Martin, Treasurer Eyster and Clerk
Gaffner
Absent: Trustee Wright, Trustee Hayes and Trustee Williams
Public Comment for agenda & non-agenda items
Since there was no one in the audience there was no call for public comment.
Supervisor Martin closed Public Comments at 10:10
Treasurer Eyster presented information on the rational, costs and logistics of
implementation of new computer hardware and conversion upgrade of the
Township’s bookkeeping software from BS&A. To stay current with Ingham County
and other municipalities using BS&A software, there is a need for Williamstown
Township to approve the conversion to BS&A.NET
The cost of conversion and the required larger server along with training for
Township staff and installation is $23,425.
Assessing and Tax $7,200
Financial $3,175
Building $3,750
Training $2,400
Server and Installation $6,900
Total $23,425
Treasurer Eyster stated that the total cost for this conversion exceeded the
2011-2012 budgeted amounts for these costs but BS&A would allow payments over
the next two years and no interest charges will be assessed. Trustee Wilbrink,
stated he believed there was sufficient reason to use some money from the
Township surplus and pay the total amount at the present time.
Consensus of the board discussion was that knowing there may be additional
costs to the Township in other budget areas requiring movement of funds from
the surplus, it would be best to take advantage of the offer from BS&A and
address the issue later in the 2011-2012 budget year.
Motion by Clerk Gaffner that the Williamstown Township Board approve the BS&A
software conversion to BS&A.NET and purchase of additional computer hardware
required to meet the specifications of the software conversion and provide
training of Township Staff, at a total cost of $23,425. It is also understood
that the payment of $23,425 will be spread over the next two years, with no
interest charge and final payment to BS&A will be paid in April 2013. It is
further understood further staff training may be required at an additional
cost.
Second by Treasurer Eyster
Motion Approved
Motion by Trustee Wilbrink to adjourn the meeting at 10:20 a.m.
Meeting adjourned.

Communications Chair, Marvin Thompson, gave a report of the problems that have
been challenging for providing consistent service. FreedomNet did a pilot of
new equipment in Grand Rapids and found a few problems that need to be
addressed before installation. This will move service to a licensed frequency.
At a May 5 th meeting with FreedomNet, a lease agreement was approved.
FreedomNet has ordered the equipment. Installation should be quick once it is
in. Priority will go to residents with problems. Money allocated to date by the
Township has been primarily for the road to the tower. Lease payments are
received for the land the tower sits on and we benefit with free service to the
Township. May take a couple of years to adequately service all residents.
Discussion:
·   Cost to the residents will remain the same.
·   Intereference: Currently two frequencies that are the same as the

been very cooperative and willing to work with the Township to create a
solution.
·   Reliability has been good except for interference with amateur radio.
·   FreedomNet has extended service in other areas. Interference has been in
Locke, Wheatfield and Williamstown Twps.
·   Thanks to Marvin Thompson and Kurt Guter for their dedication to the
residents of the Township.

recommendation. Variance would be needed to waive paving.

allowable.

variance.
·   Spruce trees planted as screening would interfere with utilities.

·   Deposit landscaping waste and remove weekly. Consenses on weekly removal of

residents only and the ability to limit the number of times the survey can be
taken.

Business License
Supervisor Martin explained the reasoning for addressing the use of a business
license. Several options were included in packet. Business license would insure
it was a permitted use, provide the building inspector a chance to inspect the
premises for safety. This would apply to commercial and industrial businesses
only. This would allow the Township to inform new business owners of the zoning
ordinances.
Discussion included:
·   Burden on private sector.
·   Vehicle for them to know what the regulations are up front.
·   Owner of property would have to report new businesses.
·   Nominal fee recommended
·   Would help reduce amount of misunderstanding before moving in.
·   Reasonable renewal allows for dealing with issues, complaints, etc.
·   More mediation instead of code violations.
·   Transfer of ownership would require relicensing
·   Safety issues would be caught
·   Uses not permitted would be caught before established.
·   Points of the three sample ordinances that should be in our requirements.
·   Better handle on businesses going out of business and dealing with personal
property taxes.
·   Before board only if concerns or rejected.
·   Final approval would be from board.
·   Would be part of a consent agenda.
·   Township should send out renewals.
·   Would renewals go to property owner or to individual mailing address.
·   Could not open until the business had license.
·   Would be an ordinance.
·   Important for permitted use and signage.
·   Get us in ahead before money being spent by business and changes needed.
·   Merit for us to do this.
·   Save the township and business owners conflicts and money.
·   Hazardous waste handling is important to be part of new ordinance.
·   Good points in sample ordinances to consider in developing Townships.
·   Consensus to move forward with draft for board to consider.
·   Packet for new business owners similar to resident welcome packet with
ordinance information for getting started.
·   Packet on line for businesses considering moving into the Township

Planning Commission Report
Chair Fielek reviewed the PC meeting of 11/15/11. Two public hearings were
held; one on the revisions to Article 8 through Article 22 and the other on
Auction Regulations. The Planning Commission voted to recommend the Board
approve revisions to Art.8-Art.22 and deliberation will take place in January
on the Auction Regulations.
The Planning Commission also reviewed Dr. Shannon’s request for a shared drive
regarding lot splits based on the option to split for non-farm dwellings. The
Planning Commission voted to deny this request based on design, poor planning
with two abutting drives, was not in keeping with the rural character and lack
of driveway restrictions and agreement on maintenance.
Commissioners would like to see a survey go out with the property assessment to
aid in the review of the Master Plan. The Board should have the survey for
review at the January meeting.
Article 8-22 were in the Board’s packet for review. In light of what transpired
at the meeting, there was a party affected by the changes. At the end of the
meeting it was determined to recommend the revisions to the Board for approval.
As chair, in the public interest, recommend sending back to the PC for further
deliberation.
The Planning Commission finished their deliberation on the Green Zone language
and has recommended the board approve the language presented. The Planning
Commission deliberated over several months and addressed the issues brought
forward to them in this current language. There was no opposition at the last
meeting to the Green Zone. There was discussion over the use of the Green Zone
as an overlay vs. zoning amendment. The zoning amendment will give consistency
to the design of the area where the overlay could end up with partial
participation. This will expand the uses available to land owners with
development. The view shed protects the Township. Already seen with Pine Knoll
and proposed developments. Green Zone only applies to parcels over 20 acres.
Supervisor Martin was pleased with the changes brought forward. Business owners
were concerned and felt the changes were sufficient.
Discussion included:
·   Favor overlay as it provides either/or.
·   Would create inconsistency
·   Might be too restrictive
·   Not common throughout the area
·   Might find problems since not tested in other areas
·   Concepts are popular in other states with LEED
·   Gold LEED home being built within the Green Zone
·   Landowner could request rezoning
·   Meridian working on Urban Service Boundary
·   Incentive for Innovative Development
·   Existing uses can continue
·   350 ft. setback seems excessive
·   Pine Knoll currently has more than a 350 ft. setback
·   Proposed Ashton Meadows also had 350 ft. setback
·   Natural buffer is desired
·   Could split a parcel off without affecting the Green Zone
·   Parcels less than 20 acres would stay in current zoning
·   Parcels could be combined to use the Green Zone
·   Preference as overlay.
Trustee Williams moved the Williamstown Township Board approve the adoption of
Zoning Ordinance Article 25.00C, the Green Zone Planned Development District.
Seconded by Treasurer Eyster
Trustee Hayes arrived.

Motion approved.

Road Maintenance 7 year proposals
Supervisor Martin expressed her appreciation of the work by the road committee
and the participation of the ICRC. The concern being addressed is over cost to
keep maintenance up on the paved roads within the township. Only 2 miles remain
unpaved. The roads are rated on a pacer system: looks at cracks, rolling, etc.
This is a very defined procedure with ratings from 1 to 10. 1 is the worst. It
has been determined that if you can keep your roads at a 5 or 6 and repaired on
a continual basis, this is the most cost effective approach. All roads have
been inspected.
Williamston, Sherwood, Meridian, Haslett and Zimmer are county primary roads.
North of Haslett, Zimmer is not a county road. Maintenance of all roads in the
county is the responsibility of the county, however they must have a match if
they are going to do major work on a local or collector road. Does not have to
come from the Township but this is generally where it will come from. The
Township can request any improvements they want but the responsibility is still
with the road commission. The match is for resurfacing and major repairs/
improvements. The Roads Committee has submitted the following three proposals
for review of the Board of how funds could be used to repair our roads.
Option A would only maintain collector roads but would not cover local roads.
Could revert roads to ground asphalt roads. Ingham County takes care of all
gravel roads. This is not true of all counties. Some townships buy the gravel
for road maintenance. Most of the roads of this county are paved which is
unusual. Livingston has a majority of their roads unpaved. The Township Board
committed last year to put aside $30,000 per year.
·   Option A is assuming the 30,000 from Ingham County. Concern of cost
increases and being able to maintain roads appropriately. One solution would be
to move some roads from collector roads to local road.
·   Option B looks at the above scenario.
The Roads Committee did not anticipate ever getting more than the $30,000 from
the county.
The County provides road ratings (pacer score), this is done by hiring state
trained personnel.
If a road gets below a 4 then the cost increases to bring it back up to par.
Cost curve minimizes at the 4/5 level.
Are there examples of any 7’s? Most of the roads are 4 or 5’s. There are short
segments that are 3 or 2. Do not have a pacer score for GR. Agate and Thatcher
are a 2 along with a portion of Vanneter Rd. and Meadowdale.
Clarification of the three alternatives:
A. Would maintain only 16.5 miles of twp. Other roads would need to be done by
Special Assessment or other method. County maintains ground asphalt roads which
are not as loose as gravel. Not as good as chip and seal. This might work well
for less traveled roads.
John McLaughlin spoke to the pacer rating: The higher the pacer rating the less
surface maintenance needed. A lower rating indicates the subsurface of the road
has been compromised.
B. Could reclassify some of the roads from township collector roads as local
roads. This would drop the miles down to 10.5 to be placed on the 7 year
maintenance plan. This would leave $20,000 for local road maintenance along
with special assessments. Special assessment would be higher the further the
pacer number dropped.
Discussion:
·   How long will the road commission forward the unused funds to the next
year?
·   In any given year you could have a number of projects come forward.
·    Qualifiers that help score the roads would include traffic count and
speed.
·   Bill Conklin of ICRC has been involved in the 7 year cycle.
·   What will happen when the road commission board is demolished?
·   Current funding is provided by the state gas tax. Revenue could be
declining.
·   The committee has been very thorough in their discussion of these issues.
·   Will need to prioritize roads.
·   There is not enough money to maintain all the roads in the Township. This
is different for each township in the county.
C. Millage request of 1 mil would maintain all roads at a pacer level of 7 or
better on a 7 year cycle.
Discussion:
·   It is up to the Board to decide how to move forward.
·   The township is not responsible for principal arterial roads.
·   Option C assumes property values continue to go up with 1 mil. In order to
increase funding.
·   Could look at millage on a 7 year cycle.
·   Special assessment would be a loan and we would need to finance the special
assessment.
·   Bonds may be needed to be able to loan the money for special assessments.
·   Bad weather could affect the amount of money received from the county due
to maintenance.
·   There is a formula cap used by the county.
·   Options A and C use the same classifications for the roads.
·   Option C would include all the roads.
·   Is there a need to expand the options?
·   The Board would like to review the pacer ratings for all roads along with
estimates on cost.
·   Need to come up with an overall plan and prioritize roads.
·   Would also like to see a scenario of not getting any money from the county.
Not sure if this is productive. The Board will have to review this issue
frequently to stay on track.
·   Looking at special assessment over a period of time could cause cash flow
issues.
·   Would like to see the best way to fund a special assessment. The Township
could cap amount spent each year.
·   How to be fair gets difficult.
·   Roads may need to get so bad before residents are willing to pay for them.
Need to provide an incentive to keep roads in good condition.
·   Mitchell and Vanneter were taken over by the county due to school traffic.

Police Report
Chief Hall reviewed the police report. Numbers are up a bit. On March 31st,
the department was dispatched to the Red Cedar Antique Mall. Called from the
alarm, building was broken into. Antique jewelry was taken. This has been
happening around the state in Antique Malls, also in Indiana and Illinois.
Trends: more calls but nothing out of line. Comparison chart shows three years
comparison and includes the ICSD. Eight assist to ambulance this month.
Officers are limited as to supplies that can be carried. County and Township/EL
dispatches should be combined sometime in May. The State Police reported back
on the Mitchell Rd study with an average speed of 45 to 48 mph. No change in
the speed limit was recommended at this time. Chief Hall will verify the report
with the Board.
Julie Chrsinske CADL Report
Annual reports were distributed to trustees and officers. Julie is the Head
librarian for the Williamston Branch. Williamston highlights for year: Library
had over 66,800 visits. This is an increase over previous years. Over 500 kids
participated in summer reading programs. Provide literacy training to the
schools. Friends group held quarterly book sales and they also provide special
programs. 2012 programs coming up: Mother’s Day event and a special author
visit.
Open for questions:
Appreciative of the presence of the library.
E-books are available through the library as well as training on the new
devices.
There is a misconception of the need for libraries with the advent of internet
access. Borrowing is always better than buying. Research material and access is
available through the library.
Media specialists go into the high school to teach researching and explain the
professional data bases that are available through the library. Genealogy
information is available through the library. Offer adult computer programs. No
charge for these services. Provide access to those that don’t have it- rural
areas are affected due to lack of internet access.

Senior Center – Resolution
60 year resident, Virginia Taschner, gave a brief history of the Senior Center.
Senior Center is celebrating 20 years of service. The Senior Center began as
part of the school district. Lost funding in 2005 from the Williamston School
District and the Tri-County Office on Aging (TCOA). There is currently enough
money to fund through 2013. The Senior Center Board decided to try for a
millage. The Senior Center is currently meeting at the community center owned
by the city. May need to find space in approximately 3 years if not sooner.
Served over 6200 lunches last year. Currently meet 3 days a week. Lunch comes
from TCOA. Funding would allow an increase of staff to accommodate the need for
future growth. Currently have fundraisers and generous donors that help support
the center. Asking Locke, Wheatfield, Leroy, City of Williamston along with
Williamstown Township to place on their respective ballots. The City of
Williamstown and Leroy Township have agreed to place it on the ballot. Need
approval by units of government to let the residents decide. Would like to be
able to help people participate in programs being offered with increased
funding. Currently cooperate with the library regarding programs. Active group
of participants.
Discussion:
The township has contributed over the years but has never been presented with a
budget.
Would like to see a budget presentation to see what will happen with monies
collected.

City is not under obligation to support.

May 22, 2012
Call to Order
The Williamstown Township Board of Trustees convened at 5:30 pm. at the
Williamstown Township Hall located at 4990 Zimmer Rd., Williamston, Michigan.
Supervisor Mickey Martin called the meeting to order and reviewed the agenda
and explained the procedure for public comment.
Roll Call
Present: Trustee Williams, Supervisor Martin, Clerk Gaffner, Treasurer Eyster,

Absent: Trustee Wright
Public Comment
None
Supervisor Martin closed Public Comment at 5:32
Senior Center – Resolution
Several representatives of the Williamston Senior Center were in attendance and
all deferred to Representative Dawn Marie Joseph, as their spokesperson for
this meeting with the Williamstown Township Board. A proposed Senior Center
Budget, based upon monies available, should a Senior Center millage vote be
successful in the City of Williamston and the townships of Wheatfield, Locke,
Leroy and Williamstown, was provided for each board member. The budget included
amounts for facility rental and maintenance as well as revised staffing and
money for a new building.
At present the Senior Center uses space, rent free, provided by the City of
Williamston, however, it is not known how long this arrangement will continue.
The Senior Center space is limited, the funds are very limited and the Senior
Center Board does not believe the Center will be allowed to continue without
the passage of the requested millage.
Some discussion centered on the possibility of the Senior Center and the
Williamston Library representatives working together to seek millage for one
facility to serve both entities. There was discussion about a lack of interest
between the two entities of working together but it was thought by some that a
joint effort would have a much better chance of gaining the required support
than to have each entity working individually.
The Township board voiced concerns on the timing of the Senior Center
Resolution and the fact that more time was needed. An additional concern was
about the amount of money being requested and just what amount may be needed to
continue the Senior Center with additional staff and more programs, without
additional funding for a new building. There were a lot of questions and
insufficient answers available to satisfy the Board at the present time.
Motion by Treasurer Eyster, that the Williamstown Township Board approve the
Senior Center Resolution 2012, To Adopt the following Millage Proposal in
Williamstown Township, Ingham County, Michigan
‘WHEREAS, the Williamston Area Senior Center is a private nonprofit corporation
providing senior citizen services, programs and activities in the Township; and
WHEREAS, the Township Board may impose and levy ad valorem property taxes as
authorized by the Michigan Constitution and laws, including providing senior
citizen services as
authorized by MCL 400.571, at seq, and other applicable statutes; and
WHEREAS, the Township Board proposes to levy ‘/2 roil for twelve (12) years
(2012
through 2023) to support the Williamston Area Senior Center.
NOW, THEREFORE, the Township Board resolves to approve the following millage
proposal and directs the Clerk to submit it on the August, 2012, election
ballot:
Williamstown Township
Proposal for Senior Center Millage
Shall the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan
Constitution in
Williamstown Township be increased by 1/2 mil (50 cents per $1,000 of taxable
value) and
levied for twelve (12) years, 2012 through 2023 inclusive, to support the
Williamston Area
Senior Center, raising an estimated $111,532 in 2012.
Roll call vote:
Yes: Trustee Williams
No: Trustee Hayes, Supervisor Martin, Treasurer Eyster, Clerk Gaffner and
Trustee Wilbrink
The Supervisor declared the resolution failed.
Trustee Hayes moved to adjourn at 6:55 pm.

Unfinished Business
Library- Building Authority
Library Foundation representative, Marlene Epley and Tom Colis with Miller
Canfield, presented the request to the Township Board of a resolution to
establish a Joint Building Authority with the City of Williamston for a new
library. At this time, Wheatfield Township has decided not to participate
despite a petition request from area residents. Treasurer Eyster attended a
meeting along with the City of Williamston Mayor and city manager and
representatives of the Williamston Library Foundation regarding the formation
of a joint authority. The purpose of the authority would be to finance the
construction of a new building to house the library. A sample contract was also
included in the packet to facilitate discussion.
Discussion included:
·   Number of members in an authority is open.
·   By Statute, cannot be an elected official.
·   Each municipality would adopt the same resolution.
·   The purpose is only for financing the construction of the building.
·   An authority is the financing arm of the community.
·   Authority is filed with County Clerk and Secretary of State.
·   The authority brings forward to each municipality amount to be financed and
how to share the cost.
·   Can be based on whatever formula is agreed upon such as Taxable Value,
Population, Usage, etc.
·   Does not commit the Board until a contract is ratified by the three bodies;
the building authority, city and township.
·   Formation of the authority is the first step, second is contract and has to
be approved by the voters.
·   Township and city residents vote separately. If either says no then there
is no contract.
·   If contracts are approved, bonds can be levied for financing.
·   Treasurer Eyster attended the city council meeting when the Foundation
presented the resolution. She suggested the Township Board meet with City
Council to discuss pertinent items of the contract and be brought up to date on
the library plans. Would also like to garner input from residents.
·   Wheatfield Township: Foundation representative Jack Helder met with the
Wheatfield Board and presented a petition signed from residents. They are not
willing to go into the joint authority. The Wheatfield Board portion would be a
small portion of the funding.
·   Board must make decision regarding forming authority.
·   Vote by residents is for the contract and is the commitment to pay.
·   Makes sense to have a working group meeting with representatives, and or
boards and councils to answer questions.
·   Foundation is willing to supply any needed information needed for the
meeting.
·   Property is about 2/3 paid for.
·   Fundraisers are well attended. Received a $50,000 bequest from a will to be
applied toward the library. Conceptual plan is in place but will need
modification to meet CADL’s (Capital Area District Library) needs.
·   Reiterated need to meet with the city.
·   Elected officials cannot serve on the board.
·   NIESA was formed under a different statute.
·   Appointee of the board answers to the township board.
·   Steps include:
      1.      appointee
      2.      contract
      3.      city approve contract
      4.      twp. approve contract
   Per Act 31 of 1948.
·   The City and Township would jointly own the building.
·   What if one party wants out.
·   Issues could be addressed ahead of time in the contract.
·   CADL contract specifies communities.
·   CADL has original document.
·   Largest use of library by city residents.
·   CADL has the data regarding specifics as to use of the library.
·   Need to address future problems.
·   Separate endowment set up by foundation to maintain the building.
·   Details would be in place with the contract.
·   Approval of bond sales would need to be addressed with the city.
·   NIESA was developed under a different statute.
·   This statute is for building authorities.
·   The details are always built into the contract. Funding can come from
general fund or levy a tax. Vote is for contract. This allows the township to
be able to levy a tax.
·   Senior center should be participating in discussion.
·   Do not feel that the township can support two buildings.
·   Interest by community groups for use of a community room. Can be used when
the library is closed.
·   This is a government tax exempt building. Open to the public. Up to 5% can
be for private use. Need to make sure tax exempt status is maintained.
·   Need to have discussion while the Board can participate in the discussion
before authority is formed. Three way meeting.
·   Suggest meeting with the city in September.
·   Joint meeting is with all groups. Open meetings act.
·   Set joint meeting with city as soon as possible.
·   Could have small committee to work out some details before large group
meetings.
New Business
None

JBA Committee
The Township Board held a meeting August 5th with the Williamston City Council
to discuss creating a JBA (joint building authority). The Library Foundation
was present as well as representatives from the Senior Center. The city is
willing to request their council appoint two members to a committee to bring
back proposals to both municipalities. The Library Foundation has approached
the Township regarding the possibility of a millage for a building to house the
library as has the Senior Center. Discussion considered the possibility of
combining into one building that would serve multiple purposes. The city
purchased the community center which is currently housing the library, senior
center and food bank and is considering their options as to what they will do
with the building. Would like to appoint two board members to meet with
appointed city council members. This is the first step in a process that will
need voter approval of both municipalities as the final step.
Treasurer Eyster volunteered to serve as she has worked with both groups.
Supervisor Martin will also serve.
New Business
FreedomNet Agreement Extension
Communications chair Marvin Thompson reported that Kurt Guter, Supervisor
Mickey Martin and himself had worked on the agreement with FreedomNet. The
financial impact of the amended contract will increase rent payment from $1 a
month to $2 a month over the next 5 years. Internet will remain free for the
Township. Subscriber fees will be held at $39.95 a month for the next 5 years.
Basic install rate is increasing from $95 to $150. Insurance is available for
equipment if subscribers are interested. Fee of $1 for a paper bill. Will not
be able to provide VOIP for subscribers so this was removed from the contract.
Trustee Wilbrink moved the Williamstown Township Board approve AMENDMENT # 1 TO
THE NON-EXCLUSIVE AGREEMENT FOR BROADBAND WIRELESS INTERNET AND VoIP TELEPHONE
SERVICE
Seconded by Trustee Williams
Discussion:
Is everything else the same as the original contract?
Legal counsel reviewed the contract. Recommended revisions were incorporated.
Motion approved.
PA116 release resolution
The PA 116 program is an agreement between the State of MI that individuals
keep land in agriculture from 10 to 50 years. A portion can be removed provided
the local municipality passes a resolution that it is permissible. This removes
2 acres so the remainder can be farmed.
Trustee Hayes moved the Williamstown Township Board approve the resolution for
Partial Termination of the PA 116 Agreement number 33-0110-123116 as it relates
to the Virginia Powell Trust.
Seconded by Treasurer Eyster
Discussion:
Has this split been approved by the Township?
This is based on a survey provided by the Trust.
An application for the split will have to be submitted to complete the process.
Motion Approved.
MTT MTA assistance for appeal
Supervisor Martin submitted a memo as part of the packet regarding the MTT
(Michigan Tax Tribunal). A resident can appeal the decision of the Tax Tribunal
to the Court of Appeals. As in the past, these can been appealed all the way to
the Supreme Court. It has been requested that MTA (Michigan Township
Association) become involved due to the impact this would have on other
communities. Legal Counsel, Fahey, Schultz, Burzych and Rhodes, PLC will move
forward asking for support from MTA.
Clerk Gaffner moved that the Williamstown Township Board approve requesting the
Michigan Township Association to join the Township with financial support,
regarding the Township's legal challenge at the Michigan Tax Tribunal, as the
outcome will affect all Michigan Townships.
Seconded by Trustee Wright.
Discussion:
Spent over $10,000 on legal fees without restrictions from board.
Suggest institute any further increase in spending be approved by the board.
Trustee Wilbrink moved to amend the motion that the board must approve
expenditures, before they are spent, for Tax Tribunal.
Motion died for lack of support.
Board has a fiduciary duty to residents.
Legal Counsel advised the Township in setting up assessment.
Cost is fair and equitable to residents.
Different interpretation to Public Act 33.
Need to follow through.
Money allocated to attorney fees to use.
Board has been aware of what is happening.
Assistance from MTA will serve all communities.
Question if the board should be appealing the decision.
Last two months attorney fees of $10,000.
When resident takes a MTT decision to the Court of Appeals the resident wins if
not appealed.
If board wants another way to deal with Tax tribunal issues then a policy needs
to be set.
In budget of general appropriations-Legal defense budget.
Notification of MTT issues but not approval from board is current policy.
Resident impacting other residents by appealing.
Need to defend tax base.
Implications are state wide.
Assessment can be based on other methods beside millage.
Farmland not affected.
Not just a matter of few dollars for one person.
Longer reaching implications if not appealed.
How much are we going to spend defending an issue instead of using for police
services?
To date a hearing has not been scheduled.
Motion approved

Audit Report
Shannon Rodriguez with Layton and Richardson, PC reviewed highlights of the
audit report presented to the Board. The Township had an increase of total
assets that included increases in police and cemetery funds. There were no
expenditures greater than the budgeted amounts. Everything was in order and
looked good. There was approximately $302,000 added to the fund balances. A
letter was attached addressing the segregation of duties.
Police Report
Chief David Hall presented the monthly report to the Board. There were fewer
billable hours this month. Chief Hall met with the public safety committee. The
force has a new K-9 dog named Uby. Officer Erin Lynn will be working with Uby.
The department has requested a second K-9 dog as part of the proposed budget
before Meridian Township Board. There will be a Halloween Open House from 10-
1 on the last Saturday of the month. Equipment will be on display for residents
to inspect as well as child safety seat inspection. Three new marked Tauruses
have been purchased along with one new unmarked car for traffic enforcement.
Will be adding a new 2013 Explorer to the force for Supervisors. Supervisor
cars carry more equipment and are on the road 24/7. The force contracts with a
company out of Detroit for their cars.
