Discussion Items
Recommended revisions to the Zoning Ordinance – Accessory Dwelling Units - The
Board commended the work of the Planning Commission on these recommendations.
Updated revisions, increased square footage of the units, and the options this
ordinance provides with regards to housing and aging in place were discussed.
It was noted that residents would still need to seek approval from the Drain
Commission and Health Department, as currently required.
Park House – Supervisor Bloomquist reviewed findings of the recent assessment
completed on the Park House. Next steps would include seeking an RFP for
architectural services to complete a design of the house based on the future
use of the building. The Board questioned the vision and viability building as
an assembly spot, the feasibility of it as a revenue generating asset, and the
costs of redesigning and maintenance over time. Supervisor Bloomquist added
that any construction would have to be funded through a grant. The Board agreed
that a logical next step is to seek an architectural plan to determine possible
future costs and viability.
Reports – Departments and Committees
NIESA – Trustee Duffy reported on the March 14 th NIESA meeting. The Board
discussed MI Class transfer guidelines, as well as information and costs
regarding the potential purchase of a boat and a UTV. The Board also approved
committee members.  
Parks Committee – Trustee Steinberg updated the Board on their progress for the
new signage at the Community Park, as well as their plans for the new trees and
acorns to be planted in the forest.
Senior Center/Ingham County Board of Commissioners – Trustee Steinberg updated
the Board on the recent support of the Ingham County Board of Commissioners to
match 50% of the $750,000 needed to purchase the old Merindorf building and
relocate the Senior Center to this location to use as their new facility.
Trustee Creagh also noted that the County Board also passed a resolution to
authorize contracts for trails and parks millage (round 8 applications). This
includes the Red Cedar River Multi-Jurisdictional Clearing Project that
includes Meridian and Williamstown Townships and the City of Williamston.
Cemetery – Supervisor Bloomquist noted that the Cemetery Board will be working
on opening and closing fees for Green Burials.
Supervisor Updates – Supervisor Bloomquist shared that she was notified of a
follow-up community meeting with the Williamston Board of Education and
Superintendent Spina on May 9th. She will be able to attend and invited other
Board members to join her. There will be a postcard communication sent to
residents regarding accessing the Master Plan Survey online. Treasurer Cutshaw
requested that a paper format be available for residents who do not have access
to the internet or for those who prefer that format. Supervisor Bloomquist
confirmed that all recent FOIA requests have been fulfilled. There will be a
Celebration of Life in honor of Planning Assistant Jim Howard on April 21st at
2pm. Regarding Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) funding from the
Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, a link will be placed on the township
website and Facebook page to encourage residents to participate in sharing
their status with regards to broadband access and whether they are served/
unserved/under-served at their current address in Ingham County. Supervisor
Bloomquist updated the Board on the current status of the Consumer’s Energy
Pipeline Project within township. There is a November 24th initial completion
date with final restoration planned for April 2025.

None.
Closed at 8:49 PM

Williamston Community Schools Update
- Dr. Adam Spina, Superintendent of Williamston Community Schools, shared
highlights and district accomplishments from the past school year. He also
addressed upcoming projects and focus areas for the 2024-2025 school year
including the district’s two ballot initiatives.
Senior Center Millage Proposal Update
– Julie Rudd, Director of the Williamston Senior Center, presented updates and
future action plans for the organization. She will attend the July Township
Board Meeting to finalize November election ballot language for the Senior
Center millage proposal.
Planning Commission Report
- Chair Eidt shared a summary of the Planning Commission’s Annual Report and
their May 22nd Meeting. He noted Public Hearings were held for the proposed
changes to the Wind and Solar Energy Ordinance and the amendments to the
ordinance for Parking Standards for Multiple Family Residences. The commission
recommended the approval of the parking standards to the Township Board. The
commission declined approval of a Special Land Use Application for 5820
Shoeman. The revised Site Plan for Red Cedar Bend Apartments was reviewed. A
July public hearing was set for the 3840 Vanneter Rezoning request. The Annual
Report for 2023-2024 was approved and submitted to the Township Board. Chair
Eidt also noted the May 29th visioning workshop occurred and was well-attended
by residents.
Trustee Duffy left the meeting at 7:54pm

Planning Commission Report – Chair Eidt shared a summary of the Planning
Commission’s (PC) July 24th Meeting. He noted that Planning Consultant Doozan
provided an update on wind and solar energy systems since the last public
hearing. It was explained that new approaches have been made at the State
level, which would amend the previously reviewed regulations. It was requested
that the PC call for another public hearing on the revised regulations which
will be September 25th. A public hearing was held for the rezoning application
for 3840 Vanneter Rd. The proposed Private Road Ordinance was reviewed. A
revised ordinance will be presented at the September meeting. It was noted that
this ordinance should not be confused with regulating driveways. It was further
clarified that this ordinance does not regulate long driveways or shared
driveways. Ron Poth was elected Vice Chair of the Planning Commission in light
of the resignation of Mr. Rob Stanford. Additional public hearings were
scheduled for the September 25th Meeting for Energy Storage Systems and the
3962 Vanneter Rezoning application. Due to the number of public hearings in the
queue, Trustee Creagh suggested that it might be in the Planning Commission’s
best interest to hold a special extra meeting to ensure they are able to
complete all their tasks in timely manner.

department stay above 36 or more officers. It was also noted that there is 13%
increase in overall costs in 2025 with an additional 3% increase in 2026 and
2027.
Recycling Grant Extension – Supervisor Bloomquist reviewed the past work on
Township Recycling initiatives and the grant that had been awarded last year in
support of this work. The Township is able to seek an extension to the grant
for one year. This additional time will provide for opportunities to explore
more options and potentially partner with the county for recycling. The Board
was in consensus to move forward with the extension.

Safe Routes to School Grant Application
Trustee Creagh moved the Williamstown Township Board adopt Resolution #133
supporting the construction of a non-motorized pathway in Williamstown
Township.
Seconded by: Trustee Steinberg
Discussion: Supervisor Bloomquist provided an overview of the scope of the
project, cost estimates for the segment to be completed, ineligible costs
related to the grant/project, and the timeline should the grant be awarded. In
addition, she reviewed the revised map and the current schools that would be
included in this grant cycle. The Board discussed this project as a first step
towards the goal of having a more expansive network of sidewalks/paths for the
township neighborhoods, students, and residents to improve their access to the
schools and the broader township community. It was noted that it may be useful
to create a map that could be accessed by residents to show not only what the
overall goal of the Safe Routes to School is, but the progression of the
expansion and/or future additions, as well as what has been completed through
the grant thus far.

revisions to the Neighborhood Road Policy and recommended petition process as
amended.
Seconded by: Trustee Duffy
Discussion: The Board discussed components of the updated process to further
clarify the roles and responsibilities of the stakeholders, as well as utilize
active vs passive language in the steps. Two specific edits include: 
6. After the petitions are turned into the Township, the Township will conduct
a verification process and if the petitions meet the requirements of the
policy, public hearings will be scheduled to complete the process.
8. The petitioner(s) will be the contact person(s) for correspondence between
the Township and neighborhood for items that are not addressed in the
Neighborhood Road Policy *such as dates of construction, time frame, etc.) The
petitioners should make arrangements to inform residents that some services may
be interrupted during the construction and will need to adjust during road work
and may need to make other arrangements for services.

Discussion Items
Recycling Schedule – The Board discussed the need to continue to review the
current schedule to analyze the cost and benefits to the Township in comparison
to how many estimated residents are utilizing this monthly service. It was
noted that some initial findings indicate that plastics are increasingly
difficult to recycle because so little is accepted. There is no rebate for
glass. Paper and cardboard are the main items that generate income. The Board
recalled that the Township’s population increased as of the last census and met
the state standard whereas curbside recycling will need to be offered to
residents. There was support to continue to move forward with the analysis and
options.
Expansion of Park Board, Art Tour Board, and ZBA – Supervisor Poth addressed
the need for additional membership on some important Township committees. It
was noted that participants could be Board Members or residents and that an odd
number up to 7 would be an ideal goal. It was also noted that with our
population now over 5,000 that the ZBA should adjust to be a five member
committee versus three members. Due to this requirement, it will be sent to the
Planning Commission to be addressed.
Strategic Planning – Supervisor Poth sought the Board’s input regarding agenda
development for the upcoming Strategic Planning session on Friday, January 17
th . Topics suggested include future plans for Park House, connectivity of park
trails, recycling, and township storage. It was also suggested that Chris
Doozan be invited so that he could update members on the Master Planning and
the proposed land use changes.
Green Burial Vehicle Problems – Supervisor Poth shared recent issues with
visitors to the Summit Cemetery Green Burial section. Some are mistakenly
perceiving that the walking path is accessible with their vehicles and getting
stuck. He noted that there may need to be some considerations/site plan
adjustments moving forward to prevent this from occurring in the future. One
suggestion was a gate.
New Sick Time Laws to be approved in February – Clerk Cleveland and Treasurer
VanErp shared their policy revision work in preparation for this new state law
that goes into effect on February 21st. Once complete, they will share a draft
with the Board for their input, as well as have it reviewed by the Township
attorney. They hope to have it voted on by the February meeting.
Budget 2025 Rough Draft by February Meeting – Supervisor Poth plans to have a
draft budget for 2025-2026 to review at the February Board meeting. The Board
further discussed the Budget and Public Hearing process.
New Door Locks for Township Hall – Supervisor Poth sought the Board’s interest
in seeking proposals for new door locks, including the option of keyless entry
systems. The Board supported this initiative.
Wamhoff Display Update – Supervisor Poth confirmed receipt of Ms. Alchin’s
complaint that was recently filed. In addition, he provided the Board with an
update on the Wamhoff December display that included inspections by Meridian
Township Police, NIESA, and the Township Building Inspector. The Board
requested a copy of Ms. Alchin’s complaints. Discussion ensued regarding Event
Barn Ordinance language, visitor safety at the site, liability should an
accident occur, the applicability of a Special Use Permit in this situation,
nuisance protections for neighbors, and next steps in seeking solutions.
State Shared Revenue (SSR) – Treasurer VanErp shared this report with the Board
and explained its importance as SSR is generated from Michigan’s sales tax and
is the main source of income for the Township. The report is updated every
other month and will be included with the Treasurers report moving forward. She
noted that we are currently below the estimates from last year’s levels.  
Reports – Departments and Committees
NIESA – Trustee Duffy reported on the December 12, 2024, NIESA Board Meeting.
Public Hearings for the 2025 General and Building & Equipment Budgets were held
and approved. A Letter of Engagement to use Drake Accounting was also approved.
Twelve outdated training mannequins were donated to Williamston and Webberville
schools.
Parks Committee – No report.
Senior Center – The center was moved on Friday, December 13 th to its new
location. Due to the help, the endeavor only took two hours.
Elections – No report.
Cemetery – Treasurer VanErp noted that the committee is working to schedule a
meeting.
Roads – Supervisor Poth noted that Ingham Country Road Commission will be
hosting individual meetings with Township Supervisors in the coming weeks. A
couple of township neighborhoods have expressed interest in improving their
roads.

Township Board Meeting Minutes

Supervisor Poth called the meeting to order at 1:00 pm.

Supervisor Poth made opening comments.
Supervisor Poth welcomed participants, made opening comments, and provided an
overview of the Strategic Planning process that had occurred in the Township
since 2022. He reviewed the accomplishments of the Plan, Board, and staff. He
noted the resources that would inform the discussion for the session and the
topics that would be discussed.
Planning Consultant Chris Doozan presented a Master Plan Update. He shared the
process that has informed the work thus far and key findings with regards to
Township demographics, housing, transportation, land use, economics, and parks
and recreation.
Participants provided updates regarding trails, recycling, storage, the Park
House, and Township communications. Discussion ensued around each topic. Needs
were addressed and next steps were planned.
Committee chairs and members from the Cemetery, Historic Branch School, Roads,
Parks, and Art Tour/Harvest Festival provided highlights from 2024, possible
projects for 2025, the status of their membership, and upcoming needs for their
domain.

Public Hearing for Police Assessment Roll
Trustee Creagh moved to open the Public Hearing for the Police Assessment Roll.
Seconded by Trustee Steinberg
Discussion: The Board discussed Meridan Township Police’s current monthly
contracted hours (40), and the implications should the proposed increase (60
hours) occur. The Board noted that the most budget-feasible increase, based on
the current assessment funds that will be collected, would be 50 contracted
hours per month. It was emphasized that Meridian Township Police staffing and
the increased traffic on area roads due to the Grand River Bridge Construction
are important factors to consider when determining the necessary patrol hours.
The impact of past reductions was discussed, as well as the possible need to
increase the assessment in the future. Current assessment language stipulates
that only a 3% yearly increase can be applied to the residents each fiscal
year. This possible increase would be utilized to help fund future increases in
hours should the need dictate, and staffing allow.
Trustee Creagh moved to close the Public Hearing for the Police Assessment
Roll.
Seconded by Trustee Steinberg
Motion Passes.
Public Hearing for the Proposed Budget
Trustee Brinker moved to open the Public Hearing for the Proposed Budget.
Seconded by Trustee Steinberg
Discussion: Supervisor Poth reviewed the process he used when creating the
proposed budget. Discussion ensued on the proposed budget related to Capital
Improvement Plan Projects from 2024 that the Board would like to pursue, as
well as Township needs noted in January’s Strategic Planning Meeting.
Increasing designated budgets to reflect inflation and increased goods and
services was also addressed. Other budget-related topics discussed included
ARPA funds, Policy 12, roads, as well as the needs at the Community Park and
how best to fund them. It was noted that it has been nine years since the Park
and Township Field Usage Fee Schedule has been reviewed, and with the proposed
improvements, it may be a logical consideration for the future.
Clerk Cleveland moved to close the Public Hearing for the Proposed Budget.
Seconded by Treasurer VanErp
Motion Passes.

Seconded by Brinker

budget will be considered at the March 12, 2025 Board meeting.

Police Report
Chief Grillo reviewed quarterly Township public safety data and shared recent
staffing updates. He noted that the department recently discovered an error in
their information dashboard programming, impacting the reporting of citations
dating back to 2024. While the State fixes the error, the department completed
a hand count of all citations. Chief Grillo provided the actual number of
citations issued in 2024 as 93 and this year, as of March 21, 2025, 22
citations have been issued. Meridian Township will issue new reports that
provide the updated data. In addition, he reviewed the fiscal benefits of
adopting the Michigan Motor Vehicle Code and Meridian Township’s experience
with it over the last 15 years. Chief Grillo also provided car deer crash data
from the Township spanning 2020-2025. He credited Meridian Township’s success
in managing their deer population to the department’s collaboration with
scientists and the DNR to target problematic areas. The Board expressed
interest in inviting the staff who oversee the program to the Board’s Deer
Management Subcommittee meeting.

Public Schools. Williamstown Township will consolidate with Perry Township for
this election. The 255 Perry Schools voters in our Township have been notified
by letter of this plan for this election. Voters who are on the Permanent
Ballot List were mailed their ballots on April 1 st . The Township will be open
additional hours, from 8am to 4 pm on Saturday, May 3 rd , and from 7:00am to
8:00pm on Tuesday, May 6 th – Election Day for voter registration.
Cemetery – No new updates.
Roads – Supervisor Poth noted that brush clearing has been completed on Turner
and Barry Roads and repaving will begin soon.

information from Trustee Creagh regarding updates on the river clean-up and
that the Safe Routes To School Grant had been awarded and what will be
completed with these funds.

Prime Housing Donation

Prime Housing donation of $7,000 to be spent on Parks and Parks related
activities.
 
Seconded by: Trustee Brinker

was reminded that this money goes into a restricted fund that can only be spent
on the parks.

Ayes: Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker,
Trustee Duffy, Trustee Creagh, and Trustee Steinberg.
Nays: None
 
Motion Passed.
 
Discussion Items
 
Michigan Class Participation – Board discussion ensued regarding the liquidity
of the investments that Michigan Class offers, as well as the higher yields.
 
Deer Management – Trustee Creagh updated the Board on the recent subcommittee
meeting and the details of their session including a plan to meet with Meridian
Township to understand their deer management process, meet with Mr. Chad Fedewa
Michigan DNR Deer/Elk Specialists to get a statewide perspective, as well as
create and implement a resident survey to inform how best to tailor a program
to fit the Township’s needs. It was suggested that utilizing the summer
newsletter to share information could be a useful tool to disseminate
information. Trustee Creagh noted that thoughtful consideration to the various
perspectives regarding deer management needs to be given throughout the
process.
 
Park Bathroom & Pavilion – Supervisor Poth shared the recent findings from the
Township Building Inspector regarding the current conditions of the Park
Bathrooms and Pavilion. He noted that considerable infrastructure and
replacement work needs to be done. McKenna Planning Consultant Chris Doozan
will be working on a master plan for the park to provide a vision for moving
forward.
 
Adoption of Michigan Motor Vehicle Code – Supervisor Poth noted that he is
gathering more information regarding this Code and seeking legal counsel.
 
Truck Routes Ordinance – Supervisor Poth noted that there is a connection
between the Truck Ordinance and the Motor Vehicle Code. He would like to
revisit this ordinance when more information is gathered.
 
Reports – Departments and Committees
 
NIESA – No report.
 
Parks Committee – Trustee Steinberg updated the Board on the status of new oak
tree plantings. It will likely take place in early June. A team of residents
will be working to identify the variety species of trees around the perimeter
of the park trails. It was also suggested that the Board consider drafting a
policy regarding the financial support of local Eagle Scout Projects. It was
noted that there are some deep potholes in the bus stop parking lot and
questions were raised if those could be filled. Supervisor Poth requested that
the Park Committee review the Public Parks Ordinance No. 39 and report any
recommendations back to the Board. This could be completed in tandem with the
master plan work for the park. Supervisor Poth wants to ensure signage for the
trails is sufficient and provides those who bring animals to the parks the
correct information. Trustee Creagh updated the Board on the status of the Red
Cedar River being designated a Blue Water Trail. In addition, he noted that Top
Notch tree removal will be in the river in the next few weeks removing debris
and that signage will need to be added at the M-43/Grand River bridge launch
alerting kayakers that it is closed due to the MDOT bridge construction.
Kayakers will be routed on to Harris Nature Center.
 
Elections/Clerk – Clerk Cleveland reminded the Board of the upcoming election
for Perry Schools, as well as the hours the Township is required to be open to
accommodate any voter needs ahead of May 6th. She also requested that
subcommittees communicate meeting times to ensure that they can be properly
noticed for the residents, as well as noting participant attendance after
meetings so that payroll can be adjusted, if necessary. Clerk Cleveland updated
the Board recent IT security conversations with Meridian Township Police and
reminded the Board to report any suspicious emails or activity so that
authorities can be contacted.
 
Cemetery – Treasurer VanErp updated the Board on discussions and decisions at
the recent Cemetery Committee meeting on April 30th. The committee will be
seeking additional designs and choices for the gate to the Green Burial site.
In addition, it was determined that the current rocks on the Shepherd’s Wall
are too small for the optional engraving to commemorate those buried in the
Green Burial section at Summit Cemetery. Future considerations will need to be
made for this memorialization effort. Improvements and projects that have been
completed were checked against the current Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) so
that the CIP subcommittee can move forward with their projections.
 
Roads – Supervisor Poth noted that road work that has begun on Barry and Turner
Roads. Residents have expressed concern regarding the recent tree trimming and
branch removal on area roads. This will be shared with Ingham County. There are
no neighborhoods seeking a special assessment for road work thus far. The Road
Committee will be meeting in June.
 
Public comment for agenda and non-agenda items
Opened at 8:26 PM
 
Kevin Mark – Township Resident and Planning Commission Vice-Chair – shared his
former work experiences with investigating financial crimes and his perspective
on making fiscal decisions with careful consideration to ensure security and
minimize risk.
 
Donna Tocarchick – Township Resident and Planning Commission Secretary – shared
questions about the plans for the Smart Office monitors in the Board Room,
streaming the meetings for residents to access online from home, where to fine
previous meetings’ merged documents on the website, and sought clarifications
on how revenue is generated through the adoption of the Michigan Motor Vehicle
Code. Clerk Cleveland noted that the technicians had finalized their repairs on
the Smart Home system on April 29th and training is currently scheduled,
streaming meetings live is a possibility, and that, once uploaded, Board
Meeting merged documents remain on the website until the week before the next
scheduled monthly meeting. Supervisor Poth clarified that townships that adopt
the Michigan Motor Vehicle code collect approximately $18-20 for every ticket
issued. Currently, funds from traffic tickets issued do not come to
Williamstown Township.
 
Trustee Creagh departed the meeting at 8:30pm.
 
Closed at 8:35 PM
 
Adjournment and Review
 
Trustee Steinberg moved to adjourn the meeting.
 
Seconded by Clerk Cleveland.
 
Meeting adjourned at 8:36 PM
 
Minutes approved by:

Discussion Items
Eagle Scout Policy – The Board supports moving forward with an updated policy
that is congruent both with the guidelines and process set forth by Scouting
and procedures currently in place at the Township. A draft will be brought back
to the next meeting.
Park House Security – The Board supports seeking security system estimate
should plans move forward with utilizing Park House for storage.
Allowable Park Trail Uses – The Board discussed the current language regarding
horses at the Community Park. The Parks and Trails subcommittee is going to
review it and make suggestions. 
Replacement Check Policy – The Board considered processes for when vendors
misplace or lose checks. Members discussed proactive ideas to employ to
minimize this potential including mailing checks after events, vendors picking
up checks in person, and possibly offering ACH. These options would be
determined and included in future vendor contracts.

business” model.

number (36) of new oak tree plantings that will be donated to the Community
Park from Wild Type. Planting plans are in process. Trustee Steinberg noted
that there are other park supporters who would also like to donate items to the
park at no recognition or reimbursement. He inquired about the process for
accepting donations and suggested a policy be developed. The responsibilities
of the Harvest Festival have been transitioned to the Parks Committee. The date
is Saturday, October 4 th . The Township Office will begin contacting potential
vendors soon.

May 6 th and went smoothly. There were no audits for us or Perry Township for
this election.

alternative gate ideas for the Green Burial Site.

soon.

They are hoping to set a meeting for June.

Township Historical Committee Update
– Resident and Township Historical Committee member, Mitch Lutzke, updated the
Board on the Committee’s recent endeavor towards seeking a State Historic Site
designation for Branch School. This would be the needed first step before
seeking a designation from the National Registry. It is a 12-18 month process
which also may require some costs to the Township (for example, should the
designation be granted there would be a requirement to purchase a sign). The
Historic Committee thought it important to seek Board support and approval for
this endeavor before moving forward. The Board also inquired about the status
of the school bell tower and the need for preventative maintenance.

Planning Commission Report - Chair Eidt shared a summary of the Planning
Commission’s (PC) July 24th meeting. He noted that an application for parcel
boundary change submitted by Carol and Randy Reagan, at 1201 Germany Rd., was
considered and denied. It did not comply with the current zoning in the area.
It was suggested that a zoning request to change the current zoning to rural
estate, with possible modified setbacks, may be a better option for the Reagans
to pursue. A draft of the Master Plan was presented to the PC, who then
referred on to the Township Board. A Community Park Master Plan Workshop
immediately followed the meeting where many diverse ideas for the future of the
park were shared.
Cemetery Report – Township Sexton Mac Donnelly updated the Board on a recent
request for a temporary variance to place a memorial marker for someone buried
in the Green Burial section whose site is not near a pathway. This request
requires Board approval. Currently, the ordinance states that only pathway
adjacent spaces may have memorials. The Shepherd’s Wall was intended to provide
an optional acknowledgement for non-pathway burial sites. However, it was
recently determined that the stones on the current wall are not large enough
for carving. A new alternative will need to be developed and considered. The
timeline for this has not yet been determined. Discussion ensued around this
precedent setting request, the size stone that could be considered, if this
marker would provide maintenance obstacles for cemetery staff, and the length
of time it would be allowed placed on site. Sexton Donnelly noted that this
variance would be short term, and the stone marker would be removed once the
new memorial wall was constructed. Additional projects established by the
Cemetery Committee were also presented including a new gate at the entrance of
the Green Burial section, designing a new Shepherd’s Wall for memorializing
those in the Green Burial site, completing the landscaping plan, bringing in an
arborist to evaluate the trees in the cemetery, and paving the cemetery
driveways.

Brenda Seelman, Clark Schaefer Hackett CPAs and Advisors – Audit Presentation –
Ms. Seelman presented a summary of the recent Williamstown Township Audit for
the fiscal year ending March 31, 2025. She noted that the Township received an
unmodified clean opinion for 2024-2025. Highlights of the report included the
Township’s current revenue and expenditures, as well as changes in the fund
balance that resulted in an overall increase. Her summary included information
on internal controls and an overview of recommendations that were made and/or
implemented.
Meridian Township Police Report - Chief Grillo reviewed quarterly Township
public safety data including calls for service, traffic updates due to
construction and current detours, as well as upcoming areas of focus for the
department. He noted that with their improved staffing there is a related
increase in enforcement. A traffic team was recently formed to focus on
resident needs and observations. Chief Grillo reminded the Board to encourage
anyone who has suggestions for enforcement areas to visit the Police Department
page on Meridian Township’s website and complete a Traffic Concern Form. In
addition, with deer on the move, he said the department is seeing an uptick in
car/deer accidents and reminds residents to drive cautiously.
Planning Commission Report – Secretary Tocarchick shared a summary of the
Planning Commission’s (PC) September 24th meeting. She noted that the
Commission made the Parks and Recreation Master Plan Draft available for public
review and comment. A proposed Amendment to the Zoning Ordinance regarding

information was needed. Discussions will resume at the October meeting. A lot
split application for property 33-03-03-36-201-040 was approved. Amendments
were made to the Planning Meeting Schedule, the draft of the Capital
Improvement Plan was reviewed, and the commission was updated on recent
legislation.

Wamhoff Special Use Permit Update – Supervisor Poth reviewed the timeline set
forth in July when the Special Use Permit (SUP) was issued. Mr. Wamhoff and the
new owner of the home, located next to the seasonal display barn, sent a formal
communication to the Township regarding the construction of a fence between the
two properties. The new neighbor indicated that a fence is no longer necessary,
nor do the trucks need to be moved to create a barrier during the holiday
events. In addition, it was requested that this stipulation be removed from the
SUP. The Board discussed the intent of the original motion and the request
presented in the letter. They agreed it was acceptable to suspend the specific
fence and truck requirements so long as Mr. Wamhoff and the new neighbor’s
association remain harmonious. Should future issues arise, the Board may
require reverting back to the initial SUP criteria.

determined by the recent budget adopted by the State. The new projections will
come in by the end of the month.
∙   changes at the county level regarding Special Assessment Districts and road
engineering services. This service will no longer be offered by the Ingham
County Road Department. Townships in our county would have to hire engineering
firms to do this work.
∙   his plan to discuss the recent road work done on Barry Road with the Ingham

Williamstown Township

January 7, 2026 Strategic Planning Session
Call to Order
Supervisor Poth called the meeting to order at 6:02 pm.
Supervisor Poth welcomed participants, made opening comments, and provided an
overview of the format of the evening’s meeting.
Present:
Township Board: Supervisor Poth (Facilitator), Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer
VanErp, Trustee Brinker, Trustee Creagh, Trustee Duffy, and Trustee Steinberg.

Public Comment
Opened at 6:05
Joe Strachota, resident, expressed concerns about the proposed placements for
the ITC high voltage electric transmission line in the township, as well as the
need to create data center regulations ahead of any expressed interest by
developers.
Closed at 6:08
Master Plans - Planning Consultant Chris Doozan presented an overview of the
current Master Plan draft and the Parks and Recreation approved Master Plan,
highlighted information, as well as determinations, included in both the
Township and Parks Master Plans. Supervisor Poth noted the potential use of the
Park House for both storage and location for future restrooms.
Cemetery - Treasurer VanErp reported on the committee’s continued focus of
completing components of the Green Burial Section of Summit Cemetery including
exploration of options for an improved and larger memorial wall with
appropriate stones that can accommodate the memorial information of the
deceased (the current Shepherd’s wall cannot accommodate memorial etching),
additional landscape plans, and an entrance gate. It was noted that maintenance
on the black top cemetery road commenced in late fall of 2025 and will be
completed in the spring of 2026. A pricing structure/business model to help
offset the funding of the new memorial wall was suggested and discussed.
Historic Branch School – Historical Committee member and co-chair, Tim Green,
noted the goal of the committee is the preservation and maintenance of Branch
School and its contents. 2026 budget items that have been prioritized include
addressing the continued bee issues around the exterior of the school, sealing
and siding repairs where the hives are consistently found, maintenance of the
bell tower, preservation of the McGuffy Reader charts, continued efforts in
seeking State Historic designation, and partnering with the Cemetery Committee
on QR coding of historical elements within Foote and Summit Cemeteries.
Supervisor Poth would like to explore ways to regulate the heat in the building
in a more efficient manner.
Township Roads - Supervisor Poth noted that designated road maintenance for
2026 will be determined soon. Currently there are two neighborhoods exploring
the Special Assessment District option for road surfacing. Road funding at the
state level and engineering changes at the county level have required the
Township to revise and update the policy to reflect the impact of these shifts.
This is currently in progress.
Parks Committee - Trustee Mark Steinberg reiterated the opportunities,
projects, and plans referenced in the Parks & Recreation Master Plan. He noted
the current priorities include operational restrooms, restoration and
maintenance of the soccer fields, repairs and maintenance of the pavilion, a
reliable and robust water source for the projects that require this resource,
and continued partnership with neighboring communities for the Red Cedar Water
Trail efforts.
Participant Reports - Trustee Keith Creagh noted the upcoming focus of the
Planning Commission including their review and possible updating of Township
Ordinances with maintaining open spaces, rural character, and farmland
standards being the guiding priority. In addition, they will be strategically
examining the 425 Agreements the Township has with the City of Williamston. He
also commented on the recent work of the Deer Management Subcommittee and the
possible funding needed for components such as creating a database, resident
outreach, educational resources, and farmer/hunter/food bank coordination.
Public Comment
Opened at 8:10
None.
Closed at 8:10
NOTE:  No Board action was taken on any item at this meeting; the meeting’s
purpose was to help plan the prioritization of the numerous projects identified
in the Master Plan and Parks & Recreation Master Plan process.
Adjournment
The strategic planning session was adjourned at 8:11 p.m.

The Williamstown Township Board of Trustees held their regular meeting at 6:30

Presentation
ITC Oneida-Sabine Lake Project – Ben Tirrell, Regional Manager – Mr. Tirrell
presented information about ITC Holdings Corporation and their work in
electricity transmission, as well as connecting energy resources in Michigan’s
Lower Peninsula. He provided an overview of their current initiative: the ITC
Oneida – Sabine Lake Project. This transmission project would require
construction of a station in Livingston County (Sabine Lake) followed by a 50-
mile line connecting the Oneida Station to the Sabine Lake Station. He noted
that the process of route determination for the high voltage powerlines is
complex requiring input from many stakeholders and consideration of multiple
factors. As a result, ITC will be hosting community listening sessions across
Mid-Michigan from January 26 th through February 5 th . Locally, a session will
be held a Brookshire Golf Club on Tuesday, February 3 rd from 12pm – 7pm.
Ultimately, all the information and resident feedback will be considered by the
Michigan Public Service Commission who has the authority to make the final
determination of the powerline route. The Board asked questions and sought
information about:
∙   the timeline of the project
∙   the overall need for this initiative
∙   the themes of concern expressed to ITC by Mid-Michigan residents
potentially impacted by the project
∙   resources and materials used to construct the project
∙   easement and set back requirements due to the size of the foundations and
poles
∙   clarity on the easement agreements for and tax responsibilities of property
owners
∙   how the projects benefit the area and citizens of Williamstown Township
∙   the possible use of existing corridors for the new route
∙   how updates on the project will be issued
∙   the role of DTE and Consumers Energy, their stake in the process, and how
their customers benefit
Public Comment for agenda or non-agenda items
Opened at 7:01PM
Deborah Barone – Township Resident – expressed concern regarding the health
hazards from the high voltage wires and questioned if there was consideration
or plans for adjacent property owner compensation. She also requested the
following concerns/topics to be addressed when the Planning Commission begins
their ordinance work on data centers: water usage, power usage, impacts to
residents, and noise generation.
Monica Schafer – Ingham County Commissioner and Township Resident – expressed
gratitude to the Board for hosting the ITC Regional Manager. She also noted
that if residents had any questions or concerns regarding the recent staffing
changes at the Ingham County Road Department to reach out to her.
Joe Strachota – Township Resident – questioned ITC’s communication process. He
stated he was not notified as a property owner whose property is impacted by
one of the proposed routes. He questioned the information presented by ITC and
the viability of Sherwood Rd as a route.
Nathaniel Goodman – Non-Resident – expressed health concerns about the proposed
ITC Project as well as data centers. He also questioned the proposed routes
under consideration for the powerlines.

Police Report – Chief Grillo provided a summary of Meridian Township Police
Department’s 2025 goals and achievements. He shared the aspirations for 2026.
Planning Commission – Chair Jerry Eidt shared a summary of recent Planning
Commission (PC) Meetings. He noted that Parks and Recreation Master Plan was
reviewed and minor corrections to the document were made. The draft of this
plan was approved and sent on to the Board for a Public Hearing. In December,
the resignation of Gwen Chirico-Brandon was accepted and the open seat posted.
A Public Hearing for the Amendments to Section 4.01, subsection (F)(1)(c) was
held. The updated draft of the Master Plan was reviewed and a Public Hearing
scheduled for the January 28 th PC Meeting. An Application for a Farmland
Development Rights Agreement (formerly PA 116) for R & D Hamlin LLC was
reviewed. A Slate of Officers election was held and the existing officers will
continue through October 2026. The PC Bylaws were reviewed and updated.
Discussion was held on regulation language for data centers as a topic to
address in 2026.
ACTION ITEMS
2026 Property Tax Poverty Exemptions
Treasurer VanErp moved the Williamstown Township Board adopt the 2026 Property
Tax Exemption Resolution, #97-2026.
Second by: Trustee Brinker
Discussion: The Board discussed the total petitions received this year as
compared with previous years. There has been no increase. The process for
determining the regulations was reviewed.
Roll Call Vote:
Ayes: Trustee Brinker, Trustee Duffy, Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, Clerk
Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp,
Nays: None
Motion Passed.
Hall Rental Agreement and Fees
Clerk Cleveland moved the Williamstown Township Board approve the changes to
the Township Hall Rental Agreement with the added amendment that any excess use
of medical supplies, as a result of Renter's use, will be deducted from their
deposit. The Renter agrees that Williamstown Township shall determine the cost
of any supplies and agrees to be bound by Williamstown Township's
determination.
Second by: Trustee Brinker
Discussion: The Board discussed adding amended language to address the addition
of medical supplies that were recently installed at the Township Hall. Renters
will have access to these resources should an emergency dictate. Language was
added to the motion by Trustee Brinker.
Roll Call Vote:
Ayes: Trustee Duffy, Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland,
Treasurer VanErp, and Trustee Brinker.
Nays: None
Motion Passed.
Sewer Line Access Agreement with City of Williamston
Trustee Duffy moved the Williamstown Township Board approve the Sanitary Sewer
Utility Franchise Agreement between the Township and the City of Williamston.
Second by: Trustee Brinker
Discussion: Supervisor Poth confirmed that agreement ensures there is no
expense to the Township for this sewer services, nor does it impact any of the
Township property. Both Williamston City and Township attorneys have reviewed
the agreement. It was approved by the Williamston City Council on Tuesday,
January 13 th .
Roll Call Vote:
Ayes: Trustee Duffy, Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland,
Treasurer VanErp, and Trustee Brinker.
Nays: None
Motion Passed.
RV, Boat, and Trailer Parking Ordinance Amendments
Trustee Brinker moved the Williamstown Township Board adopt the changes
suggested in the letter from Planning Consultant, Chris Doozan.
Second by: Trustee Duffy
Discussion: It was clarified that this amendment is for platted subdivisions.
Clerk Cleveland noted that this particular amendment was presented in a
different format than how the Board typically receives Ordinance Amendments.
Roll Call Vote:
Ayes: Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp,
Trustee Brinker, and Trustee Duffy.
Nays: None
Motion Passed
Data Center Moratorium
Trustee Duffy moved the Williamstown Township Board approve a 12-month
moratorium on Data Centers in Williamstown Township.
Second by: Clerk Cleveland
Discussion: Supervisor Poth noted that as the Data Center Ordinance work
commences at the Planning Commission, the Township sought legal counsel on
creating a 12-month moratorium. This will allow time for proper research and
resident input.
Roll Call Vote:
Ayes: Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker,
Trustee Duffy, and Trustee Steinberg. 
Nays: None
Motion Passed
River Trail Resolution
Trustee Steinberg moved the Williamstown Township Board adopt the resolution
supporting the State designation of the Middle Grand River Water Trail.
Second by: Supervisor Poth
Discussion: The Board expressed their support of this recognition and
acknowledged the efforts of those who work so diligently for the development
and improvements of the Red Cedar River and the Middle Grand River Water
Trails.
Roll Call Vote:
Ayes:, Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker, Trustee Duffy,
Trustee Steinberg, and
Supervisor Poth.
Nays: None
Motion Passed
Discussion Items
26-27 Budget Preview – Supervisor Poth noted that budget preparations for
fiscal year 2026-2027 are underway. He reminded the Board that State changes in
funding are resulting in a likely revenue loss for the Township. The best
estimate for the upcoming year is approximately $33,000 in lost revenue.
Discussion ensued on possible ways to make up for the expected loss of funding.
Some of the budget items that Supervisor Poth will be examining more closely
ahead of his recommendations include recent audit fees, utility usage, the
increase in police hours from 40 to 60 hours and the Police Assessment funds,
improved tracking of resources that come from sports field and pavilion usage,
and how best to plan for the funding the restrooms at the Community Park.
Reports – Departments and Committees
Supervisor’s Report – No Report
NIESA – Trustee Duffy reported on the last three NIESA meetings. Highlights
included recognition of confined space training and staff who received this
specialized instruction. This was recently put to good use with a rescue of a
farmer who fell into a grain elevator. New officers will be elected in
February, and one Member at Large position is open for interested Township
residents. Chairperson Dorothy Hart has informed the NIESA Board that she will
retire at the end of her term as the Chairperson.
Parks Committee – Trustee Steinberg reported on the recent Strategic Planning
session, specifically the expressed priorities of the restrooms, pavilion
restoration, and sports field maintenance. He noted that detailed planning
needs to begin. The Sunrise Rotary is looking to host a bluebird nesting box
program and is interested in using the Township Hall as the site for the
program.
Elections/Clerk – Clerk Cleveland noted that there will be three elections in
2026. May 5 th will be a special election for Ingham ISD (and perhaps other
millages/proposals). There will be no Early Voting for this election, and both
the precincts will vote at the Township Hall. The August and November Elections
will have Early Voting. Clerk Cleveland will be communicating with residents
who expressed interest in working as Election Inspectors.
Cemetery – No report.
Roads – Supervisor Poth noted that the Road Committee met on Monday, January 12
th and identified roads to resurface or chip seal. The county planning meeting
will be occurring soon. There are two neighborhoods considering a Special
Assessment however, the process has been delayed with the recent changes at the
Ingham County Road Department.
Branch School – No report.
Deer Management Subcommittee – Trustee Brinker reported on the recent meeting
held on Monday, January 12 th . He referenced the draft outline of next steps
that will be needed to move forward. The Board discussed the need for a
timeline for the anticipated goal for implementation and an estimate of the
hours that the committee predicts will be needed to carry out the plan. PC
Chair Jerry Eidt (subcommittee member) noted the need to put the plans into a
formal document or ordinance. It was discussed that Planning Consultant Chris
Doozan may be able assist with this. With more communities implementing
programs like this, there are examples to reference. The next meeting will be
February 5 th at 6:00pm.
Public comment for agenda and non-agenda items
Opened at 8:32 PM
Joe Strachota – Township Resident – expressed his concern for the proposed ITC
route on Sherwood Road. He also shared several data center concerns that he
would like the Planning Commission to consider/research when developing the
ordinance.
Sara Jacobs – Township Resident – expressed her concern for the proposed ITC
route on Sherwood Road. She recently purchased her property on Sherwood before
this information from ITC was disseminated and is concerned that the route
renders her land as unusable and stated her plans to build on her property
would be greatly impacted.
Kevin Mark – Planning Commission Vice-Chair and Township Resident – shared
concerns about the Township’s investment options in the current economy, the
condition of the CATA bus stop located near the Community Park, and funding of
the park sports fields. He expressed his support for the Meridian Township
Police and confirmed the rate could be increased back to $120/year, if needed.
Closed at 8:41 PM
